71    /// Apply the established unsupported-syscall refusal policy to a *supported*
72    /// syscall whose particular operation Detcore cannot serve deterministically.
73    ///
74    /// This exists so such a refusal cannot invent its own policy. Three separate
75    /// config knobs govern how a fail-closed run dies -- `shutdown_on_unsupported_syscall`
76    /// (hard `exit(1)` through `unrecoverable_shutdown`), `exit_on_unsupported_syscall`
77    /// (a typed `UnsupportedSyscallError` the backend terminates on without
78    /// unwinding), and the `panic!` fallback -- and `Detcore::handle_unsupported_syscall`
79    /// consults all three in that order. The normal `hermit run` CLI happens to set
80    /// `shutdown_on_unsupported_syscall = panic_on_unsupported_syscalls`, so reading
81    /// only the latter looks equivalent, but that coupling is a CLI default, not an
82    /// invariant: an embedder that sets just `exit_on_unsupported_syscall` would get a
83    /// process-wide `exit(1)` from a bespoke call site where the standard path returns
84    /// a catchable error.
85    ///
86    /// When the run is *not* fail-closed, the caller's `fallback` errno is returned,
87    /// because the operation itself is legal and the guest is entitled to a normal
88    /// failure code (`handle_unsupported_syscall` passes the call through instead,
89    /// which is not available here -- passing through is precisely the thing the
90    /// caller has determined it cannot do).
91    pub(crate) async fn refuse_unserviceable_operation<G: Guest<Self>>(
92        &self,
93        guest: &mut G,
94        sysno: reverie::syscalls::Sysno,
95        fallback: Errno,
96    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
97        refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
98            guest,
99            self.cfg.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
100            sysno,
101            fallback,
102            None,
103        )
104        .await
105    }
106
107    /// [`Self::refuse_unserviceable_operation`], with the backend's own
108    /// description of why it cannot perform the operation, which a
109    /// fail-closed refusal reports as its reason.
110    pub(crate) async fn refuse_unserviceable_operation_because<G: Guest<Self>>(
111        &self,
112        guest: &mut G,
113        sysno: reverie::syscalls::Sysno,
114        fallback: Errno,
115        reason: &str,
116    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
117        refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
118            guest,
119            self.cfg.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
120            sysno,
121            fallback,
122            Some(reason),
123        )
124        .await
125    }

127    /// A backend that does not implement a guest's call declines it with an
128    /// errno and the typed refusal `operation` (`reverie::UnsupportedRefusal`),
129    /// as for `flock` and for a signal it cannot deliver. Report that refusal
130    /// by name ([`report_refusal_reason`]), and route it through the
131    /// unsupported-operation policy
132    /// ([`Self::refuse_unserviceable_operation_because`]), instead of handing
133    /// the guest the backend's errno as if Linux had answered the call: a
134    /// fail-closed run ends as a policy refusal, and a run that allows
135    /// unsupported operations gives the guest the refusal's errno. Callers
136    /// pass the handler's result right after the injection that may have been
137    /// refused, since the next injection replaces the backend's record. A
138    /// result that is not the refusal's errno, and a backend that records no
139    /// refusal, pass through unchanged; a refusal of another operation passes
140    /// the result through with a warning. No backend is named here: the policy
141    /// is keyed on the backend's refusal alone.
142    pub(crate) async fn report_backend_refusal<G: Guest<Self>>(
143        &self,
144        guest: &mut G,
145        sysno: Sysno,
146        operation: reverie::UnsupportedOperation,
147        result: Result<i64, Error>,
148    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
149        let errno = match &result {
150            Err(Error::Errno(errno)) => *errno,
151            _ => return result,
152        };
153        let Some(refusal) = guest.take_unsupported_refusal() else {
154            return result;
155        };
156        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
157        if refusal.operation != operation || refusal.errno != errno {
158            tracing::warn!(
159                "[dtid {dettid}] {sysno}: the backend's refusal ({:?}, {}) is not the one this \
160                 call can be refused with ({operation:?}, {errno}): {}",
161                refusal.operation,
162                refusal.errno,
163                refusal.diagnostic
164            );
165            // Judged as any other last refusal of an event is, as it would
166            // have been had this call not taken it.
167            judge_backend_refusal::<T, G>(guest, Some(refusal), sysno);
168            return result;
169        }
170        report_refusal_reason(
171            self.cfg.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
172            &format!(
173                "[dtid {dettid}] {sysno} refused by the backend: {}",
174                refusal.diagnostic
175            ),
176        );
177        if !self.cfg.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls {
178            crate::tool_global::report_unsupported_syscall(guest, sysno).await;
179        }
180        self.refuse_unserviceable_operation_because(guest, sysno, refusal.errno, refusal.diagnostic)
181            .await
182    }

184    /// Record or replay a BLOCKING syscall without stalling the current thread (and thus
185    /// deadlocking).  This uses a protocol of an extra resource request before/after the
186    /// syscall to inform the scheduler that the thread is leaving/rejoining the runnable
187    /// threads pool.
188    ///
189    /// This is only valid to use (1) in hermit record/replay modes, or (2)
190    /// when we're in "hermit run", but we're NOT sequentializing threads, because in
191    /// that case it's ok to use the blocking versions of system calls.
192    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking<G: Guest<Self>>(
193        &self,
194        guest: &mut G,
195        call: Syscall,
196    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
197        self.record_or_replay_blocking_with_mask(guest, call, None)
198            .await
199    }
200
201    /// `record_or_replay_blocking`, running `after_grant` once the
202    /// scheduler has granted the blocking request and before the call
203    /// runs natively — the same mask and input-lease semantics, with a
204    /// post-grant receipt point for callers that must prove admission
205    /// happened (a receipt emitted before this point would only prove
206    /// the route was chosen).
207    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking_then<G: Guest<Self>>(
208        &self,
209        guest: &mut G,
210        call: Syscall,
211        after_grant: impl FnOnce(&mut G),
212    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
213        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
214        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
215        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then(
216            guest,
217            (call, call),
218            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id),
219            None,
220            false,
221            after_grant,
222        )
223        .await
224    }

226    /// `record_or_replay_blocking`, with `run` the call that runs for `call`,
227    /// or that replay serves: the scheduler, the checks and the continuation
228    /// mask all see `call`. A kernel-run poll's restart is the one such pair:
229    /// the guest's own `restart_syscall` runs for the poll
230    /// (`Detcore::resume_kernel_poll`). Only x86_64 has `poll`.
231    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
232    pub(crate) async fn record_or_replay_blocking_as<G: Guest<Self>>(
233        &self,
234        guest: &mut G,
235        call: Syscall,
236        run: Syscall,
237    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
238        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
239        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
240        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then(
241            guest,
242            (call, run),
243            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id),
244            None,
245            false,
246            |_| {},
247        )
248        .await
249    }

251    /// `record_or_replay_blocking` for a call that sleeps under its own
252    /// temporary signal mask (`ppoll`, `pselect6`, or an `rt_sigsuspend` that
253    /// finds a signal already pending): `blocked_signal_mask` is the mask the
254    /// kernel installs for the call, read in this thread's turn
255    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask`). `None` means the call sleeps under
256    /// the thread's own mask.
257    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking_with_mask<G: Guest<Self>>(
258        &self,
259        guest: &mut G,
260        call: Syscall,
261        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
262    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
263        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
264        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
265        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource(
266            guest,
267            call,
268            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id),
269            blocked_signal_mask,
270            false,
271        )
272        .await
273    }

275    /// `record_or_replay_blocking` for a call that sleeps under a temporary
276    /// mask its turn cannot vouch for (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`):
277    /// the scheduler records no sleeping mask for it.
278    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask<G: Guest<Self>>(
279        &self,
280        guest: &mut G,
281        call: Syscall,
282    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
283        self.record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask_then(guest, call, |_| {})
284            .await
285    }

287    /// `record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask`, running `after_grant` once
288    /// the scheduler has granted the call and before it runs: after any
289    /// sibling that ran while the request waited. In replay nothing else runs
290    /// until the served call finishes; in recording a sibling turn may still
291    /// run before the call enters the kernel.
292    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask_then<G: Guest<Self>>(
293        &self,
294        guest: &mut G,
295        call: Syscall,
296        after_grant: impl FnOnce(&mut G),
297    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
298        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
299        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
300        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then(
301            guest,
302            (call, call),
303            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id),
304            None,
305            true,
306            after_grant,
307        )
308        .await
309    }

311    /// Execute the real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the runnable set while preserving
312    /// its signal-only completion condition for the scheduler. `temporary_mask`
313    /// is the mask the call sleeps under, as `Resources::blocked_signal_mask`
314    /// describes.
315    pub async fn record_or_replay_rt_sigsuspend<G: Guest<Self>>(
316        &self,
317        guest: &mut G,
318        call: syscalls::RtSigsuspend,
319        temporary_mask: u64,
320    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
321        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
322        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
323        let result = self
324            .record_or_replay_blocking_resource(
325                guest,
326                call.into(),
327                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op_id),
328                Some(temporary_mask),
329                false,
330            )
331            .await;
332        // Linux's rt_sigsuspend ends only with ERESTARTNOHAND, which a handler
333        // turns into EINTR and never restarts. The host call reports
334        // ERESTARTSYS instead when the signal reached the thread before the
335        // call ran, which depends on host timing; under SA_RESTART the guest
336        // then slept again where Linux returns
337        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4320). This fixes the
338        // result and the restart only: in that case the call never ran, so
339        // the kernel never installed its temporary mask, and the handler runs
340        // under the thread's pre-call mask, still a host-timed difference when
341        // the two masks differ (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4338).
342        // Whether the kernel ran the call, before that normalization hides it
343        // (`signal_shadow::kernel_ran_the_wait`). A replayed result is not
344        // taken as evidence, so under replay the wait never counts as run.
345        if !self.cfg.replaying {
346            let ran = !matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)));
347            super::signal_shadow::note_wait_ran(guest, ran);
348        }
349        match result {
350            Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)) => Err(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND.into()),
351            other => other,
352        }
353    }

355    async fn record_or_replay_blocking_resource<G: Guest<Self>>(
356        &self,
357        guest: &mut G,
358        call: Syscall,
359        blocking_resource: ResourceID,
360        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
361        blocked_signal_mask_unknown: bool,
362    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
363        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then(
364            guest,
365            (call, call),
366            blocking_resource,
367            blocked_signal_mask,
368            blocked_signal_mask_unknown,
369            |_| {},
370        )
371        .await
372    }

374    /// `record_or_replay_blocking_resource`, running `after_grant` between the
375    /// grant and the call, and running `run` for `call`
376    /// (`record_or_replay_blocking_as`).
377    async fn record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then<G: Guest<Self>>(
378        &self,
379        guest: &mut G,
380        (call, run): (Syscall, Syscall),
381        blocking_resource: ResourceID,
382        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
383        blocked_signal_mask_unknown: bool,
384        after_grant: impl FnOnce(&mut G),
385    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
386        // D41 (A5 step 3c.1c): the first statement of every background
387        // external call and `rt_sigsuspend`, the two kernel-run families
388        // filed here, before anything below refuses, files or runs it.
389        if let Some(refused) = kernel_run_entry_refusal(guest)? {
390            return Err(refused);
391        }
392        // A host wait on descriptors that may include a timerfd on virtual
393        // time would never see it readable (`crate::syscalls::timerfd`).
394        crate::syscalls::timerfd::refuse_host_wait_for(guest, call);
395        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
396        let op_id = match &blocking_resource {
397            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id) | ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op_id) => {
398                *op_id
399            }
400            _ => unreachable!("blocking syscall helper requires a blocking resource"),
401        };
402        // Replay serves some of these calls from the recording, so they cannot block.
403        // They still run in the background, as they did during recording, so that the
404        // schedule matches the recording's. The flag makes the scheduler commit no
405        // other turn until they finish. Otherwise a stand-in descriptor that replay
406        // creates for an accepted connection could take its slot before or after
407        // another thread's open or close, and which of these calls had finished, and
408        // so the order in which they rejoin, would depend on host timing
409        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3871).
410        let replay_served_from_log = self.cfg.replaying
411            && (replay_serves_blocking_call_from_log(call)
412                || replay_serves_socket_call_from_log(guest, call));
413        // Internal-vs-external fd classification happens at the call sites that hold the
414        // typed, nonblockize-able syscall (see execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall):
415        // container-internal pipes are routed to the InternalIOPolling nonblockize-retry
416        // path and must NOT reach this external-blocking protocol. BlockingExternalIO
417        // deschedules the thread to run in the background and rejoin nondeterministically,
418        // which is unsafe for a pipe whose reader and writer are interdependent -- doing
419        // so is the root cause of the record/replay pipe deadlock. The remaining callers
420        // (external poll, wait4) are external by construction (their fd is not a single
421        // extractable internal pipe). Guard the invariant in debug builds while the
422        // deterministic scheduler is active. With thread sequentialization disabled,
423        // resource requests are no-ops and internal pipes intentionally use a blocking
424        // host syscall, as documented by this method.
425        debug_assert!(
426            !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads || !syscall_targets_internal_fd(guest, call),
427            "record_or_replay_blocking (BlockingExternalIO) reached for an internal fd \
428             (pipe or socketpair endpoint) on syscall {}; internal fds must use the \
429             InternalIOPolling path",
430            call.name()
431        );
432        // Classify the actual substituted native buffers before releasing
433        // the turn. EntryImport snapshots alone do not make indirect kernel
434        // inputs immutable. The lease survives native return and decoder
435        // copyout until the matching continuation really admits this task.
436        let input_access = crate::reserved_input::BackgroundAccess::acquire(guest, run)?;
437        crate::reserved_input::before_native_call(guest, run)?;
438        {
439            let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
440            // With sequentialization enabled, only truly EXTERNAL endpoints reach here.
441            // Without it, resource_request is a no-op and internal fds may block directly.
442            rsrcs.reads_signalfd = matches!(blocking_resource, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
443                && call_reads_signalfd(guest, call);
444            if matches!(blocking_resource, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_)) {
445                rsrcs.read_fd =
446                    read_family_fd(call).map(|fd| (guest.thread_state().files_id(), fd));
447            }
448            rsrcs.insert(blocking_resource, Permission::RW);
449            rsrcs.fyi(call.name());
450            rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask = blocked_signal_mask;
451            rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = blocked_signal_mask_unknown;
452            rsrcs.replay_served_from_log = replay_served_from_log;
453            // A send leaving the turn reports a possible pass-out with this
454            // request (`Detcore::passes_descriptors_out_outside_the_turn`).
455            Detcore::<T>::passes_descriptors_out_outside_the_turn(guest, call);
456            resource_request(guest, rsrcs).await;
457        }
458        after_grant(guest);
459        // Race probes (docs/RACE_PROBES.md) may delay the call or its rejoin;
460        // both are host timing this protocol already treats as nondeterministic.
461        crate::race_probe::delay(crate::race_probe::BG_PRE_CALL).await;
462        tracing::trace!(
463            "Guest proceeding to execute potentially blocking call {}...",
464            call.name()
465        );
466        let res = {
467            // This explicit child owner was created before grant release and
468            // owns these exact background leases. It replaces the enclosing
469            // callback's observation binding only for this native operation.
470            let mut native_guest = reverie::NativeOperationGuest::<_, Self>::optional(
471                guest,
472                input_access
473                    .as_ref()
474                    .map(|access| access.native_operation()),
475            )?;
476            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(&mut native_guest, run)
477                .await
478        };
479        let native_returned = res.is_ok() || matches!(&res, Err(Error::Errno(_)));
480        if native_returned && let Some(access) = &input_access {
481            access.returned()?;
482        }
483        crate::race_probe::delay(crate::race_probe::BG_POST_CALL).await;
484        // N.B. BlockingExternalIO is a "oneshot" resource, so no need to release
485        // explicitly here:
486        {
487            let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
488            rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
489            rsrcs.fyi(call.name());
490            // The mask the thread is stopped under here, as the scheduler may
491            // decide from it before this turn (`BlockedPool::continuation_masks`).
492            match continuation_mask(call, &res) {
493                ContinuationMask::Temporary => {
494                    rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask = blocked_signal_mask;
495                    rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = blocked_signal_mask_unknown;
496                }
497                ContinuationMask::Unknown => rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = true,
498                ContinuationMask::Restored => {}
499            }
500            resource_request(guest, rsrcs).await;
501        }
502        if native_returned && let Some(access) = input_access {
503            // Synchronous retirement, before any subsequent yield or RPC.
504            access.readmitted()?;
505        }
506        res
507    }

509    /// Whether [`Self::execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall`] runs `call` as a
510    /// blocking call outside this thread's turn
511    /// ([`Self::record_or_replay_blocking`]), where other threads may run
512    /// before the kernel reads the call's arguments: without sequentialized
513    /// threads, for an external descriptor under record and replay, for a
514    /// descriptor that is blocking in the kernel as well, and where the
515    /// descriptor cannot be classified. Decided as that function decides it.
516    pub(crate) fn nonblockable_call_runs_outside_turn<G, C>(&self, guest: &mut G, call: C) -> bool
517    where
518        G: Guest<Self>,
519        C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall> + Copy,
520    {
521        let wrapped: Syscall = call.into();
522        match ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, call) {
523            Err(_) => true,
524            Ok(action) => {
525                !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads
526                    || (self.cfg.recordreplay_modes && !syscall_targets_internal_fd(guest, wrapped))
527                    || action == IOAction::Blocking
528            }
529        }
530    }
531
532    /// Executes a nonblockable syscall according to the following strategy:
533    /// - Record mode: Execute possibly blocking syscall
534    /// - Run mode: Transform the syscall to nonblocking if required before executing
535    ///
536    /// These are fd-oriented syscalls in the sense that whether they block or not depends
537    /// on whether NONBLOCK was set on the corresponding file descriptor.
538    pub async fn execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall<
539        G: Guest<Self>,
540        C: SyscallInfo + NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
541    >(
542        &self,
543        guest: &mut G,
544        call: C,
545    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
546        let wrapped: Syscall = call.into();
547
548        let action = match ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, call) {
549            Ok(action) => action,
550            Err(errno) => {
551                // Descriptor metadata is advisory for choosing an execution strategy. If the
552                // descriptor is invalid or cannot be classified, execute through the
553                // scheduler-safe blocking path and let the kernel provide the syscall errno.
554                // Returning the metadata error (or panicking on it) can change Linux error
555                // precedence, for example connect(-1, invalid_sockaddr, ...).
556                tracing::trace!(
557                    "NonblockableSyscall: fd classification failed with {}; executing kernel-authoritatively: {}",
558                    errno,
559                    call.name()
560                );
561                return self.record_or_replay_blocking(guest, wrapped).await;
562            }
563        };
564
565        // Is this operation on a container-INTERNAL fd (a pipe, a socketpair
566        // endpoint, or a socket whose peer is a guest)? Internal fds are made
567        // physically nonblocking even in record/replay (see handle_pipe2,
568        // handle_socketpair and classify_socket_peer), so they can take the
569        // deterministic InternalIOPolling nonblockize-and-retry path. They must NOT be
570        // forced onto the BlockingExternalIO path in R/R: a reader and its paired
571        // writer are not independent, so descheduling the reader as "external
572        // blocking IO" deadlocks the sequentialized scheduler (the documented R/R pipe
573        // hang), and a one-shot read on the physically nonblocking fd returns EAGAIN.
574        // Truly external endpoints (host fds, network sockets, sockets whose peer
575        // is a host process) still use BlockingExternalIO.
576        let internal_fd = syscall_targets_internal_fd(guest, wrapped);
577
578        if !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads
579            || (self.cfg.recordreplay_modes && !internal_fd)
580            || action == IOAction::Blocking
581        {
582            tracing::trace!(
583                "NonblockableSyscall: executing in blocking mode after all: {}",
584                call.name()
585            );
586            // We let these have nondeterminstic timing in record mode:
587            Ok(self.record_or_replay_blocking(guest, wrapped).await?)
588            // If in the future we want to record EXTERNAL network traffic only, we have a
589            // challenge to overcome.  We don't know if we need to record until after the
590            // accept completes, so we need an API for *post-facto* recording.
591        } else if action == IOAction::NonblockizeRetry {
592            tracing::trace!(
593                "NonblockableSyscall: converting to nonblocking syscall (internal polling): {}",
594                call.name()
595            );
596            let mut rsrc = Resources::new(guest.thread_state().dettid);
597            rsrc.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
598            rsrc.fyi(call.name());
599            // A later part of a call run in parts files this fresh request
600            // without the guest having resumed since the previous part,
601            // which transferred bytes: on the wire it is retry number 1
602            // after progress, not a new call's first attempt, so the
603            // scheduler does not count its grant as guest progress for
604            // the SIGCHLD fence (`Scheduler::unblock_guest`).
605            if guest
606                .thread_state()
607                .call_parts
608                .as_ref()
609                .is_some_and(|parts| parts.progress)
610            {
611                rsrc.upgraded_from_attempt = 1;
612                rsrc.previous_attempt_made_progress = true;
613            }
614            // Binary record/replay keeps the internal-FD authority captured at
615            // entry, as its existing FIFO-open policy requires. Plain runs
616            // instead need revocable proof of closed guest membership.
617            if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
618                rsrc.polls_guest_state_only = internal_fd;
619                refresh_guest_poll_state(guest, wrapped, &mut rsrc);
620            } else {
621                (rsrc.polls_guest_state_only, rsrc.relies_on_guest_held_marks) =
622                    single_fd_poll_readiness(guest, wrapped, internal_fd);
623            }
624            // A named FIFO may also be held by a process outside the guest.
625            rsrc.polls_a_named_fifo =
626                internal_fd && get_fd(wrapped).is_some_and(|fd| is_named_fifo(guest, fd));
627            // A pipe read: a recorded private `SIGCHLD` ends it as on Linux.
628            rsrc.private_sigchld_decides = reads_a_pipe(guest, wrapped);
629            // ... and names the read it polls for, which binds a SIGALRM
630            // reserved for one of its probes (`Scheduler::reserve_sigalrm_poll`).
631            if rsrc.private_sigchld_decides {
632                rsrc.read_fd =
633                    read_family_fd(wrapped).map(|fd| (guest.thread_state().files_id(), fd));
634            }
635            // A read waits for data, a write for room (`--pipe-wake-latency`).
636            rsrc.polls_channel = crate::pipe_wake::poll_of(&wrapped).and_then(|(fd, wants)| {
637                self.pipe_channel_end(guest, fd)
638                    .map(|end| Box::new((end.channel, wants)))
639            });
640            // In record/replay mode, route an internal-fd (pipe or socketpair) read/write through the
641            // record/replay subtool so its data is captured on record and reproduced on
642            // replay (see retry_nonblocking_syscall). In plain `hermit run` there is no
643            // recorder, so execute directly (subtool = None).
644            let subtool = (self.cfg.recordreplay_modes && internal_fd).then_some(self);
645            // A logically blocking socket call waits only as long as the
646            // socket's timeout allows: `SO_RCVTIMEO` for a receive or an
647            // accept, `SO_SNDTIMEO` for a send or a connect
648            // (`socket_timeout_fd`). The socket is physically nonblocking,
649            // so no kernel timeout can fire; without a deadline the retry
650            // below would poll forever instead of giving Linux's answer
651            // for a wait that outlasts the timeout: EAGAIN for a send
652            // (`sock_alloc_send_pskb`, net/core/sock.c:2936,2951-2956),
653            // a receive (`__unix_dgram_recvmsg`,
654            // net/unix/af_unix.c:2611-2615), an accept and an AF_UNIX
655            // connect (net/unix/af_unix.c:1720-1733) -- but EINPROGRESS
656            // for a TCP connect, which is already in progress when it
657            // gives up waiting and continues in the background
658            // (`inet_stream_connect`, net/ipv4/af_inet.c:690-703), all at
659            // v6.17. The timeout and the connect's family are read once
660            // here and the entry time below, as Linux reads the timeout
661            // once when the call begins; the interrupt class the retry
662            // loop uses derives from this same snapshot (passed to the
663            // retry loop), not from a second read after the entry time's
664            // yield, across which a setsockopt through an alias could
665            // have changed it. An `Unknown` model (a setsockopt whose
666            // value Detcore could not read) keeps the unbounded wait, as
667            // it does for the interrupt errno.
668            let socket_timeout = socket_timeout_fd(wrapped).and_then(|(fd, direction)| {
669                guest
670                    .thread_state()
671                    .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
672                        matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Socket).then(|| match direction {
673                            SocketTimeoutDirection::Receive => detfd.receive_timeout(),
674                            SocketTimeoutDirection::Send => detfd.send_timeout(),
675                        })
676                    })
677                    .ok()
678                    .flatten()
679            });
680            let entry_interrupt_errno = socket_timeout.map(|timeout| {
681                socket_timeout_interrupt_errno(call.signal_interrupt_errno(), Some(timeout))
682            });
683            let connect_family = match wrapped {
684                Syscall::Connect(connect) => connect
685                    .uservaddr()
686                    .and_then(|addr| guest.memory().read_value(addr.cast::<u16>()).ok()),
687                _ => None,
688            };
689            let expiry = socket_timeout_expiry(wrapped, connect_family);
690            let immediate_expiry = matches!(socket_timeout, Some(ReceiveTimeout::Immediate));
691            let maybe_timeout = match socket_timeout {
692                Some(ReceiveTimeout::After(duration)) => {
693                    Some((thread_observe_time(guest).await + duration, Err(expiry)))
694                }
695                Some(ReceiveTimeout::Immediate) => {
696                    Some((thread_observe_time(guest).await, Err(expiry)))
697                }
698                _ => None,
699            };
700            Ok(retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(
701                guest,
702                call,
703                rsrc,
704                maybe_timeout,
705                subtool,
706                entry_interrupt_errno,
707                immediate_expiry,
708            )
709            .await?)
710        } else {
711            assert!(action == IOAction::PassThru);
712            tracing::trace!(
713                "NonblockableSyscall: just passing it through: {}",
714                call.name()
715            );
716            // Otherwise, the socket was already nonblocking, so we can safely execute it just once.
717            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, wrapped)
718                .await
719        }
720    }
721
722    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
723    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#547)
724    /// Complete a logically blocking pipe writev after Hermit has made the pipe physically
725    /// nonblocking. A positive short write is an implementation artifact here: without
726    /// O_NONBLOCK, Linux blocks until the full vector is written unless a signal or error
727    /// interrupts it. Atomic vectors retain a private iovec snapshot for every retry; larger
728    /// vectors advance a positive short-write remainder through scalar writes.
729    pub async fn execute_blocking_pipe_writev<G: Guest<Self>>(
730        &self,
731        guest: &mut G,
732        call: syscalls::Writev,
733        expected_open_file: OpenFileId,
734    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
735        const MAX_IOVECS: usize = 1024;
736        // Linux limits a single vectored transfer to INT_MAX rounded down to a page.
737        let max_rw_count = crate::page::max_rw_count();
738        // Linux guarantees pipe writes through this size are atomic.
739        const PIPE_BUF: usize = 4096;
740        // Every backend provides at least 512 bytes of tool scratch. Linux's
741        // own fast-iovec path is smaller; this covers common vectors.
742        const STACK_IOVECS: usize = 32;
743
744        let Some(iov_addr) = call.iov() else {
745            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
746        };
747        if call.len() == 0 || call.len() > MAX_IOVECS {
748            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
749        }
750
751        let iovecs: Vec<(usize, usize)> = {
752            let mut raw_iovecs = vec![
753                libc::iovec {
754                    iov_base: std::ptr::null_mut(),
755                    iov_len: 0,
756                };
757                call.len()
758            ];
759            guest.memory().read_values(iov_addr, &mut raw_iovecs)?;
760            raw_iovecs
761                .into_iter()
762                .map(|iovec| (iovec.iov_base as usize, iovec.iov_len))
763                .collect()
764        };
765        // The array as the call began, in the form the guest's own `writev`
766        // copies it: that attempt may come after another thread has run
767        // (`EntryImport`), unlike the later ones, which write from `iovecs`.
768        // Boxed, so the call's future stays small (`hot_path_futures_stay_small`).
769        let entry_import =
770            EntryImport::capture(&guest.memory(), &Syscall::Writev(call)).map(Box::new);
771        let requested = iovecs.iter().try_fold(0usize, |total, (_, length)| {
772            total.checked_add(*length).ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)
773        })?;
774        if requested > isize::MAX as usize {
775            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
776        }
777        let target = requested.min(max_rw_count);
778        if target == 0 {
779            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
780        }
781
782        let atomic_pipe_write = target <= PIPE_BUF;
783
784        tracing::trace!(
785            "NonblockableSyscall: converting to nonblocking syscall (internal polling): writev"
786        );
787        let guest_held = syscall_targets_guest_held_fd(guest, call.into());
788        let mut resources = pipe_writev_resources(guest.thread_state().dettid, call, guest_held);
789        resources.polls_a_named_fifo = is_named_fifo(guest, call.fd());
790        resources.polls_guest_state_only = self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
791            || resources.polls_guest_state_only
792            || resources.polls_a_named_fifo;
793        resources.polls_channel = self
794            .pipe_channel_end(guest, call.fd())
795            .map(|end| Box::new((end.channel, crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Space)));
796        let subtool = self.cfg.recordreplay_modes.then_some(self);
797        let mut current = Syscall::Writev(call);
798        let mut written_total = 0usize;
799
800        // Keep ordinary signals pending while the scheduler and the target-side
801        // disposition check decide whether a wakeup interrupts this write. The
802        // ptrace-owned backends need the explicit mask while inspecting the
803        // target's current disposition.
804        let blocked_mask = blocked_signal_mask();
805        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
806        let atomic_scratch_iov = if atomic_pipe_write && iovecs.len() <= STACK_IOVECS {
807            let mut raw_iovecs = [libc::iovec {
808                iov_base: std::ptr::null_mut(),
809                iov_len: 0,
810            }; STACK_IOVECS];
811            for (raw, (base, length)) in raw_iovecs.iter_mut().zip(&iovecs) {
812                raw.iov_base = *base as *mut libc::c_void;
813                raw.iov_len = *length;
814            }
815            let scratch_iov: Addr<libc::iovec> = stack.push(raw_iovecs).cast();
816            Some(scratch_iov.as_raw())
817        } else {
818            None
819        };
820        let blocked_mask_addr = stack.push(blocked_mask);
821        let old_mask_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
822        let turn_mask_cell = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
823        let action_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
824        let _mask_guard = stack.commit()?;
825        // A parked pipe write under the in-guest delivery gate (A5 step 3c.1c,
826        // D50 reader 1) installs no private mask: once an attempt would wait
827        // for room, the design's deliverable set under the thread's published
828        // mask decides (`gated_wait_ends`).
829        let gated = guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery;
830        let checks_at_turn =
831            !gated && decides_interruption_at_turn(guest, guest_signal_state_task(guest));
832        // Where the turn decides (`read_turn_signals`), the state is read, and
833        // the first attempt made, in the slice of the call's own entry, as the
834        // scalar writer's first attempt is, under the guest's own mask: that
835        // attempt is the guest's own `writev`, which the backend runs as plain
836        // ptrace runs it, with every pending signal left queued in the kernel,
837        // and a copy pending at entry ends the call after it (rules 5 and 6).
838        // No other thread runs between Detcore's snapshot of the iovec array,
839        // taken as it handles the call, and that attempt, so the kernel imports
840        // the array Detcore copied, which every later attempt writes from. A
841        // rewrite that lands before the snapshot (while the call waits at a
842        // checkpoint before its handler runs) is one Linux could also see,
843        // before the call imports the array.
844        // Requesting a turn first let another thread rewrite the array before
845        // the import, and an atomic write to a full pipe then wrote its bytes
846        // (writev_determinism's atomic full-pipe case, which reverted the
847        // first landing of R2b-1). Only a call that goes on polling installs the
848        // private mask, through `KernelSignalWait::block`, in the same turn
849        // (`install_turn_mask`); no copy that ends the call is pending then,
850        // and one Linux discarded at send is held until the call returns.
851        // Installing it first let two such copies stop the installation, and
852        // the backend's single held slot kept only the second (the Claude
853        // implementation review of R2b-1, F2;
854        // https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1012).
855        let mut first_turn = if checks_at_turn {
856            let turn = read_turn_signals(guest, None, 0, NamedRealTime::ByDisposition).await?;
857            Some((ResumeStatus::Normal, turn))
858        } else {
859            None
860        };
861        let mut turn_wait = checks_at_turn
862            .then(|| KernelSignalWait::new(guest, 0, false, call.signal_interrupt_errno()));
863        let mut turn_mask: Option<KernelSigset> = None;
864        let guest_signal_mask = if checks_at_turn || gated {
865            0
866        } else {
867            block_signals_for_disposition(guest, blocked_mask_addr, old_mask_addr).await?
868        };
869
870        let result: Result<i64, Error> = loop {
871            let written_before = written_total;
872            // A cross-task signal can replace the initial scheduler request,
873            // before the first physical attempt, as well as a later retry.
874            let (status, turn) = match first_turn.take() {
875                Some((status, turn)) => (status, Some(turn)),
876                None => {
877                    if let Some(wait) = turn_wait.as_mut()
878                        && turn_mask.is_none()
879                    {
880                        match install_turn_mask(guest, wait, turn_mask_cell).await {
881                            Ok(mask) => turn_mask = Some(mask),
882                            Err(Error::Errno(errno)) => {
883                                break if written_total > 0 {
884                                    Ok(written_total as i64)
885                                } else {
886                                    Err(errno.into())
887                                };
888                            }
889                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
890                        }
891                    }
892                    refresh_guest_poll_state(guest, call.into(), &mut resources);
893                    let status = resource_request(guest, resources.clone()).await;
894                    let turn = if checks_at_turn {
895                        // A named signal counts if the guest's own mask leaves
896                        // it unblocked; the private mask keeps every such
897                        // signal pending until this read.
898                        match read_turn_signals(
899                            guest,
900                            turn_mask,
901                            committed_signals(&status),
902                            NamedRealTime::ByDisposition,
903                        )
904                        .await
905                        {
906                            Ok(turn) => Some(turn),
907                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
908                        }
909                    } else {
910                        None
911                    };
912                    (status, turn)
913                }
914            };
915            if turn.is_none() && !gated {
916                let disposition = match wait_signal_disposition(
917                    guest,
918                    status.clone(),
919                    &guest_signal_mask,
920                    action_addr,
921                    true,
922                )
923                .await
924                {
925                    Ok(disposition) => disposition,
926                    Err(error) => break Err(error),
927                };
928                if matches!(status, ResumeStatus::Signaled(_))
929                    && let Some(result) =
930                        interrupted_write_result(&call, written_total, disposition)
931                {
932                    break result;
933                }
934            }
935
936            if resources.poll_attempt > 0
937                && !guest
938                    .thread_state()
939                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
940                        detfd.open_file_id() == expected_open_file
941                    })
942                    .unwrap_or(false)
943            {
944                break if written_total > 0 {
945                    Ok(written_total as i64)
946                } else {
947                    self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::writev, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP)
948                        .await
949                };
950            }
951
952            // The first attempt of a call that decides at its turn runs under
953            // the guest's own mask, where a pending signal would stop a
954            // private injection and the backend's single held slot keeps only
955            // the last of two. So it is always the guest's own `writev`, which
956            // the backend runs with every pending signal left queued in the
957            // kernel (the Claude re-check of R2b-1, N2).
958            let own_first_attempt = turn_wait.is_some() && turn_mask.is_none();
959            let result = if atomic_pipe_write && !own_first_attempt {
960                self.execute_atomic_pipe_writev_attempt(guest, call, &iovecs, atomic_scratch_iov)
961                    .await
962            } else {
963                // The guest's own `writev` copies the guest's array again; a
964                // segment `write` names Hermit's copy.
965                let displaced = matches!(current, Syscall::Writev(_))
966                    .then(|| entry_import.as_ref())
967                    .flatten()
968                    .map(|entry| entry.reinstate(&mut guest.memory()));
969                let result = match subtool {
970                    Some(detcore) => {
971                        detcore
972                            .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, current)
973                            .await
974                    }
975                    None => guest.inject_with_retry(current).await.map_err(Error::from),
976                };
977                if let Err(error) =
978                    put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced, result.is_ok())
979                {
980                    break Err(error);
981                }
982                result
983            };
984            match result {
985                Ok(written) if written > 0 => {
986                    let written = match usize::try_from(written) {
987                        Ok(written) => written,
988                        Err(_) => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
989                    };
990                    written_total = match written_total.checked_add(written) {
991                        Some(written_total) => written_total,
992                        None => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
993                    };
994                    if written_total >= target {
995                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
996                    }
997                    if atomic_pipe_write {
998                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
999                    }
1000                    // A short attempt filled the pipe, so the write would wait:
1001                    // a wake ends it with the bytes written, decided after the
1002                    // attempt, as Linux tests for room first (R2b-1 rule 6).
1003                    if turn.is_some_and(|turn| turn.ends(true)) {
1004                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
1005                    }
1006                    if gated {
1007                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
1008                            Ok(true) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1009                            Ok(false) => {}
1010                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1011                        }
1012                    }
1013                    current = match remaining_writev_segment(
1014                        call.fd(),
1015                        &iovecs,
1016                        written_total,
1017                        target - written_total,
1018                    ) {
1019                        Ok(Some(write)) => Syscall::Write(write),
1020                        Ok(None) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1021                        Err(_) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1022                    };
1023                }
1024                Ok(0) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1025                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN))
1026                    if turn.is_some_and(|turn| turn.ends(written_total > 0)) =>
1027                {
1028                    break if written_total > 0 {
1029                        Ok(written_total as i64)
1030                    } else {
1031                        Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
1032                    };
1033                }
1034                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN)) => {
1035                    if gated {
1036                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
1037                            Ok(true) => {
1038                                break if written_total > 0 {
1039                                    Ok(written_total as i64)
1040                                } else {
1041                                    Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
1042                                };
1043                            }
1044                            Ok(false) => {}
1045                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1046                        }
1047                    }
1048                    if !atomic_pipe_write && matches!(current, Syscall::Writev(_)) {
1049                        current = match remaining_writev_segment(call.fd(), &iovecs, 0, target) {
1050                            Ok(Some(write)) => Syscall::Write(write),
1051                            Ok(None) => break Ok(0),
1052                            Err(error) => break Err(error.into()),
1053                        };
1054                    }
1055                }
1056                Err(error) => {
1057                    break finish_partial_record_or_replay_write(written_total as i64, error);
1058                }
1059                Ok(_) => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
1060            }
1061
1062            resources.previous_attempt_made_progress = written_total > written_before;
1063            // Bytes this attempt wrote ready the readers before this thread
1064            // polls for room (`--pipe-wake-latency`).
1065            if resources.previous_attempt_made_progress {
1066                self.note_fd_readied(guest, call.fd(), crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Data)
1067                    .await;
1068            }
1069            resources.poll_attempt += 1;
1070            tracing::trace!(
1071                "Retry #{} for {}blocking pipe writev after EAGAIN: {}",
1072                resources.poll_attempt,
1073                if atomic_pipe_write { "atomic " } else { "" },
1074                call.display(&guest.memory())
1075            );
1076            record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
1077        };
1078        keep_entry_view(guest, entry_import);
1079
1080        match turn_wait {
1081            Some(mut wait) => {
1082                let restored = wait.restore(guest, Some(turn_mask_cell)).await;
1083                if turn_mask.is_some() {
1084                    crate::tool_global::withdraw_wait_mask(guest).await;
1085                }
1086                match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
1087                    Ok(result) => refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, Sysno::writev, result).await,
1088                    Err(error) => Err(error),
1089                }
1090            }
1091            None if gated => result,
1092            None => {
1093                restore_signals_after_disposition(guest, old_mask_addr).await?;
1094                result
1095            }
1096        }
1097    }
1098
1099    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
1100    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#2176): Review scalar blocking-pipe write completion and
1101    // the fail-closed descriptor-replacement boundary.
1102    /// Complete a logically blocking scalar pipe write after Hermit has made the pipe
1103    /// physically nonblocking.
1104    ///
1105    /// Linux may return a positive short write for a request larger than `PIPE_BUF`, then
1106    /// continue blocking for the remainder. Hermit's physical `O_NONBLOCK` is an internal
1107    /// scheduler mechanism, so exposing that first short write changes guest behavior. Retry
1108    /// the unconsumed suffix until the logical write completes, a signal arrives, or a real
1109    /// error occurs. A signal or error after progress returns the partial byte count, matching
1110    /// Linux.
1111    ///
1112    /// A concurrent close/dup2 can replace the numeric fd while this helper is yielded. Linux
1113    /// keeps the original open-file description alive inside a blocking syscall, but Reverie
1114    /// does not yet expose a backend-neutral retained-fd handle. Detect replacement before a
1115    /// retry and fail closed rather than writing the suffix into an unrelated object.
1116    pub async fn execute_blocking_pipe_write<G: Guest<Self>>(
1117        &self,
1118        guest: &mut G,
1119        call: syscalls::Write,
1120        expected_open_file: OpenFileId,
1121    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
1122        let max_rw_count = crate::page::max_rw_count();
1123
1124        let target = call.len().min(max_rw_count);
1125        if target == 0 {
1126            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
1127        }
1128
1129        tracing::trace!(
1130            "NonblockableSyscall: converting to nonblocking syscall (internal polling): write"
1131        );
1132        let mut resources = Resources::new(guest.thread_state().dettid);
1133        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
1134        resources.fyi(call.name());
1135        // Interruptible by a cross-task signal the kernel would deliver, as a
1136        // polled read is (`retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`): the scheduler
1137        // answers the next request `Signaled`, and the write returns the
1138        // bytes it wrote, or ERESTARTSYS before any
1139        // (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187>).
1140        resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(call.signal_interrupt_errno());
1141        resources.signal_state_task = guest_signal_state_task(guest);
1142        // A pipe write: a recorded private `SIGCHLD` ends it as on Linux
1143        // (`Resources::private_sigchld_decides`).
1144        resources.private_sigchld_decides = true;
1145        resources.polls_a_named_fifo = is_named_fifo(guest, call.fd());
1146        resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks = syscall_targets_guest_held_fd(guest, call.into());
1147        resources.polls_guest_state_only = self.cfg.recordreplay_modes
1148            || resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks
1149            || resources.polls_a_named_fifo;
1150        resources.polls_channel = self
1151            .pipe_channel_end(guest, call.fd())
1152            .map(|end| Box::new((end.channel, crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Space)));
1153        // Without a thread whose signal state the scheduler can filter by
1154        // (`guest_signal_state_task`: KVM without sequentialized threads),
1155        // the scheduler keeps every signal and the write checks after the
1156        // wake, as `execute_blocking_pipe_writev` does, whether one would be
1157        // delivered: a blocked or ignored signal must not end a write that
1158        // has made progress, which would return a short count where Linux
1159        // keeps waiting. Wherever a reader answers, the drain has already
1160        // filtered by that state, so a `Signaled` wake is one Linux would
1161        // deliver.
1162        let disposition_scratch = if resources.signal_state_task.is_none() {
1163            resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself = true;
1164            let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
1165            let mask_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
1166            let action_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
1167            let guard = stack.commit()?;
1168            Some((mask_addr, action_addr, guard))
1169        } else {
1170            None
1171        };
1172        let subtool = self.cfg.recordreplay_modes.then_some(self);
1173        let mut current = call;
1174        let mut written_total = 0usize;
1175        // Under the in-guest delivery gate (A5 step 3c.1c, D50 reader 1), as
1176        // for a pipe `writev`: no private mask, and the design's deliverable
1177        // set decides once an attempt would wait for room.
1178        let gated = guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery;
1179        let checks_at_turn =
1180            !gated && decides_interruption_at_turn(guest, resources.signal_state_task);
1181        // The write owns the guest's mask while it blocks every blockable
1182        // signal, as the generic poll does (`retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`):
1183        // an attempt after the first is a private injection of the
1184        // unwritten suffix, which a pending signal could stop and move into
1185        // the backend's single held slot, where a second one replaces it
1186        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, stage 2).
1187        let mut turn_wait = checks_at_turn
1188            .then(|| KernelSignalWait::new(guest, 0, false, call.signal_interrupt_errno()));
1189        let mut published = PublishedWaitMask::default();
1190
1191        let result: Result<i64, Error> = loop {
1192            let written_before = written_total;
1193            // A signal ends the write only if it would still wait for room:
1194            // the attempt below runs first, as Linux's `pipe_write` checks
1195            // for a pending signal only when it must wait. After the signal,
1196            // the bytes written so far are returned, or the restart errno if
1197            // there are none.
1198            let status = if resources.poll_attempt > 0 {
1199                refresh_guest_poll_state(guest, call.into(), &mut resources);
1200                Some(resource_request(guest, resources.clone()).await)
1201            } else {
1202                None
1203            };
1204            // Read before every attempt, the turnless first one included
1205            // (`read_turn_signals`): a copy pending at the write's own entry
1206            // is decided in this slice, before the writer can yield, so a later
1207            // `SIG_IGN` and a new handler cannot take it
1208            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, R2b-1 rule 4).
1209            // Once the write blocks, the turn decides under the guest's own
1210            // mask, which the write owns (Codex review of the R2b-2 design
1211            // rev3, P2-1).
1212            let turn = if checks_at_turn {
1213                let committed = status.as_ref().map_or(0, committed_signals);
1214                // The first attempt is the guest's own write, which the
1215                // backend runs with every pending signal left queued, so only
1216                // a later attempt needs the block.
1217                match turn_signals_with_block(
1218                    guest,
1219                    &mut turn_wait,
1220                    if resources.poll_attempt > 0 {
1221                        ProbeMaskPolicy::PendingSignals
1222                    } else {
1223                        ProbeMaskPolicy::Guest
1224                    },
1225                    committed,
1226                    resources.private_sigchld_decides,
1227                    &mut published,
1228                )
1229                .await
1230                {
1231                    Ok(turn) => Some(turn),
1232                    Err(error) => break Err(error),
1233                }
1234            } else {
1235                None
1236            };
1237            let signaled = if turn.is_some() || gated {
1238                false
1239            } else {
1240                match (&status, &disposition_scratch) {
1241                    (Some(ResumeStatus::Signaled(_)), None) => true,
1242                    (
1243                        Some(status @ ResumeStatus::Signaled(_)),
1244                        Some((mask_addr, action_addr, _)),
1245                    ) => {
1246                        match own_disposition_interrupts(
1247                            guest,
1248                            status.clone(),
1249                            *mask_addr,
1250                            *action_addr,
1251                        )
1252                        .await
1253                        {
1254                            Ok(interrupts) => interrupts,
1255                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1256                        }
1257                    }
1258                    _ => false,
1259                }
1260            };
1261
1262            if resources.poll_attempt > 0
1263                && !guest
1264                    .thread_state()
1265                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
1266                        detfd.open_file_id() == expected_open_file
1267                    })
1268                    .unwrap_or(false)
1269            {
1270                break if written_total > 0 {
1271                    Ok(written_total as i64)
1272                } else {
1273                    self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::write, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP)
1274                        .await
1275                };
1276            }
1277
1278            let result = match subtool {
1279                Some(detcore) => {
1280                    detcore
1281                        .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, current)
1282                        .await
1283                }
1284                None => guest.inject_with_retry(current).await.map_err(Error::from),
1285            };
1286            // As in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`, an attempt that the
1287            // pending signal stopped under record and replay is not made again.
1288            match result {
1289                Ok(written) if written > 0 => {
1290                    let Ok(written) = usize::try_from(written) else {
1291                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1292                    };
1293                    let Some(remaining) = target.checked_sub(written_total) else {
1294                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1295                    };
1296                    if written > remaining {
1297                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1298                    }
1299                    let Some(total) = written_total.checked_add(written) else {
1300                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1301                    };
1302                    written_total = total;
1303                    // A short attempt filled the pipe, so the write would wait:
1304                    // a wake ends it with the bytes written (`TurnSignals::ends`).
1305                    if written_total == target || turn.map_or(signaled, |turn| turn.ends(true)) {
1306                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
1307                    }
1308                    if gated {
1309                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
1310                            Ok(true) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1311                            Ok(false) => {}
1312                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1313                        }
1314                    }
1315                    let Some(buffer) = call.buf() else {
1316                        break Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
1317                    };
1318                    let Some(next_buffer) = buffer
1319                        .as_raw()
1320                        .checked_add(written_total)
1321                        .and_then(Addr::<u8>::from_raw)
1322                    else {
1323                        break finish_partial_record_or_replay_write(
1324                            written_total as i64,
1325                            Errno::EFAULT.into(),
1326                        );
1327                    };
1328                    current = call
1329                        .with_buf(Some(next_buffer))
1330                        .with_len(target - written_total);
1331                }
1332                Ok(0) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1333                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN))
1334                    if turn.map_or(signaled, |turn| turn.ends(written_total > 0)) =>
1335                {
1336                    break if written_total > 0 {
1337                        Ok(written_total as i64)
1338                    } else {
1339                        Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
1340                    };
1341                }
1342                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN)) => {
1343                    if gated {
1344                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
1345                            Ok(true) => {
1346                                break if written_total > 0 {
1347                                    Ok(written_total as i64)
1348                                } else {
1349                                    Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
1350                                };
1351                            }
1352                            Ok(false) => {}
1353                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1354                        }
1355                    }
1356                }
1357                Err(error) => {
1358                    break finish_partial_record_or_replay_write(written_total as i64, error);
1359                }
1360                Ok(_) => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
1361            }
1362
1363            resources.previous_attempt_made_progress = written_total > written_before;
1364            // Bytes this attempt wrote ready the readers before this thread
1365            // polls for room (`--pipe-wake-latency`).
1366            if resources.previous_attempt_made_progress {
1367                self.note_fd_readied(guest, call.fd(), crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Data)
1368                    .await;
1369            }
1370            resources.poll_attempt += 1;
1371            tracing::trace!(
1372                "Retry #{} for blocking pipe write: {}",
1373                resources.poll_attempt,
1374                call.display(&guest.memory())
1375            );
1376            record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
1377        };
1378
1379        // The single exit, as in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`: the
1380        // guest's mask goes back, through `Guest::set_blocked_signals` with no
1381        // scratch memory, before the result is returned.
1382        match turn_wait {
1383            Some(mut wait) if wait.effective_mask().is_some() => {
1384                let restored = wait.restore(guest, None).await;
1385                publish_wait_mask(guest, None, &mut published).await;
1386                match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
1387                    Ok(result) => refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, Sysno::write, result).await,
1388                    Err(error) => Err(error),
1389                }
1390            }
1391            _ => result,
1392        }
1393    }
1394
1395    async fn execute_atomic_pipe_writev_attempt<G: Guest<Self>>(
1396        &self,
1397        guest: &mut G,
1398        call: syscalls::Writev,
1399        iovecs: &[(usize, usize)],
1400        stack_iov: Option<usize>,
1401    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
1402        if let Some(stack_iov) = stack_iov {
1403            let scratch_call = call.with_iov(Addr::from_raw(stack_iov));
1404            return if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
1405                self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, scratch_call)
1406                    .await
1407            } else {
1408                guest
1409                    .inject_with_retry(scratch_call)
1410                    .await
1411                    .map_err(Error::from)
1412            };
1413        }
1414
1415        let mapping_len = iovecs
1416            .len()
1417            .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<libc::iovec>())
1418            .expect("validated iovec count cannot overflow scratch length");
1419        let mapped = guest
1420            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
1421                syscalls::Mmap::new()
1422                    .with_addr(None)
1423                    .with_len(mapping_len)
1424                    .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
1425                    .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
1426                    .with_fd(-1)
1427                    .with_offset(0),
1428            ))
1429            .await
1430            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to map atomic writev scratch: {error}"));
1431        let mapped = usize::try_from(mapped)
1432            .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("atomic writev scratch mmap returned {mapped}"));
1433        let scratch_iov = Addr::<libc::iovec>::from_raw(mapped)
1434            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("atomic writev scratch mmap returned a null address"));
1435        let mapping_addr: Addr<libc::c_void> = scratch_iov.cast();
1436        let write_result = {
1437            let raw_iovecs: Vec<libc::iovec> = iovecs
1438                .iter()
1439                .map(|(base, length)| libc::iovec {
1440                    iov_base: *base as *mut libc::c_void,
1441                    iov_len: *length,
1442                })
1443                .collect();
1444            // SAFETY: the injected anonymous mapping is exclusively owned scratch space.
1445            guest
1446                .memory()
1447                .write_values(unsafe { scratch_iov.into_mut() }, &raw_iovecs)
1448        };
1449        if let Err(write_error) = write_result {
1450            guest
1451                .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
1452                    syscalls::Munmap::new()
1453                        .with_addr(Some(mapping_addr))
1454                        .with_len(mapping_len),
1455                ))
1456                .await
1457                .unwrap_or_else(|cleanup_error| {
1458                    panic!(
1459                        "failed to populate atomic writev scratch ({write_error}); cleanup failed ({cleanup_error})"
1460                    )
1461                });
1462            panic!("failed to populate atomic writev scratch: {write_error}");
1463        }
1464
1465        let scratch_call = call.with_iov(Some(scratch_iov));
1466        let result = if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
1467            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, scratch_call)
1468                .await
1469        } else {
1470            guest
1471                .inject_with_retry(scratch_call)
1472                .await
1473                .map_err(Error::from)
1474        };
1475        guest
1476            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
1477                syscalls::Munmap::new()
1478                    .with_addr(Some(mapping_addr))
1479                    .with_len(mapping_len),
1480            ))
1481            .await
1482            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to unmap atomic writev scratch: {error}"));
1483        result
1484    }
1485
1486    /// Override physically_nonblocking to true for the file descriptor, if appropriate.
1487    pub fn maybe_set_nonblocking_fd<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &G, fd: i32) {
1488        if self.cfg.sequentialize_threads && !self.cfg.debug_externalize_sockets {
1489            guest
1490                .thread_state()
1491                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1492                    detfd.set_physically_nonblocking();
1493                })
1494                .unwrap();
1495        }
1496    }
1497}
1498
1499fn remaining_writev_segment(
1500    fd: i32,
1501    iovecs: &[(usize, usize)],
1502    mut consumed: usize,
1503    remaining_limit: usize,
1504) -> Result<Option<syscalls::Write>, Errno> {
1505    for (base, length) in iovecs {
1506        if consumed >= *length {
1507            consumed -= *length;
1508            continue;
1509        }
1510        let base = base.checked_add(consumed).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
1511        let buffer = Addr::<u8>::from_raw(base).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
1512        return Ok(Some(
1513            syscalls::Write::new()
1514                .with_fd(fd)
1515                .with_buf(Some(buffer))
1516                .with_len((*length - consumed).min(remaining_limit)),
1517        ));
1518    }
1519    Ok(None)
1520}
1521
1522/// A blocking syscall that involves a fail descriptor may be handled in these three ways:
1523#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
1524pub enum IOAction {
1525    /// It may physically block and we can't change that.  Treat it as ExternalBlockingIO.
1526    Blocking,
1527    /// We can nonblockize and retry the call.
1528    NonblockizeRetry,
1529    /// The call is nonblocking already, and safe to execute.
1530    PassThru,
1531}
1532
1533/// Returns the strategy for an FD-based call that may block when executed.
1534///
1535/// Failure means descriptor metadata could not classify the call; the caller must preserve the
1536/// kernel's authority over the syscall result rather than exposing this advisory lookup error.
1537pub fn ioaction_based_on_fd_status<
1538    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
1539    T: RecordOrReplay,
1540    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
1541>(
1542    guest: &mut G,
1543    call: C,
1544) -> Result<IOAction, Errno> {
1545    let wrapped: Syscall = call.into();
1546    let fd = get_fd(wrapped).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("Failed to get fd for {}", call.name()));
1547    let (phys, virt, error_queue_never_waits) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1548        (
1549            detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
1550            detfd.is_nonblocking(),
1551            detfd.error_queue_never_waits(),
1552        )
1553    })?;
1554    tracing::trace!(
1555        "Checking FD {} for nonblocking: physical {} / virtual {}",
1556        fd,
1557        phys,
1558        virt
1559    );
1560    let action = ioaction_for_fd_status(fd, virt, phys, call.flags_forbid_waiting());
1561    // A receive with MSG_ERRQUEUE on a socket whose protocol reads that
1562    // queue without waiting also runs once, as Linux does.
1563    if action == IOAction::NonblockizeRetry && error_queue_never_waits && call.reads_error_queue() {
1564        Ok(IOAction::PassThru)
1565    } else {
1566        Ok(action)
1567    }
1568}
1569
1570/// [`ioaction_based_on_fd_status`] for the descriptor `fd` alone, before any
1571/// flag of the call itself, for a caller whose call does not implement
1572/// [`NonblockableSyscall`].
1573pub(crate) fn ioaction_based_on_fd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1574    guest: &mut G,
1575    fd: i32,
1576) -> Result<IOAction, Errno> {
1577    let (phys, virt) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1578        (detfd.physically_nonblocking(), detfd.is_nonblocking())
1579    })?;
1580    Ok(ioaction_for_fd_status(fd, virt, phys, false))
1581}
1582
1583/// The decision of [`ioaction_based_on_fd_status`] from the descriptor's
1584/// virtual and physical nonblocking state and the call's own no-wait flags,
1585/// split out so the decision itself is unit-testable without a guest.
1586fn ioaction_for_fd_status(fd: i32, virt: bool, phys: bool, flags_forbid_waiting: bool) -> IOAction {
1587    if virt && !phys {
1588        // TF: simulate nonblocking on top of physically blocking? How?
1589        panic!(
1590            "Invariant violation, fd {fd}: we cannot simulate nonblocking behavior when set to blocking mode in the kernel."
1591        );
1592    } else if !virt && !phys {
1593        // FF: logically blocking, physically blocking, this could only work with BlockingExternalIO.
1594        IOAction::Blocking
1595    } else if virt && phys {
1596        // TT: both nonblocking, so firing once is sufficient
1597        IOAction::PassThru
1598    } else if flags_forbid_waiting {
1599        // FT, but the call itself does not wait (MSG_DONTWAIT), so firing once
1600        // is what Linux does.
1601        IOAction::PassThru
1602    } else {
1603        // FT: Need to simulate blocking on top of nonblocking.
1604        IOAction::NonblockizeRetry
1605    }
1606}
1607
1608/// Does this single-fd syscall operate on a container-INTERNAL file descriptor?
1609///
1610/// This is an execution-routing classification, not proof that only guests can
1611/// change readiness. It recognizes pipes and `socketpair(2)` endpoints. Internal
1612/// fds are made physically
1613/// nonblocking (see `handle_pipe2` and `handle_socketpair`) so a potentially-blocking
1614/// op on them can use the deterministic `InternalIOPolling` nonblockize-and-retry
1615/// strategy instead of `BlockingExternalIO`. Treating an internal fd as external
1616/// blocking IO deadlocks the sequentialized scheduler in record/replay, because a
1617/// reader and its paired writer are not independent.
1618///
1619/// Socketpair origin is known at creation time, and remains useful for routing
1620/// even after an endpoint is exported or a datagram endpoint changes its peer.
1621/// Under record and replay a connected socket whose peer is a guest, which
1622/// `Detcore::classify_socket_peer` finds from the peer's credentials after
1623/// `connect`, `accept` or an `SCM_RIGHTS` receive, is internal too. Every other
1624/// socket, including every loopback IP socket, conservatively remains external.
1625///
1626/// Readiness needs a separate decision: a socketpair endpoint can leave the guest
1627/// through `SCM_RIGHTS`, and a bound, disconnected datagram endpoint can receive
1628/// from an outside sender. See `single_fd_poll_readiness`.
1629///
1630/// A descriptor a guest RECEIVES over `SCM_RIGHTS` is recorded
1631/// (`Detcore::record_received_descriptors`) or discovered. One that names an open
1632/// file the table models joins it as an alias and keeps that file's marks. Any
1633/// other is recorded from the kernel's facts: a received pipe is a pipe here, and
1634/// under record and replay a received socket is internal when its peer is a guest
