1635/// (`Detcore::classify_socket_peer`). A received socketpair end from another process
1636/// outside record and replay is not recognized as internal: its open file
1637/// description is still physically nonblocking, and the kernel's `O_NONBLOCK` is all
1638/// the receiver's record knows, so a blocking read through it can return EAGAIN
1639/// where Linux would wait.
1640///
1641/// Syscalls whose fd is not directly extractable (e.g. poll/ppoll, which carry a
1642/// pointer to an fd array) return false and keep their existing handling.
1643pub fn syscall_targets_internal_fd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1644    guest: &mut G,
1645    call: Syscall,
1646) -> bool {
1647    // An epoll wait's descriptor is the epoll set it waits on, never a pipe it
1648    // reads; a guest that passes a pipe gets EINVAL from the kernel.
1649    match call {
1650        Syscall::EpollPwait(_) => return false,
1651        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
1652        Syscall::EpollWait(_) => return false,
1653        _ => {}
1654    }
1655    match get_fd(call) {
1656        Some(fd) => guest
1657            .thread_state()
1658            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1659                // This is read-end provenance, not a blanket external-fd
1660                // classification: writes and socketpairs retain the guard.
1661                if matches!(call, Syscall::Read(_) | Syscall::Readv(_))
1662                    && detfd.inherited_external_read().is_some()
1663                {
1664                    return false;
1665                }
1666                matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Pipe) || detfd.is_internal_socket()
1667            })
1668            .unwrap_or(false),
1669        None => false,
1670    }
1671}
1672
1673/// Whether `call`'s one descriptor is guest-held (`DetFd::is_guest_held`):
1674/// only guests hold its other end, so only a guest can make the call ready.
1675/// It feeds only `Resources::polls_guest_state_only`, never the record/replay
1676/// routing `syscall_targets_internal_fd` decides. An epoll wait's descriptor
1677/// is its set, which this does not track.
1678fn syscall_targets_guest_held_fd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1679    guest: &mut G,
1680    call: Syscall,
1681) -> bool {
1682    // x86_64 has both epoll_wait and epoll_pwait; aarch64 has
1683    // epoll_pwait (and epoll_pwait2) alone.
1684    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
1685    if matches!(call, Syscall::EpollWait(_) | Syscall::EpollPwait(_)) {
1686        return false;
1687    }
1688    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
1689    if matches!(call, Syscall::EpollPwait(_)) {
1690        return false;
1691    }
1692    get_fd(call).is_some_and(|fd| {
1693        guest
1694            .thread_state()
1695            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_guest_held())
1696            .unwrap_or(false)
1697    })
1698}
1699
1700/// The generic single-fd poll's guest-only claim and whether it rests on
1701/// revocable guest-held marks. Socketpair origin selects live internal routing,
1702/// but only its current guest-held mark can establish guest-only readiness.
1703/// Mark-dependent requests remain subject to the scheduler's export revocation,
1704/// including requests that were already published when the export was reported.
1705/// Other internal descriptors retain their existing readiness classification.
1706/// In particular, this does not repair guest-only claims for pipes exported
1707/// through SCM_RIGHTS or received from outside the guest.
1708fn single_fd_poll_readiness<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1709    guest: &mut G,
1710    call: Syscall,
1711    internal_fd: bool,
1712) -> (bool, bool) {
1713    let socketpair = get_fd(call).is_some_and(|fd| {
1714        guest
1715            .thread_state()
1716            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_socketpair_endpoint())
1717            .unwrap_or(false)
1718    });
1719    let relies_on_guest_held_marks =
1720        (!internal_fd || socketpair) && syscall_targets_guest_held_fd(guest, call);
1721    let polls_guest_state_only = (internal_fd && !socketpair) || relies_on_guest_held_marks;
1722    (polls_guest_state_only, relies_on_guest_held_marks)
1723}
1724
1725/// The most entries a `poll` or `ppoll` may have for
1726/// `poll_targets_guest_held` to read them.
1727const GUEST_HELD_POLL_MAX_FDS: usize = 1024;
1728
1729/// Whether only guests can make a `poll` or `ppoll` of the `nfds` entries at
1730/// `fds` ready: every entry Linux polls (a non-negative descriptor) names a
1731/// guest-held descriptor (`DetFd::is_guest_held`) in the caller's table.
1732/// Linux ignores an entry with a negative descriptor. An empty array, one
1733/// larger than `GUEST_HELD_POLL_MAX_FDS` or one Detcore cannot read counts as
1734/// not guest-held, which keeps the call's classification as it was. It feeds
1735/// only `Resources::polls_guest_state_only`. Record/replay retains its prior
1736/// classification and does not use these new guest-held marks.
1737pub(crate) fn poll_targets_guest_held<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1738    guest: &mut G,
1739    fds: Option<usize>,
1740    nfds: usize,
1741) -> bool {
1742    if guest.config().recordreplay_modes || nfds == 0 || nfds > GUEST_HELD_POLL_MAX_FDS {
1743        return false;
1744    }
1745    let Some(address) = fds.and_then(Addr::<u8>::from_raw) else {
1746        return false;
1747    };
1748    let mut bytes = vec![0u8; nfds * std::mem::size_of::<libc::pollfd>()];
1749    if guest.memory().read_exact(address, &mut bytes).is_err() {
1750        return false;
1751    }
1752    let polled = pollfd_descriptors(&bytes);
1753    !polled.is_empty()
1754        && polled.into_iter().all(|fd| {
1755            guest
1756                .thread_state()
1757                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_guest_held())
1758                .unwrap_or(false)
1759        })
1760}
1761
1762/// Refresh only descriptor-based idle-poll authority, independently of the
1763/// syscall's record/replay routing. In plain runs, pipes and socketpairs also
1764/// rely on the guest-held mark: SCM export revokes that authority for queued
1765/// requests. Record/replay retains the internal-FD classification captured by
1766/// its handler at entry, including across descriptor replacement during a
1767/// retry, for its existing FIFO-open decisions. It does not enable the new
1768/// idle-poller jumps.
1769/// Non-FD primitives retain the proof supplied by their own handlers.
1770pub(crate) fn refresh_guest_poll_state<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1771    guest: &mut G,
1772    call: Syscall,
1773    resources: &mut Resources,
1774) {
1775    if guest.config().recordreplay_modes {
1776        resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks = false;
1777        return;
1778    }
1779    // A flock waiting in Detcore's flock model waits on guest state alone,
1780    // which no descriptor's mark decides (`flock_model`): the caller's
1781    // classification stands.
1782    if matches!(call, Syscall::Flock(_)) {
1783        return;
1784    }
1785    let held = match call {
1786        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
1787        Syscall::Poll(call) => poll_targets_guest_held(
1788            guest,
1789            call.fds().map(|fds| fds.as_raw()),
1790            call.nfds() as usize,
1791        ),
1792        Syscall::Ppoll(call) => poll_targets_guest_held(
1793            guest,
1794            call.fds().map(|fds| fds.as_raw()),
1795            call.nfds() as usize,
1796        ),
1797        _ if get_fd(call).is_some() => syscall_targets_guest_held_fd(guest, call),
1798        _ => return,
1799    };
1800    resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks = held;
1801    resources.polls_guest_state_only = held;
1802}
1803
1804/// The descriptors Linux polls in a `pollfd` array's bytes: each entry's
1805/// `fd` when it is not negative.
1806fn pollfd_descriptors(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<i32> {
1807    let (entries, _) = bytes.as_chunks::<{ std::mem::size_of::<libc::pollfd>() }>();
1808    entries
1809        .iter()
1810        .map(|entry| i32::from_ne_bytes([entry[0], entry[1], entry[2], entry[3]]))
1811        .filter(|fd| *fd >= 0)
1812        .collect()
1813}
1814
1815/// The descriptors an in-flight call's guest-held proof actually describes.
1816/// A scheduled sibling can replace a descriptor or a pollfd operand while a
1817/// request waits. `Scheduler::latest_progress` and `note_committed_turn` make
1818/// the poller retry after such a turn before it can prove terminal deadlock;
1819/// each granted retry must therefore validate this capture before probing.
1820/// Once lost, the proof stays lost for this call, even if the old slot returns.
1821///
1822/// This does not retain the original Linux open file description across
1823/// private probes. Linux's `do_readv` retains its `fd_pos` reference through
1824/// `vfs_readv` (fs/read_write.c, v7.1.3), whereas each injected call looks up
1825/// the slot again. Likewise `do_sys_poll` copies its pollfd array per syscall
1826/// (fs/select.c). This guard only prevents a stale terminal-deadlock proof.
1827pub(crate) struct GuestHeldPollProof {
1828    call: Syscall,
1829    targets: Option<GuestHeldPollTargets>,
1830    /// Whether the call claimed a proof at capture: a claimed proof, once
1831    /// lost, stays lost for this call.
1832    claimed: bool,
1833}
1834
1835#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]
1836enum GuestHeldPollTargets {
1837    Single(i32, OpenFileId),
1838    Poll {
1839        address: usize,
1840        entries: Vec<(i32, Option<OpenFileId>)>,
1841    },
1842}
1843
1844impl GuestHeldPollProof {
1845    pub(crate) fn capture<T, G>(guest: &mut G, call: Syscall, resources: &mut Resources) -> Self
1846    where
1847        T: RecordOrReplay,
1848        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
1849    {
1850        let targets = resources
1851            .relies_on_guest_held_marks
1852            .then(|| Self::read_targets(guest, call))
1853            .flatten();
1854        // No proof needed (for example a named FIFO) differs from a failed
1855        // capture of a proof the caller claimed. Unknown must clear the latter
1856        // before its very first request is published.
1857        if resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks && targets.is_none() {
1858            Self::clear(resources);
1859        }
1860        Self {
1861            claimed: resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks,
1862            call,
1863            targets,
1864        }
1865    }
1866
1867    pub(crate) fn revalidate<T, G>(&mut self, guest: &mut G, resources: &mut Resources)
1868    where
1869        T: RecordOrReplay,
1870        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
1871    {
1872        if self.targets.is_some() && Self::read_targets(guest, self.call) != self.targets {
1873            self.targets = None;
1874            Self::clear(resources);
1875        } else if self.targets.is_none() && (self.claimed || resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks) {
1876            // A proof once lost (or never captured for a call that claimed
1877            // one) cannot be reacquired by a later refresh of the same
1878            // call's classification: restored operands do not restore it.
1879            // Nor can a refresh manufacture mark-dependent authority for
1880            // a call that never captured an identity. Non-mark authority,
1881            // such as binary record/replay's internal-FD routing, is separate.
1882            Self::clear(resources);
1883        }
1884    }
1885
1886    fn clear(resources: &mut Resources) {
1887        resources.polls_guest_state_only = false;
1888        resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks = false;
1889    }
1890
1891    fn identity<T, G>(guest: &mut G, fd: i32) -> Option<OpenFileId>
1892    where
1893        T: RecordOrReplay,
1894        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
1895    {
1896        guest
1897            .thread_state()
1898            .with_detfd(fd, |entry| {
1899                entry.is_guest_held().then(|| entry.open_file_id())
1900            })
1901            .ok()
1902            .flatten()
1903    }
1904
1905    fn read_targets<T, G>(guest: &mut G, call: Syscall) -> Option<GuestHeldPollTargets>
1906    where
1907        T: RecordOrReplay,
1908        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
1909    {
1910        let (address, nfds) = match call {
1911            // x86_64 only: aarch64 has ppoll alone.
1912            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
1913            Syscall::Poll(call) => (call.fds()?.as_raw(), call.nfds() as usize),
1914            Syscall::Ppoll(call) => (call.fds()?.as_raw(), call.nfds() as usize),
1915            _ => {
1916                let fd = get_fd(call)?;
1917                return Some(GuestHeldPollTargets::Single(fd, Self::identity(guest, fd)?));
1918            }
1919        };
1920        if nfds == 0 || nfds > GUEST_HELD_POLL_MAX_FDS {
1921            return None;
1922        }
1923        let mut bytes = vec![0; nfds * std::mem::size_of::<libc::pollfd>()];
1924        guest
1925            .memory()
1926            .read_exact(Addr::from_raw(address)?, &mut bytes)
1927            .ok()?;
1928        let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(nfds);
1929        for entry in bytes
1930            .as_chunks::<{ std::mem::size_of::<libc::pollfd>() }>()
1931            .0
1932        {
1933            let fd = i32::from_ne_bytes([entry[0], entry[1], entry[2], entry[3]]);
1934            entries.push((
1935                fd,
1936                if fd < 0 {
1937                    None
1938                } else {
1939                    Some(Self::identity(guest, fd)?)
1940                },
1941            ));
1942        }
1943        // Keep negative operands too: changing one into a live descriptor
1944        // changes the target set. Ignore revents, which the kernel writes,
1945        // and events: interest bits do not change who can ready these OFDs.
1946        entries
1947            .iter()
1948            .any(|(fd, _)| *fd >= 0)
1949            .then_some(GuestHeldPollTargets::Poll { address, entries })
1950    }
1951}
1952
1953/// Whether descriptor `fd` is a named FIFO that joined internal polling
1954/// (`Resources::polls_a_named_fifo`).
1955fn is_named_fifo<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(guest: &mut G, fd: i32) -> bool {
1956    guest
1957        .thread_state()
1958        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_named_fifo())
1959        .unwrap_or(false)
1960}
1961
1962/// Whether `call` is a `read` or `readv` of a descriptor Detcore records as
1963/// a pipe (`FdType::Pipe`: a pipe, or a FIFO that joined internal polling),
1964/// the restartable reads a recorded private `SIGCHLD` ends
1965/// (`Resources::private_sigchld_decides`; R2b-2 stage 3,
1966/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273). A socket read keeps
1967/// holding it (rev4 1e).
1968fn reads_a_pipe<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(guest: &mut G, call: Syscall) -> bool {
1969    matches!(call, Syscall::Read(_) | Syscall::Readv(_))
1970        && get_fd(call).is_some_and(|fd| {
1971            guest
1972                .thread_state()
1973                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Pipe))
1974                .unwrap_or(false)
1975        })
1976}
1977
1978/// Does `call` read a descriptor Detcore records as a signalfd
1979/// (`Resources::reads_signalfd`)? Only `read`, `readv` and `preadv2` at the
1980/// current offset can: a positioned read of a signalfd fails with ESPIPE.
1981fn call_reads_signalfd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1982    guest: &mut G,
1983    call: Syscall,
1984) -> bool {
1985    let fd = match call {
1986        Syscall::Read(c) => c.fd(),
1987        Syscall::Readv(c) => c.fd(),
1988        Syscall::Preadv2(c) => c.fd(),
1989        _ => return false,
1990    };
1991    guest
1992        .thread_state()
1993        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.ty() == crate::fd::FdType::Signalfd)
1994        .unwrap_or(false)
1995}
1996
1997/// The descriptor a `read`, `readv` or `preadv2` reads (`Resources::read_fd`).
1998fn read_family_fd(call: Syscall) -> Option<i32> {
1999    match call {
2000        Syscall::Read(c) => Some(c.fd()),
2001        Syscall::Readv(c) => Some(c.fd()),
2002        Syscall::Preadv2(c) => Some(c.fd()),
2003        _ => None,
2004    }
2005}
2006
2007/// Does replay answer this call from the recording rather than by running it?
2008///
2009/// This follows the replayer's dispatch. It serves `accept`, `accept4`, `connect`,
2010/// `sendto`, `sendmsg`, `recvfrom` and `recvmsg` from its log whatever the descriptor
2011/// is, so they count on any descriptor, a listener received over `SCM_RIGHTS` (an
2012/// exported alias, or a new description another process sent) included; an
2013/// untagged accept there would let its stand-in take a slot at a host-timed point.
2014/// `read`, `readv`, `write` and `writev` count only on a
2015/// socket Detcore created with `socket(2)` or `accept(2)`: on other descriptors,
2016/// replay may run them for real as eventfd operations, which can block, so an unknown
2017/// descriptor is not assumed to be served from the log. `recvmmsg` and `sendmmsg` are
2018/// recorded by neither recorder nor replayer (on an accepted connection record/replay
2019/// refuses them, see `refuse_log_served_mmsg`).
2020fn replay_serves_socket_call_from_log<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
2021    guest: &mut G,
2022    call: Syscall,
2023) -> bool {
2024    let fd = match call {
2025        Syscall::Accept(_)
2026        | Syscall::Accept4(_)
2027        | Syscall::Connect(_)
2028        | Syscall::Sendto(_)
2029        | Syscall::Sendmsg(_)
2030        | Syscall::Recvfrom(_)
2031        | Syscall::Recvmsg(_) => return true,
2032        Syscall::Read(s) => s.fd(),
2033        Syscall::Readv(s) => s.fd(),
2034        Syscall::Write(s) => s.fd(),
2035        Syscall::Writev(s) => s.fd(),
2036        _ => return false,
2037    };
2038    is_log_served_socket(guest, fd)
2039}
2040
2041/// Does replay answer this otherwise blocking call from the recording alone?
2042///
2043/// The replayer serves `poll`, `ppoll`, `select` and `pselect6` from the log
2044/// without running them. `epoll_wait` is excluded because replay reapplies its
2045/// side effects on live descriptors, which may block.
2046fn replay_serves_blocking_call_from_log(call: Syscall) -> bool {
2047    match call {
2048        Syscall::Ppoll(_) | Syscall::Pselect6(_) => true,
2049        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2050        Syscall::Poll(_) | Syscall::Select(_) => true,
2051        _ => false,
2052    }
2053}
2054
2055/// Is `fd` a socket whose connection record and replay keep only in the log?
2056///
2057/// That is a socket Detcore created with `socket(2)` or `accept(2)`, but not a
2058/// socketpair endpoint: replay recreates a socketpair, and its operations run
2059/// live.
2060fn is_log_served_socket<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(guest: &mut G, fd: i32) -> bool {
2061    guest
2062        .thread_state()
2063        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2064            matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Socket) && !detfd.is_socketpair_endpoint()
2065        })
2066        .unwrap_or(false)
2067}
2068
2069/// Is `fd` a connection that `accept(2)` or `accept4(2)` returned? Record and
2070/// replay keep such a connection only in the log, and replay stands in an
2071/// eventfd for it, so an operation that runs live during replay meets that
2072/// eventfd rather than a connected socket.
2073pub(crate) fn is_accepted_connection<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
2074    guest: &mut G,
2075    fd: i32,
2076) -> bool {
2077    guest
2078        .thread_state()
2079        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_accepted_connection())
2080        .unwrap_or(false)
2081}
2082
2083/// A large subset of system calls have a single, unique file descriptor argument.  This
2084/// is a convenience function for grabbing that argument.
2085///
2086/// It does not cover system calls with multiple fd arguments, with pointers to heap
2087/// structures that contain fds.
2088pub(crate) fn get_fd(s: Syscall) -> Option<i32> {
2089    match s {
2090        Syscall::Recvfrom(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2091        Syscall::Recvmsg(s) => Some(s.sockfd()),
2092        Syscall::Recvmmsg(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2093        Syscall::Sendto(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2094        Syscall::Sendmsg(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2095        Syscall::Sendmmsg(s) => Some(s.sockfd()),
2096        Syscall::Accept(s) => Some(s.sockfd()),
2097        Syscall::Accept4(s) => Some(s.sockfd()),
2098        Syscall::Connect(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2099        Syscall::Bind(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2100        Syscall::Listen(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2101        Syscall::Getsockname(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2102        Syscall::Getpeername(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2103        Syscall::Setsockopt(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2104        Syscall::Getsockopt(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2105
2106        Syscall::Read(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2107        Syscall::Write(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2108        Syscall::Close(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2109        Syscall::Fstat(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2110        Syscall::Lseek(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2111        Syscall::Mmap(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2112        Syscall::Ioctl(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2113        Syscall::Pread64(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2114        Syscall::Pwrite64(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2115        Syscall::Readv(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2116        Syscall::Writev(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2117
2118        Syscall::Shutdown(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2119        Syscall::Fcntl(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2120        Syscall::Flock(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2121        Syscall::Fsync(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2122        Syscall::Fdatasync(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2123        Syscall::Ftruncate(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2124        Syscall::Fchdir(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2125        Syscall::Fchmod(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2126        Syscall::Fchown(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2127        Syscall::Fstatfs(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2128        Syscall::Readahead(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2129        Syscall::Fsetxattr(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2130        Syscall::Fgetxattr(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2131        Syscall::Flistxattr(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2132        Syscall::Fremovexattr(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2133        Syscall::Fadvise64(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2134        Syscall::InotifyAddWatch(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2135        Syscall::InotifyRmWatch(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2136        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2137        Syscall::SyncFileRange(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2138        Syscall::Vmsplice(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2139        Syscall::Utimensat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2140        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2141        Syscall::Signalfd(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2142        Syscall::Fallocate(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2143        Syscall::TimerfdSettime(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2144        Syscall::TimerfdGettime(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2145        Syscall::Signalfd4(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2146        Syscall::Preadv(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2147        Syscall::Pwritev(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2148        Syscall::Syncfs(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2149        Syscall::Setns(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2150        Syscall::FinitModule(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2151        Syscall::Preadv2(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2152        Syscall::Pwritev2(s) => Some(s.fd()),
2153
2154        Syscall::Openat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2155        Syscall::Mkdirat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2156        Syscall::Mknodat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2157        Syscall::Fchownat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2158        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2159        Syscall::Futimesat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2160        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2161        Syscall::Newfstatat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2162        #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
2163        Syscall::Fstatat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2164        Syscall::Unlinkat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2165        Syscall::Readlinkat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2166        Syscall::Fchmodat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2167        Syscall::Faccessat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2168        Syscall::NameToHandleAt(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2169        Syscall::Execveat(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2170        Syscall::Statx(s) => Some(s.dirfd()),
2171        Syscall::Symlinkat(s) => Some(s.newdirfd()),
2172        Syscall::PerfEventOpen(s) => Some(s.group_fd()),
2173        Syscall::OpenByHandleAt(s) => Some(s.mount_fd()),
2174
2175        Syscall::EpollCtl(s) => Some(s.epfd()),
2176        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]

2178        Syscall::EpollPwait(s) => Some(s.epfd()),
2179
2180        // Ambiguous, 2 fds, no answer:
2181        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]

2183        // Ambiguous, 2 fds, no answer:
2184        Syscall::Sendfile(_) => None,
2185        // Ambiguous, 2 fds, no answer:
2186        Syscall::Renameat(_) => None,

2188        Syscall::Linkat(_) => None,
2189        // Ambiguous, 2 fds, no answer:

2191        // Ambiguous, 2 fds, no answer:

2193        // Ambiguous, 2 fds, no answer:
2194        Syscall::Dup3(_) => None,
2195        // Ambiguous, 2 fds, no answer:
2196        Syscall::KexecLoad(_) => None,
2197
2198        // Takes a pointer to fd, not directly accessible:
2199        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2200        Syscall::Poll(_) => None,
2201        // Takes a pointer to fd, not directly accessible:
2202        Syscall::Ppoll(_) => None,

2208/// A system call which may or may not block, but which can be MADE nonblocking.
2209// `async_trait` rewrites `into_nonblocking` to return a boxed future and marks it
2210// `#[must_use]`; the future is already `#[must_use]` in its own right, so clippy sees a double
2211// annotation. Both are generated, so the lint's own suggestion -- give the `must_use` an explicit
2212// reason -- cannot be applied at this source. Allowed at the item rather than crate-wide so any
2213// hand-written double `must_use` elsewhere still fails `#![deny(clippy::all)]` (detcore/src/lib.rs:35).
2214// Appeared with nightly-2026-08-08 (rustc 1.99.0-nightly 1a98b1e13) against an unchanged tree.
2215#[allow(clippy::double_must_use)]
2216#[async_trait]
2217pub trait NonblockableSyscall: SyscallInfo {
2218    /// Convert the system call to a nonblocking version of itself.  Sometimes this means
2219    /// setting a zero timeout, and sometimes it means something else.
2220    ///
2221    /// This may need to stack allocate, so it returns a StackGuard.
2222    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2223        self,
2224        guest: &mut G,
2225    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>);
2226
2227    /// Check if the result (in nonblocking mode) is analogous to blocking in blocking mode.
2228    /// I.e. the result means "try again".
2229    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
2230        res == Ok(0)
2231    }
2232
2233    /// Whether the call's own flags keep it from waiting on a file the guest
2234    /// left blocking: `MSG_DONTWAIT` on a socket send or receive, which Linux
2235    /// turns into a zero timeout (`sock_rcvtimeo`, `sock_sndtimeo`), so the
2236    /// call returns at once, failing with `EAGAIN` where it would wait. Linux
2237    /// adds the same flag to every call on an `O_NONBLOCK` socket, so such a
2238    /// call runs once, as on a nonblocking file (`IOAction::PassThru`), instead
2239    /// of being retried until it stops failing with `EAGAIN`.
2240    fn flags_forbid_waiting(&self) -> bool {
2241        false
2242    }
2243
2244    /// Whether the call is a receive with `MSG_ERRQUEUE`, which reads the
2245    /// socket's error queue. Whether that waits depends on the socket's
2246    /// protocol (`crate::fd::error_queue_read_never_waits`): a UDP or TCP socket
2247    /// fails with `EAGAIN` at once when the queue is empty, while AF_UNIX
2248    /// ignores the flag and receives as usual.
2249    fn reads_error_queue(&self) -> bool {
2250        false
2251    }
2252
2253    /// Return the errno used when a signal interrupts this internally polled syscall.
2254    /// Most blocking I/O is restartable when its handler uses `SA_RESTART`.
2255    fn signal_interrupt_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2256        Errno::ERESTARTSYS
2257    }
2258
2259    /// Return the errno for an interrupting signal that ends this wait after it began,
2260    /// on a backend that decides interruption from the kernel's signal state
2261    /// (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`). The kernel applies the
2262    /// guest's disposition to it on resume, so it must be the restart code Linux uses
2263    /// for this call: a handler then turns it into `EINTR` or a restart, and a signal
2264    /// with no handler restarts the call.
2265    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2266        self.signal_interrupt_errno()
2267    }
2268
2269    /// Whether Linux restarts this call, after [`kernel_restart_errno`](Self::kernel_restart_errno)
2270    /// with no handler, through a restart block that keeps its absolute deadline: a
2271    /// `poll` with a positive timeout (`do_restart_poll`) and a timed `FUTEX_WAIT` or
2272    /// `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` (`futex_wait_restart`). Its restart code is then
2273    /// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, and
2274    /// Detcore keeps the deadline in a [`RestartBlock`] for the `restart_syscall` that
2275    /// the kernel runs next (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358>).
2276    ///
2277    /// Such a wait is also not ended by a default job-control stop signal
2278    /// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`), so that a stop Linux discards in an
2279    /// orphaned process group does not end the call before its deadline.
2280    fn restart_keeps_deadline(&self) -> bool {
2281        false
2282    }
2283
2284    /// Signals the wait itself accepts rather than being interrupted by, read from
2285    /// guest memory. Only `rt_sigtimedwait` has any.
2286    fn signals_consumed_by_wait<M: MemoryAccess>(&self, _memory: &M) -> KernelSigset {
2287        0
2288    }
2289
2290    /// Whether this call is a receive that Linux ends without waiting once
2291    /// its socket's read side is shut down (`finish_after_read_shutdown`).
2292    fn ends_at_read_shutdown(&self) -> bool {
2293        false
2294    }
2295
2296    /// Convert a physical nonblocking completion into the result expected by the guest.
2297    /// `retried` is true after a prior result was classified as blocked.
2298    fn normalize_nonblocking_result(
2299        &self,
2300        res: Result<i64, Errno>,
2301        _retried: bool,
2302    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
2303        res
2304    }
2305}
2306
2307/// A system call which can logically timeout and then would return a given value
2308/// indicating that timeout.
2309pub trait TimeoutableSyscall: SyscallInfo {
2310    /// What would the syscall return IF it timed out?
2311    fn timeout_return_val(&self) -> Result<i64, Errno>;
2312}
2313
2314fn interrupted_write_result<C: NonblockableSyscall>(
2315    call: &C,
2316    written_total: usize,
2317    disposition: Option<WaitSignalDisposition>,
2318) -> Option<Result<i64, Error>> {
2319    match disposition {
2320        None => None,
2321        Some(_) if written_total > 0 => Some(Ok(written_total as i64)),
2322        Some(_) => Some(Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())),
2323    }
2324}

2326fn pipe_writev_resources(
2327    dettid: DetTid,
2328    call: reverie::syscalls::Writev,
2329    guest_held: bool,
2330) -> Resources {
2331    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
2332    resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
2333    resources.fyi(call.name());
2334    resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(call.signal_interrupt_errno());
2335    // Polls with every ordinary signal blocked and checks the target's
2336    // disposition itself after a `Signaled` wake, so the scheduler's drain
2337    // must not filter by the kernel mask (`execute_blocking_pipe_writev`).
2338    resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself = true;
2339    resources.polls_guest_state_only = guest_held;
2340    resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks = guest_held;
2341    resources
2342}

2344#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2345#[async_trait]
2346impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Poll {
2347    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2348        self,
2349        _guest: &mut G,
2350    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2351        (self.with_timeout(0), None)
2352    }
2353
2354    fn signal_interrupt_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2355        Errno::EINTR
2356    }
2357
2358    /// Linux ends an interrupted `poll` with a restart code that a handler turns into
2359    /// `EINTR` and that restarts the call when no handler runs.
2360    ///
2361    /// With a positive timeout that code is Linux's own, `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`: the
2362    /// kernel then runs `restart_syscall`, which Detcore resumes with the deadline it
2363    /// kept ([`RestartBlock`]), as `do_restart_poll` does
2364    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358). An infinite timeout has no
2365    /// deadline to keep, so it returns `ERESTARTNOHAND`, and running `poll` again with
2366    /// its original arguments is the same restart.
2367    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2368        if self.restart_keeps_deadline() {
2369            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
2370        } else {
2371            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
2372        }
2373    }
2374
2375    /// A zero timeout never blocks, and a negative one never expires.
2376    fn restart_keeps_deadline(&self) -> bool {
2377        self.timeout() > 0
2378    }
2379}

2388#[async_trait]
2389impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Ppoll {
2390    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2391        self,
2392        guest: &mut G,
2393    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2394        let (tp, guard) = zero_timespec(guest).await;
2395        // SAFETY: `tp` points to exclusively owned scratch storage kept alive by `guard`.
2396        let tp = unsafe { tp.into_mut() };
2397        (self.with_timeout(Some(tp)), Some(guard))
2398    }

2401        Errno::EINTR
2402    }

2405    /// `EINTR` and that restarts the call when no handler runs.
2406    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2407        Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
2408    }

2439// `epoll_pwait` was the one member of the
2440// poll/epoll family with no nonblocking form, even though `Ppoll` -- the
2441// sigmask variant of `poll` -- has had one all along. Programs that issue
2442// `epoll_pwait` DIRECTLY (libuv does, which is how the `cmake` hang surfaced)
2443// therefore reached an unhandled path while the `EpollWait` impl above went
2444// unused by them. Note this is NOT glibc's `epoll_wait(2)` on x86_64: glibc
2445// only spells it `epoll_pwait` where `__NR_epoll_wait` is absent, which x86_64
2446// is not. With a NULL sigmask the two calls are semantically identical, so the
2447// nonblocking form is the same: timeout 0, EINTR, and a 0 (no events) timeout
2448// return.

2455        (self.with_timeout(0), None)
2456    }

2459        Errno::EINTR
2460    }
2461}

2469/// What to do with the copy of the standard `signal` this thread just took
2470/// (`rt_sigtimedwait`, a signalfd record), after which its queues held
2471/// `after` (when read): drop it, as a copy Linux discarded when it was sent
2472/// or a stale POSIX timer entry, or return it with another siginfo
2473/// (`DiscardedSignalControl::Take`). The scheduler pops and promotes either
2474/// way.
2475pub(crate) async fn take_outcome<T, G>(
2476    guest: &mut G,
2477    signal: i32,
2478    after: Option<(u64, u64)>,
2479) -> crate::scheduler::posix_timer_coalesce::TakeOutcome
2480where
2481    T: RecordOrReplay,
2482    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2483{
2484    use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalAnswer;
2485    use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalControl;
2486    use crate::scheduler::posix_timer_coalesce::TakeOutcome;
2487    let at = guest.thread_state().thread_logical_time.as_nanos();
2488    match crate::tool_global::discarded_signal(
2489        guest,
2490        DiscardedSignalControl::Take { signal, at, after },
2491    )
2492    .await
2493    {
2494        DiscardedSignalAnswer::Taken(outcome) => outcome,
2495        _ => TakeOutcome {
2496            skip: false,
2497            rewrite: None,
2498        },
2499    }
2500}
2501
2502async fn zero_timespec<'stack, T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2503    guest: &mut G,
2504) -> (Addr<'stack, Timespec>, <G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard) {
2505    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
2506    let tp_val = Timespec {
2507        tv_sec: 0,
2508        tv_nsec: 0,
2509    };
2510    let tp = stack.push(tp_val);
2511    let guard = stack.commit().expect("stack.commit to succeed");
2512    (tp, guard)
2513}

2515#[async_trait]
2516impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Wait4 {
2517    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2518        self,
2519        _guest: &mut G,
2520    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2521        let call2 = self.with_options(self.options() | WaitPidFlag::WNOHANG);
2522        (call2, None)
2523    }
2524
2525    // Child has not changed state yet, so we go to the scheduler and wait to poll again.
2526    // In scenarios with lots of outstanding waits, this polling strategy can change the asymptotic
2527    // complexity of the program. Ideally, we would model the blocking `wait4` (and process state
2528    // transitions) directly in the scheduler, and execute it only when we know it will complete.
2529    //
2530    // The polling backoff strategy mitigates this problem however.
2531    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
2532        res == Ok(0)
2533    }
2534}

2536#[async_trait]
2537/// Used only for FUTEX_WAIT
2538impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Futex {
2539    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2540        self,
2541        guest: &mut G,
2542    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2543        let (tp, guard) = zero_timespec(guest).await;
2544        (self.with_timeout(Some(tp)), Some(guard))
2545    }
2546
2547    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
2548        // EAGAIN can mean the futex wait's compare-and-block failed and we should return that to
2549        // the guest.  With timeout=0, the timeout is what shows that it would have blocked.
2550        res == Err(Errno::ETIMEDOUT)
2551    }
2552
2553    /// Linux restarts an untimed `FUTEX_WAIT` under `SA_RESTART` (`-ERESTARTSYS`), but a
2554    /// timed wait returns `-ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, which a handler always turns into
2555    /// `EINTR` (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
2556    ///
2557    /// A timed `FUTEX_WAIT` or `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` returns Linux's code: with no
2558    /// handler the kernel then runs `restart_syscall`, which Detcore resumes with the
2559    /// deadline it kept ([`RestartBlock`]), as `futex_wait_restart` does
2560    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358). Linux's `futex_wait` keeps
2561    /// the absolute deadline of every timed wait in the restart block, so a
2562    /// `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` deadline the guest moves in memory after the wait began
2563    /// does not change when the restarted wait ends. `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` used to
2564    /// return `ERESTARTNOHAND`, which ran the call again with its original
2565    /// arguments and so read the deadline again (round-10 finding Medium 4 on
2566    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
2567    ///
2568    /// FUTEX_LOCK_PI and FUTEX_LOCK_PI2 return `-ERESTARTNOINTR`, which the
2569    /// kernel restarts whatever the handler (`futex_lock_pi`,
2570    /// kernel/futex/pi.c:1124 at v6.16).
2571    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2572        if matches!(
2573            self.futex_op() & libc::FUTEX_CMD_MASK,
2574            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI | libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI2
2575        ) {
2576            Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR
2577        } else if self.restart_keeps_deadline() {
2578            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
2579        } else if self.timeout().is_some() {
2580            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
2581        } else {
2582            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
2583        }
2584    }
2585
2586    /// Every timed wait: `FUTEX_WAIT`'s relative timeout and `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET`'s
2587    /// absolute deadline both become the absolute deadline Linux's restart keeps.
2588    fn restart_keeps_deadline(&self) -> bool {
2589        matches!(
2590            self.futex_op() & libc::FUTEX_CMD_MASK,
2591            libc::FUTEX_WAIT | libc::FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET
2592        ) && self.timeout().is_some()
2593    }
2594}

2596impl TimeoutableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Futex {
2597    fn timeout_return_val(&self) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
2598        Err(Errno::ETIMEDOUT)
2599    }
2600}

2602#[async_trait]
2603impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::RtSigtimedwait {
2604    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2605        self,
2606        guest: &mut G,
2607    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2608        // This is a bit more complicated because we need a new timespec to point to in
2609        // the guest memory.
2610        let (tp, guard) = zero_timespec(guest).await;
2611        (self.with_timeout(Some(tp)), Some(guard))
2612    }
2613
2614    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
2615        res == Err(Errno::EAGAIN)
2616    }
2617
2618    fn signal_interrupt_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2619        Errno::EINTR
2620    }
2621
2622    /// Signals in the wait's own set are accepted by it, not interrupting. A set
2623    /// that cannot be read counts as empty, which nothing observes: the wait's
2624    /// first probe runs before any pending signal is considered
2625    /// (`KernelSignalWait::inject_first_probe`) and fails with `EFAULT`, as Linux
2626    /// fails the call when it cannot copy the set.
2627    fn signals_consumed_by_wait<M: MemoryAccess>(&self, memory: &M) -> KernelSigset {
2628        self.set()
2629            .and_then(|set| memory.read_value(set.cast::<KernelSigset>()).ok())
2630            .unwrap_or(0)
2631    }
2632}

2635    fn timeout_return_val(&self) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
2636        Err(Errno::EAGAIN)
2637    }
2638}

2739/// Whether socket call flags, which Linux reads as an `unsigned int`, carry
2740/// `MSG_DONTWAIT`.

2743}

2745/// A common helper shared among several network syscalls.
2746/// We can't actually CONVERT these syscalls into nonblocking, but we can assert that they are by
2747/// checking the status of their file descriptor.
2748fn network_comm_syscall<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, C: SyscallInfo + Into<Syscall>>(
2749    call: C,
2750    guest: &mut G,
2751) -> (C, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2752    // Already nonblocking because we've assured the socket is.
2753    let fd = get_fd(call.into()).unwrap_or_else(|| {
2754        panic!(
2755            "network_comm_syscall called on invalid syscall / unknown fd: {}",
2756            call.name()
2757        );
2758    });
2759    guest
2760        .thread_state()
2761        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2762            assert!(
2763                detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
2764                "expecting sockets/pipes to be physically nonblocking"
2765            );
2766        })
2767        .unwrap();
2768    (call, None)
2769}

2847#[async_trait]
2848impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Recvmmsg {
2849    // This system call has a timeout argument. `handle_recvmmsg` checks it
2850    // the way Linux does before the call reaches here. A valid one is
2851    // forwarded untouched to each attempt, which is not quite what Linux
2852    // does with it: the host kernel treats it as a real-time budget for
2853    // the datagrams after the first inside that one attempt, writes the
2854    // remaining host time back when it delivered any (`__sys_recvmmsg`'s
2855    // `put_timespec64`, net/socket.c at v6.17), and a tiny budget can cut
2856    // an attempt's count at a host-chosen point; the retry then returns
2857    // that partial count at once where blocking Linux without
2858    // MSG_WAITFORONE keeps waiting for the rest of the batch. The first
2859    // datagram's wait is the part the virtual deadline bounds, by
2860    // `SO_RCVTIMEO` through `execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall`. The
2861    // writeback and partial-count differences predate the socket
2862    // deadlines and are tracked separately (see the diff that added
2863    // this comment).
2864    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2865        self,
2866        guest: &mut G,
2867    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2868        network_comm_syscall(self, guest)
2869    }
2870
2871    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
2872        res == Err(Errno::EAGAIN) || res == Err(Errno::EWOULDBLOCK)
2873    }
2874
2875    fn ends_at_read_shutdown(&self) -> bool {
2876        true
2877    }
2878
2879    /// `MSG_WAITFORONE` does not count: Linux waits for the first datagram and
2880    /// adds `MSG_DONTWAIT` only after it (`do_recvmmsg`), which is what a
2881    /// polled attempt that returns at least one datagram gives.
2882    fn flags_forbid_waiting(&self) -> bool {
2883        has_msg_dontwait(self.flags())
2884    }
2885
2886    fn reads_error_queue(&self) -> bool {
2887        self.flags() & libc::MSG_ERRQUEUE as u32 != 0
2888    }
2889}

2973/// Transform a syscall to nonblocking, then retry it until it returns a successful result.
2974/// Retry a nonblockizable syscall (e.g. a pipe/socket read or write) until it succeeds.

2977/// `Some(detcore)` in record/replay mode for a container-INTERNAL fd (currently pipes):
2978/// each iteration is then routed through `Detcore::record_or_replay`, so the read's
2979/// bytes (and every intervening `EAGAIN`) are captured in the recording and reproduced
2980/// verbatim on replay. Without this, an internal-pipe read on the InternalIOPolling path
2981/// bypasses the recorder and replay reads live from a pipe whose cross-process writer
2982/// schedule is not reproduced -- the reader sees EOF instead of the recorded data and
2983/// replay desyncs. Pass `None` for plain `hermit run` (no recording) or for external fds.

2985    guest: &mut G,
2986    call: C,

2988    subtool: Option<&Detcore<T>>,

2991    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
2992    T: RecordOrReplay,
2993    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2994{
2995    // Bogus 99 return value is dead code below:
2996    retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(guest, call, rsrc, None, subtool, None, false).await
2997}

2999/// What a wait that ended with `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` keeps for the
3000/// `restart_syscall` that Linux runs next when no handler runs
3001/// (`NonblockableSyscall::restart_keeps_deadline`). Linux keeps the call and its
3002/// absolute deadline in the thread's restart block (`do_restart_poll`,
3003/// `futex_wait_restart`). Detcore emulates the wait, so the kernel's restart block
3004/// does not describe it, and Detcore keeps its own
3005/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358). A `poll` with a positive
3006/// timeout that Detcore runs in the kernel keeps one too: the kernel's restart
3007/// block describes that poll, but Detcore runs the restart through its
3008/// recorder (`RestartCall::KernelPoll`).
3009///
3010/// The record lives until the thread's next syscall, which takes it
3011/// (`Detcore::handle_syscall_event`). Other first syscalls, sigreturn and exec
3012/// discard the record; separate threads and newly initialized children have
3013/// independent records. A caught handler does not discard it: Linux resets its
3014/// restart block at sigreturn (`restore_sigcontext`), not when it sets up the
3015/// handler, so a handler whose first syscall is `restart_syscall` resumes the
3016/// interrupted wait with the copied arguments and deadline. Detcore does the
3017/// same when that call stops at the interrupted call's address, as it does
3018/// through libc's `syscall()` (the `restartfirst` mode of the
3019/// `external_signal_interrupt` guest). Linux also keeps its restart block across
3020/// the handler's other syscalls and resumes it from any address; Detcore does
3021/// not, so a `restart_syscall` after another syscall or at another address takes
3022/// the unsupported-syscall policy.
3023///
3024/// A wait that Detcore ran in the kernel as the guest made it keeps a record
3025/// too, holding no deadline: its `restart_syscall` then goes to the kernel,
3026/// whose restart block describes the wait (`RestartCall::InKernel`).
3027#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
3028pub(crate) struct RestartBlock {
3029    /// The instruction pointer at the interrupted call's syscall stop: the address
3030    /// after its `syscall` instruction. The kernel's restart moves the instruction
3031    /// pointer back onto that instruction with `restart_syscall` in `rax`, so the
3032    /// restart stops at the same address.
3033    pub(crate) rip: u64,
3034    /// The wait's absolute deadline, or `None` for a wait without one and for a
3035    /// kernel-run poll, which keeps its own (`RestartCall::KernelPoll`).
3036    pub(crate) deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
3037    /// The interrupted call.
3038    pub(crate) call: RestartCall,
3039}
3040
3041/// Guest scratch for one injected `poll` probe, reserved with the rest of a
3042/// caller's scratch before it commits the stack ([`PollProbe::reserve`]).
3043///
3044/// aarch64 has no `poll` syscall. Its `ppoll` runs the same `do_sys_poll`
3045/// (`fs/select.c`) but takes the timeout by pointer, so a probe there needs a
3046/// slot of guest memory for the timeout. x86_64 injects `poll` itself and
3047/// reserves nothing.
3048#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
3049pub(crate) struct PollProbe {
3050    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
3051    timeout: AddrMut<'static, Timespec>,
3052}
3053
3054impl PollProbe {
3055    /// Reserve the probe's scratch on `stack`, before the caller commits it.
3056    pub(crate) fn reserve<S: Stack>(stack: &mut S) -> Self {
3057        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
3058        return {
3059            let _ = stack;
3060            Self {}
3061        };
3062        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
3063        return Self {
3064            timeout: stack.reserve(),
3065        };
3066    }
3067
3068    /// The probe of the `nfds` entries at `fds`, waiting at most
3069    /// `timeout_millis` (forever when negative), as `poll` takes them.
3070    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
3071    pub(crate) fn call<M: MemoryAccess>(
3072        self,
3073        _memory: M,
3074        fds: AddrMut<'_, libc::pollfd>,
3075        nfds: libc::nfds_t,
3076        timeout_millis: libc::c_int,
3077    ) -> Result<syscalls::Poll, Errno> {
3078        Ok(syscalls::Poll::new()
3079            .with_fds(Some(fds.cast()))
3080            .with_nfds(nfds)
3081            .with_timeout(timeout_millis))
3082    }
3083
3084    /// The probe of the `nfds` entries at `fds`, waiting at most
3085    /// `timeout_millis` (forever when negative), as `poll` takes them: a
3086    /// `ppoll` with no signal mask, whose timeout this stages first.
3087    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
3088    pub(crate) fn call<M: MemoryAccess>(
3089        self,
3090        mut memory: M,
3091        fds: AddrMut<'_, libc::pollfd>,
3092        nfds: libc::nfds_t,
3093        timeout_millis: libc::c_int,
3094    ) -> Result<syscalls::Ppoll, Errno> {
3095        let timeout = if timeout_millis < 0 {
3096            None
3097        } else {
3098            let timeout = Timespec {
3099                tv_sec: libc::time_t::from(timeout_millis / 1000),
3100                tv_nsec: libc::c_long::from(timeout_millis % 1000) * 1_000_000,
3101            };
3102            memory.write_value(self.timeout, &timeout)?;
3103            Some(self.timeout)
3104        };
3105        Ok(syscalls::Ppoll::new()
3106            .with_fds(Some(fds.cast()))
3107            .with_nfds(nfds)
3108            .with_timeout(timeout)
3109            .with_sigmask(None)
3110            .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE))
3111    }
3112}
3113
3114/// A call whose restart keeps its deadline.
3115#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
3116pub(crate) enum RestartCall {
3117    /// Only x86_64 has `poll`; aarch64's `ppoll` restarts with
3118    /// `ERESTARTNOHAND`, not a restart block.
3119    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
3120    Poll(syscalls::Poll),
3121    /// A `poll` with a positive timeout that Detcore ran in the kernel
3122    /// (`Detcore::handle_external_poll`: record and replay, and
3123    /// `--no-sequentialize-threads`), with the end of its timeout. Its restart
3124    /// runs the poll again in the kernel, through the recorder, with the time
3125    /// left (`Detcore::resume_kernel_poll`). Only x86_64 has `poll`.
3126    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
3127    KernelPoll(syscalls::Poll, KernelPollDeadline),
3128    /// A woken `poll` that ended with `ERESTARTSYS` on a backend that restarts
3129    /// it by running the guest's own `poll` again (KVM,
3130    /// `Detcore::keep_deadline_for_rerun`). Only that rerun takes the record,
3131    /// the same call at the same address ([`RestartBlock::rerun_deadline`]);
3132    /// `restart_syscall` never does. Only x86_64 has `poll`.
3133    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
3134    PollRerun(syscalls::Poll),
3135    Futex(syscalls::Futex),
3136    /// A relative `nanosleep` or `clock_nanosleep` that ended for a claimed
3137    /// `SIGCHLD` (`syscalls::signal::SleepSignal::Claimed`).
3138    Nanosleep(reverie::syscalls::family::NanosleepFamily),
3139    /// A timed wait that Detcore ran in the kernel as the guest made it, which
3140    /// the kernel's own restart block describes (`inject_keeping_kernel_restart`):
3141    /// a sleep or futex wait without sequentialized threads. Its
3142    /// `restart_syscall` goes to the kernel, which resumes the wait until the
3143    /// end it kept.
3144    InKernel(Sysno),
3145}
3146
3147/// Where the timeout of a `poll` Detcore runs in the kernel ends
3148/// (`RestartCall::KernelPoll`), on the host's monotonic clock. That clock is
3149/// the one the kernel wait runs on and the one Linux's restart keeps its end
3150/// time on (`poll_select_set_timeout`, `do_restart_poll`), while the thread's
3151/// logical time stands still as long as it blocks in the kernel, so an end on
3152/// logical time would let every restart wait the whole timeout again.
3153///
3154/// `None` under record and replay: there the restart reruns the poll with the
3155/// timeout it was issued with. The recording holds each poll's arguments and
3156/// replay checks them, and no clock that replay reproduces moves while the
3157/// poll blocks, so a time left is not replayed today.
3158#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
3159#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
3160pub(crate) struct KernelPollDeadline(pub(crate) Option<std::time::Instant>);
3161
3162/// The result of an injected `restart_syscall` (`resume_kernel_wait`).
3163fn resumed_kernel_wait_result(result: Result<i64, Errno>) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
3164    match result {
3165        Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS) => Err(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK),
3166        other => other,
3167    }
3168}
3169
3170impl RestartBlock {
3171    /// The record, if a `restart_syscall` that stopped at `rip` is the kernel's
3172    /// restart of the interrupted call. At any other address the guest made the
3173    /// call itself.
3174    pub(crate) fn resumed_at(self, rip: u64) -> Option<Self> {
3175        (self.rip == rip).then_some(self)
3176    }
3177
3178    /// The deadline a woken `poll` kept for its rerun
3179    /// ([`RestartCall::PollRerun`]), if `call`, stopped at `rip`, is that rerun:
3180    /// the same call at the same address. No other record is taken here, so
3181    /// a record kept for the kernel's `restart_syscall` serves only that
3182    /// restart: a program's own `poll` after `EINTR` waits its whole timeout
3183    /// again, from its own call (`do_sys_poll`), and only `restart_syscall`
3184    /// resumes the old end time (`do_restart_poll`).
3185    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
3186    pub(crate) fn rerun_deadline(
3187        self,
3188        rip: u64,
3189        call: syscalls::Poll,
3190    ) -> Option<Option<LogicalTime>> {
3191        self.resumed_at(rip)
3192            .filter(|block| block.call == RestartCall::PollRerun(call))
3193            .map(|block| block.deadline)
3194    }
3195}

3197/// Injects `call`, which the kernel runs as the guest made it, and keeps a
3198/// record for the kernel's restart when a signal ends it with
3199/// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` (`RestartCall::InKernel`). Linux then restarts the
3200/// wait through `restart_syscall` with the end time it stored in the thread's
3201/// restart block (`hrtimer_nanosleep_restart`, `futex_wait_restart`), and that
3202/// block is the one this call left: nothing else Detcore runs for the thread
3203/// before the restart sets or resets it.
3204pub(crate) async fn inject_keeping_kernel_restart<T, G, S>(
3205    guest: &mut G,
3206    call: S,
3207) -> Result<i64, Error>
3208where
3209    T: RecordOrReplay,
3210    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3211    S: SyscallInfo,
3212{
3213    let sysno = call.number();
3214    let result = guest.inject(call).await.map_err(Error::from);
3215    keep_restart_block(guest, &result, RestartCall::InKernel(sysno), None).await;
3216    result
3217}

3219/// The kernel's restart of a wait Detcore ran in the kernel
3220/// (`RestartCall::InKernel`): `restart_syscall` itself, which resumes the wait
3221/// from the thread's restart block. A signal that ends the resumed wait
3222/// leaves `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` and the block again, so the record is kept
3223/// again. A signal that stops the injected call before it runs leaves the
3224/// block unused; the result is then the same `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, never
3225/// the `ERESTARTSYS` the backend reports, which would make the kernel rerun
3226/// `restart_syscall` without a record (`resumed_kernel_wait_result`).
3227pub(crate) async fn resume_kernel_wait<T, G>(
3228    guest: &mut G,
3229    restart: Syscall,
3230    sysno: Sysno,
3231) -> Result<i64, Error>
3232where
3233    T: RecordOrReplay,
3234    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3235{
3236    let result = resumed_kernel_wait_result(guest.inject(restart).await).map_err(Error::from);
3237    keep_restart_block(guest, &result, RestartCall::InKernel(sysno), None).await;
3238    result
3239}
3240
3241/// Keeps `deadline` for the kernel's restart of `call` when the wait ended with
3242/// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` (`RestartBlock`).
3243pub(crate) async fn keep_restart_block<T, G>(
3244    guest: &mut G,
3245    result: &Result<i64, Error>,
3246    call: RestartCall,
3247    deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
3248) where
3249    T: RecordOrReplay,
3250    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3251{
3252    if matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(errno)) if *errno == Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK) {
3253        let rip = crate::arch::instruction_pointer(&guest.regs().await);
3254        let block = RestartBlock {
3255            rip,
3256            deadline,
3257            call,
3258        };
3259        tracing::trace!(
3260            "[tid {}] the wait keeps {:?} for its restart",
3261            guest.tid(),
3262            block
3263        );
3264        guest.thread_state_mut().restart_block = Some(block);
3265    }
3266}
3267
3268/// The restart code that ends a wait for a signal the backend holds and delivers
3269/// when the guest resumes. The backend passes a held signal on without reporting it
3270/// to the tool when the call returns `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, so for any signal but
3271/// `SIGSTOP`, which it never reports, the wait returns `ERESTARTNOHAND` instead. A
3272/// handler turns either code into `EINTR`, and a signal that kills the process
3273/// leaves no restart. The difference is a stop, which `SIGSTOP` alone can be here:
3274/// a default job-control stop does not end a wait whose restart keeps its deadline
3275/// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`).
3276///
3277/// A claimed relative `nanosleep` makes the opposite choice on purpose
3278/// (`syscalls::time`, `RestartCall::Nanosleep`): it returns
3279/// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, so the held `SIGCHLD` is passed on unreported, and
3280/// the kernel's `restart_syscall` alone says no handler ran
3281/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4346).
3282fn held_signal_restart_errno(restart_errno: Errno, signal: i32) -> Errno {
3283    if restart_errno == Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK && signal != libc::SIGSTOP {
3284        Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
3285    } else {
3286        restart_errno
3287    }
3288}
3289
3290/// The deadline a polling request carries so the scheduler can restore a
3291/// backed-off poller once committed virtual time passes it
3292/// (`Resources::poll_deadline`, <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
3293/// `None` under record/replay, whose schedule must not change.
3294pub(crate) fn poll_deadline_for<T, G>(
3295    guest: &G,
3296    deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
3297) -> Option<LogicalTime>
3298where
3299    T: RecordOrReplay,
3300    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3301{
3302    if guest.config().recordreplay_modes {
3303        None
3304    } else {
3305        deadline
3306    }
3307}
3308
3309/// Retry a non-blocking syscall until it succeeds. Set the timeout to zero for the actual
3310/// syscalls (retries), while monitoring the clock to see if/when the logical timeout
3311/// should trigger.  Timeout is passed as an ABSOLUTE TIME (not duration).
3312pub async fn retry_nonblocking_syscall_with_timeout<T, G, C>(
3313    guest: &mut G,
3314    call: C,
3315    rsrc: Resources,
3316    // Logical timeout:
3317    maybe_timeout: Option<LogicalTime>,
3318) -> Result<i64, Error>
3319where
3320    C: NonblockableSyscall + TimeoutableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
3321    T: RecordOrReplay,
3322    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3323{
3324    let maybe_tup = maybe_timeout.map(|t| (t, call.timeout_return_val()));
3325    // Under the in-guest delivery gate the private-mask machinery is never
3326    // taken (A5 step 3c.1c, D50): the helper below decides by the published
3327    // mask instead (`gated_wait_ends`).
3328    if guest
3329        .config()
3330        .backend
3331        .supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption
3332        && !guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery
3333    {
3334        return retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state(guest, call, rsrc, maybe_tup).await;
3335    }
3336    // poll/epoll_wait/futex/rt_sigtimedwait keep their existing execution (raw
3337    // inject_with_retry): their record/replay handling is out of scope for the internal
3338    // pipe data-ordering fix, and their fds are not necessarily internal pipes.
3339    retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(guest, call, rsrc, maybe_tup, None, None, false).await
3340}
3341
3342/// The task whose signal state the scheduler may read to decide which signal
3343/// ends an internal IO poll: the guest thread itself wherever a reader
3344/// answers for it. Where guest thread IDs name host tasks that is the
3345/// kernel's `/proc` state; where they do not (KVM), the state its backend
3346/// reports (`Scheduler::backend_signal_state`, SIGSHARE S2), which the
3347/// scheduler reads through the run-scoped signal control installed only for
3348/// sequentialized threads. `None` for KVM without sequentialized threads,
3349/// where no reader answers and `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` would describe an
3350/// unrelated host task.
3351pub(crate) fn guest_signal_state_task<T, G>(guest: &G) -> Option<(i32, i32)>
3352where
3353    T: RecordOrReplay,
3354    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3355{
3356    let config = guest.config();
3357    let reader_answers = crate::procfs_inode::guest_tids_name_host_tasks(&config.backend, None)
3358        || (crate::syscalls::reads_signal_state_from_backend(&config.backend)
3359            && config.sequentialize_threads);
3360    reader_answers.then(|| (guest.pid().as_raw(), guest.tid().as_raw()))
3361}
3362
3363/// Whether a signal that woke a poll would be delivered to this thread now,
3364/// read from the backend's own state of the thread: its current mask (the
3365/// old set of a query-only `rt_sigprocmask`) and each signal's disposition
3366/// (`wait_signal_disposition`). A blocked or ignored signal, or one whose
3367/// default action ignores it, does not.
3368async fn own_disposition_interrupts<T, G>(
3369    guest: &mut G,
3370    status: ResumeStatus,
3371    mask_addr: AddrMut<'_, KernelSigset>,
3372    action_addr: AddrMut<'_, KernelSigaction>,
3373) -> Result<bool, Error>
3374where
3375    T: RecordOrReplay,
3376    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3377{
3378    let query = syscalls::RtSigprocmask::new()
3379        .with_how(libc::SIG_BLOCK)
3380        .with_set(None)
3381        .with_oldset(Some(mask_addr.cast()))
3382        .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE);
3383    guest.inject_with_retry(query).await?;
3384    let mask: KernelSigset = guest.memory().read_value(mask_addr)?;
3385    Ok(
3386        wait_signal_disposition(guest, status, &mask, action_addr, true)
3387            .await?
3388            .is_some(),
3389    )
3390}
3391
3392/// Whether the signal that woke a part of a call that made progress
3393/// (`CallParts::progress`), or a read of an inotify instance that is
3394/// nonblocking for the guest by now (`interrupted_wait_errno`), on a backend
3395/// whose turn does not decide interruption, would be delivered to the caller
3396/// now, by its own mask and dispositions (`own_disposition_interrupts`): a
3397/// blocked or ignored signal leaves the read waiting, as it leaves Linux's
3398/// read waiting.
3399async fn progress_signal_interrupts<T, G>(
3400    guest: &mut G,
3401    status: ResumeStatus,
3402) -> Result<bool, Error>
3403where
3404    T: RecordOrReplay,
3405    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3406{
3407    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
3408    let mask_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
3409    let action_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
3410    let _guard = stack.commit()?;
3411    own_disposition_interrupts(guest, status, mask_addr, action_addr).await
3412}
3413
3414/// The open file description of the inotify instance a read began on, if
3415/// `call` is a read of one: Linux's read keeps that file through
3416/// `ksys_read` whatever another thread later puts at its number
3417/// (<https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.17/fs/read_write.c#L704-L720>),
3418/// so the errno a signal wake returns is that description's to decide
3419/// (`interrupted_wait_errno`). A clone shares the description with every
3420/// alias, so a later F_SETFL or FIONBIO through any of them shows here.
3421fn inotify_description_of<T, G, C>(guest: &G, call: C) -> Option<crate::fd::DetFd>
3422where
3423    T: RecordOrReplay,
3424    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3425    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
3426{
3427    let fd = get_fd(call.into())?;
3428    guest
3429        .thread_state()
3430        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3431            (detfd.ty() == FdType::Inotify).then(|| detfd.clone())
3432        })
3433        .ok()
3434        .flatten()
3435}
3436
3437/// The errno a polled call that would still wait returns when a signal ends
3438/// the wait: the call's interrupt errno, read at its entry (`interrupt_errno`,
3439/// `interrupt_errno_at_entry`: its restart code,
3440/// `NonblockableSyscall::signal_interrupt_errno`, or EINTR for a receive with a
3441/// finite receive timeout), except for a read that began on an inotify
3442/// instance (`began_on`, `inotify_description_of`) that is nonblocking for the
3443/// guest by now, which another thread's F_SETFL or FIONBIO made it while the
3444/// read waited.
3445/// `inotify_read` tests the file's current O_NONBLOCK before it looks for a
3446/// pending signal, so Linux returns EAGAIN there
3447/// (<https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.17/fs/notify/inotify/inotify_user.c#L249-L299>).
3448/// A mode change alone ends no wait: Linux's reader sleeps on until an event
3449/// or a signal it would deliver wakes it, and this applies only at such a
3450/// wake (where the turn does not decide, the woken read asks,
3451/// `progress_signal_interrupts`). What another thread puts at the
3452/// descriptor's number while the read waits changes nothing: the
3453/// description the read began on decides.
3454fn interrupted_wait_errno(began_on: Option<&crate::fd::DetFd>, interrupt_errno: Errno) -> Errno {
3455    if began_on.is_some_and(crate::fd::DetFd::is_nonblocking) {
3456        Errno::EAGAIN
3457    } else {
3458        interrupt_errno
3459    }
3460}
3461
3462/// A call Detcore runs in parts, one after another (a readv reading on into a
3463/// later iovec, `Detcore::readv_inotify`; `ThreadState::call_parts`).
3464#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
3465pub(crate) struct CallParts {
3466    /// Whether an earlier part transferred bytes. A wake that would deliver
3467    /// a signal then ends the part now running with those bytes, and any
3468    /// other wake leaves it waiting (`retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`).
3469    pub(crate) progress: bool,
3470    /// A signal an earlier part completed with pending. It ends the first
3471    /// later part that would wait: Linux's next `->read` finds it with
3472    /// `signal_pending()` before it sleeps, so `do_loop_readv_writev` returns
3473    /// the bytes read so far
3474    /// (<https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.17/fs/read_write.c#L835-L866>).
3475    pub(crate) carried: Option<CarriedSignal>,
3476}
3477
3478/// What the turn on which a part of a call run in parts completed knew of a
3479/// signal that would end a later part (`CallParts::carried`).
3480#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
3481pub(crate) enum CarriedSignal {
3482    /// The turn decided it (`TurnSignals::ends`: a named wake or a pending
3483    /// copy that the call's mask and the signal's disposition deliver).
3484    Decided,
3485    /// A wake the turn did not decide: on a backend whose guest threads are
3486    /// not host tasks (KVM), the later part decides from the guest's own mask
3487    /// and dispositions (`progress_signal_interrupts`); a backend's own
3488    /// observation of a signal (`ResumeStatus::Signaled(None)`) is trusted, as
3489    /// a turn trusts it.
3490    Wake(ResumeStatus),
3491}
3492
3493/// The signal a part completing on this turn carries to the parts after it
3494/// (`CallParts::carried`): one the turn found that would end a part after
3495/// progress (`turn`, read where the turn decides), or the turn's signal wake
3496/// where it does not. Under the in-guest delivery gate none is carried: each
3497/// part decides at its own turns (`gated_wait_ends`).
3498fn carried_signal(
3499    turn: Option<TurnSignals>,
3500    resumed: &ResumeStatus,
3501    gated: bool,
3502) -> Option<CarriedSignal> {
3503    match turn {
3504        Some(turn) => turn.ends(true).then_some(CarriedSignal::Decided),
3505        None if gated => None,
3506        None => matches!(resumed, ResumeStatus::Signaled(_))
3507            .then(|| CarriedSignal::Wake(resumed.clone())),
3508    }
3509}
3510
3511/// Whether the signal an earlier part of a call run in parts completed with
3512/// (`CallParts::carried`) ends the part now running, which would wait. Taken
3513/// once: one that would not be delivered leaves the part waiting, and its
3514/// later wakes decide. `decides_itself`: the backend's turn does not decide
3515/// interruption (KVM), so the guest's own mask and dispositions decide
3516/// (`progress_signal_interrupts`).
3517async fn carried_signal_ends<T, G>(
3518    guest: &mut G,
3519    decides_itself: bool,
3520    gated: bool,
3521) -> Result<bool, Error>
3522where
3523    T: RecordOrReplay,
3524    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3525{
3526    let carried = guest
3527        .thread_state_mut()
3528        .call_parts
3529        .as_mut()
3530        .and_then(|parts| parts.carried.take());
3531    match carried {
3532        None => Ok(false),
3533        Some(CarriedSignal::Decided) => Ok(true),
3534        Some(CarriedSignal::Wake(status)) if decides_itself => {
3535            progress_signal_interrupts(guest, status).await
3536        }
3537        Some(CarriedSignal::Wake(_)) => Ok(!gated),
3538    }
3539}
3540
3541/// The errno a signal that ends `call` after it began returns, given the one
3542/// its kind returns (`default`, its `signal_interrupt_errno` or
3543/// `kernel_restart_errno`), read once, at the call's entry, and kept for the
3544/// whole call however long it polls: a later `setsockopt` through an alias
3545/// does not change it, as Linux reads the timeout once, when the call begins
3546/// (`sock_rcvtimeo`: net/unix/af_unix.c:2951, net/ipv4/tcp.c:2635,
3547/// net/core/datagram.c:294 and net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:678 at
3548/// v6.17).
3549///
3550/// A receive (`recvfrom`, `recvmsg`, `recvmmsg`, or `read` or `readv` on a
3551/// socket) and an `accept` wait by the socket's receive timeout, and a
3552/// send and a connect by its send timeout (`socket_timeout_fd`). Linux
3553/// ends one that a signal interrupts with `sock_intr_errno(timeo)`
3554/// (include/net/sock.h:2627-2630; af_unix.c:3012-3013, tcp.c:2743-2744,
3555/// datagram.c:127-128, which AF_UNIX's accept reaches through
3556/// `skb_recv_datagram`, af_unix.c:1880, and inet_connection_sock.c:645):
3557/// ERESTARTSYS for an untimed wait, which a handler with `SA_RESTART`
3558/// restarts, but EINTR for a finite timeout, whatever the handler's
3559/// flags. So such a call returns EINTR here
3560/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929>, the Codex review of
3561/// slice 2, round 2). The timeout is Detcore's model of the description's
3562/// `SO_RCVTIMEO` or `SO_SNDTIMEO` (`DetFd::receive_timeout`,
3563/// `DetFd::send_timeout`), which every alias Detcore tracks shares; every
3564/// other call keeps `default` (`socket_timeout_interrupt_errno`).
3565fn interrupt_errno_at_entry<T, G, C>(guest: &G, call: &C, default: Errno) -> Errno
3566where
3567    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
3568    T: RecordOrReplay,
3569    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3570{
3571    let timeout = socket_timeout_fd((*call).into()).and_then(|(fd, direction)| {
3572        guest
3573            .thread_state()
3574            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3575                matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Socket).then(|| match direction {
3576                    SocketTimeoutDirection::Receive => detfd.receive_timeout(),
3577                    SocketTimeoutDirection::Send => detfd.send_timeout(),
3578                })
3579            })
3580            .ok()
3581            .flatten()
3582    });
3583    socket_timeout_interrupt_errno(default, timeout)
3584}
3585
3586/// Which of a socket's two timeouts bounds a call's wait.
3587#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3588enum SocketTimeoutDirection {
3589    /// `SO_RCVTIMEO`: a receive's or an accept's wait.
3590    Receive,
3591    /// `SO_SNDTIMEO`: a send's or a connect's wait.
3592    Send,
3593}
3594
3595/// The descriptor whose socket timeout, if it is a socket, bounds
3596/// `syscall`'s wait, and which timeout that is. `None` for every other
3597/// call. A receive (`recvfrom`, `recvmsg`, `recvmmsg`, `read`, `readv`)
3598/// and an accept wait by `SO_RCVTIMEO`; a send (`sendto`, `sendmsg`,
3599/// `sendmmsg`, `write`, `writev`) and a connect wait by `SO_SNDTIMEO`
3600/// (`sock_sndtimeo` in `unix_stream_connect`, net/unix/af_unix.c:1672,
3601/// and `inet_stream_connect`, net/ipv4/af_inet.c:694, at v6.17). A `read`
3602/// or `write` on a descriptor that is not a socket never reaches the
3603/// timeout: callers check `FdType::Socket` first.
3604fn socket_timeout_fd(syscall: Syscall) -> Option<(i32, SocketTimeoutDirection)> {
3605    let direction = match syscall {
3606        Syscall::Recvfrom(_)
3607        | Syscall::Recvmsg(_)
3608        | Syscall::Recvmmsg(_)
3609        | Syscall::Read(_)
3610        | Syscall::Readv(_)
3611        | Syscall::Accept(_)
3612        | Syscall::Accept4(_) => SocketTimeoutDirection::Receive,
3613        Syscall::Sendto(_)
3614        | Syscall::Sendmsg(_)
3615        | Syscall::Sendmmsg(_)
3616        | Syscall::Write(_)
3617        | Syscall::Writev(_)
3618        | Syscall::Connect(_) => SocketTimeoutDirection::Send,
3619        _ => return None,
3620    };
3621    get_fd(syscall).map(|fd| (fd, direction))
3622}
3623
3624/// The errno a socket wait that outlasts its timeout returns. Every
3625/// timed socket wait fails with EAGAIN -- a send, a receive, an accept
3626/// and an AF_UNIX connect (see `execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall`) --
3627/// except an Internet connect: a TCP connect is already in progress
3628/// when it gives up waiting, so it returns EINPROGRESS and the attempt
3629/// continues in the background (`inet_stream_connect` presets
3630/// `-EINPROGRESS` and leaves by `goto out` when its wait's timeo runs
3631/// out, net/ipv4/af_inet.c:690-703 at v6.17). `family` is the connect
3632/// address's `sa_family`, read with the timeout snapshot; an unreadable
3633/// or short address fails on its first attempt with its own errno, so
3634/// the expiry it never reaches may default to EAGAIN. A non-connect
3635/// call ignores `family`.
3636fn socket_timeout_expiry(syscall: Syscall, family: Option<u16>) -> Errno {
3637    match syscall {
3638        Syscall::Connect(_)
3639            if matches!(
3640                family,
3641                Some(family) if family == libc::AF_INET as u16 || family == libc::AF_INET6 as u16
3642            ) =>
3643        {
3644            Errno::EINPROGRESS
3645        }
3646        _ => Errno::EAGAIN,
3647    }
3648}
3649
3650/// [`interrupt_errno_at_entry`]'s rule: a call that would end with
3651/// ERESTARTSYS ends with EINTR when it waits by a socket's finite timeout
3652/// (`socket_timeout`, `None` for any other call). An `Immediate`
3653/// timeout never waits, and an `Unknown` one keeps the untimed call's
3654/// ERESTARTSYS.
3655fn socket_timeout_interrupt_errno(default: Errno, socket_timeout: Option<ReceiveTimeout>) -> Errno {
3656    match (default, socket_timeout) {
3657        (Errno::ERESTARTSYS, Some(ReceiveTimeout::After(_))) => Errno::EINTR,
3658        _ => default,
3659    }
3660}
3661
3662/// Whether `call`, woken by a signal while it would still block, ends the way
3663/// Linux ends it only through [`woken_poll_errno`]: a `poll` or an unmasked
3664/// `ppoll`, whose Linux interrupt is a restart code (`ERESTARTNOHAND`, or
3665/// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` for a `poll` with a deadline;
3666/// [`NonblockableSyscall::kernel_restart_errno`]), on a backend that restarts a
3667/// woken call only through `ERESTARTSYS`'s protocol and cannot hand the
3668/// delivery Linux's other restart codes
3669/// ([`crate::syscalls::restarts_woken_calls_only_through_erestartsys`], KVM)
3670/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929>). Every other call, and
3671/// every other backend, keeps its interrupt errno.
3672fn restarts_without_a_handler_through_erestartsys<T, G, C>(guest: &G, call: &C) -> bool
3673where
3674    C: NonblockableSyscall,
3675    T: RecordOrReplay,
3676    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3677{
3678    woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys(
3679        crate::syscalls::restarts_woken_calls_only_through_erestartsys(&guest.config().backend),
3680        call,
3681    )
3682}
3683
3684/// [`restarts_without_a_handler_through_erestartsys`], given whether the
3685/// backend restarts a woken call only through `ERESTARTSYS`.
