3686fn woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys<C: NonblockableSyscall>(
3687    restarts_only_through_erestartsys: bool,
3688    call: &C,
3689) -> bool {
3690    restarts_only_through_erestartsys
3691        && call.signal_interrupt_errno() == Errno::EINTR
3692        && matches!(
3693            call.kernel_restart_errno(),
3694            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND | Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
3695        )
3696}
3697
3698/// The errno a `poll` or an unmasked `ppoll` returns when a signal woke it and
3699/// it would still block, on a backend that restarts a call only through
3700/// `ERESTARTSYS` ([`restarts_without_a_handler_through_erestartsys`]); the
3701/// network trace's wait on a recorded socket ends the same way there
3702/// (`Detcore::network_wait`).
3703///
3704/// Linux ends such a call with a restart code (`do_poll`'s `-ERESTARTNOHAND`,
3705/// fs/select.c:929-934 at v6.17, which `poll` keeps as `-ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`
3706/// with its end time, 1076-1090) and settles it at the return to user mode,
3707/// from what that return delivers: `get_signal` drops each ignored copy it
3708/// dequeues and goes on (kernel/signal.c:2931-2932), and the first handler
3709/// it reaches turns the restart code into `EINTR`, whether or not the handler
3710/// has `SA_RESTART` (arch/x86/kernel/signal.c:266-270); with no handler the
3711/// call is restarted (344-357). That return delivers every signal pending for
3712/// the thread, in its own queue or its process's, that its mask leaves
3713/// unblocked, not only the one that woke it, and `get_signal` takes them one
3714/// after another under the signal lock, so no other thread takes a copy
3715/// between two of its dequeues.
3716///
3717/// This backend's return delivers the same signals in the same order
3718/// (reverie-linuxemu `next_matching`), but each through a Tool callback whose
3719/// turn can hand the thread to the scheduler, so other threads run between two
3720/// of its deliveries and can take a copy from the process's queue in between:
3721/// an ignored copy's turn let another thread take the caught copy behind it,
3722/// and the call returned `EINTR` with no handler run (the Codex review of
3723/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929>, round 4). Only the first
3724/// delivery comes before any such turn. So the answer is decided from that one
3725/// signal ([`woken_poll_errno_from_sets`]): `EINTR` when it has a handler,
3726/// which then runs with that result, and `ERESTARTSYS` otherwise, which leaves
3727/// every later delivery to the backend's `ERESTARTSYS` protocol, applied at the
3728/// delivery itself: a handler without `SA_RESTART` then gets `EINTR`, and no
3729/// handler at all a restart. Two outcomes of that protocol are not Linux's,
3730/// and each delivery of the return is checked for them
3731/// ([`check_woken_wait_delivery`], the Codex review of round 5): a handler
3732/// with `SA_RESTART` for a signal pending behind the first, which restarts the
3733/// call where Linux fails it with `EINTR`; and an `EINTR` whose handler a
3734/// sibling removed during the delivery's turn, with no other handler left at
3735/// that return, which leaves the call failed with no handler run. Either
3736/// refuses the run by name. A handler without `SA_RESTART` behind a first
3737/// signal with no handler gets `EINTR` from the protocol, as on Linux, and
3738/// the record kept for the call's rerun is dropped then.
3739///
3740/// It is answered twice. Here, where the wait ends, for what observes the
3741/// call's result before its return (the DETLOG result line, the restart
3742/// record, the posthook trace); and again at the return itself, by
3743/// [`settle_woken_wait_at_return`], the syscall handler's last step, from the
3744/// sets as they stand after its last await, which is the answer the backend
3745/// gets: the handler's later awaits can let other threads run. A backend that
3746/// does not report the sets is answered here alone, as before, from the woken
3747/// signals' actions (`wait_signal_disposition`, [`woken_poll_errno_for`]).
3748pub(crate) async fn woken_poll_errno<T, G>(
3749    guest: &mut G,
3750    status: ResumeStatus,
3751) -> Result<Errno, Error>
3752where
3753    T: RecordOrReplay,
3754    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3755{
3756    if let Ok(sets) = guest.signal_sets(guest.tid()) {
3757        guest.thread_state_mut().woken_wait = WokenWait::Poll;
3758        return Ok(woken_poll_errno_from_sets(sets));
3759    }
3760    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
3761    let mask_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
3762    let action_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
3763    let _guard = stack.commit()?;
3764    let query = syscalls::RtSigprocmask::new()
3765        .with_how(libc::SIG_BLOCK)
3766        .with_set(None)
3767        .with_oldset(Some(mask_addr.cast()))
3768        .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE);
3769    guest.inject_with_retry(query).await?;
3770    let mask: KernelSigset = guest.memory().read_value(mask_addr)?;
3771    let disposition = wait_signal_disposition(guest, status, &mask, action_addr, true).await?;
3772    Ok(woken_poll_errno_for(disposition))
3773}
3774
3775/// [`woken_poll_errno`]'s answer from the thread's signal sets: `EINTR` when the
3776/// first signal the return delivers ([`first_delivered`]) has a handler
3777/// (`SigCgt`), and `ERESTARTSYS` when it has none (it is ignored, or at a
3778/// default action) or nothing is pending that the mask leaves unblocked.
3779fn woken_poll_errno_from_sets(sets: reverie::SignalSets) -> Errno {
3780    match first_delivered(sets) {
3781        Some(signal) if sets.caught & kernel_sigset_bit(signal) != 0 => Errno::EINTR,
3782        _ => Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
3783    }
3784}
3785
3786/// The signal a return to user mode with the thread's signal sets `sets`
3787/// dequeues first, as Linux's `dequeue_signal` takes it: from the thread's own
3788/// queue before its process's (kernel/signal.c:634-639 at v6.12), and in each
3789/// a synchronous signal first, then the lowest number (`next_signal`,
3790/// 196-218), among those its mask leaves unblocked
3791/// (`KernelSignalState::next_dequeued`). The KVM backend selects in that order
3792/// (reverie-linuxemu `take_signal_event_locked`, `next_matching`). `None` when
3793/// nothing is pending that the mask leaves unblocked.
3794fn first_delivered(sets: reverie::SignalSets) -> Option<i32> {
3795    let state = KernelSignalState {
3796        thread_pending: sets.pending,
3797        shared_pending: sets.shared_pending,
3798        ..KernelSignalState::default()
3799    };
3800    state.next_dequeued(sets.blocked).map(|(signal, _)| signal)
3801}
3802
3803/// What a signal that ended the current syscall's wait leaves for the return
3804/// to user mode, on a backend that restarts a call only through
3805/// `ERESTARTSYS`'s protocol (KVM): `ThreadState::woken_wait`.
3806///
3807/// That protocol settles the call at each delivery of the return: a handler
3808/// without `SA_RESTART` gets `EINTR`, one with `SA_RESTART` restarts the call,
3809/// and no handler at all restarts it too. A woken `poll` must instead fail
3810/// with `EINTR` whenever a handler runs, and restart only when none does
3811/// (Linux's `ERESTARTNOHAND`, which reverie-kvm refuses). Detcore cannot tell
3812/// the backend which; it chooses the errno once, at the return
3813/// ([`settle_woken_wait_at_return`]), and checks each delivery of that return
3814/// against the choice ([`check_woken_wait_delivery`]), refusing the run by
3815/// name where the backend would give a result Linux never gives.
3816#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
3817pub(crate) enum WokenWait {
3818    /// The current syscall's wait was not ended that way.
3819    #[default]
3820    None,
3821    /// A woken `poll`, unmasked `ppoll`, or wait on a recorded socket,
3822    /// answered where its wait ended ([`woken_poll_errno`]).
3823    Poll,
3824    /// A blocking send on a recorded socket that a wake with nothing sent and
3825    /// only ignored copies to deliver ended with `ERESTARTSYS`
3826    /// (`Detcore::network_send_wait`).
3827    Send,
3828    /// The settlement at the return, which its deliveries are checked against.
3829    Settled(SettledWait),
3830}
3831
3832/// The settlement of a woken wait at its return ([`WokenWait::Settled`]).
3833#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3834pub(crate) struct SettledWait {
3835    /// A recorded send ([`WokenWait::Send`]); otherwise a poll.
3836    send: bool,
3837    /// The call, whose number the deliveries at its return report in
3838    /// `orig_rax`, where a delivery anywhere else reports `-1` or another call.
3839    sysno: Sysno,
3840    /// The errno the backend got: `EINTR`, or `ERESTARTSYS`.
3841    errno: Errno,
3842    /// The signals pending for the thread at the settlement that its mask left
3843    /// unblocked: one of them is already there when Linux's return runs, and
3844    /// cannot have come after it.
3845    pending: u64,
3846    /// Whether a delivery at the return ran a handler: the first frame decides
3847    /// the call's result, and later ones stack on its handler.
3848    handler_seen: bool,
3849}
3850
3851/// What [`settle_woken_wait_at_return`] decided.
3852#[derive(Debug)]
3853pub(crate) enum Settlement {
3854    /// Return this result.
3855    Return(Result<i64, Error>),
3856    /// End the run with this named refusal, which the caller prints.
3857    Refuse(String),
3858}
3859
3860/// Settles the errno of a syscall `sysno` whose woken wait
3861/// ([`WokenWait::Poll`] or [`WokenWait::Send`]) ended it, as the syscall
3862/// handler's last step (`Detcore::handle_syscall_event`), from the thread's
3863/// signal sets as they stand there, and returns `res` with it, or a refusal.
3864///
3865/// On KVM the return is committed here. This is a plain function, called
3866/// after the handler's last await, and the backend dequeues the first signal
3867/// its return delivers before it makes any Tool callback there: reverie-kvm's
3868/// syscall return selects it (`filter_one_pending_signal_with_tool`) before
3869/// calling `handle_signal_event`, and a timer request due at the return runs
3870/// its callback first only for a call that made no Tool callback, which this
3871/// one did. So no scheduling point separates the read below from that
3872/// dequeue, and the signal found first here is the one dequeued first there.
3873/// (Only KVM ends a wait this way; on ptrace the kernel settles it.)
3874///
3875/// - A poll: the answer given where the wait ended can be stale by now: the
3876///   handler's later awaits (a slice end at its post-hook, a schedule trace)
3877///   can let other threads run, and take or send a signal. It is decided again
3878///   ([`woken_poll_errno_from_sets`]); where the two differ, the delivery's
3879///   record of the result (`ThreadState::delivery_interruption`) follows the
3880///   new one, while the DETLOG result line and the posthook trace, already
3881///   written, keep the old one (DEBUG names the change). Where the answer is
3882///   `EINTR`, a handler runs at this return and the call is not run again, so
3883///   the deadline kept for that run is dropped (`Detcore::keep_deadline_for_rerun`).
3884/// - A recorded send: its `ERESTARTSYS` is admitted again, after the last
3885///   scheduling point: a signal with an effect may have come during the
3886///   handler's later awaits, or a disposition may have changed, and then the
3887///   network record's refusal applies (`Detcore::network_send_wait`).
3888///
3889/// Either way the settlement is kept for the deliveries of the return
3890/// ([`check_woken_wait_delivery`]). Any other result, and a call that did not
3891/// end that way, is returned unchanged.
3892pub(crate) fn settle_woken_wait_at_return<T, G>(
3893    guest: &mut G,
3894    sysno: Sysno,
3895    res: Result<i64, Error>,
3896) -> Settlement
3897where
3898    T: RecordOrReplay,
3899    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3900{
3901    let send = match std::mem::take(&mut guest.thread_state_mut().woken_wait) {
3902        WokenWait::Poll => false,
3903        WokenWait::Send => true,
3904        WokenWait::None | WokenWait::Settled(_) => return Settlement::Return(res),
3905    };
3906    let answered = match &res {
3907        Err(Error::Errno(errno)) if matches!(*errno, Errno::EINTR | Errno::ERESTARTSYS) => *errno,
3908        _ => return Settlement::Return(res),
3909    };
3910    let Ok(sets) = guest.signal_sets(guest.tid()) else {
3911        return Settlement::Return(res);
3912    };
3913    let settled = if send {
3914        if delivers_a_signal_with_an_effect(sets) {
3915            return Settlement::Refuse(crate::syscalls::network_trace::send_interruption_refusal());
3916        }
3917        answered
3918    } else {
3919        let settled = woken_poll_errno_from_sets(sets);
3920        if settled != answered {
3921            tracing::debug!(
3922                "[dtid {}] {} settles at its return with {} where its wait ended with {}: the \
3923                 first signal the return delivers is {}",
3924                guest.thread_state().dettid,
3925                sysno,
3926                settled,
3927                answered,
3928                first_delivered(sets)
3929                    .map_or_else(|| "none".to_string(), |signal| signal.to_string()),
3930            );
3931            if let Some(reverie::Interruption::Return { syscall, .. }) =
3932                guest.thread_state().delivery_interruption
3933            {
3934                guest.thread_state_mut().delivery_interruption =
3935                    Some(reverie::Interruption::Return {
3936                        syscall,
3937                        result: -i64::from(settled.into_raw()),
3938                    });
3939            }
3940        }
3941        if settled == Errno::EINTR {
3942            guest.thread_state_mut().restart_block = None;
3943        }
3944        settled
3945    };
3946    guest.thread_state_mut().woken_wait = WokenWait::Settled(SettledWait {
3947        send,
3948        sysno,
3949        errno: settled,
3950        pending: (sets.pending | sets.shared_pending) & !sets.blocked,
3951        handler_seen: false,
3952    });
3953    Settlement::Return(Err(settled.into()))
3954}
3955
3956/// Whether a return to user mode with the thread's signal sets `sets` would
3957/// deliver a signal with an effect: one its mask leaves unblocked, pending for
3958/// it or its process, that is neither ignored nor ignored by default, so that
3959/// a handler runs, or a default action ends or stops the process. Linux's
3960/// `get_signal` drops the others without a trace (kernel/signal.c:2815-2816
3961/// and 2830-2831 at v6.12), and a call they interrupted is made again
3962/// (`Detcore::network_send_wait`).
3963pub(crate) fn delivers_a_signal_with_an_effect(sets: reverie::SignalSets) -> bool {
3964    let deliverable = (sets.pending | sets.shared_pending) & !sets.blocked;
3965    deliverable & !crate::syscalls::threads::ignored_at_generation(sets.ignored, sets.caught) != 0
3966}
3967
3968/// Checks a delivery of `signal` (`delivered`: whether Detcore let the backend
3969/// deliver it) against the settlement of the woken wait it returns from
3970/// ([`WokenWait::Settled`]), after the last scheduling point of the delivery's
3971/// callback (`Detcore::handle_signal_event`), and returns the named refusal if
3972/// the backend would now give a result Linux never gives. The disposition read
3973/// here is the one the backend applies: after the callback returns, the
3974/// backend reads it (`signal_disposition`) and builds the frame with no Tool
3975/// callback in between, and it takes the next pending signal before any
3976/// await. Only the deliveries at that return are checked (their registers
3977/// name the call in `orig_rax`), and only until one runs a handler, whose
3978/// frame decides the call's result.
3979///
3980/// - A poll settled `EINTR`, whose return ends with no handler run: the last
3981///   delivery at that return, after which no signal the thread's mask leaves
3982///   unblocked is pending for it or its process, runs no handler, and no
3983///   earlier one did. A sibling ignored the signal during its delivery's turn
3984///   (or Detcore dropped the copy). The backend leaves the `EINTR` with no
3985///   handler run, while Linux, which takes the action under the signal lock,
3986///   either runs the handler or, finding the signal ignored, restarts the
3987///   call. Refused. While another signal is pending, the backend takes it next,
3988///   at the same return, so the check is made again at its delivery: one with
3989///   a handler gets the `EINTR`, as Linux's return that finds it does.
3990/// - A poll settled `ERESTARTSYS` (its first signal had no handler), whose
3991///   delivery runs a handler with `SA_RESTART` while a signal that was already
3992///   pending at the settlement, with a handler, is that signal or is still
3993///   pending: the backend restarts the call after the handler, while Linux,
3994///   whose return finds that signal with the first, fails it with `EINTR`.
3995///   Refused. Signals are matched by number, not by copy: a later copy of a
3996///   signal that was pending at the settlement, which came after another
3997///   thread took that copy during an earlier delivery's turn, is taken for it
3998///   and refused, where Linux's next pass of the return would restart the
3999///   call after its handler. A handler without `SA_RESTART` gets `EINTR`, as on
4000///   Linux, and the record kept for the call's rerun
4001///   (`RestartCall::PollRerun`) is dropped then, so the program's next `poll`
4002///   waits its whole timeout; a handler with `SA_RESTART` for a signal that
4003///   came after the settlement, during an earlier delivery's turn, when no
4004///   signal pending at the settlement with a handler is left, restarts the
4005///   call after it, as Linux's next pass of the return does once the first
4006///   restarted it.
4007/// - A recorded send settled `ERESTARTSYS`, whose delivery runs a handler
4008///   without `SA_RESTART`: the send would fail with `EINTR`, which the network
4009///   record does not model (`Detcore::network_send_wait`). Refused; with
4010///   `SA_RESTART` the send is made again, as recorded and replayed.
4011pub(crate) async fn check_woken_wait_delivery<T, G>(
4012    guest: &mut G,
4013    signal: i32,
4014    delivered: bool,
4015) -> Option<String>
4016where
4017    T: RecordOrReplay,
4018    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4019{
4020    let WokenWait::Settled(mut settled) = guest.thread_state().woken_wait else {
4021        return None;
4022    };
4023    if settled.handler_seen {
4024        return None;
4025    }
4026    if crate::arch::syscall_number(&guest.regs().await) as i64 != settled.sysno as i64 {
4027        return None;
4028    }
4029    let sets = guest.signal_sets(guest.tid()).ok();
4030    let delivery = WokenDelivery::new(signal, delivered, sets);
4031    settled.handler_seen = delivery.runs_handler;
4032    guest.thread_state_mut().woken_wait = WokenWait::Settled(settled);
4033    let sa_restart = if delivery.needs_restart_flag(&settled) {
4034        caught_action_flags(guest, signal)
4035            .await
4036            .ok()
4037            .map(|flags| flags & libc::SA_RESTART as u64 != 0)
4038    } else {
4039        None
4040    };
4041    if delivery.fails_with_eintr(&settled, sa_restart) {
4042        // The backend fails the call with EINTR at this handler's frame, so the
4043        // program's next `poll` is its own and waits its whole timeout: the
4044        // record kept for a rerun is not taken (`keep_deadline_for_rerun`).
4045        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
4046        if matches!(
4047            guest.thread_state().restart_block,
4048            Some(RestartBlock {
4049                call: RestartCall::PollRerun(_),
4050                ..
4051            })
4052        ) {
4053            guest.thread_state_mut().restart_block = None;
4054        }
4055    }
4056    let refusal = delivery.refusal(&settled, sa_restart)?;
4057    tracing::error!(
4058        "[dtid {}] signal {} at the return of a woken {} settled with {}: {:?}",
4059        guest.thread_state().dettid,
4060        signal,
4061        settled.sysno,
4062        settled.errno,
4063        refusal
4064    );
4065    Some(refusal.message(settled.sysno, signal))
4066}
4067
4068/// A delivery at the return of a woken wait ([`check_woken_wait_delivery`]).
4069#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
4070struct WokenDelivery {
4071    /// The signal's bit in a signal set.
4072    bit: u64,
4073    /// The delivery runs a handler: Detcore let the backend deliver it, and
4074    /// the signal is caught now.
4075    runs_handler: bool,
4076    /// The delivery ends the process: Detcore let the backend deliver it, and
4077    /// its default action ends the process.
4078    ends_process: bool,
4079    /// The signals still pending for the thread or its process that its mask
4080    /// leaves unblocked, after this delivery's dequeue: the backend takes the
4081    /// next of them at the same return.
4082    remaining: u64,
4083    /// The signals with a handler now.
4084    caught: u64,
4085}
4086
4087/// A delivery at the return of a woken wait that the backend would settle as
4088/// Linux never does ([`check_woken_wait_delivery`]).
4089#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
4090enum WokenRefusal {
4091    /// A poll settled `EINTR`, whose return ends with no handler run.
4092    EintrWithoutHandler,
4093    /// A poll settled `ERESTARTSYS`, whose first handler has `SA_RESTART`
4094    /// while a signal pending at the settlement, with a handler, is its own
4095    /// or still pending.
4096    RestartAfterHandler,
4097    /// A recorded send, whose first handler has no `SA_RESTART`.
4098    SendEintr,
4099}
4100
4101impl WokenDelivery {
4102    /// The delivery of `signal`, which Detcore let the backend deliver if
4103    /// `delivered`, under the thread's signal sets `sets` (`None`: unread), as
4104    /// they stand after the delivery's dequeue.
4105    fn new(signal: i32, delivered: bool, sets: Option<reverie::SignalSets>) -> Self {
4106        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
4107        Self {
4108            bit,
4109            runs_handler: delivered && sets.is_some_and(|sets| sets.caught & bit != 0),
4110            ends_process: delivered
4111                && sets.is_some_and(|sets| {
4112                    crate::syscalls::threads::default_action_ends_process(
4113                        sets.ignored,
4114                        sets.caught,
4115                        signal,
4116                    )
4117                }),
4118            remaining: sets.map_or(0, |sets| {
4119                (sets.pending | sets.shared_pending) & !sets.blocked
4120            }),
4121            caught: sets.map_or(0, |sets| sets.caught),
4122        }
4123    }
4124
4125    /// Whether [`Self::refusal`] or [`Self::fails_with_eintr`] needs the
4126    /// handler's `SA_RESTART`: a handler runs at a return settled
4127    /// `ERESTARTSYS`.
4128    fn needs_restart_flag(&self, settled: &SettledWait) -> bool {
4129        self.runs_handler && (settled.send || settled.errno == Errno::ERESTARTSYS)
4130    }
4131
4132    /// Whether the backend fails a poll settled `ERESTARTSYS` with `EINTR` at
4133    /// this delivery: its handler has no `SA_RESTART` (`None`: unread, taken
4134    /// as none).
4135    fn fails_with_eintr(&self, settled: &SettledWait, sa_restart: Option<bool>) -> bool {
4136        !settled.send
4137            && settled.errno == Errno::ERESTARTSYS
4138            && self.runs_handler
4139            && sa_restart != Some(true)
4140    }
4141
4142    /// The refusal this delivery calls for, if any, as
4143    /// [`check_woken_wait_delivery`] describes, given its handler's
4144    /// `SA_RESTART` (`None`: unread, which refuses).
4145    fn refusal(&self, settled: &SettledWait, sa_restart: Option<bool>) -> Option<WokenRefusal> {
4146        if settled.send {
4147            return (self.runs_handler && sa_restart != Some(true))
4148                .then_some(WokenRefusal::SendEintr);
4149        }
4150        match settled.errno {
4151            Errno::EINTR if !self.runs_handler && !self.ends_process && self.remaining == 0 => {
4152                Some(WokenRefusal::EintrWithoutHandler)
4153            }
4154            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
4155                if self.runs_handler
4156                    && (settled.pending & self.bit != 0
4157                        || settled.pending & self.remaining & self.caught != 0)
4158                    && sa_restart != Some(false) =>
4159            {
4160                Some(WokenRefusal::RestartAfterHandler)
4161            }
4162            _ => None,
4163        }
4164    }
4165}
4166
4167impl WokenRefusal {
4168    /// The refusal as printed, for call `sysno` and signal `signal`.
4169    fn message(self, sysno: Sysno, signal: i32) -> String {
4170        match self {
4171            WokenRefusal::EintrWithoutHandler => format!(
4172                "hermit: unsupported on the KVM backend: a {sysno} that a signal woke returned \
4173                 EINTR, which only a handler gives it, but its return ended with signal {signal} \
4174                 delivered with no handler and no handler run (another thread ignored the \
4175                 signal while it was being delivered); Linux either runs a handler or, finding \
4176                 none, restarts the call, and KVM cannot restart it once EINTR is chosen; \
4177                 refusing the run rather than failing the call with no handler run \
4178                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929)"
4179            ),
4180            WokenRefusal::RestartAfterHandler => format!(
4181                "hermit: unsupported on the KVM backend: a {sysno} that a signal woke would be \
4182                 restarted after the handler of signal {signal}, which has SA_RESTART, while a \
4183                 signal with a handler was pending behind a signal with no handler when the call \
4184                 returned; Linux fails the call with EINTR whenever a handler interrupts it, and \
4185                 KVM restarts a call only through ERESTARTSYS, which SA_RESTART restarts; \
4186                 refusing the run rather than restarting the call \
4187                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929)"
4188            ),
4189            WokenRefusal::SendEintr => crate::syscalls::network_trace::send_interruption_refusal(),
4190        }
4191    }
4192}
4193
4194/// [`woken_poll_errno`]'s answer for the woken signals' `disposition`, on a
4195/// backend that does not report the signal sets: `EINTR` only for a handler
4196/// with `SA_RESTART` (`WaitSignalDisposition::Restart`), which `ERESTARTSYS`
4197/// would restart; `ERESTARTSYS` for a handler without it, a fatal default, an
4198/// ignored copy, or none (`None`).
4199fn woken_poll_errno_for(disposition: Option<WaitSignalDisposition>) -> Errno {
4200    if matches!(disposition, Some(WaitSignalDisposition::Restart)) {
4201        Errno::EINTR
4202    } else {
4203        Errno::ERESTARTSYS
4204    }
4205}
4206
4207// Private helper. `entry_interrupt_errno` is the interrupt class a
4208// caller already derived from the same entry snapshot as
4209// `maybe_timeout` (the socket dispatcher, whose snapshot a yield
4210// separates from this loop); `None` derives it here, at entry.
4211// `immediate_expiry` is a deadline already passed when the call began
4212// (a socket timeout Linux stores as zero): the first would-block
4213// attempt returns the timeout result without a signal check, as Linux
4214// fails such a call before it ever waits.
4215async fn retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper<T, G, C>(
4216    guest: &mut G,
4217    call0: C,
4218    mut rsrc: Resources,
4219    maybe_timeout: Option<(LogicalTime, Result<i64, Errno>)>,
4220    subtool: Option<&Detcore<T>>,
4221    entry_interrupt_errno: Option<Errno>,
4222    immediate_expiry: bool,
4223) -> Result<i64, Error>
4224where
4225    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
4226    T: RecordOrReplay,
4227    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4228{
4229    // Capture the same mark-dependent classification that the first retry
4230    // will publish, before conversion or a resource request can yield. An
4231    // ordinary internal pipe's routing alone does not request this capture.
4232    refresh_guest_poll_state(guest, call0.into(), &mut rsrc);
4233    let mut guest_held = GuestHeldPollProof::capture(guest, call0.into(), &mut rsrc);
4234    // The signals the wait takes from the queue (rt_sigtimedwait's set).
4235    let consumed = call0.signals_consumed_by_wait(&guest.memory());
4236    // The memory a vectored call copies when it begins (its iovec array, and
4237    // a message's header, address and control data), which every attempt
4238    // below sees as it was now, as the kernel's one copy would be
4239    // (`EntryImport`). Linux copies it before the call can wait, so a thread
4240    // that rewrites it while the call waits changes nothing the call moves.
4241    // Boxed, so the call's future stays small (`hot_path_futures_stay_small`).
4242    let entry_import = EntryImport::capture(&guest.memory(), &call0.into()).map(Box::new);
4243    let mut completed_observation = None;
4244    // The stack-allocated memory here needs to live across the loop, which means
4245    // surviving multiple syscall injections:
4246    let (mut call, mut maybe_stackguard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
4247    rsrc.poll_deadline = poll_deadline_for(guest, maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline));
4248    rsrc.poll_expires = maybe_timeout.is_some();
4249    // A restartable call parked in internal IO polling, such as a `read` of an
4250    // empty pipe, is interrupted by a signal another task sends, as a parked
4251    // pipe write is (`pipe_writev_resources`). The marker lets the scheduler
4252    // record the signal for it (`Scheduler::notify_signal_pending`) and answer
4253    // its next turn `Signaled`; the call then returns `ERESTARTSYS`, and the
4254    // kernel applies the guest's disposition when it resumes: a handler runs
4255    // and the call fails with `EINTR` or restarts under `SA_RESTART`. Without
4256    // it, the poll never saw the signal and waited forever
4257    // (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187>).
4258    if rsrc.signal_interrupt_errno().is_none()
4259        && rsrc.resources.len() == 1
4260        && rsrc.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
4261        && call.signal_interrupt_errno() == Errno::ERESTARTSYS
4262    {
4263        rsrc.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
4264        // Where guest thread IDs are not host tasks (KVM) the scheduler keeps
4265        // every signal: the call has made no progress when it returns
4266        // ERESTARTSYS, and the backend restarts it unless a signal it would
4267        // deliver is pending, so a blocked or ignored signal leaves it waiting.
4268        rsrc.signal_state_task = guest_signal_state_task(guest);
4269    }
4270    // D50 reader 2 under the in-guest delivery gate (A5 step 3c.1c): no
4271    // private kernel mask; once an attempt would block, the design's
4272    // deliverable set under the thread's published mask decides
4273    // (`gated_wait_ends`), at each turn, the first included.
4274    let gated = guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery;
4275    let checks_at_turn = !gated
4276        && rsrc.signal_interrupt_errno() == Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
4277        && decides_interruption_at_turn(guest, rsrc.signal_state_task);
4278    // A part of a call that transferred bytes in an earlier part (a readv
4279    // reading on into a later iovec, `Detcore::readv_inotify`): Linux's
4280    // per-iovec loop returns those bytes once the next iovec's read ends
4281    // early, so any wake that would deliver a signal ends this part, a named
4282    // wake as well as a copy still pending (`TurnSignals::ends`), while a
4283    // blocked or ignored signal leaves it waiting. Where the turn does not
4284    // decide (a backend whose guest threads are not host tasks), the woken
4285    // part decides from the guest's own mask and dispositions, as a parked
4286    // pipe write does (`execute_blocking_pipe_write`): the restart errno would
4287    // end the call with a short count, which the backend's restart of a call
4288    // with no progress cannot undo.
4289    let progress = guest
4290        .thread_state()
4291        .call_parts
4292        .as_ref()
4293        .is_some_and(|parts| parts.progress);
4294    let decides_itself = !checks_at_turn && !gated;
4295    let decides_progress_itself = progress && decides_itself;
4296    // The inotify instance a read began on, whose own O_NONBLOCK decides the
4297    // errno a signal wake returns (`interrupted_wait_errno`).
4298    let began_on = inotify_description_of(guest, call0);
4299    // Where the turn decides, each probe owns the guest's mask while it blocks
4300    // every blockable signal (`KernelSignalWait::block_in_place`). The mask
4301    // goes back before a retry yields, so target selection still sees which
4302    // signals the guest admits. Even an empty pending
4303    // snapshot needs that protection: a signal arriving afterward could
4304    // stop the probe, move into the backend's held slot, and disappear from
4305    // every later pending read while inject_with_retry kept polling. Two
4306    // such signals could also replace one another in the single held slot
4307    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, stage 2).
4308    // The errno a signal that ends this call returns, read at its entry
4309    // (`interrupt_errno_at_entry`), or the class the caller derived from
4310    // the same snapshot as its deadline, which no later read replaces.
4311    let interrupt_errno = entry_interrupt_errno
4312        .unwrap_or_else(|| interrupt_errno_at_entry(guest, &call0, call0.signal_interrupt_errno()));
4313    let mut turn_wait =
4314        checks_at_turn.then(|| KernelSignalWait::new(guest, 0, false, interrupt_errno));
4315    let mut published = PublishedWaitMask::default();
4316    // The pipe read descriptions an attempt of this send passed, whose
4317    // SIGALRM status it untracked (`Detcore::pipe_reads_an_attempt_passes`).
4318    let mut untracked_pipe_reads = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
4319
4320    let result: Result<i64, Error> = loop {
4321        // A sibling can replace a descriptor while the previous request
4322        // waits. Classify the next attempt against the current table. The
4323        // scheduler's progress/freshness checks prevent the older queued
4324        // request from justifying an idle jump before this new probe.
4325        refresh_guest_poll_state(guest, call.into(), &mut rsrc);
4326        // The refresh above recomputes the classification from the current
4327        // table; a guest-held proof this call already lost stays lost.
4328        guest_held.revalidate(guest, &mut rsrc);
4329        let resumed = match call.into() {
4330            Syscall::Read(read) if maybe_timeout.is_none() && maybe_stackguard.is_none() => {
4331                crate::tool_global::polled_read_request(guest, read, rsrc.clone()).await
4332            }
4333            _ => resource_request(guest, rsrc.clone()).await,
4334        };
4335        guest_held.revalidate(guest, &mut rsrc);
4336        // The turn's signals, read before its first injection
4337        // (`read_turn_signals`): the timerfd publication and the real-time
4338        // action below may inject, and a pending copy could stop that
4339        // injection and move into the backend's held slot. Every turn reads,
4340        // the first included, since a signal sent before the poll filed its
4341        // first request was admitted by no drain
4342        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273). A backend's own
4343        // observation of a signal (`Signaled(None)`) is trusted as it is: that
4344        // signal has already left the kernel's queue.
4345        // Once the call blocks, the turn decides under the guest's own mask,
4346        // which the call owns during each probe, never under the full one installed (Codex
4347        // review of the R2b-2 design rev3, P2-1).
4348        let turn = if checks_at_turn && !matches!(resumed, ResumeStatus::Signaled(None)) {
4349            match turn_signals_with_block(
4350                guest,
4351                &mut turn_wait,
4352                ProbeMaskPolicy::PrivateProbe,
4353                committed_signals(&resumed),
4354                rsrc.private_sigchld_decides,
4355                &mut published,
4356            )
4357            .await
4358            {
4359                Ok(turn) => Some(turn),
4360                Err(error) => break Err(error),
4361            }
4362        } else {
4363            None
4364        };
4365        // A virtual timerfd this probe may observe is readable on the host
4366        // exactly when its virtual deadline has passed by this turn
4367        // (`crate::syscalls::timerfd`); its next deadline restores this
4368        // poller if it backs off.
4369        // Publishing may take the scratch stack, which the nonblocking form
4370        // holds; release it first and convert again after.
4371        let reconvert =
4372            maybe_stackguard.is_some() && crate::syscalls::timerfd::may_publish(guest, call.into());
4373        if reconvert {
4374            maybe_stackguard = None;
4375        }
4376        rsrc.poll_deadline = crate::syscalls::timerfd::publish_before_probe(
4377            guest,
4378            call.into(),
4379            maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline),
4380        )
4381        .await;
4382        if reconvert {
4383            (call, maybe_stackguard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
4384        }
4385        // A signal ends the call only if it would still block, as Linux
4386        // checks for a pending signal only when the call must wait: a byte
4387        // written, or the last writer closed, before the signal is read
4388        // first. The probe below goes through the record/replay path like
4389        // every attempt (Codex review of
4390        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4198).
4391        // A call that has transferred nothing ends only for a copy still
4392        // pending; a part after progress ends for a named wake too
4393        // (`TurnSignals::ends`, `progress` above).
4394        // A read that began on an inotify instance that is nonblocking for
4395        // the guest by now ends at a signal wake with EAGAIN
4396        // (`interrupted_wait_errno`), which, unlike the restart errno, no
4397        // backend's restart of a call whose signal it would not deliver
4398        // undoes. Where the turn does not decide, it decides as a part after
4399        // progress does: a blocked or ignored signal leaves it waiting, as
4400        // it leaves Linux's reader asleep.
4401        let mode_wake_decides_itself = decides_itself
4402            && began_on
4403                .as_ref()
4404                .is_some_and(crate::fd::DetFd::is_nonblocking);
4405        let signaled = match turn {
4406            Some(turn) => turn.ends(progress),
4407            None if gated => false,
4408            // Continuation parts are scalar reads, whose nonblocking form
4409            // holds no scratch stack (`network_comm_syscall`), as does every
4410            // read and readv.
4411            None if (decides_progress_itself || mode_wake_decides_itself)
4412                && maybe_stackguard.is_none()
4413                && matches!(resumed, ResumeStatus::Signaled(_)) =>
4414            {
4415                match progress_signal_interrupts(guest, resumed.clone()).await {
4416                    Ok(interrupts) => interrupts,
4417                    Err(error) => break Err(error),
4418                }
4419            }
4420            None => matches!(resumed, ResumeStatus::Signaled(_)),
4421        };
4422        // A pending real-time timer expiration in the set this wait takes
4423        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089).
4424        let pending = pending_real_time_among(guest, consumed).await;
4425        act_on_pending_real_time(guest, pending, consumed, 0).await;
4426        // The call's memory as it began, for this attempt and for the reads
4427        // of it below, and what another thread wrote over it meanwhile, which
4428        // goes back once the attempt is made.
4429        let mut displaced = entry_import
4430            .as_ref()
4431            .map(|entry| entry.reinstate(&mut guest.memory()));
4432        // Classify the input the kernel will actually import: sendmsg keeps
4433        // its entry-time header/control, while sendmmsg reads each attempt.
4434        // The FD table may have changed during either call's retry wait.
4435        if Detcore::<T>::passes_descriptors_out_now(guest, call.into()) {
4436            // Never yield with captured bytes installed over a sibling's
4437            // writes. Restore those writes before reporting the export,
4438            // then capture the current displaced view after the new grant.
4439            if let Err(error) = put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced.take(), false)
4440            {
4441                break Err(error);
4442            }
4443            let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
4444            let _ = resource_request(guest, Resources::new(dettid)).await;
4445            displaced = entry_import
4446                .as_ref()
4447                .map(|entry| entry.reinstate(&mut guest.memory()));
4448        }
4449        // Each pipe read description this attempt passes over SCM_RIGHTS, as
4450        // Linux will import its messages and look up their descriptors,
4451        // loses its SIGALRM status first: the handler read them at entry,
4452        // and an attempt after a wait may pass others
4453        // (`Detcore::pipe_reads_an_attempt_passes`). The captured bytes go
4454        // back around the requests, as above, and the attempt reads again
4455        // after them, until it passes no description it has not untracked.
4456        let mut untracking = Ok(());
4457        loop {
4458            let ids = Detcore::<T>::pipe_reads_an_attempt_passes(
4459                guest,
4460                call.into(),
4461                &untracked_pipe_reads,
4462            );
4463            if ids.is_empty() {
4464                break;
4465            }
4466            untracking = put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced.take(), false);
4467            if untracking.is_err() {
4468                break;
4469            }
4470            Detcore::<T>::untrack_pipe_statuses(guest, &ids).await;
4471            untracked_pipe_reads.extend(ids);
4472            displaced = entry_import
4473                .as_ref()
4474                .map(|entry| entry.reinstate(&mut guest.memory()));
4475        }
4476        if let Err(error) = untracking {
4477            break Err(error);
4478        }
4479        // A receive whose descriptors Detcore names reads its geometry again
4480        // right before each attempt: a sibling may have changed it while an
4481        // earlier attempt waited (`ThreadState::receive_geometry`).
4482        if guest.thread_state().receive_geometry.is_some() {
4483            let geometry =
4484                crate::syscalls::scm_rights::ReceiveGeometry::before(&guest.memory(), &call.into());
4485            guest.thread_state_mut().receive_geometry = Some(geometry);
4486        }
4487        // A send whose `SCM_RIGHTS` descriptors Detcore inspected reads them
4488        // again right before each attempt: a sibling may have rewritten its
4489        // messages, or replaced what their descriptor numbers name, since the
4490        // inspection or while an earlier attempt waited
4491        // (`ThreadState::send_inspection`). An attempt that would pass other
4492        // placeholders than those whose copies Detcore counted is refused by
4493        // name. Boxed: only a send that may pass a placeholder carries it.
4494        if let Some(inspection) = guest.thread_state().send_inspection.clone()
4495            && let Some(reason) =
4496                Box::pin(Detcore::<T>::changed_placeholder_send(guest, &inspection)).await
4497        {
4498            tracing::error!("Detcore refuses {}: {reason}", inspection.sysno);
4499            if let Err(error) = put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced, false) {
4500                break Err(error);
4501            }
4502            let panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = guest.config().panic_on_unsupported_syscalls;
4503            break refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
4504                guest,
4505                panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
4506                inspection.sysno,
4507                Errno::EOPNOTSUPP,
4508                Some(&reason),
4509            )
4510            .await;
4511        }
4512        // A sibling may have replaced the destination descriptor while this
4513        // attempt waited for its turn. The per-attempt check above
4514        // (`passes_descriptors_out_now`) rechecks the channel immediately
4515        // before each send, independently of the mutable control data.
4516
4517        // An inotify read counts its instance's queue right before each
4518        // attempt, which runs next in this turn, so that the count it keeps
4519        // is the one before the attempt that completes
4520        // (`ThreadState::inotify_queue`). Boxed: only such a read counts.
4521        if guest.thread_state().inotify_queue.is_some() {
4522            Box::pin(crate::syscalls::inotify::count_before_attempt(
4523                guest,
4524                call.into(),
4525            ))
4526            .await;
4527        }
4528        // Read actual metadata after reinstatement and all earlier awaits.
4529        // Observation adds no reads or allocation when buffer logging is off.
4530        let attempt_observation =
4531            if guest.config().detlog_io_buffers && crate::io_buffers::observed() {
4532                EntryImport::capture_observation(&guest.memory(), &call.into())
4533            } else {
4534                None
4535            };
4536        // Route through the record/replay subtool for internal pipes so each poll (an
4537        // EAGAIN, or the final data-bearing read) becomes one recorded event that replay
4538        // reproduces deterministically; otherwise execute the syscall directly.
4539        let res = match (subtool, call.into()) {
4540            // A flock waiting in Detcore's flock model asks the model, not
4541            // the kernel (`Detcore::flock_wait_attempt`).
4542            (Some(detcore), Syscall::Flock(flock)) => {
4543                let (answer, woke) = detcore.flock_wait_attempt(guest, flock).await;
4544                // A retry that blocked again but woke other requests changed
4545                // what their own retries find: progress, for the scheduler's
4546                // check that only idle pollers remain, as a partial pipe
4547                // write is (`Resources::previous_attempt_made_progress`).
4548                rsrc.previous_attempt_made_progress = woke;
4549                answer
4550            }
4551            (Some(detcore), _) => {
4552                detcore
4553                    .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
4554                    .await
4555            }
4556            (None, _) => {
4557                // The preceding placeholder inspection can await. Publish
4558                // persistent/reference effects at the actual issue cut,
4559                // not from the descriptor or ancillary view before it.
4560                match crate::reserved_input::before_native_call(guest, call.into()) {
4561                    Ok(()) => guest.inject_with_retry(call).await.map_err(Error::from),
4562                    // Keep the normal EntryImport restoration below even
4563                    // when native issue is refused before it begins.
4564                    Err(error) => Err(error),
4565                }
4566            }
4567        };
4568        if let Err(error) = put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced, res.is_ok()) {
4569            break Err(error);
4570        }
4571        // Under record and replay the attempt is a plain injection, which the
4572        // signal that woke this call, still pending, stops before it runs
4573        // (ERESTARTSYS, not run): the call then returns that restart errno,
4574        // as on main, though a byte, end of file or room may have been ready.
4575        // Making the attempt again would replace the held signal with any
4576        // other pending one (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1012),
4577        // and record and replay could not agree on when it is safe.
4578        let syscall_result = match res {
4579            Ok(value) => Ok(value),
4580            Err(Error::Errno(error)) => Err(error),
4581            Err(error) => break Err(error),
4582        };
4583        // Before the signal check: Linux looks for a pending signal only when
4584        // the call must wait, and a receive on a socket shut down for reading
4585        // does not. Record and replay poll a receive here only on a
4586        // socketpair, through `subtool`; finishing it there would add
4587        // recorded calls, a new recording format, so they keep polling.
4588        if subtool.is_none()
4589            && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result)
4590            && let Some(result) = finish_after_read_shutdown(guest, call).await
4591        {
4592            break result;
4593        }
4594        // A deadline already passed when the call began ends it here,
4595        // after its first would-block attempt and before any signal
4596        // check: Linux with a zero timeo fails at once without looking
4597        // at signals (`sock_alloc_send_pskb`'s `if (!timeo) goto
4598        // failure` before its signal check, net/core/sock.c:2951-2956;
4599        // a datagram receive loops only `while (timeo && ...)`,
4600        // net/unix/af_unix.c:2611-2615, both at v6.17), so a pending
4601        // signal neither preempts the expiry result nor is consumed
4602        // by it. A finite deadline keeps the order below.
4603        if immediate_expiry
4604            && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result)
4605            && let Some((_, timeout_result)) = maybe_timeout
4606        {
4607            break timeout_result.map_err(|e| e.into());
4608        }
4609        // A part after progress that would wait while a signal an earlier
4610        // part completed with is still pending ends, as Linux's next `->read`
4611        // does when it finds `signal_pending()` before it sleeps
4612        // (`CallParts::carried`).
4613        let carried_ends =
4614            if progress && !signaled && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
4615                match carried_signal_ends(
4616                    guest,
4617                    decides_progress_itself && maybe_stackguard.is_none(),
4618                    gated,
4619                )
4620                .await
4621                {
4622                    Ok(ends) => ends,
4623                    Err(error) => break Err(error),
4624                }
4625            } else {
4626                false
4627            };
4628        let signaled = signaled || carried_ends;
4629        if signaled && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
4630            let errno = interrupted_wait_errno(began_on.as_ref(), interrupt_errno);
4631            tracing::trace!(
4632                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: interrupted by signal while {} would block: {:?}",
4633                call.display(&guest.memory()),
4634                errno
4635            );
4636            if restarts_without_a_handler_through_erestartsys(guest, &call) {
4637                // The probe's scratch is not used again: the call ends here.
4638                drop(maybe_stackguard.take());
4639                break match woken_poll_errno(guest, resumed.clone()).await {
4640                    Ok(errno) => Err(errno.into()),
4641                    Err(error) => Err(error),
4642                };
4643            }
4644            break Err(errno.into());
4645        }
4646        // Under the gate the wait ends here, where it would block (as
4647        // Linux checks for a pending signal only then), for a signal sent
4648        // before it parked or one whose commit woke it.
4649        if gated && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
4650            match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
4651                Ok(true) => {
4652                    break Err(interrupted_wait_errno(began_on.as_ref(), interrupt_errno).into());
4653                }
4654                Ok(false) => {}
4655                Err(error) => break Err(error),
4656            }
4657        }
4658        if call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
4659            if let Some(wait) = turn_wait.as_mut() {
4660                // Both observing time and tracing a retry can yield to the
4661                // scheduler. Its ptrace signal-target selection must see the
4662                // guest's mask, not this probe's private all-blocked mask.
4663                // Only the no-execution setter is safe here: an injected
4664                // restoration could hide a pending signal in the backend's
4665                // held slot before another probe. A refusal ends this call
4666                // before any such yield; final cleanup may still restore it.
4667                if let Err(error) = wait.release_probe_mask_in_place(guest).await {
4668                    break Err(error);
4669                }
4670                publish_wait_mask(guest, None, &mut published).await;
4671            }
4672            rsrc.poll_attempt += 1;
4673            if let Some((timeout, timeout_result)) = maybe_timeout {
4674                let new_time = thread_observe_time(guest).await;
4675                if new_time >= timeout {
4676                    tracing::trace!(
4677                        "Timing out syscall after #{} retries: {}",
4678                        rsrc.poll_attempt - 1,
4679                        call.display(&guest.memory())
4680                    );
4681                    break timeout_result.map_err(|e| e.into());
4682                } else {
4683                    tracing::trace!(
4684                        "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}, {} from timeout: {}",
4685                        rsrc.poll_attempt,
4686                        syscall_result,
4687                        timeout - new_time,
4688                        call.display(&guest.memory())
4689                    );
4690                    record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
4691                }
4692            } else {
4693                tracing::trace!(
4694                    "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}: {}",
4695                    rsrc.poll_attempt,
4696                    syscall_result,
4697                    call.display(&guest.memory())
4698                );
4699                record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
4700            }
4701        } else {
4702            // A part of a call run in parts completes: a signal this turn
4703            // found, which would end a later part, stays pending for the
4704            // parts after it, as Linux's does (`CallParts::carried`).
4705            if let Some(carried) = carried_signal(turn, &resumed, gated)
4706                && let Some(parts) = guest.thread_state_mut().call_parts.as_mut()
4707            {
4708                parts.carried = Some(carried);
4709            }
4710            let normalized =
4711                call.normalize_nonblocking_result(syscall_result, rsrc.poll_attempt > 0);
4712            if normalized != syscall_result {
4713                guest.thread_state_mut().nonblocking_result_normalized = true;
4714            }
4715            let res = normalized.map_err(|e| e.into());
4716            if res.is_ok() {
4717                completed_observation = attempt_observation;
4718            }
4719            tracing::trace!(
4720                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: syscall completed after {} retries: {} = {:?}",
4721                rsrc.poll_attempt,
4722                call.display(&guest.memory()),
4723                res
4724            );
4725            break res;
4726        }
4727    };
4728    let entry_import =
4729        EntryImport::with_observation(entry_import, call0.into(), completed_observation);
4730    keep_entry_view(guest, entry_import);
4731
4732    // The single exit: the guest's mask goes back before the result is
4733    // returned. A mask `block_in_place` installed goes back through
4734    // `Guest::set_blocked_signals`, with no scratch memory, and only a
4735    // refusal falls back to an injected restoration (`KernelSignalWait::restore`).
4736    // A mask that cannot be put back ends the run before the guest resumes.
4737    match turn_wait {
4738        Some(mut wait) if wait.effective_mask().is_some() => {
4739            let restored = wait.restore(guest, None).await;
4740            publish_wait_mask(guest, None, &mut published).await;
4741            match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
4742                Ok(result) => refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, call0.number(), result).await,
4743                Err(error) => Err(error),
4744            }
4745        }
4746        _ => result,
4747    }
4748}
4749
4750/// Ends a polled blocking receive as Linux does once its socket's read side is
4751/// shut down.
4752///
4753/// Detcore polls a blocking receive on a physically nonblocking socket with
4754/// nonblocking attempts (`retry_nonblocking_syscall`). On a datagram socket
4755/// whose read side is shut down, Linux's blocking receive does not wait: with
4756/// nothing queued it returns 0 at once (`__skb_wait_for_more_packets`). The
4757/// nonblocking attempt fails with `EAGAIN` instead, every time, so the polled
4758/// receive never ended, and a thread that shut a reader's socket down and then
4759/// joined the reader waited forever.
4760///
4761/// After an attempt that would block on a socket whose read side a guest shut
4762/// down (`DetFd::read_shutdown_requested`), this asks the kernel whether it is
4763/// still shut (`read_side_shut_down`): a TCP disconnect opens it again. If it
4764/// is, the blocking call cannot wait, so this runs the guest's call once with
4765/// `O_NONBLOCK` cleared, then sets the flag back, and returns what Linux
4766/// returned, with the address lengths it wrote. `None` for any other call or
4767/// socket, or while the read side is open: the attempt's `EAGAIN` stands and
4768/// the poll goes on, with no extra call.
4769async fn finish_after_read_shutdown<T, G, C>(guest: &mut G, call: C) -> Option<Result<i64, Error>>
4770where
4771    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
4772    T: RecordOrReplay,
4773    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4774{
4775    let fd = get_fd(call.into()).filter(|_| call.ends_at_read_shutdown())?;
4776    let shut_down_by_guest = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
4777        matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Socket) && detfd.read_shutdown_requested()
4778    });
4779    if shut_down_by_guest != Ok(true) || !read_side_shut_down(guest, fd).await {
4780        return None;
4781    }
4782    let fcntl = |cmd| syscalls::Fcntl::new().with_fd(fd).with_cmd(cmd);
4783    // Nothing has changed if either of these fails: the attempt's EAGAIN stands.
4784    let flags = match guest.inject_with_retry(fcntl(FcntlCmd::F_GETFL)).await {
4785        Ok(flags) => flags as libc::c_int,
4786        Err(errno) => {
4787            tracing::warn!("socket {fd}: F_GETFL before a read-shutdown receive failed: {errno}");
4788            return None;
4789        }
4790    };
4791    let blocking = fcntl(FcntlCmd::F_SETFL(flags & !libc::O_NONBLOCK));
4792    if let Err(errno) = guest.inject_with_retry(blocking).await {
4793        tracing::warn!(
4794            "socket {fd}: clearing O_NONBLOCK for a read-shutdown receive failed: {errno}"
4795        );
4796        return None;
4797    }
4798    let result = guest.inject_with_retry(call).await.map_err(Error::from);
4799    // Every later attempt on this description assumes it is nonblocking; one
4800    // that blocked would hold the turn forever.
4801    if let Err(errno) = guest
4802        .inject_with_retry(fcntl(FcntlCmd::F_SETFL(flags)))
4803        .await
4804    {
4805        panic!("socket {fd}: restoring O_NONBLOCK after a read-shutdown receive failed: {errno}");
4806    }
4807    tracing::trace!(
4808        "retry_nonblocking_syscall: {} ran blocking after a read shutdown: {:?}",
4809        call.display(&guest.memory()),
4810        result
4811    );
4812    Some(result)
4813}
4814
4815/// Whether the kernel reports `fd`'s read side shut down: `POLLRDHUP` from a
4816/// `poll` with a zero timeout, which Linux sets exactly when the socket's
4817/// `RCV_SHUTDOWN` is set (`datagram_poll`, `unix_dgram_poll`, `tcp_poll`).
4818async fn read_side_shut_down<T, G>(guest: &mut G, fd: i32) -> bool
4819where
4820    T: RecordOrReplay,
4821    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4822{
4823    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
4824    let pollfd: AddrMut<libc::pollfd> = stack.reserve();
4825    // aarch64 has ppoll alone: its zero timeout is a zero timespec on
4826    // the same stack (x86_64 keeps the poll probe below).
4827    #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
4828    let timeout = stack.push(Timespec {
4829        tv_sec: 0,
4830        tv_nsec: 0,
4831    });
4832    let Ok(_guard) = stack.commit() else {
4833        return false;
4834    };
4835    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
4836    let probe = syscalls::Poll::new()
4837        .with_fds(Some(pollfd.cast()))
4838        .with_nfds(1)
4839        .with_timeout(0);
4840    #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
4841    let probe = syscalls::Ppoll::new()
4842        .with_fds(Some(pollfd.cast()))
4843        .with_nfds(1)
4844        // SAFETY: `timeout` points to exclusively owned stack storage
4845        // kept alive by `_guard` for the injection below.
4846        .with_timeout(Some(unsafe { timeout.into_mut() }));
4847    let request = libc::pollfd {
4848        fd,
4849        events: libc::POLLRDHUP,
4850        revents: 0,
4851    };
4852    guest.memory().write_value(pollfd, &request).is_ok()
4853        && guest.inject_with_retry(probe).await == Ok(1)
4854        && guest
4855            .memory()
4856            .read_value(pollfd)
4857            .is_ok_and(|polled| polled.revents & libc::POLLRDHUP != 0)
4858}
4859
4860/// Put back what another thread wrote over a call's memory as it began
4861/// (`EntryImport::put_back`), after an attempt that `completed` or not. The
4862/// bytes were written once already, and no guest thread has run since, so a
4863/// failure is Detcore's own and ends the call rather than leave the guest's
4864/// memory as the call began.
4865fn put_back_entry_import<T, G>(
4866    guest: &mut G,
4867    entry_import: &Option<Box<EntryImport>>,
4868    displaced: Option<Displaced>,
4869    completed: bool,
4870) -> Result<(), Error>
4871where
4872    T: RecordOrReplay,
4873    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4874{
4875    let (Some(entry), Some(displaced)) = (entry_import, displaced) else {
4876        return Ok(());
4877    };
4878    if displaced.is_empty() {
4879        return Ok(());
4880    }
4881    entry
4882        .put_back(&mut guest.memory(), displaced, completed)
4883        .map_err(|errno| {
4884            tracing::error!(
4885                "Detcore could not put back the guest's rewrite of a vectored call's memory: {errno}"
4886            );
4887            Error::from(errno)
4888        })
4889}
4890
4891/// Keep a call's memory as it began (`EntryImport`) for the observers that
4892/// read the call's arguments after it returns (`ThreadState::entry_import`),
4893/// when another thread has rewritten it since; otherwise those arguments are
4894/// still the ones the call moved its bytes through.
4895fn keep_entry_view<T, G>(guest: &mut G, entry_import: Option<Box<EntryImport>>)
4896where
4897    T: RecordOrReplay,
4898    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4899{
4900    let view =
4901        entry_import.filter(|entry| entry.has_observation() || entry.differs(&guest.memory()));
4902    guest.thread_state_mut().entry_import = view;
4903}
4904
4905/// Retry a blocking wait on a backend that decides signal interruption from the
4906/// kernel's signal state (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`).
4907///
4908/// A wait ends early only for a signal that would end it natively: one the guest
4909/// does not block and that is caught, or whose default action terminates or stops
4910/// the process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Blocked,
4911/// ignored, and default-ignored signals do not end it, and neither does a default
4912/// job-control stop when Linux's restart of the call keeps its deadline
4913/// (`NonblockableSyscall::restart_keeps_deadline`). Such a signal that stops one
4914/// of the wait's injections is absorbed, and the wait runs on. A stop that
4915/// `KernelSignalWait::inject_absorbing` cannot absorb ends the wait with a
4916/// transparent restart when the backend holds nothing whose loss matters, and
4917/// otherwise with a [`HeldSignalRefusal`], which `refuse_held_signal_loss`
4918/// turns into the unsupported-operation refusal once the guest's mask is back.
4919///
4920/// The first probe runs under the guest's own mask, and before the first check
4921/// for a pending signal (`KernelSignalWait::inject_first_probe`): Linux reports a
4922/// descriptor that is ready when the call begins, a queued event, and an
4923/// argument error before it looks at pending signals, so the probe's result
4924/// stands whenever the signal arrived. If it would block, every blockable signal
4925/// is blocked for the rest of the wait, so later probes cannot be stopped by one
4926/// and every signal that arrives stays pending in the kernel, where `/proc`
4927/// reports it. Each turn classifies the pending set against the guest's mask and
4928/// dispositions, and an interrupting signal ends the wait with the call's restart
4929/// errno (see `KernelSignalWait::interrupted_with_state`). The guest's mask is
4930/// restored before returning, so the signal is delivered as the call returns.
4931/// The signals a scheduler resume names (`ResumeStatus::Signaled`): signals the
4932/// scheduler committed to the thread at that point.
4933fn committed_signals(resumed: &ResumeStatus) -> KernelSigset {
4934    match resumed {
4935        ResumeStatus::Signaled(Some(signals)) => signals.iter().fold(0, |set, signal| {
4936            set | kernel_sigset_bit(signal.0 as libc::c_int)
4937        }),
4938        _ => 0,
4939    }
4940}
4941
4942/// What a restartable internal IO poll or a parked pipe write finds at a turn,
4943/// read from the thread's own state before the turn's first injection, while it
4944/// is still stopped at its request: every signal sent since is still in the
4945/// kernel's pending set, and none is yet in the backend's held slot. A copy
4946/// the turn's own injections later absorb is counted here
4947/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273>, R2b-1 rules 2-4).
4948#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
4949struct TurnSignals {
4950    /// The signals the turn's answer names (`committed_signals`) that the
4951    /// call's mask leaves unblocked: a kept send's wake, which Linux's
4952    /// `TIF_SIGPENDING` keeps in force until the call returns, whatever a later
4953    /// flush does. For `writev`, which the drain never filters, a real-time
4954    /// signal, outside the record of copies discarded at send, counts only if
4955    /// its disposition delivers it now (`NamedRealTime::ByDisposition`); for
4956    /// the generic poll and the scalar writer the drain's own disposition test
4957    /// has already decided it, at the wake (R2b-1 rules 1 and 2).
4958    named: KernelSigset,
4959    /// The kept copies pending now that would end the call: unblocked under the
4960    /// call's mask, caught or acting by default, not held (`SIGCHLD` and the
4961    /// host-timed signals, except one the scheduler committed:
4962    /// `futex_wait_held_after_wake`), and not discarded at send
4963    /// (`threads::without_discarded`).
4964    pending: KernelSigset,
4965}
4966
4967impl TurnSignals {
4968    /// Whether a call that would wait now ends. After progress (`progress`),
4969    /// Linux returns the bytes transferred on any wake, so a named wake or a
4970    /// pending copy ends the call. With none, Linux returns `-ERESTARTSYS`,
4971    /// which delivers a pending copy or restarts invisibly, so only a pending
4972    /// copy ends it; otherwise the call keeps polling, which the guest cannot
4973    /// tell from that restart (R2b-1 rule 3).
4974    fn ends(&self, progress: bool) -> bool {
4975        self.pending != 0 || (progress && self.named != 0)
4976    }
4977}
4978
4979/// [`TurnSignals`] for a call whose mask is `mask` (the kernel's, by default:
4980/// the generic poll and the scalar writer install none) and to which the
4981/// scheduler committed `committed` at this wake (`committed_signals`; none
4982/// before a turnless first attempt). A thread that is gone ends the call with
4983/// `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which nothing observes, and a live one whose state cannot
4984/// be read ends the run (`read_wait_signal_state`).
4985async fn read_turn_signals<T, G>(
4986    guest: &mut G,
4987    mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
4988    committed: KernelSigset,
4989    real_time: NamedRealTime,
4990) -> Result<TurnSignals, Error>
4991where
4992    T: RecordOrReplay,
4993    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4994{
4995    Ok(
4996        read_turn_signals_and_state(guest, mask, committed, real_time)
4997            .await?
4998            .0,
4999    )
5000}
5001
5002/// `read_turn_signals`, also returning the thread's signal state that the
5003/// turn read.
5004async fn read_turn_signals_and_state<T, G>(
5005    guest: &mut G,
5006    mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
5007    committed: KernelSigset,
5008    real_time: NamedRealTime,
5009) -> Result<(TurnSignals, KernelSignalState), Error>
5010where
5011    T: RecordOrReplay,
5012    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5013{
5014    let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
5015    let mask = mask.unwrap_or(state.blocked);
5016    let host_timed = host_timed_signals(guest).await;
5017    Ok((
5018        turn_signals_from_state(guest, &state, mask, host_timed, committed, real_time, 0).await,
5019        state,
5020    ))
5021}
5022
5023/// [`TurnSignals`] from the thread's state `state` read in this turn, with the
5024/// record of copies Linux discarded at send applied
5025/// (`threads::without_discarded`); `private` as for
5026/// `turn_signals_before_discard`.
5027async fn turn_signals_from_state<T, G>(
5028    guest: &mut G,
5029    state: &KernelSignalState,
5030    mask: KernelSigset,
5031    host_timed: KernelSigset,
5032    committed: KernelSigset,
5033    real_time: NamedRealTime,
5034    private: KernelSigset,
5035) -> TurnSignals
5036where
5037    T: RecordOrReplay,
5038    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5039{
5040    let before =
5041        turn_signals_before_discard(state, mask, host_timed, committed, real_time, private);
5042    let pending =
5043        crate::syscalls::threads::without_discarded(guest, state, before.pending, committed).await;
5044    TurnSignals { pending, ..before }
5045}
5046
5047/// Which private mask a turn may install. The scalar writer retains its
5048/// existing pending-only policy after its first guest attempt. A generic
5049/// read probe needs protection even when its preceding snapshot was empty.
5050#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
5051enum ProbeMaskPolicy {
5052    Guest,
5053    PendingSignals,
5054    PrivateProbe,
5055}
5056
5057/// A restartable poll's turn on a pipe or a socket that decides at its turn:
5058/// read the thread's signal state before the turn's first injection, block
5059/// every blockable signal in place according to `mask_policy`
5060/// (`KernelSignalWait::block_in_place`, stage 2 of
5061/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273), then decide the turn's
5062/// signals under the guest's own mask, which the call owns once it blocks.
5063/// `PrivateProbe` also protects an empty snapshot: a signal arriving after it
5064/// stays in the kernel's queue for the next turn, rather than being held by
5065/// a private injection and hidden from subsequent pending-state reads.
5066///
5067/// A `SIGCHLD` a guest sent the thread, which the schedule recorded in its
5068/// private queue, ends the call where `private_decides`
5069/// (`Resources::private_sigchld_decides`), as on Linux (stage 3): it is
5070/// admitted only while the block holds (`saved_mask`), so no injection of
5071/// this turn can take it into the backend's single held slot, and only if
5072/// the read found it in the thread's own queue, from which only this stopped
5073/// thread can take it. Nothing runs between the read and the block. The
5074/// host-timed signals and the record come in one round trip, before any
5075/// injection (`host_timed_and_private_sigchld`).
5076async fn turn_signals_with_block<T, G>(
5077    guest: &mut G,
5078    wait: &mut Option<KernelSignalWait>,
5079    mask_policy: ProbeMaskPolicy,
5080    committed: KernelSigset,
5081    private_decides: bool,
5082    published: &mut PublishedWaitMask,
5083) -> Result<TurnSignals, Error>
5084where
5085    T: RecordOrReplay,
5086    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5087{
5088    let mask = wait.as_ref().and_then(KernelSignalWait::effective_mask);
5089    let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
5090    let (host_timed, recorded) = crate::tool_global::host_timed_and_private_sigchld(guest).await;
5091    let mut private = 0;
5092    if let Some(wait) = wait.as_mut() {
5093        // Block before the publication and the probe, so neither can be
5094        // stopped by a blockable signal, and every pending one stays in the
5095        // kernel's queue until the guest resumes.
5096        let needs_protection = match mask_policy {
5097            ProbeMaskPolicy::Guest => false,
5098            ProbeMaskPolicy::PendingSignals => {
5099                state.pending & !state.blocked & blocked_signal_mask() != 0
5100            }
5101            ProbeMaskPolicy::PrivateProbe => true,
5102        };
5103        if needs_protection && wait.needs_block() && wait.block_in_place(guest, host_timed).await? {
5104            publish_wait_mask(guest, wait.effective_mask(), published).await;
5105        }
5106        if private_decides
5107            && wait.saved_mask.is_some()
5108            && state.thread_pending & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) != 0
5109        {
5110            private = recorded;
5111        }
5112    }
5113    let mask = mask.unwrap_or(state.blocked);
5114    Ok(turn_signals_from_state(
5115        guest,
5116        &state,
5117        mask,
5118        host_timed,
5119        committed,
5120        NamedRealTime::Woken,
5121        private,
5122    )
5123    .await)
5124}
5125
5126/// [`TurnSignals`] from the thread's state (`state`), the call's mask (`mask`),
5127/// the host-timed signals (`host_timed`) and the scheduler's commitment
5128/// (`committed`), before the record of copies Linux discarded at send is
5129/// applied to `pending` (`threads::without_discarded`). The hold leaves out
5130/// `SIGCHLD` and every host-timed signal, except a signal the scheduler
5131/// committed that no host-timed source can post (`futex_wait_held_after_wake`),
5132/// and a recorded private `SIGCHLD` the turn admits (`private`).
5133fn turn_signals_before_discard(
5134    state: &KernelSignalState,
5135    mask: KernelSigset,
5136    host_timed: KernelSigset,
5137    committed: KernelSigset,
5138    real_time: NamedRealTime,
5139    private: KernelSigset,
5140) -> TurnSignals {
5141    use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::STANDARD_SIGNALS;
5142    // A `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, which the schedule recorded in its
5143    // private queue, is not held where the turn admits it (`private`,
5144    // `turn_signals_with_block`).
5145    let held =
5146        crate::syscalls::threads::futex_wait_held_after_wake(host_timed, committed) & !private;
5147    let pending = state.pending_interrupting(mask, false) & !held;
5148    let counted = match real_time {
5149        NamedRealTime::Woken => !0,
5150        NamedRealTime::ByDisposition => {
5151            STANDARD_SIGNALS | (state.interrupting(mask) & !STANDARD_SIGNALS)
5152        }
5153    };
5154    let named = committed & !mask & counted;
5155    TurnSignals { named, pending }
5156}
5157
5158/// How a turn counts a real-time signal its answer names
5159/// ([`TurnSignals::named`]).
5160#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
5161enum NamedRealTime {
5162    /// As any named signal: the drain woke the call only for one whose
5163    /// disposition delivered it then, and Linux's wake stands after a later
5164    /// flush (the generic poll and the scalar writer).
5165    Woken,
5166    /// Only if its disposition delivers it now: the drain never filters
5167    /// `writev` (R2b-1 rule 2).
5168    ByDisposition,
5169}
5170
5171/// Whether a poll or a parked pipe write decides interruption at its own turn
5172/// (`signals_interrupting_poll`): where the record of copies Linux discarded
5173/// at send is kept (`discarded_at_send::records`, ptrace with sequentialized
5174/// threads), the thread's state can be read (`task`, its
5175/// `Resources::signal_state_task`, which needs guest thread IDs that name host
5176/// tasks), and the pending sets that state holds are the kernel's own
5177/// (`kernel_signal_state_is_guests`), so a process-directed copy pending there
5178/// reaches the poller as Linux delivers it. Elsewhere the earlier decision
5179/// stands: on KVM the backend restarts the call unless it would deliver a
5180/// signal, and its polled-read observation (`Guest::polled_read_signal_site`)
5181/// takes a caught signal before the turn, where a `/proc` read could not see
5182/// it (the Claude re-check of the R2b-1 design, R4-4). KVM keeps the record
5183/// since SIGSHARE S3b, but its shared queue is not delivered by a kernel: a
5184/// copy goes to the thread the tool reserves a delivery permit for, so a
5185/// poller's turn that took any shared copy would take one the tool did not
5186/// choose (a POSIX timer's SIGUSR1 that Linux leaves to a `sigtimedwait`
5187/// waiter: `posix-sigwait` in `process_signal_target.c`).
5188fn decides_interruption_at_turn<T, G>(guest: &G, task: Option<(i32, i32)>) -> bool
5189where
5190    T: RecordOrReplay,
5191    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5192{
5193    task.is_some() && turn_decides_interruption(guest.config())
5194}
5195
5196/// The configuration half of [`decides_interruption_at_turn`].
5197fn turn_decides_interruption(cfg: &crate::config::Config) -> bool {
