5198    crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::records(cfg) && cfg.backend.kernel_signal_state_is_guests
5199}
5200
5201/// Install the private mask of a pipe `writev` that decides at its turn
5202/// (`decides_interruption_at_turn`) and goes on polling after its first
5203/// attempt, through `wait` (`KernelSignalWait::block`, scratch `cell`), and
5204/// publish the guest's own mask to the scheduler while it is installed
5205/// (`set_saved_guest_sigmask`). Returns the guest's own mask. A signal that
5206/// stops the installation is held as `inject_absorbing` holds one, a
5207/// host-timed one and a copy Linux discarded at send included
5208/// (`hold_until_return`), and one that would replace a
5209/// held signal whose loss matters ends the call: with the restart errno, as
5210/// `Error::Errno`, when the held one would end it natively, and otherwise with
5211/// a [`HeldSignalRefusal`], which the caller turns into the refusal once the
5212/// guest's mask is back (`refuse_held_signal_loss`; R2b-1 rule 5). A mask that
5213/// cannot be installed ends the call with `EFAULT`, as a failed
5214/// scratch-stack commit does.
5215async fn install_turn_mask<T, G>(
5216    guest: &mut G,
5217    wait: &mut KernelSignalWait,
5218    cell: AddrMut<'_, KernelSigset>,
5219) -> Result<KernelSigset, Error>
5220where
5221    T: RecordOrReplay,
5222    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5223{
5224    // A copy Linux discarded at send that the kernel still holds (a traced
5225    // task's copy is queued whatever its disposition) is left out of the
5226    // turn's `pending` (`without_discarded`), so it must not end the call
5227    // here either: it is held until the call returns, where it is delivered
5228    // late (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3995), as the turn
5229    // decided (the Claude re-check of R2b-1, N1).
5230    let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
5231    let kept = crate::syscalls::threads::without_discarded(guest, &state, state.pending, 0).await;
5232    wait.hold_until_return(host_timed_signals(guest).await | (state.pending & !kept));
5233    wait.block(guest, Some(cell)).await?;
5234    let Some(mask) = wait.effective_mask() else {
5235        return Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
5236    };
5237    crate::tool_global::begin_wait_mask(guest, Some(mask)).await;
5238    Ok(mask)
5239}
5240
5241/// A5 step 3c.1c (design 16.11, D50): under the in-guest delivery gate, the
5242/// guest mask a wait under the thread's own mask decides by, in the thread's
5243/// own turn: the mask it publishes at its requests
5244/// (`tool_global::publish_request_guest_mask`), or, when it publishes none,
5245/// `fallback`, which is the kernel's `SigBlk` unless the caller knows the
5246/// guest's mask better. No backend records the guest's mask apart from the
5247/// kernel's before step 3c.1e, and step 3c.1b's readers take `SigBlk` then
5248/// too.
5249pub(crate) fn gated_own_mask<T, G>(guest: &G, fallback: KernelSigset) -> KernelSigset
5250where
5251    T: RecordOrReplay,
5252    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5253{
5254    let own = Resources::new(guest.thread_state().dettid);
5255    crate::tool_global::publish_request_guest_mask(guest, &own).unwrap_or(fallback)
5256}
5257
5258/// A5 step 3c.1c (design 16.11, D50): under the in-guest delivery gate, what
5259/// ends this thread's wait now, read in its own turn from its `/proc` status
5260/// and its own published mask ([`gated_own_mask`], with `fallback` for
5261/// `SigBlk` when the caller knows the guest's own mask better). `None` when no
5262/// signal is deliverable, and always with the gate off. A state that cannot be
5263/// read is handled as a wait's first read is (`read_thread_wait_signal_state`):
5264/// a thread that no longer exists ends the call with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, and
5265/// otherwise the run ends with a diagnostic.
5266pub(crate) fn gated_wait_end<T, G>(
5267    guest: &G,
5268    fallback: Option<KernelSigset>,
5269) -> Result<Option<crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd>, Error>
5270where
5271    T: RecordOrReplay,
5272    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5273{
5274    gated_wait_end_with_virtual(guest, fallback, 0)
5275}
5276
5277/// [`gated_wait_end`] with `virtual_caught`, caught signals the scheduler
5278/// knows are pending on the process's shared queue with no physical copy
5279/// (signal phase 1's virtual SIGALRM;
5280/// `wait_signal_end::wait_end_with_virtual`).
5281pub(crate) fn gated_wait_end_with_virtual<T, G>(
5282    guest: &G,
5283    fallback: Option<KernelSigset>,
5284    virtual_caught: KernelSigset,
5285) -> Result<Option<crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd>, Error>
5286where
5287    T: RecordOrReplay,
5288    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5289{
5290    if !guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery {
5291        return Ok(None);
5292    }
5293    let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
5294    let mask = gated_own_mask(guest, fallback.unwrap_or(state.blocked));
5295    Ok(crate::wait_signal_end::wait_end_with_virtual(
5296        &state,
5297        mask,
5298        guest.config().in_guest_reserved_signals,
5299        virtual_caught,
5300    ))
5301}
5302
5303/// [`gated_wait_end`], recording a found end as the current call's D40 flag
5304/// (`ThreadState::wait_signal_end`) for the restart checkpoint. Returns
5305/// whether a signal ends the wait.
5306pub(crate) fn gated_wait_ends<T, G>(
5307    guest: &mut G,
5308    fallback: Option<KernelSigset>,
5309) -> Result<bool, Error>
5310where
5311    T: RecordOrReplay,
5312    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5313{
5314    let end = gated_wait_end(guest, fallback)?;
5315    if let Some(end) = end {
5316        tracing::info!(
5317            "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, {:?} ends the wait",
5318            guest.thread_state().dettid,
5319            end
5320        );
5321        guest.thread_state_mut().wait_signal_end = Some(end);
5322    }
5323    Ok(end.is_some())
5324}
5325
5326/// A5 step 3c.1c, design D41 (amending 16.26), with IR-5 and IR-14: under the
5327/// in-guest delivery gate, a default-fatal signal already deliverable when a
5328/// kernel-run call begins (`ResourceID::is_kernel_run_blocking`: a background
5329/// external call, `rt_sigsuspend`, `vfork`) is one Linux would have delivered
5330/// before the call, ending the process. So the call is not run: its handler
5331/// calls this as its first statement, before any guest-visible effect, and
5332/// returns the error this gives, `ERESTARTNOINTR` with the D40 flag `Fatal`
5333/// recorded, which the restart checkpoint turns into `-EINTR` (the death path
5334/// of step 3c.1e follows at the return). A `BehindCaught` end (a caught
5335/// signal first, and a later delivery in the same loop that could end the
5336/// process) means the call is not run either: the flag is recorded as it is,
5337/// and the checkpoint resolves it. `Fatal` gives `-EINTR`. `Caught` (the
5338/// handlers' masks hold the default-fatal signal, or no reset instance is
5339/// reached) would need the handler run and then the call restarted, which
5340/// 3c.1 cannot do, so the checkpoint refuses it by name
5341/// (HERMIT_RESTART_AFTER_HANDLER, fail closed); in that schedule Linux runs
5342/// the handler and, unless it changes the default-fatal signal's disposition
5343/// or mask, ends the process at its `rt_sigreturn`, before the call is made
5344/// again. Only a single caught signal at entry, or none, keeps today's path
5345/// (`None`): the call runs. With the gate off, `None`.
5346pub(crate) fn kernel_run_entry_refusal<T, G>(guest: &mut G) -> Result<Option<Error>, Error>
5347where
5348    T: RecordOrReplay,
5349    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5350{
5351    match gated_wait_end(guest, None)? {
5352        Some(
5353            end @ (crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd::Fatal(_)
5354            | crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd::BehindCaught(_)),
5355        ) => {
5356            tracing::info!(
5357                "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, {:?} is deliverable at a kernel-run \
5358                 call's entry: the call is not run",
5359                guest.thread_state().dettid,
5360                end
5361            );
5362            guest.thread_state_mut().wait_signal_end = Some(end);
5363            Ok(Some(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR.into()))
5364        }
5365        _ => Ok(None),
5366    }
5367}
5368
5369/// The most instances [`remove_ignored_signals`] dequeues in one call before
5370/// it gives up: far more than a thread's queues can hold, which
5371/// `RLIMIT_SIGPENDING` bounds for real-time signals and one per queue bounds
5372/// for standard ones; reached, the removal fails closed.
5373const MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS: usize = 1 << 16;
5374
5375/// A5 step 3c.1d, design D37: remove the pending instances of `set` (ignored
5376/// signals Linux would not hold, `ignored_signals::removable`) from the
5377/// calling thread's queues, in its own turn, by repeated trusted zero-timeout
5378/// `rt_sigtimedwait` calls until `EAGAIN`. Each call dequeues one instance,
5379/// the thread's private queue first and then the shared one
5380/// (`dequeue_signal`, kernel/signal.c:626-639 at v6.12), and with a zero
5381/// timeout it never sleeps: no instance left gives `-EAGAIN`
5382/// (`do_sigtimedwait`, :3629-3676). SIGKILL and SIGSTOP are never in `set`
5383/// (they are never ignored), and the kernel drops them from it anyway
5384/// (:3648). Nothing is injected for an empty set. An error other than
5385/// `EAGAIN`, more instances than any queue can hold, or no scratch stack for
5386/// the call's two cells is Hermit's own failure (`Error::Tool`), never an
5387/// errno the guest's call could see.
5388pub(crate) async fn remove_ignored_signals<T, G>(guest: &mut G, set: u64) -> Result<(), Error>
5389where
5390    T: RecordOrReplay,
5391    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5392{
5393    remove_pending_ignored(guest, set, IgnoredRemoval::NotHeldByLinux).await
5394}
5395
5396/// [`remove_ignored_signals`] for the ignored signals a masked wait's
5397/// temporary mask lets in, pending under the thread's own mask, which Linux
5398/// discards as the call returns (`get_signal`, kernel/signal.c), on a
5399/// backend that runs the call itself and cannot discard them inside it
5400/// (`Detcore::settle_masked_ppoll_enosys`). The same removal, with its own
5401/// log line.
5402pub(crate) async fn remove_signals_discarded_under_a_temporary_mask<T, G>(
5403    guest: &mut G,
5404    set: u64,
5405) -> Result<(), Error>
5406where
5407    T: RecordOrReplay,
5408    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5409{
5410    remove_pending_ignored(guest, set, IgnoredRemoval::LetInByTemporaryMask).await
5411}
5412
5413/// [`remove_signals_discarded_under_a_temporary_mask`] in two cells a caller
5414/// that holds the scratch stack reserved itself: `set_cell`, into which `set`
5415/// is written, and `timeout`, which is zeroed. The caller writes back what
5416/// they held.
5417pub(crate) async fn remove_signals_discarded_under_a_temporary_mask_in<T, G>(
5418    guest: &mut G,
5419    set: u64,
5420    set_cell: usize,
5421    timeout: AddrMut<'_, Timespec>,
5422) -> Result<(), Error>
5423where
5424    T: RecordOrReplay,
5425    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5426{
5427    if set == 0 {
5428        return Ok(());
5429    }
5430    let cell = AddrMut::<u64>::from_raw(set_cell).ok_or_else(|| {
5431        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
5432            "removing ignored signals {set:#x}: no cell for the set"
5433        ))
5434    })?;
5435    guest.memory().write_value(cell, &set)?;
5436    guest.memory().write_value(
5437        timeout,
5438        &Timespec {
5439            tv_sec: 0,
5440            tv_nsec: 0,
5441        },
5442    )?;
5443    remove_pending_ignored_in(
5444        guest,
5445        set,
5446        cell.cast::<libc::sigset_t>(),
5447        timeout.into(),
5448        IgnoredRemoval::LetInByTemporaryMask,
5449    )
5450    .await
5451}
5452
5453/// Why [`remove_pending_ignored`] removes ignored signals, which its log line
5454/// names.
5455#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
5456enum IgnoredRemoval {
5457    /// D37: ones Linux would not hold, under the in-guest delivery gate.
5458    NotHeldByLinux,
5459    /// Ones a temporary mask lets in, which Linux discards as the call returns.
5460    LetInByTemporaryMask,
5461}
5462
5463/// The removal of [`remove_ignored_signals`], logged for `why`, in two cells
5464/// of its own.
5465async fn remove_pending_ignored<T, G>(
5466    guest: &mut G,
5467    set: u64,
5468    why: IgnoredRemoval,
5469) -> Result<(), Error>
5470where
5471    T: RecordOrReplay,
5472    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5473{
5474    if set == 0 {
5475        return Ok(());
5476    }
5477    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
5478    let set_cell = stack.push(set);
5479    let timeout = stack.push(Timespec {
5480        tv_sec: 0,
5481        tv_nsec: 0,
5482    });
5483    // A stack with no room for the two cells is Hermit's own failure too, never
5484    // an EFAULT of the guest's call (round-3 ruling 4).
5485    let _stack_guard = stack.commit().map_err(|errno| {
5486        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
5487            "removing ignored signals {set:#x}: no scratch stack for the trusted \
5488             rt_sigtimedwait ({errno})"
5489        ))
5490    })?;
5491    // SAFETY: the kernel only reads the set; Reverie types the argument as
5492    // mutable.
5493    let set_cell = unsafe { set_cell.cast::<libc::sigset_t>().into_mut() };
5494    remove_pending_ignored_in(guest, set, set_cell, timeout, why).await
5495}
5496
5497/// The removal of [`remove_ignored_signals`]: trusted zero-timeout
5498/// `rt_sigtimedwait` calls for `set`, held in `set_cell`, with the zero
5499/// timeout in `timeout`, until `EAGAIN`.
5500async fn remove_pending_ignored_in<T, G>(
5501    guest: &mut G,
5502    set: u64,
5503    set_cell: AddrMut<'_, libc::sigset_t>,
5504    timeout: Addr<'_, Timespec>,
5505    why: IgnoredRemoval,
5506) -> Result<(), Error>
5507where
5508    T: RecordOrReplay,
5509    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5510{
5511    for _ in 0..MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS {
5512        let taken = guest
5513            .inject(
5514                syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new()
5515                    .with_set(Some(set_cell))
5516                    .with_info(None)
5517                    .with_timeout(Some(timeout))
5518                    .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE),
5519            )
5520            .await;
5521        match (taken, why) {
5522            (Ok(signal), IgnoredRemoval::NotHeldByLinux) => tracing::info!(
5523                "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, removed ignored signal {} that Linux \
5524                 would not hold (D37)",
5525                guest.thread_state().dettid,
5526                signal
5527            ),
5528            (Ok(signal), IgnoredRemoval::LetInByTemporaryMask) => tracing::info!(
5529                "[dtid {}] removed ignored signal {} that a temporary mask lets in, which Linux \
5530                 discards as the call returns",
5531                guest.thread_state().dettid,
5532                signal
5533            ),
5534            (Err(Errno::EAGAIN), _) => return Ok(()),
5535            // Hermit's own failure, never the guest's result: the guest's call
5536            // (rt_sigaction, rt_sigsuspend, a masked wait) cannot return it.
5537            (Err(errno), _) => {
5538                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
5539                    "removing ignored signals {set:#x}: the trusted rt_sigtimedwait failed with \
5540                     {errno}"
5541                )));
5542            }
5543        }
5544    }
5545    Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
5546        "removing ignored signals {set:#x} dequeued {MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS} instances without \
5547         emptying the queues"
5548    )))
5549}
5550
5551/// Which of a thread's two queues [`remove_ignored_from_queue`] empties of a
5552/// signal.
5553#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
5554pub(crate) enum OneQueue {
5555    /// The thread's private queue (`SigPnd`).
5556    Private,
5557    /// Its thread group's shared queue (`ShdPnd`).
5558    Shared,
5559}
5560
5561/// A5 step 3c.1e A, D37's R2 per queue: remove every pending instance of the
5562/// ignored signal `signal` from `queue` only, leaving the other queue's
5563/// instances as they are, in the thread's own turn. `rt_sigtimedwait`
5564/// dequeues the private queue first (`dequeue_signal`, kernel/signal.c:
5565/// 626-639 at v6.12), so:
5566///
5567/// - `Private`: one trusted zero-timeout `rt_sigtimedwait` per instance, for
5568///   as long as the thread's `/proc` status shows `signal` in `SigPnd`.
5569/// - `Shared`: the private instances are dequeued first, each with its
5570///   siginfo, then the shared ones until `EAGAIN`, then the private ones are
5571///   queued again, in their order, with their own siginfo, by
5572///   `rt_tgsigqueueinfo` to the thread itself (`do_rt_tgsigqueueinfo` lets a
5573///   thread queue any siginfo to itself, kernel/signal.c:4112-4114; the
5574///   signal is blocked by the kernel's mask then, the guest's own mask, which
5575///   blocks it since Linux kept it, or the in-guest runtime's, so it is
5576///   queued and not discarded, `sig_ignored`, :104-120).
5577///
5578/// Nothing is injected when `signal` is not pending in `queue`. A failed
5579/// injection, more instances than any queue holds, or no scratch stack is
5580/// Hermit's own failure (`Error::Tool`), never an errno of the guest's call.
5581pub(crate) async fn remove_ignored_from_queue<T, G>(
5582    guest: &mut G,
5583    signal: i32,
5584    queue: OneQueue,
5585) -> Result<(), Error>
5586where
5587    T: RecordOrReplay,
5588    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5589{
5590    let bit = crate::syscalls::kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
5591    let failed = |what: &str| {
5592        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
5593            "removing ignored signal {signal} from the {queue:?} queue: {what}"
5594        ))
5595    };
5596    let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
5597    let in_queue = match queue {
5598        OneQueue::Private => state.thread_pending,
5599        OneQueue::Shared => state.shared_pending,
5600    };
5601    if in_queue & bit == 0 {
5602        return Ok(());
5603    }
5604    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
5605    let set_cell = stack.push(bit);
5606    let timeout = stack.push(Timespec {
5607        tv_sec: 0,
5608        tv_nsec: 0,
5609    });
5610    // A siginfo cell, kept as bytes: `siginfo_t` holds raw pointers, so an
5611    // address typed by it could not live across an await.
5612    let info = stack.reserve::<[u8; 128]>();
5613    let _stack_guard = stack
5614        .commit()
5615        .map_err(|errno| failed(&format!("no scratch stack ({errno})")))?;
5616    // SAFETY: the kernel only reads the set; Reverie types it as mutable.
5617    let set_cell = unsafe { set_cell.cast::<libc::sigset_t>().into_mut() };
5618    let dequeue = move |with_info: bool| {
5619        syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new()
5620            .with_set(Some(set_cell))
5621            .with_info(with_info.then(|| info.cast()))
5622            .with_timeout(Some(timeout))
5623            .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE)
5624    };
5625    // The private instances, dequeued one at a time while `SigPnd` shows
5626    // them; their siginfo is kept to queue them again for `Shared`.
5627    let mut kept: Vec<[u8; 128]> = Vec::new();
5628    let mut removals = 0;
5629    while crate::syscalls::read_guest_wait_signal_state(guest)?.thread_pending & bit != 0 {
5630        removals += 1;
5631        if removals > MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS {
5632            return Err(failed("too many instances"));
5633        }
5634        match guest.inject(dequeue(queue == OneQueue::Shared)).await {
5635            Ok(_) => {
5636                if queue == OneQueue::Shared {
5637                    kept.push(guest.memory().read_value(info)?);
5638                }
5639            }
5640            Err(errno) => return Err(failed(&format!("rt_sigtimedwait failed with {errno}"))),
5641        }
5642    }
5643    if queue == OneQueue::Private {
5644        tracing::info!(
5645            "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, removed ignored signal {} from the \
5646             private queue, which Linux discarded at send (D37)",
5647            guest.thread_state().dettid,
5648            signal
5649        );
5650        return Ok(());
5651    }
5652    loop {
5653        removals += 1;
5654        if removals > MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS {
5655            return Err(failed("too many instances"));
5656        }
5657        match guest.inject(dequeue(false)).await {
5658            Ok(_) => {}
5659            Err(Errno::EAGAIN) => break,
5660            Err(errno) => return Err(failed(&format!("rt_sigtimedwait failed with {errno}"))),
5661        }
5662    }
5663    for siginfo in kept {
5664        guest.memory().write_value(info, &siginfo)?;
5665        let requeue = syscalls::RtTgsigqueueinfo::new()
5666            .with_tgid(guest.pid().as_raw())
5667            .with_tid(guest.tid().as_raw())
5668            .with_sig(signal)
5669            .with_siginfo(Some(info.cast()));
5670        if let Err(errno) = guest.inject(requeue).await {
5671            return Err(failed(&format!(
5672                "queueing a kept private instance again failed with {errno}"
5673            )));
5674        }
5675    }
5676    tracing::info!(
5677        "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, removed ignored signal {} from the shared \
5678         queue, which Linux discarded at send, keeping its private instances (D37)",
5679        guest.thread_state().dettid,
5680        signal
5681    );
5682    Ok(())
5683}
5684
5685/// What a temporary-mask wait's check finds under the in-guest delivery gate
5686/// ([`temporary_mask_check`]).
5687#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
5688pub(crate) enum TemporaryMaskCheck {
5689    /// Nothing ends the wait; the ignored signals Linux would not hold were
5690    /// removed (D37 rule (ii)).
5691    Waits,
5692    /// A default-fatal signal the temporary mask lets in ends it: the D40
5693    /// flag `Fatal` is recorded, and the call returns its restart code
5694    /// (`-ERESTARTNOHAND`; `-EINTR` for the `epoll` forms), which the restart
5695    /// checkpoint turns into `-EINTR` for the death path of step 3c.1e.
5696    Fatal,
5697    /// A masked `epoll_pwait` or `epoll_pwait2` at its park: an ignored signal
5698    /// pending at entry that only the temporary mask lets in, removed, and
5699    /// the call returns `EINTR` (D37's exception, IR-3).
5700    EpollInterrupted,
5701    /// A caught signal would end the wait (or be delivered first): its
5702    /// handler would run under the temporary mask, which step 3c.w owns and
5703    /// which 3c.1 never reaches (phase 1 refuses every temporary-mask call in
5704    /// a process that handles SIGALRM, F8). The stopping refusal
5705    /// HERMIT_TEMPORARY_MASK_CAUGHT_END was filed (D49); were the run to go
5706    /// on, the call returns `EINTR`.
5707    Refused,
5708}
5709
5710/// A5 step 3c.1d (design D37, D39, D50, IR-7): the check of a wait under a
5711/// temporary mask `m_temp` (`rt_sigsuspend`, a masked `pselect6`, `ppoll`,
5712/// `epoll_pwait` or `epoll_pwait2`), at the point where Linux tests for a
5713/// pending signal: the call would wait (nothing ready), in the thread's own
5714/// turn, from its `/proc` status (one read).
5715///
5716/// 1. The design's deliverable set under `m_temp` (`wait_signal_end`): a
5717///    default-fatal signal ends the wait (`Fatal`, the D40 flag recorded). A
5718///    caught one would run its handler under the temporary mask (step 3c.w,
5719///    unreachable in 3c.1): a named stopping refusal (`Refused`).
5720/// 2. D37 rule (ii) with IR-7's per-instance masks: the ignored signals `I`
5721///    pending now, less `I ∩ M_req ∩ M_next`, are removed, where `M_next` is
5722///    `m_temp` and `M_req` is the mask in force when the instance was
5723///    queued. `entry` is `Some(!0)` at the wait's first check, which every
5724///    form makes in the call's own turn, before any scheduler request, so
5725///    every instance pending then was pending at entry and was queued under
5726///    the guest's own mask ([`gated_own_mask`]); `None` at any later check,
5727///    where every instance kept from entry is in both masks, so `M_req` =
5728///    `m_temp` for all of them. (A narrower `entry` set limits the at-entry
5729///    rule to those bits.)
5730/// 3. `epoll` (a masked `epoll_pwait` or `epoll_pwait2`) at the first check:
5731///    an instance pending at entry in `I ∩ M_own ∖ M_temp` makes the call
5732///    return `EINTR` (`EpollInterrupted`), as `ep_poll` does
5733///    (`ignored_signals::epoll_interrupting`).
5734///
5735/// With the gate off it is never called.
5736pub(crate) async fn temporary_mask_check<T, G>(
5737    guest: &mut G,
5738    m_temp: KernelSigset,
5739    entry: Option<KernelSigset>,
5740    epoll: bool,
5741) -> Result<TemporaryMaskCheck, Error>
5742where
5743    T: RecordOrReplay,
5744    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5745{
5746    use crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd;
5747    let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
5748    let reserved = guest.config().in_guest_reserved_signals;
5749    match crate::wait_signal_end::wait_end(&state, m_temp, reserved) {
5750        None => {}
5751        Some(end @ WaitSignalEnd::Fatal(_)) => {
5752            tracing::info!(
5753                "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, {:?} ends the wait under its \
5754                 temporary mask {:#x}",
5755                guest.thread_state().dettid,
5756                end,
5757                m_temp
5758            );
5759            guest.thread_state_mut().wait_signal_end = Some(end);
5760            return Ok(TemporaryMaskCheck::Fatal);
5761        }
5762        Some(end) => {
5763            let signal = match end {
5764                WaitSignalEnd::Caught(signal) => signal,
5765                _ => {
5766                    (state.pending & !m_temp & state.caught & !reserved).trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1
5767                }
5768            };
5769            let reason = crate::refused_signal_controls::temporary_mask_caught_end_refusal(
5770                guest.thread_state().dettid.as_raw(),
5771                signal,
5772            );
5773            tracing::error!("{}", reason);
5774            crate::tool_global::stopping_refusal(guest, reason).await;
5775            return Ok(TemporaryMaskCheck::Refused);
5776        }
5777    }
5778    let own = gated_own_mask(guest, state.blocked);
5779    let now = crate::ignored_signals::pending_ignored(&state, reserved);
5780    let (removed, interrupted) = match entry {
5781        Some(entry) => {
5782            let at_entry = KernelSignalState {
5783                pending: state.pending & entry,
5784                ..state
5785            };
5786            let since = KernelSignalState {
5787                pending: state.pending & !entry,
5788                ..state
5789            };
5790            let interrupted = epoll
5791                && crate::ignored_signals::epoll_interrupting(&at_entry, own, m_temp, reserved)
5792                    != 0;
5793            (
5794                crate::ignored_signals::removable(&at_entry, own, m_temp, reserved)
5795                    | crate::ignored_signals::removable(&since, m_temp, m_temp, reserved),
5796                interrupted,
5797            )
5798        }
5799        None => (now & !m_temp, false),
5800    };
5801    remove_ignored_signals(guest, removed).await?;
5802    Ok(if interrupted {
5803        TemporaryMaskCheck::EpollInterrupted
5804    } else {
5805        TemporaryMaskCheck::Waits
5806    })
5807}
5808
5809/// The `sa_flags` of `signal`'s current action, as the guest set it, read in
5810/// this thread's turn with a query `rt_sigaction` (the in-guest runtime
5811/// answers it from the guest's action, phase 1's virtual SIGALRM included):
5812/// for the restart checkpoint's caught row (A5 design D40).
5813pub(crate) async fn caught_action_flags<T, G>(guest: &mut G, signal: i32) -> Result<u64, Error>
5814where
5815    T: RecordOrReplay,
5816    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5817{
5818    Ok(caught_action(guest, signal).await?.flags)
5819}
5820
5821/// The `sa_mask` and `sa_flags` of `signal`'s current action, as the guest set
5822/// it, read in this thread's turn with a query `rt_sigaction` (the in-guest
5823/// runtime answers it from the guest's action, phase 1's virtual SIGALRM
5824/// included): for the restart checkpoint's resolution of a
5825/// `WaitSignalEnd::BehindCaught` (A5 design D40) and its caught row. Called
5826/// only where the thread holds no committed scratch stack.
5827pub(crate) async fn caught_action<T, G>(
5828    guest: &mut G,
5829    signal: i32,
5830) -> Result<crate::wait_signal_end::CaughtAction, Error>
5831where
5832    T: RecordOrReplay,
5833    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5834{
5835    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
5836    let action = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
5837    let _stack_guard = stack.commit()?;
5838    guest
5839        .inject_with_retry(
5840            syscalls::RtSigaction::new()
5841                .with_signum(signal)
5842                .with_action(None)
5843                .with_old_action(Some(action.cast()))
5844                .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE),
5845        )
5846        .await?;
5847    let action: KernelSigaction = guest.memory().read_value(action)?;
5848    Ok(crate::wait_signal_end::CaughtAction {
5849        mask: action.mask,
5850        flags: action.flags,
5851    })
5852}
5853
5854/// Whether the scheduler keeps a guest mask that differs from the kernel's
5855/// `SigBlk` (`Scheduler::saved_guest_sigmasks`) and reads it in its place, so
5856/// that a thread must publish it: under signal-target modelling
5857/// (`Config::models_signal_targets`, which is where the discarded-at-send
5858/// record is kept, `discarded_at_send::records`), and under the in-guest
5859/// delivery gate (`Config::in_guest_signal_delivery`; A5 step 3c.1b), where the
5860/// kernel's mask may be the in-guest runtime's. With both off, nothing is
5861/// published and every reader takes `SigBlk`, as before step 3c.1b.
5862pub(crate) fn publishes_guest_masks(cfg: &crate::Config) -> bool {
5863    crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::records(cfg) || cfg.in_guest_signal_delivery
5864}
5865
5866/// The waiting thread's mask as last told to the scheduler
5867/// (`publish_wait_mask`). It is deliberately not `Copy`: a wait loop in an
5868/// `async move` block must reborrow it, or the block would publish into a
5869/// copy and the clear after the block would see nothing to clear.
5870#[derive(Debug, Default)]
5871pub(crate) struct PublishedWaitMask(Option<KernelSigset>);
5872
5873/// Tell the scheduler the waiting thread's effective mask
5874/// (`KernelSignalWait::effective_mask`, or `None` once the wait is over) if it
5875/// differs from `published`, the last one told. The scheduler reads it in
5876/// place of the thread's `SigBlk` (`set_saved_guest_sigmask`), for example to
5877/// decide whether a leader ignores an `ITIMER_REAL` expiry at generation
5878/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139). Only where the scheduler
5879/// reads it for a wait (`publishes_guest_masks`): under signal-target
5880/// modelling, or under the in-guest delivery gate.
5881pub(crate) async fn publish_wait_mask<T, G>(
5882    guest: &mut G,
5883    mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
5884    published: &mut PublishedWaitMask,
5885) where
5886    T: RecordOrReplay,
5887    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5888{
5889    if mask == published.0 || !publishes_guest_masks(guest.config()) {
5890        return;
5891    }
5892    // A wait publication begins (or ends, for `None`) the thread's
5893    // wait-mask interval, with the legacy saved mask in the same
5894    // mutation (`Scheduler::begin_wait_mask` / `withdraw_wait_mask`).
5895    match mask {
5896        Some(mask) => crate::tool_global::begin_wait_mask(guest, Some(mask)).await,
5897        None => crate::tool_global::withdraw_wait_mask(guest).await,
5898    }
5899    published.0 = mask;
5900}
5901
5902/// End a wait's publication at its return: an interrupted end hands the
5903/// interval off to the delivery (the overlay ends; the legacy mask stays
5904/// published until the thread's next request, as Linux keeps the
5905/// temporary mask in `blocked` through the handler), and any other end
5906/// withdraws it with the legacy saved mask. No publication in force is
5907/// no end, as in `publish_wait_mask`.
5908pub(crate) async fn finish_wait_mask<T, G>(
5909    guest: &mut G,
5910    interrupted: bool,
5911    published: &mut PublishedWaitMask,
5912) where
5913    T: RecordOrReplay,
5914    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5915{
5916    if published.0.is_none() || !publishes_guest_masks(guest.config()) {
5917        return;
5918    }
5919    if interrupted {
5920        crate::tool_global::end_wait_mask(guest).await;
5921    } else {
5922        crate::tool_global::withdraw_wait_mask(guest).await;
5923    }
5924    published.0 = None;
5925}
5926
5927async fn retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state<T, G, C>(
5928    guest: &mut G,
5929    call0: C,
5930    rsrc: Resources,
5931    maybe_timeout: Option<(LogicalTime, Result<i64, Errno>)>,
5932) -> Result<i64, Error>
5933where
5934    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
5935    T: RecordOrReplay,
5936    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5937{
5938    retry_blocking_wait_under_mask(guest, call0, rsrc, maybe_timeout, None)
5939        .await
5940        .0
5941}
5942
5943/// `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` for a call that sleeps under
5944/// `wait_mask` instead of the guest's own mask, when it is set: the temporary
5945/// mask of an `epoll_pwait` (`KernelSignalWait::with_wait_mask`). `call0`
5946/// carries no mask, so its probes run under the guest's own mask until every
5947/// blockable signal is blocked, as for any other wait. Also returns whether the
5948/// signal that ended the wait must still be delivered under `wait_mask`: one
5949/// that only `wait_mask` lets in, pending in the kernel under the guest's own
5950/// mask once it is put back, which the caller delivers with
5951/// `inject_signal_delivery`, as a masked pselect6 does.
5952pub(crate) async fn retry_blocking_wait_under_mask<T, G, C>(
5953    guest: &mut G,
5954    call0: C,
5955    mut rsrc: Resources,
5956    maybe_timeout: Option<(LogicalTime, Result<i64, Errno>)>,
5957    wait_mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
5958) -> (Result<i64, Error>, bool)
5959where
5960    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
5961    T: RecordOrReplay,
5962    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5963{
5964    let mut guest_held = GuestHeldPollProof::capture(guest, call0.into(), &mut rsrc);
5965    // The restart code of this call, read at its entry
5966    // (`interrupt_errno_at_entry`).
5967    let restart_errno = interrupt_errno_at_entry(guest, &call0, call0.kernel_restart_errno());
5968    let mut signals = KernelSignalWait::new(
5969        guest,
5970        call0.signals_consumed_by_wait(&guest.memory()),
5971        call0.restart_keeps_deadline(),
5972        restart_errno,
5973    )
5974    .with_deadline(maybe_timeout.is_some())
5975    .with_wait_mask(wait_mask);
5976    // Set when a signal that only `wait_mask` lets in ends the wait.
5977    let mut deliver_under_wait_mask = false;
5978    let mut published = PublishedWaitMask::default();
5979    publish_wait_mask(guest, signals.effective_mask(), &mut published).await;
5980    rsrc.poll_deadline = poll_deadline_for(guest, maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline));
5981    rsrc.poll_expires = maybe_timeout.is_some();
5982    let (mut call, mut guard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
5983    let mut first_turn = true;
5984    // Set when only a signal the scheduler committed in this turn ends the
5985    // wait: the turn's probe runs first, and the wait ends with the restart
5986    // errno only if the call has nothing to report.
5987    let mut interrupt_after_probe;
5988
5989    let result = loop {
5990        interrupt_after_probe = false;
5991        // A scheduler `Signaled` answer only says a signal may be pending. The kernel's
5992        // state below decides whether it ends the wait.
5993        let resumed = resource_request(guest, rsrc.clone()).await;
5994        guest_held.revalidate(guest, &mut rsrc);
5995        // Read in this turn, before any injection: another thread may have
5996        // armed a host-timed source since the last turn, and none can until
5997        // this turn ends. The same round trip gives the `SIGCHLD` a guest sent
5998        // this thread that the schedule recorded in its private queue, which
5999        // an injection of this turn (the timerfd publication below) could
6000        // otherwise take into the backend's single held slot (R2b-2 stage 3,
6001        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
6002        let (host_timed, recorded) =
6003            crate::tool_global::host_timed_and_private_sigchld(guest).await;
6004        signals.hold_until_return(host_timed);
6005        // A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler committed to this thread in this turn, sent
6006        // at a commit point (a child's child-exit timer, or a POSIX timer whose
6007        // signal is `SIGCHLD`), ends the wait, as on Linux
6008        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005), and so does a
6009        // recorded private one: both are admitted (`KernelSignalWait::admit`).
6010        let committed = committed_signals(&resumed) & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
6011        let private = match signals
6012            .admit_under_block(guest, committed, recorded, host_timed, &mut published)
6013            .await
6014        {
6015            Ok(private) => private,
6016            Err(error) => break Err(error),
6017        };
6018        signals.admit(committed, private);
6019        // As in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`: virtual timerfds first.
6020        // As in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`: release the nonblocking
6021        // form's scratch stack before publishing, and convert again after.
6022        let reconvert =
6023            guard.is_some() && crate::syscalls::timerfd::may_publish(guest, call.into());
6024        if reconvert {
6025            guard = None;
6026        }
6027        rsrc.poll_deadline = crate::syscalls::timerfd::publish_before_probe(
6028            guest,
6029            call.into(),
6030            maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline),
6031        )
6032        .await;
6033        if reconvert {
6034            (call, guard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
6035        }
6036        // A pending real-time timer expiration that this wait would consume or
6037        // be ended by (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089).
6038        let pending = pending_real_time_among(guest, REAL_TIME_SIGNALS).await;
6039        if pending != 0 {
6040            match signals.observable_now(guest) {
6041                Ok(observable) => act_on_pending_real_time(guest, pending, observable, 0).await,
6042                Err(error) => break Err(error),
6043            }
6044        }
6045        let first = std::mem::take(&mut first_turn);
6046        // Never `inject_with_retry`: see `KernelSignalWait`.
6047        let injected = if first {
6048            // The first probe runs before the check, so a source that was ready when
6049            // the call began, or an argument error, is reported as Linux reports it
6050            // whatever signal is pending (`inject_first_probe`).
6051            signals.inject_first_probe(guest, call).await
6052        } else {
6053            let state = match signals.interrupted_with_state(guest) {
6054                Ok((false, state)) => state,
6055                // Linux takes a completion before it returns EINTR: a queued
6056                // signal of rt_sigtimedwait's set (`do_sigtimedwait` dequeues
6057                // first, and again after it sleeps), a ready descriptor of poll
6058                // or epoll_wait. A signal the scheduler committed in this turn
6059                // was sent at the same fixed point as any completion this turn
6060                // can see, so the completion wins, as on Linux (Codex review of
6061                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4039).
6062                Ok((true, state)) if signals.interrupts_only_by_committed(&state) => {
6063                    interrupt_after_probe = true;
6064                    deliver_under_wait_mask = signals.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state);
6065                    state
6066                }
6067                Ok((true, state)) => {
6068                    deliver_under_wait_mask = signals.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state);
6069                    let errno = restart_errno;
6070                    tracing::trace!(
6071                        "retry_nonblocking_syscall: pending signals interrupt {}: {:?}",
6072                        call.display(&guest.memory()),
6073                        errno
6074                    );
6075                    break Err(errno.into());
6076                }
6077                Err(error) => break Err(error),
6078            };
6079            signals.inject_absorbing_after(guest, call, state).await
6080        };
6081        let syscall_result = match injected {
6082            Ok(result) => result,
6083            Err(error) => {
6084                tracing::trace!(
6085                    "retry_nonblocking_syscall: a signal stop ends the wait in {}: {:?}",
6086                    call.display(&guest.memory()),
6087                    error
6088                );
6089                break Err(error);
6090            }
6091        };
6092        if !call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
6093            let normalized =
6094                call.normalize_nonblocking_result(syscall_result, rsrc.poll_attempt > 0);
6095            if normalized != syscall_result {
6096                guest.thread_state_mut().nonblocking_result_normalized = true;
6097            }
6098            let res = normalized.map_err(|e| e.into());
6099            tracing::trace!(
6100                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: syscall completed after {} retries: {} = {:?}",
6101                rsrc.poll_attempt,
6102                call.display(&guest.memory()),
6103                res
6104            );
6105            break res;
6106        }
6107        if interrupt_after_probe {
6108            let errno = restart_errno;
6109            tracing::trace!(
6110                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: a committed signal interrupts {}: {:?}",
6111                call.display(&guest.memory()),
6112                errno
6113            );
6114            break Err(errno.into());
6115        }
6116        if first {
6117            // The first turn's check, after its probe found nothing to report.
6118            match signals.interrupted_with_state(guest) {
6119                Ok((false, _)) => {}
6120                Ok((true, state)) => {
6121                    deliver_under_wait_mask = signals.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state);
6122                    let errno = restart_errno;
6123                    tracing::trace!(
6124                        "retry_nonblocking_syscall: pending signals interrupt {}: {:?}",
6125                        call.display(&guest.memory()),
6126                        errno
6127                    );
6128                    break Err(errno.into());
6129                }
6130                Err(error) => break Err(error),
6131            }
6132        }
6133        if signals.needs_block() {
6134            // Only one scratch-stack guard may be live, so release the probe's, block
6135            // signals from a fresh one, and rebuild the probe.
6136            guard = None;
6137            if let Err(error) = signals.block(guest, None).await {
6138                break Err(error);
6139            }
6140            publish_wait_mask(guest, signals.effective_mask(), &mut published).await;
6141            (call, guard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
6142        }
6143        rsrc.poll_attempt += 1;
6144        if let Some((timeout, timeout_result)) = maybe_timeout {
6145            let new_time = thread_observe_time(guest).await;
6146            if new_time >= timeout {
6147                tracing::trace!(
6148                    "Timing out syscall after #{} retries: {}",
6149                    rsrc.poll_attempt - 1,
6150                    call.display(&guest.memory())
6151                );
6152                break timeout_result.map_err(|e| e.into());
6153            }
6154            tracing::trace!(
6155                "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}, {} from timeout: {}",
6156                rsrc.poll_attempt,
6157                syscall_result,
6158                timeout - new_time,
6159                call.display(&guest.memory())
6160            );
6161        } else {
6162            tracing::trace!(
6163                "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}: {}",
6164                rsrc.poll_attempt,
6165                syscall_result,
6166                call.display(&guest.memory())
6167            );
6168        }
6169        record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
6170    };
6171
6172    drop(guard);
6173    let restored = signals.restore(guest, None).await;
6174    finish_wait_mask(
6175        guest,
6176        matches!(
6177            result,
6178            Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND | Errno::EINTR))
6179        ),
6180        &mut published,
6181    )
6182    .await;
6183    let result = match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
6184        Ok(result) => result,
6185        Err(error) => return (Err(error), false),
6186    };
6187    // A signal the backend holds is delivered as the guest resumes, under the
6188    // guest's own mask (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1011).
6189    let deliver = deliver_under_wait_mask && !signals.holds_signal() && result.is_err();
6190    (
6191        refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, call0.number(), result).await,
6192        deliver,
6193    )
6194}
6195
6196/// The internal failure, if any, that `refusal` names, for thread `dettid`
6197/// handling the guest's `sysno`. `UnsupportedOperation::ToolDecided` is a
6198/// backend's statement that it left a call Detcore injected to the Tool,
6199/// because the Tool decides that call on every backend (the KVM executor's
6200/// CPU, scheduling, priority, id, getrandom, prlimit64, membarrier, seccomp
6201/// and getpgrp calls). Detcore answers every such call itself, except the
6202/// getpgrp that a clone3 race passes through to the backend
6203/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4531); so one that reached the
6204/// backend is a Detcore defect or that race, never an answer for the guest.
6205/// Every other refusal belongs to the call site that injected it and is not
6206/// judged here.
6207pub(crate) fn tool_decided_injection_failure(
6208    refusal: Option<reverie::UnsupportedRefusal>,
6209    dettid: DetTid,
6210    sysno: Sysno,
6211) -> Option<String> {
6212    refusal
6213        .filter(|refusal| refusal.operation == reverie::UnsupportedOperation::ToolDecided)
6214        .map(|refusal| {
6215            format!(
6216                "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=tool-decided-injection dtid={dettid} \
6217                 syscall={sysno}: the backend refused a call Detcore injected, as one the Tool \
6218                 decides on every backend ({}); Detcore must answer it itself",
6219                refusal.diagnostic
6220            )
6221        })
6222}
6223
6224/// Ends the run as an internal failure when the last call Detcore injected
6225/// while handling the guest's `sysno` came back with a `ToolDecided` refusal
6226/// ([`tool_decided_injection_failure`]), instead of letting its ENOSYS reach
6227/// the guest. The panic text and the error log carry
6228/// `HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=tool-decided-injection`; the CLI's own
6229/// summary line classifies the run as `class=container-child-panic`.
6230///
6231/// This is not a general guard. That no Detcore path injects one of these
6232/// calls on KVM rests on an audit of Detcore's handlers. The one known
6233/// exception is a race: under --no-sequentialize-threads a sibling can
6234/// rewrite clone3's argument struct between Detcore's read and the KVM
6235/// executor's, so a child Detcore marks as in a nested PID namespace passes
6236/// its getpgrp through to the backend (tracked in
6237/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4531). This check mitigates
6238/// that path: it runs once per syscall event, after Detcore's handler
6239/// returns and before the result is used, and a backend's refusal describes
6240/// only the latest injection, so it sees a handler's pass-through when that
6241/// is the event's last injection. It does not see:
6242/// - an injection of one of these calls followed by another injection in the
6243///   same event, which clears the first one's refusal;
6244/// - a refusal that a consumer takes and filters first, such as
6245///   `report_backend_signal_refusal` (signal.rs), behind the
6246///   thread-directed process signal capability that is false on KVM;
6247/// - injections from Tool callbacks other than the syscall handler (signal
6248///   events, thread start, post-exec, exit, timers);
6249/// - `tail_inject`, whose result goes straight to the guest.
6250///
6251/// A general guard needs a Reverie API hook and is not part of this change.
6252///
6253/// Any other refusal it takes counts the call as refused in the syscall
6254/// histogram (`crate::syscall_histogram`). A signalfd operation the backend
6255/// does not model (`UnsupportedOperation::Signalfd`: a read that would wait,
6256/// an epoll registration, a process created while one is open), or an
6257/// operation on a pidfd for another process that it does not model
6258/// (`UnsupportedOperation::Pidfd`: sending one in an `SCM_RIGHTS` message), is
6259/// named in a warning as well: no handler takes that refusal, and its ENOSYS
6260/// reaches the guest as the backend answered.
6261pub(crate) fn fail_on_tool_decided_injection<T, G>(guest: &mut G, sysno: Sysno)
6262where
6263    T: RecordOrReplay,
6264    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6265{
6266    let refusal = guest.take_unsupported_refusal();
6267    judge_backend_refusal::<T, G>(guest, refusal, sysno);
6268}
6269
6270/// [`fail_on_tool_decided_injection`]'s judgement of a refusal already taken
6271/// from the backend: also used by `Detcore::report_backend_refusal` for a
6272/// refusal that is not the one its call can be refused with.
6273pub(crate) fn judge_backend_refusal<T, G>(
6274    guest: &mut G,
6275    refusal: Option<reverie::UnsupportedRefusal>,
6276    sysno: Sysno,
6277) where
6278    T: RecordOrReplay,
6279    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6280{
6281    let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
6282    if refusal.is_some() {
6283        crate::syscall_histogram::mark_refused::<T, G>(guest);
6284    }
6285    if let Some(refusal) = refusal.filter(|refusal| {
6286        matches!(
6287            refusal.operation,
6288            reverie::UnsupportedOperation::Signalfd | reverie::UnsupportedOperation::Pidfd
6289        )
6290    }) {
6291        tracing::warn!(
6292            "[dtid {dettid}] {sysno} refused by the backend: {}",
6293            refusal.diagnostic
6294        );
6295    }
6296    if let Some(failure) = tool_decided_injection_failure(refusal, dettid, sysno) {
6297        tracing::error!("{failure}");
6298        panic!("{failure}");
6299    }
6300}
6301
6302/// Report a named refusal through tracing, and, when the run ends
6303/// (`fail_closed`, the setting `panic_on_unsupported_syscalls`), directly on
6304/// stderr as well, as the `flock` refusal does, so that neither `--log=off` nor
6305/// `--log-file` hides why the run ended. A run that allows unsupported
6306/// operations goes on with the refusal's errno and has the reason in its log
6307/// only, as the refusals of a held signal and of a `pselect6` mask do: on a
6308/// backend whose tool runs inside the guest process, stderr is the guest's own
6309/// descriptor 2, which the guest may have pointed anywhere.
6310pub(crate) fn report_refusal_reason(fail_closed: bool, message: &str) {
6311    tracing::error!("{message}");
6312    if fail_closed {
6313        let _ = std::io::Write::write_fmt(
6314            &mut crate::util::RetryingStderr,
6315            format_args!("hermit: {message}\n"),
6316        );
6317    }
6318}
6319
6320/// The policy of `Detcore::refuse_unserviceable_operation`, for a caller that
6321/// holds the guest but not the tool. `panic_on_unsupported_syscalls` is the
6322/// setting of that name: the tool's own copy in the method, the guest's
6323/// configuration in `refuse_held_signal_loss`.
6324pub(crate) async fn refuse_unserviceable_operation_with<T, G>(
6325    guest: &mut G,
6326    panic_on_unsupported_syscalls: bool,
6327    sysno: Sysno,
6328    fallback: Errno,
6329    reason: Option<&str>,
6330) -> Result<i64, Error>
6331where
6332    T: RecordOrReplay,
6333    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6334{
6335    crate::syscall_histogram::mark_refused::<T, G>(guest);
6336    if !panic_on_unsupported_syscalls {
6337        return Err(fallback.into());
6338    }
6339    if guest.config().shutdown_on_unsupported_syscall {
6340        // Fail-closed policy: the operation is unserviceable and the config
6341        // forbids passing it through. Say why first: on an in-guest backend
6342        // the exit below ends only the guest process, and the launcher learns
6343        // the reason from the coordinator.
6344        let reason = match reason {
6345            Some(reason) => format!("{sysno}: {reason}"),
6346            None => format!(
6347                "{sysno} cannot be serviced on this backend (with \
6348                 --allow-unsupported-syscalls the guest would see {fallback})"
6349            ),
6350        };
6351        crate::tool_global::report_policy_refusal(guest, reason).await;
6352        crate::tool_global::unrecoverable_shutdown(
6353            guest,
6354            detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT,
6355        )
6356        .await;
6357    }
6358    if guest.config().exit_on_unsupported_syscall {
6359        return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(
6360            crate::UnsupportedSyscallError(sysno),
6361        )));
6362    }
6363    panic!("unserviceable operation on syscall: {sysno:?}");
6364}
6365
6366/// The signals the guest ignores, blocked for one wait that Detcore runs in the
6367/// kernel under the thread's own mask: the `epoll_wait` family (`ep_poll`), and
6368/// `poll`, `select`, and `ppoll` and `pselect6` naming no mask (`do_sys_poll`,
6369/// `core_sys_select`). Linux discards a signal the process ignores when it is
6370/// generated (`sig_ignored`), so it never ends such a wait, but it queues one
6371/// for a traced thread. An epoll wait then returned `EINTR` to the guest. A
6372/// poll-family wait ended with a restart code instead: a `poll` restarts
6373/// through `restart_syscall`, which Detcore refuses, and a `select`,
6374/// `pselect6` or `ppoll` runs again in place, or returns `EINTR` when Linux
6375/// cannot write back its time left (`poll_select_finish`). Blocked for the
6376/// wait, such a signal stays pending without ending it; once the guest's mask
6377/// is back it is delivered and ignored, as it was before.
6378/// The mask changes through the backend (`Guest::set_blocked_signals`, on
6379/// ptrace `PTRACE_SETSIGMASK`), so no syscall the guest or the recorder sees is
6380/// added. Replay, which serves the wait from the recording, raises the same
6381/// shield: the scheduler reads the thread's mask when it commits the wait's
6382/// request (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask`), and record and replay must
6383/// present the same one.
6384#[must_use]
6385pub(crate) struct IgnoredSignalShield {
6386    /// The guest's mask to put back, when the shield is up.
6387    guest_mask: Option<u64>,
6388}
6389
6390impl IgnoredSignalShield {
6391    /// No shield: the wait cannot block, or runs under its own temporary mask
6392    /// (or one the tracer cannot read).
6393    pub(crate) fn none() -> Self {
6394        Self { guest_mask: None }
6395    }
6396
6397    /// Blocks the signals the guest ignores and does not block, read from the
6398    /// kernel (`KernelSignalState::discarded_at_generation`). If the state
6399    /// cannot be read or the backend refuses the change and left the mask as
6400    /// it was, the wait runs under the guest's own mask, as it did before. A
6401    /// change that may have been written without being confirmed ends the
6402    /// run: the guest must not resume as if its mask were known
6403    /// (`MaskChangeRefused::Failed`).
6404    pub(crate) async fn raise<T, G>(guest: &mut G) -> Result<Self, Error>
6405    where
6406        T: RecordOrReplay,
6407        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6408    {
6409        let state = match crate::syscalls::read_guest_thread_signal_state(guest) {
6410            Ok(state) => state,
6411            Err(errno) => {
6412                tracing::debug!("[tid {}] no ignored-signal shield: {errno}", guest.tid());
6413                return Ok(Self::none());
6414            }
6415        };
6416        let Some(mask) = ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state) else {
6417            return Ok(Self::none());
6418        };
6419        match guest.set_blocked_signals(mask).await {
6420            Ok(guest_mask) => Ok(Self {
6421                guest_mask: Some(guest_mask),
6422            }),
6423            Err(refused) if shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(&refused) => {
6424                tracing::debug!("[tid {}] no ignored-signal shield: {refused}", guest.tid());
6425                Ok(Self::none())
6426            }
6427            Err(refused) => Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
6428                "[tid {}] could not block the signals the guest ignores ({mask:#x}) for a wait, \
6429                 and its signal mask is unknown: {refused}",
6430                guest.tid()
6431            ))),
6432        }
6433    }
6434
6435    /// Puts the guest's mask back. The guest must not resume under the
6436    /// shield, so a mask that cannot be put back ends the run.
6437    pub(crate) async fn lower<T, G>(mut self, guest: &mut G) -> Result<(), Error>
6438    where
6439        T: RecordOrReplay,
6440        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6441    {
6442        let Some(guest_mask) = self.guest_mask.take() else {
6443            return Ok(());
6444        };
6445        match guest.set_blocked_signals(guest_mask).await {
6446            Ok(_) | Err(MaskChangeRefused::Gone) => Ok(()),
6447            Err(refused) => Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
6448                "[tid {}] could not put back the guest's signal mask {guest_mask:#x} after a \
6449                 wait that blocked the signals it ignores: {refused}",
6450                guest.tid()
6451            ))),
6452        }
6453    }
6454}
6455
6456/// A shield is dropped with its mask still to put back only when the
6457/// backend cancelled the handler around it, which it does when the thread
6458/// dies during the wait or an injection (a sibling's `exit_group` or
6459/// `execve`, a SIGKILL), or when a backend error is ending the run. Drop
6460/// cannot tell those apart, so its log claims neither: it says only that
6461/// the handler ended with the mask unrestored.
6462/// The log line for a shield dropped with its mask still to put back.
6463/// It must not claim the thread is gone: Drop cannot prove that (the
6464/// handler may also be cancelled by a backend error ending the run).
6465fn shield_drop_message(guest_mask: u64) -> String {
6466    format!(
6467        "an ignored-signal shield ended with its handler, leaving the guest's mask \
6468         {guest_mask:#x} unrestored; the handler ended before the mask could be put \
6469         back (the thread may have died, or the run may be ending)"
6470    )
6471}
6472
6473impl Drop for IgnoredSignalShield {
6474    fn drop(&mut self) {
6475        if let Some(guest_mask) = self.guest_mask {
6476            tracing::debug!("{}", shield_drop_message(guest_mask));
6477        }
6478    }
6479}
6480
6481/// Whether a refused shield change left the thread's mask as it was, so the
6482/// wait can run under it: every refusal but a failure after which the backend
6483/// could not confirm the mask (`MaskChangeRefused::Failed`'s `mask_unknown`).
6484fn shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(refused: &MaskChangeRefused) -> bool {
6485    !matches!(
6486        refused,
6487        MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
6488            mask_unknown: true,
6489            ..
6490        }
6491    )
6492}
6493
6494/// The mask an ignored-signal shield sets over `state`: the thread's mask and
6495/// the signals it would discard at generation, or `None` when there are none
6496/// (`IgnoredSignalShield`).
6497fn ignored_signal_shield_mask(state: &KernelSignalState) -> Option<KernelSigset> {
6498    let ignored = state.discarded_at_generation();
6499    (ignored != 0).then_some(state.blocked | ignored)
6500}
6501
6502/// Refuse the guest's `sysno` call when its wait ended with a
6503/// [`HeldSignalRefusal`], through the unsupported-operation policy
6504/// (`refuse_unserviceable_operation_with`): a fail-closed run, which ordinary
6505/// `hermit run` is, ends with the policy's exit, and a run started with
6506/// `--allow-unsupported-syscalls` gets `ERESTARTNOINTR`, the transparent
6507/// restart that such a wait returned before (round-10 High 1 on
6508/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). The message names the call,
6509/// the signals and that pull request. Callers pass the wait's result after the
6510/// wait has put the guest's mask back. Every other result passes through.
6511///
6512/// Whether a wait meets such a stop can depend on host timing, as a signal
6513/// sent from outside the guest does, so a refusal can be host-timed: it
6514/// replaces a run that would have gone on to depend on that timing.
6515pub(crate) async fn refuse_held_signal_loss<T, G>(
6516    guest: &mut G,
6517    sysno: Sysno,
6518    result: Result<i64, Error>,
6519) -> Result<i64, Error>
6520where
6521    T: RecordOrReplay,
6522    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6523{
6524    use std::io::Write as _;
6525    let refusal = match &result {
6526        Err(Error::Tool(error)) => match error.downcast_ref::<HeldSignalRefusal>() {
6527            Some(refusal) => HeldSignalRefusal {
6528                wait: Some(sysno),
6529                ..*refusal
6530            },
6531            None => return result,
6532        },
6533        _ => return result,
6534    };
6535    let panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = guest.config().panic_on_unsupported_syscalls;
6536    tracing::error!("[tid {}] {}", guest.tid(), refusal);
6537    if panic_on_unsupported_syscalls {
6538        // The run ends: report why even when logging is disabled or redirected,
6539        // as the refusal of a nonleader exec does.
6540        let _ = writeln!(crate::util::RetryingStderr, "{refusal}");
6541    }
6542    refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
6543        guest,
6544        panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
6545        sysno,
6546        Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR,
6547        None,
6548    )
6549    .await
6550}
6551
6552/// Signal handling for one blocking wait whose interruption is decided from the
6553/// kernel's signal state (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`).
6554///
6555/// A wait ends early only for a signal that would end it natively: one the guest
6556/// does not block and that is caught, or whose default action terminates or stops
6557/// the process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Blocked,
6558/// ignored, and default-ignored signals do not end it, and neither does a default
6559/// job-control stop when `defers_default_stops` is set
6560/// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`), apart from the stops that
6561/// `inject_absorbing` cannot absorb safely, which end it with a restart.
6562///
6563/// The first probe runs under the guest's own mask. If it would block, `block`
6564/// blocks every blockable signal for the rest of the wait, so later probes cannot
6565/// be stopped by one and every signal that arrives stays pending in the kernel,
6566/// where `/proc` reports it. `interrupted_with_state` classifies the pending set
6567/// against the guest's mask and dispositions each turn, and `restore` puts the
6568/// guest's mask back before the call returns, so a pending interrupting signal
6569/// is delivered as the call returns its restart errno.
6570///
6571/// Probes and the mask change go through `inject_absorbing`, never
6572/// `inject_with_retry`. A signal that stops the guest around an injection is
6573/// dequeued from the kernel and held by the backend in a single slot, so a blind
6574/// retry that is stopped again would replace it. `inject_absorbing` works out
6575/// from `/proc` which signal the backend holds and injects again only when that
6576/// signal would not end the wait natively. Before the mask is set, a signal
6577/// pending at the turn's `/proc` read that would end the wait is reported by
6578/// `interrupted_with_state`, and any other unblocked one stops the next
6579/// injection and is absorbed; a signal that arrives after the read can stop an
6580/// injection in a way that cannot be identified, and is held without ending the
6581/// wait, so the wait keeps its deadline and its checks, unless the backend held
6582/// a signal whose loss matters, which ends the wait with a
6583/// [`HeldSignalRefusal`] (`inject_absorbing`).
6584/// Afterwards only a signal that cannot be blocked can stop an injection. A stop
6585/// after a probe ran replaces its result, so a probe that consumed something (an
6586/// edge-triggered event, a dequeued signal) loses it; that remains a known gap.
6587///
6588/// No failure of this machinery reaches the guest as an errno the wait call
6589/// cannot return. A `/proc` read that fails for a thread that still exists, or a
6590/// guest mask that cannot be put back, ends the run with a
6591/// [`BlockedWaitSignalError`]; a thread that no longer exists gets
6592/// `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which nothing observes (`read_wait_signal_state`). If the
6593/// mask cannot be changed at all (no scratch room below the guest's stack
6594/// pointer, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3328), `block` leaves the
6595/// guest's own mask in place and every later probe runs under it, as the first
6596/// probe does.
6597/// The real-time signals, 32 to 64, as kernel sigset bits.
6598pub(crate) const REAL_TIME_SIGNALS: KernelSigset = !0 << 31;
6599
6600/// The signals a thread whose mask becomes `mask` lets the kernel take from
6601/// its queues: those `mask` does not block, split into the ones whose delivery
6602/// the guest observes and the ones Linux discards on delivery because their
6603/// disposition is `SIG_IGN`.
6604pub(crate) fn unblocked_by(
6605    state: &KernelSignalState,
6606    mask: KernelSigset,
6607) -> (KernelSigset, KernelSigset) {
6608    unblocked_by_ignored(state.ignored, mask)
6609}
6610
6611/// [`unblocked_by`] given only the thread's ignored set, from wherever it
6612/// comes (the kernel's `/proc` view or Detcore's copy).
6613pub(crate) fn unblocked_by_ignored(
6614    ignored: KernelSigset,
6615    mask: KernelSigset,
6616) -> (KernelSigset, KernelSigset) {
6617    let unblocked = !mask;
6618    (unblocked & !ignored, unblocked & ignored)
6619}
6620
6621/// The real-time timer expirations among `candidates` (a kernel sigset) that
6622/// are pending for the calling thread's process because every thread blocked
6623/// them when they expired (`Scheduler::pending_real_time_expirations`,
6624/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089). 0 without asking the
6625/// scheduler until one has been kept pending in this run
6626/// (`scheduler::real_time_expiration_kept_pending`), or when `candidates`
6627/// holds no real-time signal. Asked in the calling thread's turn.
6628pub(crate) async fn pending_real_time_among<T, G>(guest: &mut G, candidates: KernelSigset) -> u64
6629where
6630    T: RecordOrReplay,
6631    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6632{
6633    let candidates = candidates & REAL_TIME_SIGNALS;
6634    if candidates == 0 || !crate::scheduler::real_time_expiration_kept_pending() {
6635        return 0;
6636    }
6637    let Some(detpid) = guest.thread_state().detpid else {
6638        return 0;
6639    };
6640    crate::tool_global::pending_real_time_expirations(guest, detpid).await & candidates
6641}
6642
6643/// Where a call lets the guest observe the signals in `observable` (deliver,
6644/// dequeue or report them), refuse the run by name if one of the `pending`
6645/// real-time timer expirations (`pending_real_time_among`) is among them, and
6646/// discard the pending ones in `discarded`, which Linux discards there.
6647pub(crate) async fn act_on_pending_real_time<T, G>(
6648    guest: &mut G,
6649    pending: KernelSigset,
6650    observable: KernelSigset,
6651    discarded: KernelSigset,
6652) where
6653    T: RecordOrReplay,
6654    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6655{
6656    let observed = pending & observable;
6657    if observed != 0 {
6658        crate::scheduler::refuse_real_time_expiration(observed.trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1);
6659    }
6660    if pending & discarded != 0
6661        && let Some(detpid) = guest.thread_state().detpid
6662    {
6663        crate::tool_global::discard_pending_real_time_expirations(
6664            guest,
6665            detpid,
6666            pending & discarded,
6667        )
6668        .await;
6669    }
6670}
6671
6672/// For a call that runs under the temporary mask `mask`: refuse by name for a
6673/// pending real-time timer expiration the mask lets the kernel deliver, and
6674/// discard one it lets the kernel discard. Reads the thread's dispositions
6675/// only when one is pending.
6676pub(crate) async fn observe_under_mask<T, G>(guest: &mut G, mask: KernelSigset) -> Result<(), Error>
6677where
6678    T: RecordOrReplay,
6679    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6680{
6681    let pending = pending_real_time_among(guest, !mask).await;
6682    if pending != 0 {
6683        let ignored = match crate::syscalls::signal_shadow::copied_dispositions(guest) {
6684            Some(copied) => copied.ignored,
6685            None => crate::syscalls::read_guest_wait_signal_state(guest)?.ignored,
6686        };
6687        let (observable, discarded) = unblocked_by_ignored(ignored, mask);
6688        act_on_pending_real_time(guest, pending, observable, discarded).await;
6689    }
6690    Ok(())
6691}
6692
6693pub(crate) struct KernelSignalWait {
6694    pid: reverie::Pid,
6695    tid: reverie::Pid,
6696    /// Signals the wait itself consumes (rt_sigtimedwait's set), which never
6697    /// interrupt it.
6698    consumed: KernelSigset,
6699    /// Whether a default job-control stop leaves the wait running, because Linux's
6700    /// restart of the call keeps its deadline
6701    /// (`NonblockableSyscall::restart_keeps_deadline`).
6702    defers_default_stops: bool,
6703    /// The errno that ends the wait for an interrupting signal: the restart code
6704    /// Linux uses for the call (`NonblockableSyscall::kernel_restart_errno`). A
6705    /// signal the backend holds turns `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` into `ERESTARTNOHAND`
6706    /// (`held_signal_restart_errno`).
6707    restart_errno: Errno,
6708    /// Signals that never end the wait, even ones that would end it natively.
6709    /// They stay pending in the kernel, or held by the backend, and are
6710    /// delivered as the call returns, once the guest's mask is put back. In
6711    /// every wait but `select`'s and `pselect6`'s (`for_select`) this is
6712    /// `SIGCHLD`, whichever process sent it: the kernel also posts one for a
6713    /// child's exit, stop or continue at a moment set by host timing, and
6714    /// `/proc` shows no siginfo that would tell the two apart
6715    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). The scheduler's own
6716    /// send of a `SIGCHLD` to this thread at a commit point lifts the hold for the
6717    /// turn whose resume names it (`admit`,
6718    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). The gated loop adds,
6719    /// in each of its turns, every signal a host-timed source armed by a guest
6720    /// can post to this process (`hold_until_return`).
6721    held_until_return: KernelSigset,
6722    /// Whether the wait has a finite deadline (`with_deadline`). Hermit cannot
6723    /// install the restart block with which Linux keeps the absolute deadline
6724    /// of a restarted `poll` or timed futex wait, and a restarted `ppoll`,
6725    /// `epoll_wait`, `epoll_pwait` or `rt_sigtimedwait` runs again with the
6726    /// guest's unchanged timeout. So a transparent restart would start the
6727    /// timeout again, and such a wait never ends with `ERESTARTNOINTR`
6728    /// (`inject_absorbing`).
6729    deadline: bool,
6730    /// The guest's own mask while the wait runs with every signal blocked.
6731    saved_mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
6732    /// `block` could not change the mask, so probes run under the guest's own.
6733    unblockable: bool,
6734    /// `saved_mask` was installed by `block_in_place`, through
6735    /// `Guest::set_blocked_signals`, so `restore` puts it back the same way,
6736    /// with no injection and no scratch memory.
6737    blocked_in_place: bool,
6738    /// The signal the backend holds since `inject_absorbing` absorbed a stop;
6739    /// `None` also after a stop it could not identify (`held_unidentified`).
6740    held: Option<HeldSignal>,
6741    /// The backend holds a signal from a stop that `inject_absorbing` could not
6742    /// identify, which may be one whose loss matters, so no later stop may
6743    /// replace it (`would_replace_precious`).
6744    held_unidentified: bool,
6745    /// The signals `hold_until_return` added because a host-timed source armed
6746    /// by a guest can post them; a committed signal never lifts these
6747    /// (`admit`).
6748    host_timed: KernelSigset,
6749    /// Signals the scheduler committed to this thread in the current turn,
6750    /// which end the wait even though it holds them (`admit`).
6751    committed: KernelSigset,
6752    /// The `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, which the schedule recorded in
6753    /// its private queue, admitted in the current turn (`admit_under_block`):
6754    /// it ends the wait from the thread's own queue only, even though the
6755    /// wait holds it (R2b-2 stage 3,
6756    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
6757    private: KernelSigset,
6758    /// The mask the wait sleeps under, when it is not the guest's own: the
6759    /// temporary mask of a `pselect6` (`with_wait_mask`). A signal decides
6760    /// against it whether it ends the wait; `restore` still puts back the
6761    /// guest's own mask (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3991).
6762    wait_mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
6763}
6764
6765/// A signal that stopped one of a wait's injections and that the backend holds
6766/// for delivery when the guest resumes (`KernelSignalWait::inject_absorbing`).
6767#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
6768struct HeldSignal {
6769    signal: i32,
6770    queue: SignalQueue,
6771    kind: HeldKind,
6772}
6773
6774/// Whether losing a held signal, which a later stop would replace, changes what
6775/// the guest or the scheduler observes.
6776#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd)]
6777enum HeldKind {
6778    /// Its delivery does nothing: it is ignored, or default-ignored and not
6779    /// `SIGCHLD`.
6780    Harmless,
6781    /// Its delivery matters, or is kept as if it did: a signal the wait holds
6782    /// until the call returns (`held_until_return`), which may run a handler
6783    /// then, any other `SIGCHLD`, or a default job-control stop that the wait
6784    /// defers.
6785    Precious,
6786}
6787
6788/// How a wait would lose a signal that the backend holds, or deliver it in
6789/// place of the result Linux gives (`HeldSignalRefusal`).
6790#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
6791pub(crate) enum HeldSignalLoss {
6792    /// Another pending signal would stop the next injection, and the backend,
6793    /// which has one slot for a held signal, would drop the held one for it.
6794    Replaced,
6795    /// A stop that `/proc` cannot identify replaced a held signal whose loss
6796    /// matters (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one that could not be identified
6797    /// either and so may matter.
6798    UnidentifiedStop,
6799    /// The wait reached `MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS` absorbed stops while the backend
6800    /// held a signal whose loss matters or that could not be identified.
6801    StopBound,
6802    /// A signal that a wait without a deadline consumes stopped an injection,
6803    /// so the backend holds it and delivers it rather than the wait returning
6804    /// it, and either it is one the wait holds until the call returns
6805    /// (`held_until_return`) or it replaced a held signal whose loss matters.
6806    Consumed,
6807    /// A signal stopped an injection of `restore`, which puts the guest's mask
6808    /// back and so must run whatever is pending, and the backend dropped a held
6809    /// signal whose loss matters, or one that could not be identified, for it.
6810    Restoration,
6811}
6812
6813/// A wait that ends because going on, or restarting the call, would lose a
6814/// signal the backend holds, or deliver it in place of the result Linux gives.
6815///
6816/// Every path that used to end such a wait with a fallback that returns
6817/// success (a transparent `ERESTARTNOINTR` restart, or a wait that went on and
6818/// let a stop replace the held signal) returns this instead (round-10 High 1 on
6819/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). The wait puts the guest's mask
6820/// back, and its caller then applies the unsupported-operation policy
6821/// (`refuse_held_signal_loss`). A complete successful repair preserving signal
6822/// information needs additional framework support with the current generic
6823/// API: the backend holds one signal, does not say which, and delivers it
6824/// without the tool. A Detcore-only refusal or capability withdrawal can
6825/// prevent the determinism regression.
6826#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
6827pub(crate) struct HeldSignalRefusal {
6828    /// The guest call whose wait ends, once the caller names it
6829    /// (`refuse_held_signal_loss`).
6830    pub(crate) wait: Option<Sysno>,
6831    /// The signal the backend holds that would be lost or delivered wrongly;
6832    /// `None` when it could not be identified.
6833    pub(crate) held: Option<i32>,
6834    /// The signal that would replace it, or that stopped the injection, when
6835    /// known.
6836    pub(crate) replacing: Option<i32>,
6837    /// How it would be lost.
6838    pub(crate) loss: HeldSignalLoss,
6839}
6840
6841/// A signal's name, such as `SIGCHLD`, or its number for a real-time signal.
6842fn signal_label(signal: Option<i32>) -> String {
6843    match signal {
6844        Some(signal) => match nix::sys::signal::Signal::try_from(signal) {
6845            Ok(named) => named.as_str().to_string(),
