6846            Err(_) => format!("signal {signal}"),
6847        },
6848        None => "a signal that could not be identified".to_string(),
6849    }
6850}
6851
6852impl std::fmt::Display for HeldSignalRefusal {
6853    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
6854        let wait = self
6855            .wait
6856            .map_or_else(|| "a blocking".to_string(), |sysno| sysno.to_string());
6857        let held = match self.held {
6858            Some(_) => format!("the held signal {}", signal_label(self.held)),
6859            None => "a held signal that could not be identified".to_string(),
6860        };
6861        let replacing = signal_label(self.replacing);
6862        match self.loss {
6863            HeldSignalLoss::Replaced => write!(
6864                f,
6865                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: the pending {replacing} \
6866                 would stop the next injection and replace it"
6867            )?,
6868            HeldSignalLoss::UnidentifiedStop => write!(
6869                f,
6870                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: a signal stop that /proc \
6871                 cannot identify replaced it"
6872            )?,
6873            HeldSignalLoss::StopBound => write!(
6874                f,
6875                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: the wait absorbed the \
6876                 maximum number of signal stops"
6877            )?,
6878            HeldSignalLoss::Consumed => {
6879                write!(
6880                    f,
6881                    "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot return {replacing}, which it consumes: \
6882                     the signal stopped an injection, so the backend would deliver it instead"
6883                )?;
6884                if self.held.is_some() {
6885                    write!(f, ", in place of {held}")?;
6886                }
6887            }
6888            HeldSignalLoss::Restoration => write!(
6889                f,
6890                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: {replacing} stopped the \
6891                 injection that puts the guest's signal mask back and replaced it"
6892            )?,
6893        }
6894        write!(
6895            f,
6896            " (scope reduction of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361; rerun with \
6897             --allow-unsupported-syscalls to restart the call instead)"
6898        )
6899    }
6900}
6901
6902impl std::error::Error for HeldSignalRefusal {}
6903
6904/// What a signal that stopped one of a wait's injections means for the wait.
6905#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
6906enum StopVerdict {
6907    /// The wait goes on; the backend holds the signal.
6908    Absorb(HeldKind),
6909    /// The wait ends with this errno.
6910    End(Errno),
6911}
6912
6913/// The first real-time signal number in the kernel. A standard signal below it
6914/// is pending at most once; a second one sent while it is pending is merged.
6915const KERNEL_SIGRTMIN: i32 = 32;
6916
6917impl KernelSignalWait {
6918    pub(crate) fn new<T, G>(
6919        guest: &G,
6920        consumed: KernelSigset,
6921        defers_default_stops: bool,
6922        restart_errno: Errno,
6923    ) -> Self
6924    where
6925        T: RecordOrReplay,
6926        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6927    {
6928        Self {
6929            pid: guest.pid(),
6930            tid: guest.tid(),
6931            consumed,
6932            defers_default_stops,
6933            restart_errno,
6934            held_until_return: kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
6935            deadline: false,
6936            saved_mask: None,
6937            unblockable: false,
6938            blocked_in_place: false,
6939            held: None,
6940            held_unidentified: false,
6941            host_timed: 0,
6942            committed: 0,
6943            private: 0,
6944            wait_mask: None,
6945        }
6946    }
6947
6948    /// This wait, with a finite deadline when `deadline` is set (the `deadline`
6949    /// field): no fallback of `inject_absorbing` then ends it with
6950    /// `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which would start the guest's timeout again.
6951    pub(crate) fn with_deadline(self, deadline: bool) -> Self {
6952        Self { deadline, ..self }
6953    }
6954
6955    /// The wait of `select` and of `pselect6`, which holds no signal until the
6956    /// call returns (`held_until_return` is empty); a `pselect6` with a
6957    /// temporary mask adds it with `with_wait_mask`:
6958    /// any pending signal that could interrupt it ends it, `SIGCHLD` included.
6959    ///
6960    /// Linux ends these calls with `ERESTARTNOHAND` whenever no descriptor is
6961    /// ready and a signal is pending (`core_sys_select`), so a caught `SIGCHLD`
6962    /// ends them whoever sent it. Detcore's select and pselect6 waits did the
6963    /// same before this machinery existed: their probes ran under the guest's
6964    /// own mask, and a pending caught signal stopped one.
6965    ///
6966    /// This is a known gap that these waits had before, and it is left as it
6967    /// was: the `SIGCHLD` the kernel posts for a child's exit, stop or continue
6968    /// ends the wait at the first turn whose read sees it, and host timing
6969    /// decides which turn that is (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
6970    /// Every other wait holds `SIGCHLD` until it returns, unless the scheduler
6971    /// commits it to the thread in that turn (`admit`).
6972    pub(crate) fn for_select<T, G>(guest: &G) -> Self
6973    where
6974        T: RecordOrReplay,
6975        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6976    {
6977        Self {
6978            held_until_return: 0,
6979            ..Self::new(guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
6980        }
6981    }
6982
6983    /// This wait, sleeping under `mask` instead of the guest's own (`wait_mask`):
6984    /// a `pselect6` with a temporary mask. Linux installs that mask for the
6985    /// whole call, so a signal it blocks never ends the call, even one the
6986    /// guest's own mask leaves unblocked, and one it leaves unblocked ends the
6987    /// call although the guest's own mask blocks it.
6988    pub(crate) fn with_wait_mask(self, mask: Option<KernelSigset>) -> Self {
6989        Self {
6990            wait_mask: mask,
6991            ..self
6992        }
6993    }
6994
6995    /// The mask Linux's `blocked` holds for the waiting thread when the
6996    /// kernel's `SigBlk` does not show it: the wait's temporary mask
6997    /// (`wait_mask`), or else the guest's own mask once `block` has replaced
6998    /// it (`saved_mask`). `None` while `SigBlk` is the guest's own mask.
6999    pub(crate) fn effective_mask(&self) -> Option<KernelSigset> {
7000        self.wait_mask.or(self.saved_mask)
7001    }
7002
7003    /// Whether the backend holds a signal from a stop of one of this wait's
7004    /// injections (`held`, `held_unidentified`), which it delivers when the
7005    /// guest resumes.
7006    pub(crate) fn holds_signal(&self) -> bool {
7007        self.held.is_some() || self.held_unidentified
7008    }
7009
7010    /// Whether a signal that ends the wait, pending in the kernel per `state`,
7011    /// is one the guest's own mask blocks: it ends the wait only because the
7012    /// wait mask (`with_wait_mask`) leaves it unblocked, and it stays pending
7013    /// when the guest's own mask is put back. A signal the wait holds until
7014    /// the call returns counts once the scheduler committed it in this turn
7015    /// (`admit`), as in `interrupted_with_state`: otherwise a
7016    /// committed `SIGCHLD` that only the wait mask lets in ended the call
7017    /// without its handler (Claude review of
7018    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4217).
7019    pub(crate) fn interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&self, state: &KernelSignalState) -> bool {
7020        let own_mask = self.saved_mask.unwrap_or(state.blocked);
7021        let held_until_return = self.held_until_return & !self.committed;
7022        let could_interrupt = self.could_interrupt(state);
7023        let interrupting = (state.pending & !held_until_return
7024            | state.thread_pending & self.private)
7025            & could_interrupt;
7026        self.wait_mask.is_some() && interrupting & own_mask != 0
7027    }
7028
7029    /// Adds `signals` to the ones this wait holds until the call returns
7030    /// (`held_until_return`). The gated loop passes, in each of its turns, the
7031    /// signals that a host-timed source armed by a guest can post to this
7032    /// process, such as a parent-death signal (`tool_global::host_timed_signals`):
7033    /// the kernel posts those at a moment set by host timing, so ending the wait
7034    /// for one would make the run depend on host timing. Never called for a
7035    /// `select` wait (`for_select`), which holds nothing.
7036    pub(crate) fn hold_until_return(&mut self, signals: KernelSigset) {
7037        self.held_until_return |= signals;
7038        self.host_timed |= signals;
7039    }
7040
7041    /// Sets the signals the scheduler committed to this thread in this turn
7042    /// (`committed`): its resume named them (`ResumeStatus::Signaled`). Such a
7043    /// signal was sent at a fixed point of the schedule, so a wait may end for
7044    /// it although the wait holds it, unless a host-timed source can post it
7045    /// too (`host_timed`). The loop passes a committed `SIGCHLD`, which the
7046    /// scheduler sends at a commit point (a child's child-exit timer, or a
7047    /// POSIX timer whose signal is `SIGCHLD`); the kernel's
7048    /// own copy of it, posted at a host-timed moment, decides nothing, since
7049    /// only the resume that names it lifts the hold, for that turn alone
7050    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
7051    ///
7052    /// `private` is the `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, recorded in its
7053    /// private queue, that the turn admits (`admit_under_block`): it lifts the
7054    /// hold only against the thread's own queue, for this turn alone.
7055    pub(crate) fn admit(&mut self, committed: KernelSigset, private: KernelSigset) {
7056        self.committed = committed & !self.host_timed;
7057        self.private = private & !self.host_timed;
7058    }
7059
7060    /// The private `SIGCHLD` this turn admits (`admit`), from `recorded`, the
7061    /// schedule's record (`Scheduler::private_sigchld`). A turn that admits a
7062    /// `SIGCHLD`, committed or recorded, first blocks every blockable signal
7063    /// in place, before any injection of the turn, and publishes the guest's
7064    /// mask while it holds (`block_in_place`, `publish_wait_mask`). The
7065    /// recorded one is then kept only while that block holds (`saved_mask`;
7066    /// an earlier injected `block` that failed leaves none), and only if the
7067    /// thread's own queue holds `SIGCHLD`, read after the block: only this
7068    /// stopped thread can take it from there, and no injection can now. If
7069    /// the setter refuses, the wait keeps its fallback, the injected `block`
7070    /// after the first probe (rev4 1f), and holds the recorded `SIGCHLD` as
7071    /// before.
7072    pub(crate) async fn admit_under_block<T, G>(
7073        &mut self,
7074        guest: &mut G,
7075        committed: KernelSigset,
7076        recorded: KernelSigset,
7077        host_timed: KernelSigset,
7078        published: &mut PublishedWaitMask,
7079    ) -> Result<KernelSigset, Error>
7080    where
7081        T: RecordOrReplay,
7082        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7083    {
7084        if (committed | recorded) & !host_timed == 0 {
7085            return Ok(0);
7086        }
7087        if self.needs_block() {
7088            if self.block_in_place(guest, host_timed).await? {
7089                publish_wait_mask(guest, self.effective_mask(), published).await;
7090            } else {
7091                // Keep today's fallback for this wait.
7092                self.unblockable = false;
7093            }
7094        }
7095        if recorded == 0 || self.saved_mask.is_none() {
7096            return Ok(0);
7097        }
7098        let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
7099        Ok(recorded & state.thread_pending)
7100    }
7101
7102    /// Whether, of the signals that end the wait per `state`, only signals the
7103    /// scheduler committed in this turn do (`admit`): without them
7104    /// the wait would go on.
7105    pub(crate) fn interrupts_only_by_committed(&self, state: &KernelSignalState) -> bool {
7106        let held = self.held.map_or(0, |held| kernel_sigset_bit(held.signal));
7107        let interrupting = (state.pending | held) & self.could_interrupt(state);
7108        (self.committed | self.private) != 0 && interrupting & !self.held_until_return == 0
7109    }
7110
7111    /// Whether the caller should still call `block`: it has neither blocked the
7112    /// guest's signals nor found that it cannot.
7113    pub(crate) fn needs_block(&self) -> bool {
7114        self.saved_mask.is_none() && !self.unblockable
7115    }
7116
7117    /// The signals that would end the wait natively under the guest's mask, given
7118    /// the kernel's `state`.
7119    /// The signals whose pending presence this wait would observe now: those
7120    /// it consumes, and those that would end it under the guest's mask, or
7121    /// the wait mask when it has one (`could_interrupt`). Read from the kernel's state in this turn.
7122    pub(crate) fn observable_now<T, G>(&self, guest: &G) -> Result<KernelSigset, Error>
7123    where
7124        T: RecordOrReplay,
7125        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7126    {
7127        let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
7128        Ok(self.consumed | self.could_interrupt(&state))
7129    }
7130
7131    fn could_interrupt(&self, state: &KernelSignalState) -> KernelSigset {
7132        let guest_mask = self.wait_mask.or(self.saved_mask).unwrap_or(state.blocked);
7133        state.interrupting_wait(guest_mask, self.defers_default_stops) & !self.consumed
7134    }
7135
7136    /// `interrupted_with_state` without the state, for the tests, which read
7137    /// their own thread's `/proc` state.
7138    #[cfg(test)]
7139    pub(crate) fn interrupted(&self) -> Result<bool, Error> {
7140        Ok(self
7141            .interrupted_in(read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?)
7142            .0)
7143    }
7144
7145    /// Whether a signal that would end the wait natively is pending, in which case
7146    /// the caller returns the call's restart errno, with the kernel's state that
7147    /// this read, which `inject_absorbing_after` takes as its first read in the same
7148    /// turn. The guest thread has been stopped inside the call since it was
7149    /// intercepted, so such a signal arrived while the call was waiting, and Linux
7150    /// returns the restart errno for that. Linux reports a source that was ready
7151    /// when the call began, or an argument error, before any pending signal, so
7152    /// `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` runs its first probe before
7153    /// this check (`inject_first_probe`). There, a source that becomes ready in a
7154    /// later turn in which a signal is also pending is put behind the signal,
7155    /// because the turn cannot tell which came first. The waits of `select` and
7156    /// `pselect6` run every probe before this check, as Linux's do_select polls
7157    /// every descriptor on each pass before it tests for a pending signal. A
7158    /// signal the wait holds until the call returns (`held_until_return`) never
7159    /// counts. A signal that the backend holds since `inject_absorbing` absorbed
7160    /// it counts as pending. A failed read is never returned as the call's errno
7161    /// (`read_wait_signal_state`).
7162    pub(crate) fn interrupted_with_state<T, G>(
7163        &self,
7164        guest: &G,
7165    ) -> Result<(bool, KernelSignalState), Error>
7166    where
7167        T: RecordOrReplay,
7168        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7169    {
7170        Ok(self.interrupted_in(crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?))
7171    }
7172
7173    /// [`Self::interrupted_with_state`] given the thread's state.
7174    fn interrupted_in(&self, state: KernelSignalState) -> (bool, KernelSignalState) {
7175        let could_interrupt = self.could_interrupt(&state);
7176        let held = self.held.map_or(0, |held| kernel_sigset_bit(held.signal));
7177        let held_until_return = self.held_until_return & !self.committed;
7178        // An admitted private `SIGCHLD` counts against the thread's own queue
7179        // only (`admit`).
7180        let interrupting = ((state.pending | held) & !held_until_return
7181            | state.thread_pending & self.private)
7182            & could_interrupt;
7183        if interrupting != 0 {
7184            tracing::trace!(
7185                "[tid {}] pending signals {:#x} interrupt a blocking wait",
7186                self.tid,
7187                interrupting
7188            );
7189        }
7190        (interrupting != 0, state)
7191    }
7192
7193    /// Inject `call`, a probe or a mask change, absorbing the signal stops that do
7194    /// not end the wait. `Ok` carries the call's own result; `Err` ends the wait.
7195    ///
7196    /// A signal that stops the guest around an injection is dequeued from the
7197    /// kernel and held by the backend, which delivers it when the guest resumes,
7198    /// and the injection returns a restart errno instead of the call's result.
7199    /// The backend does not say which signal it holds, so the kernel's state is
7200    /// read before each injection (in a polling turn of
7201    /// `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` under the full mask, the
7202    /// turn's own read: `inject_absorbing_after`), which names the signal the
7203    /// kernel dequeues next (`KernelSignalState::next_dequeued`), and again
7204    /// after a stop. The stop is identified only if exactly that signal left its queue
7205    /// and the mask and dispositions did not change; it then decides:
7206    ///
7207    /// - A signal the wait consumes (`consumed`) is delivered rather than
7208    ///   consumed. In a wait without a deadline it ends the wait with
7209    ///   `ERESTARTNOINTR`, and the call runs again, unless the wait holds it
7210    ///   until the call returns (`held_until_return`), so that its delivery now
7211    ///   could follow host timing: then the wait ends with a
7212    ///   [`HeldSignalRefusal`]. In a wait with a deadline (`deadline`) it is
7213    ///   classified as if the wait did not consume it, by the rules below.
7214    /// - A signal that would end the wait natively ends it with the restart
7215    ///   errno, except a signal the wait holds until the call returns
7216    ///   (`held_until_return`), which is held.
7217    /// - Any other `SIGCHLD`, and a default job-control stop that the wait
7218    ///   defers, are held, and so are an ignored signal and a default-ignored
7219    ///   one. The injection runs again.
7220    /// - A signal that the wait mask (`with_wait_mask`) blocks is held: Linux
7221    ///   keeps it pending until the call returns.
7222    /// - Anything else, which is the backend's own preemption signal, ends the
7223    ///   wait with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, or is held in a wait with a deadline.
7224    ///
7225    /// A pending signal that would end the wait ends it before the injection,
7226    /// with the restart errno, so it is never held, except by a probe made by
7227    /// `inject_first_probe`: the first probe of a wait, and every probe of the
7228    /// waits of `select` and `pselect6`. A stop that cannot be identified, by a
7229    /// signal that arrived after the read, does not end the wait while the
7230    /// backend held nothing whose loss matters: the backend holds that signal
7231    /// in place of any held one and the injection runs again, as the blind
7232    /// retry before this machinery did, so the wait keeps its deadline and
7233    /// every check that ends it. Which signal it was would need the backend to
7234    /// say, so it is recorded only as unidentified (`held_unidentified`), and
7235    /// it is delivered as the call returns.
7236    ///
7237    /// The backend has one slot for a held signal, and a stop replaces what it
7238    /// holds. A held signal whose loss matters (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one
7239    /// that could not be identified and so may matter, is never given up for a
7240    /// result that reads as success, with or without a deadline:
7241    ///
7242    /// - An injection that another pending signal would stop is not made. If
7243    ///   the held signal would end the wait natively, the wait ends with the
7244    ///   restart errno, as Linux ends it for that signal; otherwise it ends
7245    ///   with a `HeldSignalRefusal`. The same standard signal on the same queue
7246    ///   is the exception, because Linux merges the two.
7247    /// - A stop that cannot be identified, which has already replaced such a
7248    ///   signal, ends the wait with a `HeldSignalRefusal`.
7249    /// - After `MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS` absorbed stops, a wait without a deadline
7250    ///   ends with a `HeldSignalRefusal`, or with `ERESTARTNOINTR` when the
7251    ///   backend holds nothing whose loss matters. A wait with a deadline,
7252    ///   whose restart would start the guest's timeout again, absorbs stops
7253    ///   without a bound.
7254    ///
7255    /// Each refusal is a scope reduction. It replaces a transparent
7256    /// `ERESTARTNOINTR` restart, or, in a wait with a deadline, an injection
7257    /// that went on and let a stop replace the held signal (round-10 High 1 on
7258    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361): the restart made the
7259    /// backend deliver the held signal before the wait completed, at a moment
7260    /// host timing could set. A complete successful repair preserving signal
7261    /// information needs additional framework support with the current generic
7262    /// API. A Detcore-only refusal or capability withdrawal can prevent the
7263    /// determinism regression.
7264    ///
7265    /// In a probe made by `inject_first_probe` that two pending signals would
7266    /// stop in turn, the first of which would end the wait, the wait ends with
7267    /// the restart errno before the probe has run, so a ready source, or an
7268    /// argument error, is reported behind the signal: the order compromise that
7269    /// a later turn of `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` already
7270    /// makes (`interrupted_with_state`).
7271    pub(crate) async fn inject_absorbing<T, G, S>(
7272        &mut self,
7273        guest: &mut G,
7274        call: S,
7275    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
7276    where
7277        T: RecordOrReplay,
7278        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7279        S: SyscallInfo,
7280    {
7281        self.inject_absorbing_from(guest, call, None, false).await
7282    }
7283
7284    /// The first probe of a wait, and every probe of the waits of `select` and
7285    /// `pselect6`, which runs before the turn's `interrupted_with_state` check:
7286    /// `inject_absorbing`, except that a signal that would end the wait neither
7287    /// ends it before the injection nor when it stops the injection.
7288    ///
7289    /// Linux reports a descriptor that is ready when the call begins, a queued
7290    /// event, and an argument error before it looks at pending signals:
7291    /// `do_poll` tests `signal_pending` only when no descriptor is ready, and so
7292    /// does `core_sys_select`, whose `max_select_fd` first returns `EBADF` for a
7293    /// descriptor in the sets that is not open; `ep_poll` sends queued events
7294    /// before it tests it, `do_epoll_wait` rejects a bad descriptor or
7295    /// `maxevents` first, and `do_sigtimedwait` copies its set first. So the
7296    /// probe runs even when such a signal is pending. `do_select` also polls
7297    /// every descriptor on each pass before it tests `signal_pending`, so the
7298    /// waits of `select` and `pselect6` make every probe this way; once `block`
7299    /// has blocked every blockable signal, a pending one cannot stop a probe
7300    /// there, and the check that follows a probe that would block counts it.
7301    /// A pending signal that the guest does not block stops the injection
7302    /// before the probe runs; when the stop is identified, the signal is held
7303    /// as a precious one (`HeldKind::Precious`) and the probe runs again, so
7304    /// its result stands, and the backend delivers the signal as the call
7305    /// returns. If the probe would block, the caller's check that follows
7306    /// counts the held signal (`interrupted_with_state`) and ends the wait with
7307    /// the restart errno. A stop that cannot be identified is held, as
7308    /// `inject_absorbing` describes.
7309    pub(crate) async fn inject_first_probe<T, G, S>(
7310        &mut self,
7311        guest: &mut G,
7312        call: S,
7313    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
7314    where
7315        T: RecordOrReplay,
7316        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7317        S: SyscallInfo,
7318    {
7319        self.inject_absorbing_from(guest, call, None, true).await
7320    }
7321
7322    /// `inject_absorbing` in a turn whose `interrupted_with_state` read `state`
7323    /// and found no signal that ends the wait.
7324    ///
7325    /// Once `block` has blocked every blockable signal (`saved_mask`), `state`
7326    /// serves as the first read before the injection, so a polling turn reads
7327    /// `/proc` once, as it did before injections absorbed stops. The caller must
7328    /// run nothing between the two that resumes the guest thread or changes its
7329    /// signal state. `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state`, which serves
7330    /// ppoll, poll, epoll_pwait, epoll_wait, rt_sigtimedwait and polling futex
7331    /// waits and is the only caller, runs nothing there. So between the two reads
7332    /// the guest thread stays stopped and only it can change its own mask, and
7333    /// with threads sequentialized no other guest thread runs in its turn, so a
7334    /// signal that arrives meanwhile arrives at a
7335    /// host-timed moment: sent from outside the guest, or posted by the kernel.
7336    /// A signal that the full mask blocks stays pending, cannot stop the
7337    /// injection, and is classified at the next turn's read, as one that arrives
7338    /// just after a fresh read is. One that the full mask leaves unblocked
7339    /// (`SIGKILL`, `SIGSTOP`, glibc's two reserved signals, `PERF_EVENT_SIGNAL`)
7340    /// and that stops the injection is not named by `state`, so the stop is not
7341    /// identified and is handled as a stop by a signal that arrives just after a
7342    /// fresh read is. `interrupted_with_state` found
7343    /// no signal in `state` that ends the wait, so the check before the injection
7344    /// does not end it either.
7345    ///
7346    /// Before `block` takes effect, or when it cannot, the probe runs under the
7347    /// guest's own mask and a fresh read is taken, so a signal that arrived
7348    /// after `state` is still identified or ends the wait before the injection.
7349    pub(crate) async fn inject_absorbing_after<T, G, S>(
7350        &mut self,
7351        guest: &mut G,
7352        call: S,
7353        state: KernelSignalState,
7354    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
7355    where
7356        T: RecordOrReplay,
7357        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7358        S: SyscallInfo,
7359    {
7360        let first = self.saved_mask.is_some().then_some(state);
7361        self.inject_absorbing_from(guest, call, first, false).await
7362    }
7363
7364    /// `inject_absorbing`, taking `first`, if any, as the state read before the
7365    /// first injection. For `first_probe`, a signal that would end the wait does
7366    /// not end it, and one that stops the injection is held
7367    /// (`inject_first_probe`).
7368    async fn inject_absorbing_from<T, G, S>(
7369        &mut self,
7370        guest: &mut G,
7371        call: S,
7372        mut first: Option<KernelSignalState>,
7373        first_probe: bool,
7374    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
7375    where
7376        T: RecordOrReplay,
7377        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7378        S: SyscallInfo,
7379    {
7380        // Each absorbed stop takes one signal off a kernel queue, so only signals
7381        // sent faster than the injections run can reach this. A wait with a
7382        // deadline has no bound, as the blind retry before this machinery had
7383        // none: ending it would start its timeout again (`deadline`).
7384        const MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS: usize = 64;
7385        let mut absorbed = 0;
7386        loop {
7387            let before = match first.take() {
7388                Some(state) => state,
7389                None => crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?,
7390            };
7391            let ends_wait = self.could_interrupt(&before) & !self.held_until_return;
7392            if !first_probe && before.pending & ends_wait != 0 {
7393                return Err(self.restart_errno.into());
7394            }
7395            let next = before.next_dequeued(before.blocked);
7396            if let Some((signal, queue)) = next
7397                && self.would_replace_precious(signal, queue)
7398            {
7399                if let Some(held) = self.held
7400                    && self.held_ends_wait(&before, held.signal)
7401                {
7402                    tracing::trace!(
7403                        "[tid {}] signal {} would replace the held signal {}, which ends the wait",
7404                        self.tid,
7405                        signal,
7406                        held.signal
7407                    );
7408                    return Err(held_signal_restart_errno(self.restart_errno, held.signal).into());
7409                }
7410                // Round-10 High 1 on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361:
7411                // this used to end a wait without a deadline with ERESTARTNOINTR,
7412                // and let a wait with one go on and lose the held signal.
7413                tracing::trace!(
7414                    "[tid {}] signal {} would replace the held signal {:?}; the wait is refused",
7415                    self.tid,
7416                    signal,
7417                    self.held
7418                );
7419                return Err(self.refusal(Some(signal), HeldSignalLoss::Replaced));
7420            }
7421            let result = guest.inject(call).await;
7422            let Err(errno) = result else {
7423                return Ok(result);
7424            };
7425            if !probe_was_interrupted_by_signal(errno) {
7426                return Ok(result);
7427            }
7428            let after = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
7429            // A probe that carries the call's temporary mask, as a masked
7430            // ppoll's does (`with_wait_mask`), and that the kernel itself
7431            // ended, for a pending signal the mask lets in, leaves that mask
7432            // installed with its restore pending until the signal is delivered
7433            // as the guest resumes, so `/proc` reports a mask other than the one
7434            // before the injection. That ERESTARTNOHAND is the call's own
7435            // result, not a stop, and no injection may follow it: a repeated
7436            // probe would save the temporary mask as the guest's
7437            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1003). A pselect6
7438            // wait's probes carry no mask, so this never holds for one.
7439            if self.wait_mask.is_some()
7440                && errno == Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
7441                && after.blocked != before.blocked
7442            {
7443                return Ok(result);
7444            }
7445            let identified =
7446                next.filter(|&(signal, queue)| stop_took_only(&before, &after, signal, queue));
7447            let Some((signal, queue)) = identified else {
7448                // A signal that `before` did not show stopped the injection. The
7449                // backend holds it in place of any held one and delivers it when
7450                // the guest resumes, but `/proc` cannot name it. If the backend
7451                // held a signal whose loss matters, or one it could not identify
7452                // either, that signal is gone, and the wait is refused. Otherwise
7453                // the wait goes on and the injection runs again, as the blind
7454                // retry before this machinery did, so the wait keeps its
7455                // deadline; the signals that `/proc` still shows are classified
7456                // as before, and every check that ends the wait still runs at
7457                // the read before the injection and at each turn's
7458                // `interrupted_with_state`.
7459                if self.holds_precious() {
7460                    tracing::trace!(
7461                        "[tid {}] a signal stop that cannot be identified replaced the held signal {:?}; the wait is refused",
7462                        self.tid,
7463                        self.held
7464                    );
7465                    return Err(self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::UnidentifiedStop));
7466                }
7467                if !self.deadline && absorbed >= MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS {
7468                    // The backend now holds the unidentified signal.
7469                    self.held = None;
7470                    self.held_unidentified = true;
7471                    return Err(self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::StopBound));
7472                }
7473                absorbed += 1;
7474                tracing::trace!(
7475                    "[tid {}] a signal stop that cannot be identified is held; the injection runs again",
7476                    self.tid
7477                );
7478                self.held = None;
7479                self.held_unidentified = true;
7480                continue;
7481            };
7482            let bit = kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
7483            let verdict = match self.stop_verdict(&before, signal) {
7484                // A probe made by `inject_first_probe` holds a signal that would
7485                // end the wait and runs again.
7486                StopVerdict::End(_)
7487                    if first_probe
7488                        && self.consumed & bit == 0
7489                        && self.could_interrupt(&before) & bit != 0 =>
7490                {
7491                    StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
7492                }
7493                verdict => verdict,
7494            };
7495            match verdict {
7496                StopVerdict::Absorb(kind) => {
7497                    let kind = self.held.map_or(kind, |held| held.kind.max(kind));
7498                    let unidentified = self.held_unidentified;
7499                    self.held = Some(HeldSignal {
7500                        signal,
7501                        queue,
7502                        kind,
7503                    });
7504                    self.held_unidentified = false;
7505                    if !self.deadline && absorbed >= MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS {
7506                        if kind == HeldKind::Precious || unidentified {
7507                            return Err(self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::StopBound));
7508                        }
7509                        return Err(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR.into());
7510                    }
7511                    absorbed += 1;
7512                    tracing::trace!(
7513                        "[tid {}] signal {} stopped an injection and is held ({:?})",
7514                        self.tid,
7515                        signal,
7516                        kind
7517                    );
7518                }
7519                // A signal that a wait without a deadline consumes, delivered
7520                // rather than returned: refused when the wait holds it until the
7521                // call returns, or when it replaced a held signal whose loss
7522                // matters, and otherwise ended with ERESTARTNOINTR (stop_verdict).
7523                StopVerdict::End(_)
7524                    if !self.deadline
7525                        && self.consumed & bit != 0
7526                        && (self.held_until_return & bit != 0 || self.holds_precious()) =>
7527                {
7528                    tracing::trace!(
7529                        "[tid {}] consumed signal {} stopped an injection; the wait is refused",
7530                        self.tid,
7531                        signal
7532                    );
7533                    return Err(self.refusal(Some(signal), HeldSignalLoss::Consumed));
7534                }
7535                // The backend holds `signal`, which stopped the injection.
7536                StopVerdict::End(errno) => {
7537                    return Err(held_signal_restart_errno(errno, signal).into());
7538                }
7539            }
7540        }
7541    }
7542
7543    /// What a stop by `signal` means for the wait, given the kernel's state
7544    /// `before` the injection (see `inject_absorbing`).
7545    fn stop_verdict(&self, before: &KernelSignalState, signal: i32) -> StopVerdict {
7546        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
7547        let interrupts = if self.consumed & bit != 0 {
7548            if !self.deadline {
7549                return StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR);
7550            }
7551            // The backend delivers the signal rather than the wait consuming it,
7552            // as Linux does for one the guest does not block, so it is classified
7553            // as if the wait did not consume it.
7554            let guest_mask = self.wait_mask.or(self.saved_mask).unwrap_or(before.blocked);
7555            before.interrupting_wait(guest_mask, self.defers_default_stops) & bit != 0
7556        } else {
7557            self.could_interrupt(before) & bit != 0
7558        };
7559        if interrupts {
7560            return if self.held_until_return & bit != 0 {
7561                StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
7562            } else {
7563                StopVerdict::End(self.restart_errno)
7564            };
7565        }
7566        if signal == libc::SIGCHLD
7567            || (self.defers_default_stops && before.default_job_control_stops() & bit != 0)
7568        {
7569            return StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious);
7570        }
7571        let default_ignored = [libc::SIGCONT, libc::SIGURG, libc::SIGWINCH]
7572            .into_iter()
7573            .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_sigset_bit(signal));
7574        if (before.ignored | (default_ignored & !before.caught)) & bit != 0 {
7575            return StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Harmless);
7576        }
7577        // A signal that the wait mask blocks, and the guest's own mask does
7578        // not, can stop an injection that runs before `block` takes effect.
7579        // Linux keeps it pending for the whole call, under the temporary mask,
7580        // and delivers it as the call returns, so it is held and never ends
7581        // the wait (review of
7582        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4051).
7583        if self.deadline || self.wait_mask.is_some_and(|mask| mask & bit != 0) {
7584            StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
7585        } else {
7586            StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR)
7587        }
7588    }
7589
7590    /// Whether an injection that `signal`, pending on `queue`, stops would make
7591    /// the backend drop a held signal whose delivery matters
7592    /// (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one it could not identify, which may matter
7593    /// (`held_unidentified`). Linux merges a standard signal into the same one
7594    /// pending on the same queue, so that one replaces nothing.
7595    fn would_replace_precious(&self, signal: i32, queue: SignalQueue) -> bool {
7596        self.held_unidentified
7597            || self.held.is_some_and(|held| {
7598                held.kind == HeldKind::Precious
7599                    && !(signal == held.signal && queue == held.queue && signal < KERNEL_SIGRTMIN)
7600            })
7601    }
7602
7603    /// Whether the backend holds a signal whose loss matters
7604    /// (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one it could not identify, which may matter.
7605    fn holds_precious(&self) -> bool {
7606        self.held_unidentified
7607            || self
7608                .held
7609                .is_some_and(|held| held.kind == HeldKind::Precious)
7610    }
7611
7612    /// The `HeldSignalRefusal` that ends the wait, naming the signal the backend
7613    /// holds, if known, and `replacing`, the one that would replace it or that
7614    /// stopped the injection.
7615    fn refusal(&self, replacing: Option<i32>, loss: HeldSignalLoss) -> Error {
7616        Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(HeldSignalRefusal {
7617            wait: None,
7618            held: self.held.map(|held| held.signal),
7619            replacing,
7620            loss,
7621        }))
7622    }
7623
7624    /// Whether a held `signal` would end the wait natively, given the kernel's
7625    /// state `before` an injection: it could interrupt the wait, and the wait
7626    /// does not hold it until the call returns (`held_until_return`).
7627    fn held_ends_wait(&self, before: &KernelSignalState, signal: i32) -> bool {
7628        self.could_interrupt(before) & !self.held_until_return & kernel_sigset_bit(signal) != 0
7629    }
7630
7631    /// Block every blockable signal for the rest of the wait, and keep blocked the
7632    /// signals the guest blocks itself, which the blockable set leaves out (the C
7633    /// library's reserved signals). `scratch` is a guest cell for the mask when
7634    /// the caller holds the only scratch-stack guard; otherwise a fresh guard is
7635    /// taken. The change goes through `inject_absorbing`, so a signal that stops
7636    /// it is handled as one that stops a probe. If that ends the wait, the guest's
7637    /// mask is still recorded, and the caller's final `restore` reads the
7638    /// kernel's mask and puts the guest's back if the change took effect.
7639    ///
7640    /// If the mask cannot be changed for another reason, the guest's mask is
7641    /// unchanged and no wait call can return that error, so the wait continues
7642    /// with every probe under the guest's own mask, as the first probe runs, and
7643    /// `block` is not tried again (`needs_block`). `interrupted_with_state` reads
7644    /// that mask from the kernel each turn. The scratch-stack commit fails this
7645    /// way on a guest stack with no room below its stack pointer
7646    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3328); poll and epoll_wait
7647    /// probes need no scratch of their own, so for them this is the first need.
7648    pub(crate) async fn block<'a, T, G>(
7649        &mut self,
7650        guest: &mut G,
7651        scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
7652    ) -> Result<(), Error>
7653    where
7654        T: RecordOrReplay,
7655        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7656    {
7657        let guest_mask = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?.blocked;
7658        let mask = blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask;
7659        let result = match scratch {
7660            Some(cell) => match guest.memory().write_value(cell, &mask) {
7661                Ok(()) => {
7662                    self.inject_absorbing(guest, set_signal_mask_call(cell.into()))
7663                        .await
7664                }
7665                Err(errno) => Ok(Err(errno)),
7666            },
7667            None => {
7668                let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
7669                let cell = stack.push(mask);
7670                match stack.commit() {
7671                    Ok(_guard) => {
7672                        self.inject_absorbing(guest, set_signal_mask_call(cell))
7673                            .await
7674                    }
7675                    Err(_) => Ok(Err(Errno::EFAULT)),
7676                }
7677            }
7678        };
7679        match result {
7680            Ok(Ok(_)) => {
7681                self.saved_mask = Some(guest_mask);
7682                Ok(())
7683            }
7684            Ok(Err(errno)) => {
7685                tracing::debug!(
7686                    "[tid {}] cannot block signals for a wait ({}); its probes run under the \
7687                     guest's mask",
7688                    self.tid,
7689                    errno
7690                );
7691                self.unblockable = true;
7692                Ok(())
7693            }
7694            Err(error) => {
7695                self.saved_mask = Some(guest_mask);
7696                Err(error)
7697            }
7698        }
7699    }
7700
7701    /// Block every blockable signal until restored, as `block` does,
7702    /// but through `Guest::set_blocked_signals`: no guest code runs, so no
7703    /// pending signal is taken from the kernel's queues, and every one stays
7704    /// there for the kernel to deliver, in its own order, once `restore` puts
7705    /// the guest's mask back. `block` instead injects `rt_sigprocmask`, which a
7706    /// pending signal can stop before it runs, moving that signal into the
7707    /// backend's single held slot, where a second one replaces it
7708    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, stage 2). No scratch
7709    /// memory is needed, here or in `restore` (the Claude review of the R2b-2
7710    /// design, M1).
7711    ///
7712    /// `host_timed` is the turn's host-timed signals, held until the call
7713    /// returns as `hold_until_return` holds them.
7714    ///
7715    /// Returns whether the mask is now blocked. A refusal changes nothing
7716    /// (`MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported`, `RestorePending`), and neither does a
7717    /// failure that put the old mask back, so the wait goes on under the
7718    /// guest's own mask, as before this existed. A failure that leaves the mask
7719    /// unknown ends the run before the guest resumes
7720    /// ([`BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored`]).
7721    pub(crate) async fn block_in_place<T, G>(
7722        &mut self,
7723        guest: &mut G,
7724        host_timed: KernelSigset,
7725    ) -> Result<bool, Error>
7726    where
7727        T: RecordOrReplay,
7728        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7729    {
7730        // As `install_turn_mask` does for `writev`: the signals a host-timed
7731        // source can post (`host_timed`) are held until the call returns, so a
7732        // fallback injected restoration holds one that stops it
7733        // (`absorb_restoration_stop`) rather than counting it lost.
7734        self.hold_until_return(host_timed);
7735        let guest_mask = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?.blocked;
7736        match guest
7737            .set_blocked_signals(blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask)
7738            .await
7739        {
7740            Ok(old) => {
7741                self.saved_mask = Some(old);
7742                self.blocked_in_place = true;
7743                Ok(true)
7744            }
7745            Err(MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
7746                errno,
7747                mask_unknown: true,
7748            }) => Err(self.mask_not_restored(1, Some(errno))),
7749            Err(refused) => {
7750                tracing::debug!(
7751                    "[tid {}] cannot block signals in place for a wait ({}); its attempts run \
7752                     under the guest's mask",
7753                    self.tid,
7754                    refused
7755                );
7756                // Not tried again for this wait (`needs_block`).
7757                self.unblockable = true;
7758                Ok(false)
7759            }
7760        }
7761    }
7762
7763    /// The error that ends the run when the guest's mask cannot be put back.
7764    fn mask_not_restored(&self, attempts: usize, last_error: Option<Errno>) -> Error {
7765        Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(
7766            BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored {
7767                pid: self.pid,
7768                tid: self.tid,
7769                attempts,
7770                last_error,
7771            },
7772        ))
7773    }
7774
7775    /// Release an in-place probe mask before yielding, without executing guest
7776    /// code. Linux's `PTRACE_SETSIGMASK` updates the stopped task's mask and
7777    /// leaves pending recalculation until resume (`kernel/ptrace.c`, v7.1.3),
7778    /// so a queued signal stays visible for the next protected probe.
7779    ///
7780    /// Unlike final `restore`, this cannot fall back to an injection: a signal
7781    /// stopping that injection could disappear into the backend's held slot
7782    /// before the next turn reads it. A known-unchanged refusal retains the
7783    /// saved state for final cleanup but is fatal to this retry loop. An unknown
7784    /// mask is fatal without any further speculative restoration.
7785    async fn release_probe_mask_in_place<T, G>(&mut self, guest: &mut G) -> Result<(), Error>
7786    where
7787        T: RecordOrReplay,
7788        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7789    {
7790        let Some(guest_mask) = self.saved_mask else {
7791            // An initial refusal to block still takes the original unmasked
7792            // fallback; there is no private mask to release in that case.
7793            return Ok(());
7794        };
7795        if !self.blocked_in_place {
7796            return Err(self.mask_not_restored(0, None));
7797        }
7798        match guest.set_blocked_signals(guest_mask).await {
7799            Ok(_) => {
7800                self.saved_mask = None;
7801                self.blocked_in_place = false;
7802                Ok(())
7803            }
7804            Err(MaskChangeRefused::Gone) => {
7805                self.saved_mask = None;
7806                self.blocked_in_place = false;
7807                // The same unobserved outcome as read_wait_signal_state for
7808                // a vanished task. Do not hand off or probe it again merely
7809                // to rediscover the exit through procfs.
7810                Err(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR.into())
7811            }
7812            Err(MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
7813                errno,
7814                mask_unknown: true,
7815            }) => {
7816                self.saved_mask = None;
7817                self.blocked_in_place = false;
7818                Err(self.mask_not_restored(1, Some(errno)))
7819            }
7820            Err(refused) => {
7821                let errno = match refused {
7822                    MaskChangeRefused::Failed { errno, .. } => Some(errno),
7823                    _ => None,
7824                };
7825                Err(self.mask_not_restored(1, errno))
7826            }
7827        }
7828    }
7829
7830    /// Put back the guest's mask, if `block` replaced it. A signal can stop the guest
7831    /// around the call, before or after it takes effect, so success is read back
7832    /// from the kernel and the call is repeated until the kernel reports the
7833    /// guest's mask. The guest never resumes with every signal blocked: if the
7834    /// mask cannot be put back, the run ends with
7835    /// [`BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored`].
7836    ///
7837    /// The backend holds the signal that stops one of these injections, in place
7838    /// of any it held, as it does for a probe (`inject_absorbing`). Each such
7839    /// stop is recorded from the read before the injection and the read after it
7840    /// (`absorb_restoration_stop`). If one replaced a held signal whose loss
7841    /// matters, or one that could not be identified, the mask is still put back
7842    /// and then the first such loss is returned as a [`HeldSignalRefusal`]
7843    /// (`HeldSignalLoss::Restoration`), which the caller turns into the wait's
7844    /// result (`result_after_restore`). Round-11 High F1 on
7845    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361: these stops used to be
7846    /// retried without that check, so the held signal was lost silently.
7847    pub(crate) async fn restore<'a, T, G>(
7848        &mut self,
7849        guest: &mut G,
7850        scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
7851    ) -> Result<(), Error>
7852    where
7853        T: RecordOrReplay,
7854        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7855    {
7856        let Some(guest_mask) = self.saved_mask else {
7857            return Ok(());
7858        };
7859        // A mask `block_in_place` installed goes back the same way, with no
7860        // injection, so no signal can stop the restoration and none is held.
7861        // That call is refused under the same rules as the block; a refusal
7862        // or a failure that left the mask as it was falls back to the
7863        // injected restoration below, which needs scratch memory (the Codex
7864        // and Claude reviews of https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/1083,
7865        // F4).
7866        if std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked_in_place) {
7867            match guest.set_blocked_signals(guest_mask).await {
7868                Ok(_) | Err(MaskChangeRefused::Gone) => {
7869                    self.saved_mask = None;
7870                    return Ok(());
7871                }
7872                Err(MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
7873                    errno,
7874                    mask_unknown: true,
7875                }) => {
7876                    self.saved_mask = None;
7877                    return Err(self.mask_not_restored(1, Some(errno)));
7878                }
7879                Err(refused) => {
7880                    tracing::debug!(
7881                        "[tid {}] cannot restore the mask in place ({}); injecting it",
7882                        self.tid,
7883                        refused
7884                    );
7885                }
7886            }
7887        }
7888        // `stop_verdict` reads the guest's mask from `saved_mask`, so it is cleared
7889        // only once the restoration has ended.
7890        let restored = self.restore_mask(guest, guest_mask, scratch).await;
7891        self.saved_mask = None;
7892        restored
7893    }
7894
7895    /// `restore`, for a wait whose guest mask is `guest_mask`.
7896    async fn restore_mask<'a, T, G>(
7897        &mut self,
7898        guest: &mut G,
7899        guest_mask: KernelSigset,
7900        scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
7901    ) -> Result<(), Error>
7902    where
7903        T: RecordOrReplay,
7904        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
7905    {
7906        // Under the all-blocked mask only a signal that cannot be blocked (SIGKILL,
7907        // SIGSTOP) can stop the call before it takes effect, and each such stop needs
7908        // another signal sent, so a bound this large is never reached in practice.
7909        const ATTEMPTS: usize = 16;
7910        let mut attempts = 0;
7911        let mut last_error = None;
7912        // The kernel's state before an injection that a signal stopped, until the
7913        // next read records the stop.
7914        let mut stopped = None;
7915        // The first held signal that a stop replaced, as the refusal to return once
7916        // the mask is back.
7917        let mut loss = None;
7918        while attempts < ATTEMPTS {
7919            let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
7920            if let Some(before) = stopped.take() {
7921                let replaced = self.absorb_restoration_stop(&before, &state);
7922                loss = loss.or(replaced);
7923            }
7924            if state.blocked == guest_mask {
7925                return loss.map_or(Ok(()), Err);
7926            }
7927            attempts += 1;
7928            match inject_signal_mask(guest, guest_mask, scratch).await {
7929                Ok(()) => return loss.map_or(Ok(()), Err),
7930                // Stopped by a signal: the next read records the stop and decides
7931                // whether the mask took effect.
7932                Err(errno) if probe_was_interrupted_by_signal(errno) => {
7933                    last_error = Some(errno);
7934                    stopped = Some(state);
7935                }
7936                // The call could not run, so the mask is unchanged.
7937                Err(errno) => {
7938                    last_error = Some(errno);
7939                    break;
7940                }
7941            }
7942        }
7943        let state = crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(guest)?;
7944        if let Some(before) = stopped.take() {
7945            let replaced = self.absorb_restoration_stop(&before, &state);
7946            loss = loss.or(replaced);
7947        }
7948        if state.blocked == guest_mask {
7949            return loss.map_or(Ok(()), Err);
7950        }
7951        Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(
7952            BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored {
7953                pid: self.pid,
7954                tid: self.tid,
7955                attempts,
7956                last_error,
7957            },
7958        )))
7959    }
7960
7961    /// Record a signal stop of an injection of `restore`, given the kernel's state
7962    /// `before` the injection and `after` it, as `inject_absorbing` records a stop
7963    /// of a probe: the backend holds the signal that stopped it in place of any it
7964    /// held. Returns the `HeldSignalRefusal` when that replaced a held signal
7965    /// whose loss matters, or one that could not be identified
7966    /// (`would_replace_precious`, `holds_precious`), naming the held signal as it
7967    /// was before the stop.
7968    ///
7969    /// A stop is identified only when exactly the signal that the kernel would
7970    /// take next under the mask `before` left its queue and the mask did not
7971    /// change (`stop_took_only`); a stop after which the mask took effect, or one
7972    /// that `before` did not show, is recorded as unidentified. The call's result
7973    /// is already decided, so a signal that would have ended the wait is kept as
7974    /// one whose delivery matters.
7975    fn absorb_restoration_stop(
7976        &mut self,
7977        before: &KernelSignalState,
7978        after: &KernelSignalState,
7979    ) -> Option<Error> {
7980        let identified = before
7981            .next_dequeued(before.blocked)
7982            .filter(|&(signal, queue)| stop_took_only(before, after, signal, queue));
7983        let Some((signal, queue)) = identified else {
7984            let loss = self
7985                .holds_precious()
7986                .then(|| self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::Restoration));
7987            tracing::trace!(
7988                "[tid {}] a signal stop that cannot be identified stopped the mask restoration; it replaced the held signal {:?}",
7989                self.tid,
7990                self.held
7991            );
7992            self.held = None;
7993            self.held_unidentified = true;
7994            return loss;
7995        };
7996        let loss = self
7997            .would_replace_precious(signal, queue)
7998            .then(|| self.refusal(Some(signal), HeldSignalLoss::Restoration));
7999        let kind = match self.stop_verdict(before, signal) {
8000            StopVerdict::Absorb(kind) => kind,
8001            StopVerdict::End(_) => HeldKind::Precious,
8002        };
8003        let kind = self.held.map_or(kind, |held| held.kind.max(kind));
8004        tracing::trace!(
8005            "[tid {}] signal {} stopped the mask restoration and is held ({:?}) in place of {:?}",
8006            self.tid,
8007            signal,
8008            kind,
8009            self.held
8010        );
8011        self.held = Some(HeldSignal {
8012            signal,
8013            queue,
8014            kind,
8015        });
8016        self.held_unidentified = false;
8017        loss
8018    }
8019}
8020
8021/// The wait's result once `restore` has put the guest's mask back. A
8022/// [`HeldSignalRefusal`] from the restoration (`HeldSignalLoss::Restoration`)
8023/// replaces `result`, as a loss during the wait does, unless `result` is
8024/// already such a refusal, which came first, or a fatal mask-restoration
8025/// failure. Cleanup must not turn that failure into an unsupported-operation
8026/// restart through `refuse_held_signal_loss`. Every other
8027/// restoration error, such as [`BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored`], is
8028/// returned as the error that ends the run, as before.
8029pub(crate) fn result_after_restore(
8030    restored: Result<(), Error>,
8031    result: Result<i64, Error>,
8032) -> Result<Result<i64, Error>, Error> {
8033    let is_refusal =
8034        |error: &Error| matches!(error, Error::Tool(error) if error.is::<HeldSignalRefusal>());
8035    let is_mask_failure = |error: &Error| {
8036        matches!(error, Error::Tool(error) if matches!(
8037            error.downcast_ref::<BlockedWaitSignalError>(),
8038            Some(BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored { .. })
8039        ))
8040    };
8041    match restored {
8042        Ok(()) => Ok(result),
8043        Err(refusal) if is_refusal(&refusal) => match &result {
8044            Err(error) if is_refusal(error) || is_mask_failure(error) => Ok(result),
8045            _ => Ok(Err(refusal)),
8046        },
8047        Err(error) => Err(error),
8048    }
8049}
8050
8051/// Replace the guest's signal mask with `mask`, written to `scratch` or, when the
8052/// caller holds no scratch-stack guard, to a fresh one.
8053async fn inject_signal_mask<'a, T, G>(
8054    guest: &mut G,
8055    mask: KernelSigset,
8056    scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
8057) -> Result<(), Errno>
8058where
8059    T: RecordOrReplay,
8060    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
8061{
8062    match scratch {
8063        Some(cell) => {
8064            guest.memory().write_value(cell, &mask)?;
8065            guest
8066                .inject(set_signal_mask_call(cell.into()))
8067                .await
8068                .map(drop)
8069        }
8070        None => {
8071            let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
8072            let cell = stack.push(mask);
8073            let _guard = stack.commit().map_err(|_| Errno::EFAULT)?;
8074            guest.inject(set_signal_mask_call(cell)).await.map(drop)
8075        }
8076    }
8077}
8078
8079/// `rt_sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, cell, NULL)`.
8080fn set_signal_mask_call(cell: Addr<'_, KernelSigset>) -> syscalls::RtSigprocmask {
8081    syscalls::RtSigprocmask::new()
8082        .with_how(libc::SIG_SETMASK)
8083        .with_set(Some(cell.cast()))
8084        .with_oldset(None)
8085        .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE)
8086}
8087
8088/// Whether a signal stop between the kernel states `before` and `after` took
8089/// exactly `signal` off `queue`: it is no longer there, no other signal left
8090/// either queue, and the mask and dispositions did not change. Signals may have
8091/// arrived in between.
8092fn stop_took_only(
8093    before: &KernelSignalState,
8094    after: &KernelSignalState,
8095    signal: i32,
8096    queue: SignalQueue,
8097) -> bool {
8098    let bit = kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
8099    let other = match queue {
8100        SignalQueue::Thread => SignalQueue::Shared,
8101        SignalQueue::Shared => SignalQueue::Thread,
8102    };
8103    before.blocked == after.blocked
8104        && before.ignored == after.ignored
8105        && before.caught == after.caught
8106        && after.queued(queue) & bit == 0
8107        && before.queued(queue) & !bit & !after.queued(queue) == 0
8108        && before.queued(other) & !after.queued(other) == 0
8109}
8110
8111/// Whether an injected call's error means a signal stopped the guest around it
8112/// rather than that the call produced a result: the backend's restart errno, or
8113/// `EINTR` where a backend runs the call itself. None of these calls blocks.
8114pub(crate) fn probe_was_interrupted_by_signal(errno: Errno) -> bool {
8115    matches!(
8116        errno,
8117        Errno::EINTR
8118            | Errno::ERESTARTSYS
8119            | Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR
8120            | Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
8121            | Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
8122    )
8123}
8124
8125pub(crate) async fn record_retry_event<G, C, T>(guest: &mut G, call: C)
8126where
8127    C: SyscallInfo,
8128    T: RecordOrReplay,
8129    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
8130{
8131    let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
8132    let cfg = &guest.config();
8133    if cfg.sequentialize_threads && cfg.observes_schedevents() {
8134        trace_schedevent(
8135            guest,
8136            with_guest_time(
8137                guest,
8138                SchedEvent::syscall(dettid, call.number(), SyscallPhase::Polling),
8139            ),
8140            true,
8141        )
8142        .await;
8143    }
8144}
8145
8146// A helper function for enriching the schedevent with local information.
8147pub fn with_guest_time<G, T>(guest: &G, event: SchedEvent) -> SchedEvent
8148where
8149    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
8150    T: RecordOrReplay,
8151{
8152    let dettime = &guest.thread_state().thread_logical_time;
8153    event.with_dettime(dettime)
8154}
8155
8156// Enrich the event with the RIP register from the current guest state, but only if it is unset.
8157pub async fn with_guest_rip<G, T>(guest: &mut G, mut event: SchedEvent) -> SchedEvent
8158where
8159    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
8160    T: RecordOrReplay,
8161{
8162    assert!(event.end_rip.is_none());
8163
8164    let regs = guest.regs().await;
8165    let end_rip =
8166        NonZeroUsize::new(crate::arch::instruction_pointer(&regs).try_into().unwrap()).unwrap();
8167    event.end_rip = Some(end_rip);
8168    event
8169}
8170
8171// Convert to absolute logical time point for the timeout.
8172// 0 duration means no timeout, and this will return None.
8173pub async fn millis_duration_to_absolute_timeout<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
8174    guest: &mut G,
8175    timeout_millis: i32,
8176) -> Option<LogicalTime> {
8177    match positive_millis_as_nanos(timeout_millis) {
8178        Some(timeout_nanos) => nanos_duration_to_absolute_timeout(guest, timeout_nanos).await,
8179        None => None,
8180    }
8181}
8182
8183/// Milliseconds to nanoseconds for a strictly positive timeout; `None` for the
8184/// non-positive values Linux treats as "return immediately" (0) or "wait
8185/// forever" (-1), neither of which is a deadline.
8186///
8187/// Kept as a separate, unit-bracketed function on purpose. This conversion was
8188/// previously inlined as `* 1000` instead of `* 1_000_000`, which made every
8189/// finite deadline 1000x too short (a 1 ms timeout expired after 1 us). That
8190/// is invisible in an end-to-end test that only checks a syscall's return
8191/// value, so the arithmetic is pinned here by `millis_to_nanos_conversion`.
8192fn positive_millis_as_nanos(timeout_millis: i32) -> Option<u128> {
8193    (timeout_millis > 0).then(|| (timeout_millis as u128) * 1_000_000)
8194}
8195
8196// Convert to absolute logical time point for the timeout.
8197// 0 duration means no timeout, and this will return None.
8198pub async fn nanos_duration_to_absolute_timeout<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
8199    guest: &mut G,
8200    timeout_nanos: u128,
8201) -> Option<LogicalTime> {
8202    if timeout_nanos > 0 {
8203        let ns_delta = Duration::from_nanos(timeout_nanos as u64);
8204        let base_time = thread_observe_time(guest).await;
8205        let target_time = base_time + ns_delta;
8206        Some(target_time)
8207    } else {
8208        None
8209    }
8210}
8211
8212/// The number of `pollfd` entries `poll` and `ppoll` read. Linux declares
8213/// their `nfds` parameter `unsigned int`, so only the low 32 bits of the
8214/// register count; a guest may leave the high word set. Every reader of a
8215/// guest's pollfd array sizes it from this, never from `nfds` itself.
8216pub fn poll_nfds(nfds: libc::nfds_t) -> u32 {
8217    nfds as u32
8218}

8220#[cfg(test)]
8221mod tests {
8222    use super::*;
8223
8224    /// The backend drops a handler when its thread dies during a wait, and
8225    /// the shield with it: that must not panic, though the mask was never put
8226    /// back (a debug assertion did, and ended the run).
8227    #[test]
8228    fn a_shield_dropped_with_its_handler_ends_quietly() {
8229        drop(IgnoredSignalShield {
8230            guest_mask: Some(0),
8231        });
8232        drop(IgnoredSignalShield::none());
8233    }
8234
8235    /// The drop log must not assert the thread is gone: Drop runs when
8236    /// the backend cancels the handler, which also happens when a
8237    /// backend error ends the run while the thread still exists.
8238    #[test]
8239    fn a_dropped_shield_log_does_not_claim_the_thread_is_gone() {
8240        let message = shield_drop_message(0x2a);
8241        assert!(message.contains("ended with its handler"), "{message}");
8242        assert!(message.contains("unrestored"), "{message}");
8243        assert!(!message.contains("is gone"), "{message}");
8244        assert!(!message.contains("are gone"), "{message}");
8245    }
8246
8247    #[test]
8248    fn an_ignored_signal_shield_blocks_only_what_the_guest_ignores() {
8249        use crate::syscalls::threads::kernel_sigset_bit as bit;
8250        let state = |blocked, ignored, caught| KernelSignalState {
8251            blocked,
8252            ignored,
8253            caught,
8254            ..Default::default()
8255        };
8256        let default_ignored =
8257            bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | bit(libc::SIGCONT) | bit(libc::SIGURG) | bit(libc::SIGWINCH);
8258        // With every disposition at its default, the shield blocks exactly the
8259        // default-ignored signals, on top of the thread's own mask.
8260        assert_eq!(
8261            ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state(bit(libc::SIGUSR2), 0, 0)),
8262            Some(bit(libc::SIGUSR2) | default_ignored)
8263        );
8264        // A signal set to SIG_IGN joins them; a caught one leaves them.
8265        assert_eq!(
8266            ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state(0, bit(libc::SIGUSR1), bit(libc::SIGCHLD))),
8267            Some(bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | (default_ignored & !bit(libc::SIGCHLD)))
8268        );
8269        // Nothing to block when every ignored signal is caught or already blocked.
8270        assert_eq!(
8271            ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state(
8272                bit(libc::SIGCONT) | bit(libc::SIGURG),
8273                0,
8274                bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | bit(libc::SIGWINCH)
8275            )),
8276            None
8277        );
8278        // A refused change leaves the wait under the guest's own mask, unless the
8279        // backend could not confirm what the mask is.
8280        for refused in [
8281            MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported,
8282            MaskChangeRefused::Gone,
8283            MaskChangeRefused::RestorePending {
8284                saved: 0,
8285                effective: 1,
8286            },
8287            MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
8288                errno: Errno::ESRCH,
8289                mask_unknown: false,
8290            },
8291        ] {
8292            assert!(shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(&refused), "{refused}");
8293        }
8294        assert!(!shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(
8295            &MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
8296                errno: Errno::ESRCH,
8297                mask_unknown: true,
8298            }
8299        ));
8300    }
8301
8302    /// Linux polls every entry with a non-negative descriptor and ignores the
8303    /// rest (fs/select.c `do_pollfd`), so only those decide whether a poll is
8304    /// guest-held; the `events` and `revents` halves are not descriptors.
8305    #[test]
8306    fn pollfd_descriptors_are_the_non_negative_entries() {
8307        let entries = [
8308            libc::pollfd {
8309                fd: 7,
8310                events: libc::POLLIN,
8311                revents: 0,
8312            },
8313            libc::pollfd {
8314                fd: -1,
8315                events: libc::POLLIN,
8316                revents: 0,
8317            },
8318            libc::pollfd {
8319                fd: 0,
8320                events: libc::POLLOUT,
8321                revents: libc::POLLHUP,
8322            },
8323        ];
8324        let bytes: Vec<u8> = entries
8325            .iter()
8326            .flat_map(|entry| {
8327                let mut bytes = entry.fd.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
8328                bytes.extend(entry.events.to_ne_bytes());
8329                bytes.extend(entry.revents.to_ne_bytes());
8330                bytes
8331            })
8332            .collect();
8333        assert_eq!(pollfd_descriptors(&bytes), vec![7, 0]);
8334        assert!(pollfd_descriptors(&[]).is_empty());
8335    }

8337    /// Bracket the millisecond-to-nanosecond timeout conversion in both
8338    /// directions: the non-positive values that are NOT deadlines, and the
8339    /// positive values whose magnitude must be exactly 1e6 ns per ms.
8340    ///
8341    /// The 1 ms case is the specific regression guard: an inlined `* 1000`
8342    /// yields 1_000 here instead of 1_000_000, i.e. a deadline 1000x too
8343    /// short. Asserting the exact value (not merely "nonzero" or "greater
8344    /// than") is what makes that failure visible.
8345    #[test]
8346    fn millis_to_nanos_conversion() {
8347        // Not deadlines: -1 is "infinite", 0 is "return immediately".
8348        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(-1), None);
8349        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(i32::MIN), None);
8350        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(0), None);
8351
8352        // Positive timeouts: exactly 1e6 nanoseconds per millisecond.
8353        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(1), Some(1_000_000));
8354        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(1_000), Some(1_000_000_000));
8355        assert_eq!(
8356            positive_millis_as_nanos(i32::MAX),
8357            Some(i32::MAX as u128 * 1_000_000)
8358        );
8359
8360        // The scale itself, stated independently of any single case so a
8361        // future refactor cannot satisfy the above by coincidence.
8362        for millis in [1, 2, 7, 250, 1_000, 86_400_000] {
8363            assert_eq!(
8364                positive_millis_as_nanos(millis),
8365                Some(millis as u128 * 1_000_000),
8366                "1 ms must convert to 1_000_000 ns, not 1_000"
8367            );
8368        }
8369    }

8372    fn connect_nonblocking_results() {

8386    /// `MSG_DONTWAIT` keeps every socket send and receive from waiting,
8387    /// whatever else its flags carry, and no other flag does: recvmmsg's
8388    /// `MSG_WAITFORONE` still waits for the first datagram. Calls with no
8389    /// per-call flags always follow the file.
8390    #[test]
8391    fn only_msg_dontwait_keeps_a_socket_call_from_waiting() {
8392        use reverie::syscalls::*;
8393        let dontwait = libc::MSG_DONTWAIT;
8394        let others = libc::MSG_PEEK | libc::MSG_WAITALL | libc::MSG_NOSIGNAL | libc::MSG_TRUNC;
8395        let cases: [(&str, bool, bool); 6] = [
8396            (
8397                "recvfrom",
8398                Recvfrom::new()
8399                    .with_flags(others | dontwait)
8400                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
8401                Recvfrom::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
8402            ),
8403            (
8404                "recvmsg",
8405                Recvmsg::new().with_flags(dontwait).flags_forbid_waiting(),
8406                Recvmsg::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
8407            ),
8408            (
8409                "recvmmsg",
8410                Recvmmsg::new()
8411                    .with_flags((libc::MSG_WAITFORONE | dontwait) as u32)
8412                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
8413                Recvmmsg::new()
8414                    .with_flags(libc::MSG_WAITFORONE as u32)
8415                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
8416            ),
8417            (
8418                "sendto",
8419                Sendto::new()
8420                    .with_flags(dontwait as u32)
8421                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
8422                Sendto::new()
8423                    .with_flags(others as u32)
8424                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
8425            ),
8426            (
8427                "sendmsg",
8428                Sendmsg::new().with_flags(dontwait).flags_forbid_waiting(),
8429                Sendmsg::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
8430            ),
8431            (
8432                "sendmmsg",
8433                Sendmmsg::new().with_flags(dontwait).flags_forbid_waiting(),
8434                Sendmmsg::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
8435            ),
8436        ];
8437        for (name, with_dontwait, without) in cases {
8438            assert!(with_dontwait, "{name} with MSG_DONTWAIT may wait");
8439            assert!(!without, "{name} without MSG_DONTWAIT never waits");
8440        }
8441        assert!(!Read::new().flags_forbid_waiting());
8442        assert!(
8443            Preadv2::new()
8444                .with_flags(libc::RWF_NOWAIT)
8445                .flags_forbid_waiting(),
8446            "preadv2 with RWF_NOWAIT may wait"
8447        );
8448        assert!(
8449            !Preadv2::new()
8450                .with_flags(libc::RWF_HIPRI)
8451                .flags_forbid_waiting(),
8452            "preadv2 without RWF_NOWAIT never waits"
8453        );
8454        assert!(!Accept4::new().flags_forbid_waiting());
8455        assert!(!Connect::new().flags_forbid_waiting());
8456    }

8458    /// The `ioaction_based_on_fd_status` decision itself: a call whose own
8459    /// flags forbid waiting (MSG_DONTWAIT, RWF_NOWAIT) on a descriptor the
8460    /// guest left blocking runs once (PassThru), where the same call without
8461    /// them is retried (NonblockizeRetry). A mutant dropping the flags term
8462    /// fails this test.
8463    #[test]
8464    fn ioaction_decision_runs_a_nowait_call_once_on_a_blocking_descriptor() {
8465        use super::IOAction;
8466        use super::ioaction_for_fd_status;
8467        // FT with no-wait flags: runs once, as Linux does.
8468        assert_eq!(
8469            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, false, true, true),
8470            IOAction::PassThru
8471        );
8472        // FT without them: simulate blocking by retrying.
8473        assert_eq!(
8474            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, false, true, false),
8475            IOAction::NonblockizeRetry
8476        );
8477        // TT already runs once, flags or not; FF can only block externally.
8478        assert_eq!(
8479            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, true, true, false),
8480            IOAction::PassThru
8481        );
8482        assert_eq!(
8483            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, false, false, true),
8484            IOAction::Blocking
8485        );
8486    }
