8488    /// `MSG_DONTWAIT` keeps every socket send and receive from waiting,
8489    /// whatever else its flags carry, and no other flag does: recvmmsg's
8490    /// `MSG_WAITFORONE` still waits for the first datagram. Calls with no
8491    /// per-call flags always follow the file.
8492    /// The three receive calls read the error queue exactly when their flags
8493    /// carry `MSG_ERRQUEUE`, which does not by itself keep them from waiting;
8494    /// a send's flags never read it.
8495    #[test]
8496    fn msg_errqueue_marks_only_a_receive_as_an_error_queue_read() {
8497        use reverie::syscalls::*;
8498        let errqueue = libc::MSG_ERRQUEUE;
8499        assert!(Recvfrom::new().with_flags(errqueue).reads_error_queue());
8500        assert!(
8501            Recvmsg::new()
8502                .with_flags(errqueue | libc::MSG_PEEK)
8503                .reads_error_queue()
8504        );
8505        assert!(
8506            Recvmmsg::new()
8507                .with_flags(errqueue as u32)
8508                .reads_error_queue()
8509        );
8510        assert!(
8511            !Recvfrom::new()
8512                .with_flags(libc::MSG_DONTWAIT)
8513                .reads_error_queue()
8514        );
8515        assert!(
8516            !Recvmsg::new()
8517                .with_flags(libc::MSG_PEEK)
8518                .reads_error_queue()
8519        );
8520        assert!(
8521            !Recvmmsg::new()
8522                .with_flags(libc::MSG_WAITFORONE as u32)
8523                .reads_error_queue()
8524        );
8525        assert!(!Recvmsg::new().with_flags(errqueue).flags_forbid_waiting());
8526        assert!(
8527            !Sendto::new()
8528                .with_flags(errqueue as u32)
8529                .reads_error_queue()
8530        );
8531        assert!(!Sendmsg::new().with_flags(errqueue).reads_error_queue());
8532        assert!(!Sendmmsg::new().with_flags(errqueue).reads_error_queue());
8533        assert!(!Read::new().reads_error_queue());
8534    }

8536    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929> (review round 2,
8537    /// finding A): on a backend with a process signal control, a woken `poll`
8538    /// or unmasked `ppoll`, whose Linux interrupt is a restart code, ends
8539    /// through ERESTARTSYS, which the backend restarts when no handler runs,
8540    /// unless a handler with SA_RESTART catches the signal, which ERESTARTSYS
8541    /// would restart and Linux never does: that gets EINTR. Every other call,
8542    /// and every other backend, keeps its interrupt errno.
8543    #[test]
8544    fn a_woken_poll_restarts_through_erestartsys_where_linux_restarts_it() {
8545        // x86_64 only: aarch64 has ppoll alone.
8546        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8547        let poll = reverie::syscalls::Poll::new().with_timeout(-1);
8548        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8549        let timed_poll = reverie::syscalls::Poll::new().with_timeout(100);
8550        let ppoll = reverie::syscalls::Ppoll::new();
8551        for control in [true, false] {
8552            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8553            assert_eq!(woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys(control, &poll), control);
8554            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8555            assert_eq!(
8556                woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys(control, &timed_poll),
8557                control
8558            );
8559            assert_eq!(
8560                woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys(control, &ppoll),
8561                control
8562            );
8563            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8564            assert!(!woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys(
8565                control,
8566                &reverie::syscalls::EpollWait::new()
8567            ));
8568            assert!(!woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys(
8569                control,
8570                &reverie::syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new()
8571            ));
8572            assert!(!woken_call_ends_through_erestartsys(
8573                control,
8574                &reverie::syscalls::Read::new()
8575            ));
8576        }
8577        assert_eq!(
8578            woken_poll_errno_for(Some(WaitSignalDisposition::Restart)),
8579            Errno::EINTR
8580        );
8581        assert_eq!(
8582            woken_poll_errno_for(Some(WaitSignalDisposition::Interrupt)),
8583            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
8584        );
8585        assert_eq!(woken_poll_errno_for(None), Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
8586    }

8588    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929> (the Codex review of
8589    /// slice 2, rounds 3 and 4): a woken `poll` is settled by the first signal
8590    /// its return to user mode delivers, in Linux's dequeue order: the
8591    /// thread's own queue before its process's, and in each a synchronous
8592    /// signal first, then the lowest number, outside its mask. EINTR when that
8593    /// one has a handler, whatever its SA_RESTART, and ERESTARTSYS otherwise,
8594    /// whichever signal woke it. A caught signal behind an ignored one does
8595    /// not decide it: the ignored copy's delivery can hand the thread to the
8596    /// scheduler, and another thread can take the caught copy first, so the
8597    /// backend's ERESTARTSYS protocol settles it at its own delivery.
8598    #[test]
8599    fn a_woken_poll_is_settled_by_the_signals_its_return_delivers() {
8600        let bit = |signal: i32| 1u64 << (signal - 1);
8601        let alrm = bit(libc::SIGALRM);
8602        let usr1 = bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
8603        let term = bit(libc::SIGTERM);
8604        let hup = bit(libc::SIGHUP);
8605        let segv = bit(libc::SIGSEGV);
8606        let sets_of = reverie::SignalSets::new;
8607        for (label, sets, errno) in [
8608            // Codex's shared probe: an ignored SIGUSR1 comes first, and the
8609            // caught SIGALRM behind it is left to the backend's protocol: a
8610            // sibling may take it during the SIGUSR1 delivery's turn.
8611            (
8612                "ignored first, caught behind",
8613                sets_of(0, alrm | usr1, 0, usr1, alrm),
8614                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8615            ),
8616            // The thread's own queue comes first: its ignored SIGTERM before
8617            // the process's caught SIGUSR1, whose number is lower.
8618            (
8619                "own queue first",
8620                sets_of(term, usr1, 0, term, usr1),
8621                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8622            ),
8623            // And its caught SIGTERM before the process's ignored SIGHUP.
8624            (
8625                "own queue first, caught",
8626                sets_of(term, hup, 0, hup, term),
8627                Errno::EINTR,
8628            ),
8629            // A synchronous signal comes before a lower number.
8630            (
8631                "synchronous first",
8632                sets_of(0, hup | segv, 0, segv, hup),
8633                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8634            ),
8635            // A blocked signal is not dequeued: the caught one after it is.
8636            (
8637                "blocked one skipped",
8638                sets_of(0, alrm | usr1, usr1, usr1, alrm),
8639                Errno::EINTR,
8640            ),
8641            // An ignored SIGALRM woke it, and a caught SIGUSR1 waits in the
8642            // process's queue: that handler runs at the return.
8643            (
8644                "mixed",
8645                sets_of(0, alrm | usr1, 0, alrm, usr1),
8646                Errno::EINTR,
8647            ),
8648            // The same with SIGUSR1 in the thread's own queue.
8649            (
8650                "mixed, own queue",
8651                sets_of(usr1, alrm, 0, alrm, usr1),
8652                Errno::EINTR,
8653            ),
8654            // A caught copy alone.
8655            ("caught", sets_of(0, alrm, 0, 0, alrm), Errno::EINTR),
8656            // The ignored copy alone is dropped, and the call restarts.
8657            (
8658                "ignored",
8659                sets_of(0, alrm, 0, alrm, usr1),
8660                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8661            ),
8662            // The caught copy it was woken for was taken by another thread
8663            // first: nothing is delivered, and the call restarts.
8664            (
8665                "taken",
8666                sets_of(0, 0, 0, 0, alrm | usr1),
8667                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8668            ),
8669            // A caught signal its mask blocks stays pending.
8670            (
8671                "blocked",
8672                sets_of(0, alrm | usr1, usr1, alrm, usr1),
8673                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8674            ),
8675            // A default action runs no handler: it ends the process, or the
8676            // copy is dropped and the call restarts.
8677            (
8678                "default",
8679                sets_of(0, bit(libc::SIGTERM), 0, 0, usr1),
8680                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8681            ),
8682        ] {
8683            assert_eq!(woken_poll_errno_from_sets(sets), errno, "{label}");
8684        }
8685    }

8687    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929> (the Codex review of
8688    /// slice 2, round 2): a receive or an accept on a socket with a finite
8689    /// `SO_RCVTIMEO` ends with EINTR, whatever its handler's `SA_RESTART`, as
8690    /// Linux's `sock_intr_errno` ends it; a send or a connect by a finite
8691    /// `SO_SNDTIMEO` ends the same way; an untimed one keeps ERESTARTSYS,
8692    /// which `SA_RESTART` restarts; every other call keeps its errno. The
8693    /// same mapping picks the deadline a polled socket call waits by
8694    /// (`execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall`).

8699        for (label, syscall, expected) in [

8705            (
8706                "recvmsg",

8709            ),
8710            (
8711                "recvmmsg",
8712                Syscall::from(syscalls::Recvmmsg::new().with_fd(5)),
8713                Some((5, SocketTimeoutDirection::Receive)),
8714            ),
8715            (
8716                "read",
8717                Syscall::from(syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(6)),
8718                Some((6, SocketTimeoutDirection::Receive)),
8719            ),
8720            (
8721                "readv",
8722                Syscall::from(syscalls::Readv::new().with_fd(7)),
8723                Some((7, SocketTimeoutDirection::Receive)),
8724            ),
8725            (
8726                "accept",
8727                Syscall::from(syscalls::Accept::new().with_sockfd(8)),
8728                Some((8, SocketTimeoutDirection::Receive)),
8729            ),
8730            (
8731                "accept4",
8732                Syscall::from(syscalls::Accept4::new().with_sockfd(9)),

8734            ),
8735            (
8736                "sendto",
8737                Syscall::from(syscalls::Sendto::new().with_fd(10)),
8738                Some((10, SocketTimeoutDirection::Send)),
8739            ),
8740            (
8741                "sendmsg",

8744            ),
8745            (
8746                "sendmmsg",
8747                Syscall::from(syscalls::Sendmmsg::new().with_sockfd(12)),

8749            ),
8750            (
8751                "write",
8752                Syscall::from(syscalls::Write::new().with_fd(13)),

8754            ),
8755            (
8756                "writev",
8757                Syscall::from(syscalls::Writev::new().with_fd(14)),

8761                "connect",

8766            ("poll", Syscall::from(syscalls::Poll::new()), None),

8769        }
8770        for (default, timeout, expected) in [
8771            (Errno::ERESTARTSYS, Some(second), Errno::EINTR),

8783                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,

8785                Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8786            ),
8787            (Errno::ERESTARTSYS, None, Errno::ERESTARTSYS),
8788            (Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND, Some(second), Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND),
8789            (Errno::EINTR, Some(second), Errno::EINTR),
8790            (Errno::EINTR, None, Errno::EINTR),
8791        ] {

8793                socket_timeout_interrupt_errno(default, timeout),
8794                expected,

8835    #[test]
8836    fn signal_interruption_errno_matches_linux_restart_policy() {
8837        // x86_64 only: aarch64 has no poll or epoll_wait, only ppoll and
8838        // epoll_pwait.
8839        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8840        assert_eq!(
8841            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
8842            Errno::EINTR
8843        );
8844        assert_eq!(
8845            reverie::syscalls::Ppoll::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
8846            Errno::EINTR
8847        );
8848        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8849        assert_eq!(
8850            reverie::syscalls::EpollWait::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
8851            Errno::EINTR
8852        );
8853        assert_eq!(
8854            reverie::syscalls::EpollPwait::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
8855            Errno::EINTR
8856        );
8857        let sigtimedwait = reverie::syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new();
8858        assert_eq!(sigtimedwait.signal_interrupt_errno(), Errno::EINTR);
8859        assert!(sigtimedwait.syscall_would_have_blocked(Err(Errno::EAGAIN)));
8860        assert_eq!(sigtimedwait.timeout_return_val(), Err(Errno::EAGAIN));
8861        assert_eq!(
8862            reverie::syscalls::Read::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
8863            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
8864        );
8865        // A zero-progress writev interruption returns this internal errno on
8866        // ptrace so Linux applies the handler's SA_RESTART policy.
8867        assert_eq!(
8868            reverie::syscalls::Writev::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
8869            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
8870        );
8871        assert_eq!(
8872            reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
8873            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
8874        );
8875    }

8877    #[test]
8878    fn kernel_restart_errno_matches_linux_restart_policy() {
8879        // Signal-state interruption hands the kernel the wait's own restart code, so
8880        // the guest's disposition decides between a handler's EINTR and a restart
8881        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
8882        // A poll with a positive timeout and a timed futex wait end with Linux's own
8883        // code: a handler turns it into EINTR, and with no handler the kernel runs
8884        // restart_syscall, which Detcore resumes with the deadline it kept
8885        // (`RestartBlock`, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358).
8886        // x86_64 only: aarch64 has no poll or epoll_wait, only ppoll and
8887        // epoll_pwait.
8888        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8889        assert_eq!(
8890            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new()
8891                .with_timeout(300)
8892                .kernel_restart_errno(),
8893            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
8894        );
8895        // A zero timeout never blocks and a negative one never expires, so there is
8896        // no deadline to keep, and running the call again is Linux's restart.
8897        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8898        assert_eq!(
8899            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
8900            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
8901        );
8902        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8903        assert_eq!(
8904            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new()
8905                .with_timeout(-1)
8906                .kernel_restart_errno(),
8907            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
8908        );
8909        assert_eq!(
8910            reverie::syscalls::Ppoll::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
8911            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
8912        );
8913        // epoll_wait and sigtimedwait never restart after a handler.
8914        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
8915        assert_eq!(
8916            reverie::syscalls::EpollWait::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
8917            Errno::EINTR
8918        );
8919        assert_eq!(
8920            reverie::syscalls::EpollPwait::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
8921            Errno::EINTR
8922        );
8923        assert_eq!(
8924            reverie::syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
8925            Errno::EINTR
8926        );
8927        assert_eq!(
8928            reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
8929            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
8930        );
8931        // A timed wait is never restarted after a handler runs. FUTEX_WAIT's timeout
8932        // is relative, so its deadline is kept as poll's is.
8933        let timeout = reverie::syscalls::Addr::from_raw(0x1000).unwrap();
8934        assert_eq!(
8935            reverie::syscalls::Futex::new()
8936                .with_timeout(Some(timeout))
8937                .kernel_restart_errno(),
8938            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
8939        );
8940        // FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET's timeout is an absolute deadline, which Linux copies
8941        // into the restart block as it does FUTEX_WAIT's, so a deadline the guest
8942        // moves in memory after the wait began has no effect. Running the call
8943        // again, which ERESTARTNOHAND did, read the moved deadline (round-10
8944        // finding Medium 4 on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
8945        let bitset = reverie::syscalls::Futex::new()
8946            .with_futex_op(libc::FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET | libc::FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG)
8947            .with_val3(-1);
8948        assert_eq!(bitset.kernel_restart_errno(), Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
8949        assert!(!bitset.restart_keeps_deadline());
8950        assert_eq!(
8951            bitset.with_timeout(Some(timeout)).kernel_restart_errno(),
8952            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
8953        );
8954        assert!(bitset.with_timeout(Some(timeout)).restart_keeps_deadline());
8955        // FUTEX_LOCK_PI and FUTEX_LOCK_PI2 are always restarted, timed or not, and
8956        // the restarted call reads its absolute deadline again (`futex_lock_pi`).
8957        for op in [
8958            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI,
8959            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI | libc::FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG,
8960            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI2 | libc::FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME,
8961        ] {
8962            let lock = reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().with_futex_op(op);
8963            assert_eq!(lock.kernel_restart_errno(), Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR);
8964            let timed = lock.with_timeout(Some(timeout));
8965            assert_eq!(timed.kernel_restart_errno(), Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR);
8966            assert!(!timed.restart_keeps_deadline());
8967        }
8968    }

8970    #[test]
8971    fn a_held_signal_is_reported_unless_it_is_sigstop() {
8972        // The backend passes a held signal on unreported when the call returns
8973        // ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK, so a held signal other than SIGSTOP ends the wait
8974        // with ERESTARTNOHAND, which a handler also turns into EINTR.
8975        for signal in [libc::SIGUSR1, libc::SIGTERM, libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGCHLD] {
8976            assert_eq!(
8977                held_signal_restart_errno(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK, signal),
8978                Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND,
8979                "signal {signal}"
8980            );
8981        }
8982        // SIGSTOP is never reported, and its restart must keep the deadline.
8983        assert_eq!(
8984            held_signal_restart_errno(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK, libc::SIGSTOP),
8985            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
8986        );
8987        // Every other restart code is the call's own.
8988        for errno in [
8989            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND,
8990            Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
8991            Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR,
8992            Errno::EINTR,
8993        ] {
8994            for signal in [libc::SIGUSR1, libc::SIGSTOP] {
8995                assert_eq!(held_signal_restart_errno(errno, signal), errno);
8996            }
8997        }
8998    }

9000    #[test]
9001    fn resumed_kernel_wait_result_maps_only_erestartsys() {
9002        // The backend's code for a signal that stopped the injected restart
9003        // before it ran; the kernel's restart block is still in place.
9004        assert_eq!(
9005            resumed_kernel_wait_result(Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)),
9006            Err(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK)
9007        );
9008        // Every other result is the restarted wait's own.
9009        for result in [
9010            Ok(0),
9011            Err(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK),
9012            Err(Errno::EINTR),
9013            Err(Errno::ETIMEDOUT),
9014            Err(Errno::EAGAIN),
9015        ] {
9016            assert_eq!(resumed_kernel_wait_result(result), result);
9017        }
9018    }

9020    #[test]
9021    fn a_restart_block_resumes_only_at_the_interrupted_call() {
9022        let timeout = reverie::syscalls::Addr::from_raw(0x1000).unwrap();
9023        let block = RestartBlock {
9024            rip: 0x4000_1234,
9025            deadline: Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000)),
9026            call: RestartCall::Futex(reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().with_timeout(Some(timeout))),
9027        };
9028        // The kernel's restart runs restart_syscall at the interrupted call's address.
9029        assert_eq!(block.resumed_at(0x4000_1234), Some(block));
9030        // A restart_syscall anywhere else is the guest's own call.
9031        assert_eq!(block.resumed_at(0x4000_1236), None);
9032        assert_eq!(block.resumed_at(0x4000_1232), None);
9033    }
9034
9035    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929> (the Claude review of
9036    /// slice 2, round 6, finding 1): a `poll` takes only the record a woken
9037    /// `poll` kept for its own rerun (`RestartCall::PollRerun`), at the same
9038    /// address with the same arguments. The record a `poll` interrupted by
9039    /// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` keeps for the kernel's `restart_syscall`
9040    /// (`RestartCall::Poll`) is not taken: a program's own retry after a
9041    /// handler's EINTR is a new call, which Linux gives its whole timeout
9042    /// again, and one that took that record ended at the first call's end
9043    /// time on ptrace.
9044    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
9045    #[test]
9046    fn a_poll_takes_only_the_record_kept_for_its_rerun() {
9047        let poll = reverie::syscalls::Poll::new()
9048            .with_nfds(1)
9049            .with_timeout(100);
9050        let deadline = Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(100_000_000));
9051        let record = |call| RestartBlock {
9052            rip: 0x4000_1234,
9053            deadline,
9054            call,
9055        };
9056        let rerun = record(RestartCall::PollRerun(poll));
9057        assert_eq!(rerun.rerun_deadline(0x4000_1234, poll), Some(deadline));
9058        // Another address or other arguments make another call.
9059        assert_eq!(rerun.rerun_deadline(0x4000_1236, poll), None);
9060        assert_eq!(
9061            rerun.rerun_deadline(0x4000_1234, poll.with_timeout(200)),
9062            None
9063        );
9064        // The record kept for the kernel's restart serves only that restart.
9065        let restart = record(RestartCall::Poll(poll));
9066        assert_eq!(restart.rerun_deadline(0x4000_1234, poll), None);
9067        assert_eq!(restart.resumed_at(0x4000_1234), Some(restart));
9068    }

9070    #[test]
9071    fn writev_signal_result_uses_disposition_and_progress() {

9073        for disposition in [
9074            WaitSignalDisposition::Interrupt,
9075            WaitSignalDisposition::Restart,

9077            assert!(matches!(

9079                Some(Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)))

9107        assert!(
9108            !external.polls_guest_state_only,

9115/// `KernelSignalWait` against a scripted guest and a scripted `/proc` read
9116/// (`signal_state_read_seam`). No failure of the wait's signal handling may reach
9117/// the guest as an errno its wait call cannot return, and the guest must never
9118/// resume with every signal blocked
9119/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
9120#[cfg(test)]
9121pub(crate) mod kernel_signal_wait_failures {
9122    use std::collections::VecDeque;
9123    use std::sync::Arc;
9124    use std::sync::Mutex;
9125
9126    use reverie::GlobalRPC;
9127    use reverie::GlobalTool;
9128    use reverie::Pid;
9129    use reverie::Signal;
9130    use reverie::syscalls::LocalMemory;
9131
9132    use super::*;
9133    use crate::Config;
9134    use crate::GlobalState;
9135    use crate::ThreadState;
9136    use crate::syscalls::threads::KernelSignalState;
9137    use crate::syscalls::threads::kernel_sigset_bit;
9138    use crate::syscalls::threads::signal_state_read_seam;
9139    use crate::types::DetPid;
9140
9141    /// What an injected `rt_sigprocmask` does.
9142    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
9143    enum MaskOutcome {
9144        /// The call runs: the mask changes and it returns 0.
9145        Apply,
9146        /// A signal stops the guest before the call runs: the mask is unchanged
9147        /// and the backend reports its restart errno.
9148        StoppedBefore,
9149        /// The call cannot run at all.
9150        Fail(Errno),
9151        /// `StoppedBefore`, by a signal that `/proc` never showed because it
9152        /// arrived after the read before the injection, such as a `SIGSTOP`
9153        /// sent from outside: the backend holds it in its single slot
9154        /// (`FakeKernel::held_slot`).
9155        StoppedBy(i32),
9156    }
9157
9158    /// The kernel's view of the guest thread, shared by the scripted `/proc`
9159    /// read and the scripted guest.
9160    #[derive(Default)]
9161    struct FakeKernel {
9162        /// The thread's mask (`SigBlk`).
9163        blocked: KernelSigset,
9164        /// Pending signals (`SigPnd | ShdPnd`).
9165        pending: KernelSigset,
9166        /// The signals of `pending` pending only on the thread group's shared
9167        /// queue (`ShdPnd`); every other one is on the thread's own
9168        /// (`SigPnd`).
9169        shared: KernelSigset,
9170        /// Signals with a handler (`SigCgt`).
9171        caught: KernelSigset,
9172        /// Signals whose disposition is `SIG_IGN` (`SigIgn`).
9173        ignored: KernelSigset,
9174        /// Whether a pending signal outside the mask stops each injection before
9175        /// the call runs, as on ptrace, where an ignored signal still queues for
9176        /// a traced task: it leaves the queue for the backend to hold
9177        /// (`taken`), and the injection reports a restart errno.
9178        stops_for_pending: bool,
9179        /// The signals that stopped an injection, in order.
9180        taken: Vec<i32>,
9181        /// Errors for the next reads, one per read.
9182        read_failures: VecDeque<Errno>,
9183        /// The backend confirmed exit; every later proc read sees ESRCH.
9184        gone: bool,
9185        /// Outcomes for the next `rt_sigprocmask` calls; `Apply` once empty.
9186        outcomes: VecDeque<MaskOutcome>,
9187        /// Enable an empty nonblocking read, counting the probes that actually
9188        /// run. A signal stop before the probe returns ERESTARTSYS instead,
9189        /// so Guest's real default retry wrapper must retry it.
9190        empty_read_probes: Option<usize>,
9191        /// Bound an actual retry-loop test by making this probe ready, if a
9192        /// lost signal prevents the earlier interruption it must observe.
9193        read_ready_after: Option<usize>,
9194        /// Physical masks at the private read probes that actually execute.
9195        read_probe_masks: Vec<KernelSigset>,
9196        /// Bounded scalar-write probes and their physical masks. A signal
9197        /// posted after the first attempt is first visible on its retry turn.
9198        write_probe_masks: Option<Vec<KernelSigset>>,
9199        pending_after_first_write: KernelSigset,
9200        /// Every mask the guest was asked to set, in order.
9201        requested: Vec<KernelSigset>,
9202        /// How many more signals that stop an injection are sent again, as by
9203        /// a sender faster than the injections: each such signal is pending
9204        /// again from the read after the one that follows the stop, which still
9205        /// shows it gone, so the stop is identified (`pending_repost`).
9206        repost_after_take: usize,
9207        /// The signals sent after the next snapshot, which the following read
9208        /// shows. Also models a first arrival racing an empty pending snapshot.
9209        pending_repost: KernelSigset,
9210        /// The backend's one slot for a held signal: each signal that stops an
9211        /// injection (`taken`, `MaskOutcome::StoppedBy`) replaces the one there,
9212        /// as Reverie's ptrace backend does (`hold_pending_signal`).
9213        held_slot: Option<i32>,
9214        /// The signals that a stop dropped from `held_slot`, in order. A standard
9215        /// signal that replaces itself is merged, as Linux merges a second one
9216        /// sent while the first is pending, and is not lost.
9217        lost: Vec<i32>,
9218        /// Answers for the next `Guest::set_blocked_signals` calls: `None`
9219        /// sets the mask and returns the old one; once empty, every call is
9220        /// refused as `Unsupported`, as the trait's default refuses.
9221        setter: VecDeque<Option<MaskChangeRefused>>,
9222        /// Every mask `Guest::set_blocked_signals` was asked to set, in order.
9223        set_calls: Vec<KernelSigset>,
9224        /// The scheduler's answer to `HostTimedAndPrivateSigchld`: the
9225        /// host-timed signals, then the recorded private `SIGCHLD`. `None`
9226        /// panics, as every other request does.
9227        private_record: Option<(KernelSigset, KernelSigset)>,
9228    }
9229
9230    impl FakeKernel {
9231        /// The backend holds `signal`, which stopped an injection.
9232        fn hold(&mut self, signal: i32) {
9233            if let Some(previous) = self.held_slot.replace(signal)
9234                && !(previous == signal && signal < KERNEL_SIGRTMIN)
9235            {
9236                self.lost.push(previous);
9237            }
9238        }
9239    }
9240
9241    type Kernel = Arc<Mutex<FakeKernel>>;
9242
9243    /// Room for one mask, 8-byte aligned like a real stack slot.
9244    const ARENA_WORDS: usize = 2;
9245
9246    /// A scratch stack in this process's memory whose commit can fail like the
9247    /// ptrace scratch below an `rsp` with no writable memory under it
9248    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3328).
9249    struct WaitStack {
9250        commit_fails: bool,
9251        arena: usize,
9252    }
9253
9254    struct WaitStackGuard;
9255
9256    impl Drop for WaitStackGuard {
9257        fn drop(&mut self) {}
9258    }
9259
9260    impl reverie::Stack for WaitStack {
9261        type StackGuard = WaitStackGuard;
9262
9263        fn size(&self) -> usize {
9264            panic!("a blocked wait must not query the scratch size")
9265        }
9266        fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
9267            panic!("a blocked wait must not query the scratch capacity")
9268        }
9269        fn push<'stack, T>(&mut self, value: T) -> Addr<'stack, T> {
9270            assert!(std::mem::size_of::<T>() <= ARENA_WORDS * std::mem::size_of::<u64>());
9271            // SAFETY: the arena is a live, 8-byte aligned buffer owned by the guest,
9272            // large enough for `T` (asserted above).
9273            unsafe { std::ptr::write(self.arena as *mut T, value) };
9274            Addr::from_raw(self.arena).unwrap()
9275        }
9276        fn reserve<'stack, T>(&mut self) -> AddrMut<'stack, T> {
9277            panic!("a blocked wait pushes its mask rather than reserving room")
9278        }
9279        fn commit(self) -> Result<Self::StackGuard, Errno> {
9280            if self.commit_fails {
9281                Err(Errno::EFAULT)
9282            } else {
9283                Ok(WaitStackGuard)
9284            }
9285        }
9286    }
9287
9288    struct WaitGuest {
9289        config: Config,
9290        thread: ThreadState<()>,
9291        pid: Pid,
9292        tid: Pid,
9293        commit_fails: bool,
9294        arena: Box<[u64; ARENA_WORDS]>,
9295        kernel: Kernel,
9296        proof_script: Option<Arc<Mutex<ProofScript>>>,
9297        /// The signal sets `Guest::signal_sets` reports, where it reports any.
9298        sets: Option<reverie::SignalSets>,
9299    }
9300
9301    impl WaitGuest {
9302        /// A guest for thread `tid` of this process, with the guest's own `mask`
9303        /// installed.
9304        fn new(tid: Pid, mask: KernelSigset) -> (Self, Kernel) {
9305            let config = Config::default();
9306            let thread = ThreadState::new(DetPid::from_raw(1), &config, ());
9307            let kernel = Arc::new(Mutex::new(FakeKernel {
9308                blocked: mask,
9309                ..FakeKernel::default()
9310            }));
9311            let guest = Self {
9312                config,
9313                thread,
9314                pid: Pid::from_raw(std::process::id() as i32),
9315                tid,
9316                commit_fails: false,
9317                arena: Box::new([u64::MAX; ARENA_WORDS]),
9318                kernel: kernel.clone(),
9319                proof_script: None,
9320                sets: None,
9321            };
9322            (guest, kernel)
9323        }
9324
9325        /// A guest for the calling thread, which exists.
9326        fn live(mask: KernelSigset) -> (Self, Kernel) {
9327            // SAFETY: gettid has no preconditions.
9328            Self::new(Pid::from_raw(unsafe { libc::gettid() }), mask)
9329        }
9330    }
9331
9332    /// The decision `ioaction_based_on_fd_status` takes from the call's own
9333    /// flags. On a socket the guest left blocking, which Detcore keeps
9334    /// physically nonblocking, a send or receive is retried until it stops
9335    /// failing with `EAGAIN` (`NonblockizeRetry`), unless its flags carry
9336    /// `MSG_DONTWAIT`: then it runs once (`PassThru`), as Linux runs it.
9337    /// recvmmsg's `MSG_WAITFORONE` alone still waits for the first datagram.
9338    /// On a socket the guest made `O_NONBLOCK`, every call runs once, and on
9339    /// one Detcore leaves physically blocking every call takes the blocking
9340    /// path.
9341    #[test]
9342    fn msg_dontwait_runs_a_call_once_on_a_socket_the_guest_left_blocking() {
9343        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
9344
9345        use reverie::syscalls::Recvfrom;
9346        use reverie::syscalls::Recvmmsg;
9347        use reverie::syscalls::Recvmsg;
9348        use reverie::syscalls::Sendmmsg;
9349        use reverie::syscalls::Sendmsg;
9350        use reverie::syscalls::Sendto;
9351
9352        let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
9353        let (socket, _peer) = std::os::unix::net::UnixDatagram::pair().unwrap();
9354        let fd = socket.as_raw_fd();
9355        guest
9356            .thread
9357            .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDWR, FdType::Socket, None)
9358            .unwrap();
9359        let dontwait = libc::MSG_DONTWAIT;
9360        let waitforone = libc::MSG_WAITFORONE;
9361        let once = Ok(IOAction::PassThru);
9362        let retry = Ok(IOAction::NonblockizeRetry);
9363        let decisions = |guest: &mut WaitGuest| {
9364            [
9365                (
9366                    "recvfrom",
9367                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9368                        guest,
9369                        Recvfrom::new().with_fd(fd).with_flags(dontwait),
9370                    ),
9371                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, Recvfrom::new().with_fd(fd)),
9372                ),
9373                (
9374                    "recvmsg",
9375                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9376                        guest,
9377                        Recvmsg::new().with_sockfd(fd).with_flags(dontwait),
9378                    ),
9379                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, Recvmsg::new().with_sockfd(fd)),
9380                ),
9381                (
9382                    "recvmmsg",
9383                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9384                        guest,
9385                        Recvmmsg::new()
9386                            .with_fd(fd)
9387                            .with_flags((waitforone | dontwait) as u32),
9388                    ),
9389                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9390                        guest,
9391                        Recvmmsg::new().with_fd(fd).with_flags(waitforone as u32),
9392                    ),
9393                ),
9394                (
9395                    "sendto",
9396                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9397                        guest,
9398                        Sendto::new().with_fd(fd).with_flags(dontwait as u32),
9399                    ),
9400                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, Sendto::new().with_fd(fd)),
9401                ),
9402                (
9403                    "sendmsg",
9404                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9405                        guest,
9406                        Sendmsg::new().with_fd(fd).with_flags(dontwait),
9407                    ),
9408                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, Sendmsg::new().with_fd(fd)),
9409                ),
9410                (
9411                    "sendmmsg",
9412                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9413                        guest,
9414                        Sendmmsg::new().with_sockfd(fd).with_flags(dontwait),
9415                    ),
9416                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, Sendmmsg::new().with_sockfd(fd)),
9417                ),
9418            ]
9419        };
9420        // A socket Detcore leaves physically blocking (an external socket
9421        // under record and replay) keeps the blocking path, flag or not.
9422        for (name, with_dontwait, without) in decisions(&mut guest) {
9423            let blocking = Ok(IOAction::Blocking);
9424            assert_eq!(
9425                with_dontwait, blocking,
9426                "{name} with MSG_DONTWAIT, blocking"
9427            );
9428            assert_eq!(without, blocking, "{name} without MSG_DONTWAIT, blocking");
9429        }
9430        guest
9431            .thread
9432            .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.set_physically_nonblocking())
9433            .unwrap();
9434        for (name, with_dontwait, without) in decisions(&mut guest) {
9435            assert_eq!(with_dontwait, once, "{name} with MSG_DONTWAIT");
9436            assert_eq!(without, retry, "{name} without MSG_DONTWAIT");
9437        }
9438        guest
9439            .thread
9440            .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.set_nonblocking(true))
9441            .unwrap();
9442        for (name, with_dontwait, without) in decisions(&mut guest) {
9443            assert_eq!(with_dontwait, once, "{name} with MSG_DONTWAIT, O_NONBLOCK");
9444            assert_eq!(without, once, "{name} without MSG_DONTWAIT, O_NONBLOCK");
9445        }
9446    }

9448    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
9449    enum ProofAction {
9450        None,
9451        Dup { from: i32, to: i32 },
9452        Operand { address: usize, fd: i32 },
9453        Mark { fd: i32, held: bool },
9454    }
9455
9456    #[derive(Default)]
9457    struct ProofScript {
9458        requests: Vec<Resources>,
9459        actions: VecDeque<ProofAction>,
9460        probes: usize,
9461        observe_retry_masks: bool,
9462        published_mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
9463        publications: Vec<Option<KernelSigset>>,
9464        retry_boundaries: Vec<(&'static str, KernelSigset, Option<KernelSigset>)>,
9465        route_child_on_retry: bool,
9466    }
9467
9468    impl WaitGuest {
9469        async fn proof_action(&self, action: ProofAction) {
9470            match action {
9471                ProofAction::None => {}
9472                ProofAction::Dup { from, to } => {
9473                    // Run the real mutation handler in a sibling sharing the
9474                    // descriptor table while the reader awaits its next turn.
9475                    let (mut sibling, _) = Self::new(Pid::from_raw(2), 0);
9476                    sibling.config = self.config.clone();
9477                    sibling.thread.dettid = DetTid::from_raw(2);
9478                    sibling.thread.detpid = self.thread.detpid;
9479                    sibling.thread.file_metadata = self.thread.file_metadata.clone();
9480                    sibling.proof_script = Some(Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProofScript::default())));
9481                    let tool = Detcore {
9482                        detpid: self.thread.detpid.unwrap(),
9483                        cfg: self.config.clone(),
9484                        record_or_replay: crate::record_or_replay::NoopTool,
9485                    };
9486                    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
9487                    assert_eq!(
9488                        tool.handle_dup2(
9489                            &mut sibling,
9490                            syscalls::Dup2::new().with_oldfd(from).with_newfd(to),
9491                        )
9492                        .await
9493                        .unwrap(),
9494                        i64::from(to)
9495                    );
9496                    #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
9497                    assert_eq!(
9498                        tool.handle_dup3(
9499                            &mut sibling,
9500                            syscalls::Dup3::new()
9501                                .with_oldfd(from)
9502                                .with_newfd(to)
9503                                .with_flags(nix::fcntl::OFlag::empty()),
9504                        )
9505                        .await
9506                        .unwrap(),
9507                        i64::from(to)
9508                    );
9509                }
9510                ProofAction::Operand { address, fd } => {
9511                    // A sibling can change the shared pollfd array without
9512                    // changing either descriptor-table entry.
9513                    LocalMemory::new()
9514                        .write_value(AddrMut::<i32>::from_raw(address).unwrap(), &fd)
9515                        .unwrap();
9516                }
9517                ProofAction::Mark { fd, held } => {
9518                    self.thread
9519                        .with_detfd(fd, |entry| {
9520                            if held {
9521                                entry.set_guest_held();
9522                            } else {
9523                                entry.clear_guest_held();
9524                            }
9525                        })
9526                        .unwrap();
9527                }
9528            }
9529        }
9530    }

9532    /// Reuse the local-memory guest for descriptor guards that need no injections.
9533    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
9534    pub(crate) fn fd_test_guest() -> impl Guest<Detcore> {
9535        WaitGuest::live(0).0
9536    }

9538    /// A signal that ends a polled read that would still wait returns the
9539    /// read's restart errno, except for a read that began on an inotify
9540    /// instance that is nonblocking for the guest by then, as another
9541    /// thread's F_SETFL or FIONBIO makes it during the wait: `inotify_read`
9542    /// tests O_NONBLOCK before a pending signal, so Linux returns EAGAIN. A
9543    /// pipe read keeps the restart errno, as `pipe_read`'s interrupted wait
9544    /// returns -ERESTARTSYS itself. The description the read began on
9545    /// decides, not what its number names at the wake: a pipe read whose
9546    /// number a sibling's dup2 points at a nonblocking inotify instance keeps
9547    /// the restart errno, as Linux's read keeps the pipe it began on.
9548    #[test]
9549    fn a_signal_ends_an_inotify_read_made_nonblocking_meanwhile_with_eagain() {
9550        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
9551        use std::os::fd::FromRawFd;
9552
9553        let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
9554        // SAFETY: inotify_init1 returns a new owned descriptor.
9555        let inotify = unsafe {
9556            std::fs::File::from_raw_fd(libc::inotify_init1(libc::IN_NONBLOCK | libc::IN_CLOEXEC))
9557        };
9558        let (pipe, _writer) = std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
9559        let (inotify, pipe) = (inotify.as_raw_fd(), pipe.as_raw_fd());
9560        guest
9561            .thread
9562            .add_fd(inotify, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY, FdType::Inotify, None)
9563            .unwrap();
9564        guest
9565            .thread
9566            .add_fd(pipe, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY, FdType::Pipe, None)
9567            .unwrap();
9568        for fd in [inotify, pipe] {
9569            guest
9570                .thread
9571                .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.set_physically_nonblocking())
9572                .unwrap();
9573        }
9574        let read = |fd| syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd);
9575        let inotify_read = inotify_description_of(&guest, read(inotify));
9576        let pipe_read = inotify_description_of(&guest, read(pipe));
9577        assert!(inotify_read.is_some());
9578        assert!(pipe_read.is_none(), "only an inotify read is bound");
9579        assert_eq!(
9580            interrupted_wait_errno(
9581                inotify_read.as_ref(),
9582                read(inotify).signal_interrupt_errno()
9583            ),
9584            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
9585        );
9586        assert_eq!(
9587            interrupted_wait_errno(pipe_read.as_ref(), read(pipe).signal_interrupt_errno()),
9588            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
9589        );
9590        for fd in [inotify, pipe] {
9591            guest
9592                .thread
9593                .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.set_logical_nonblocking(true))
9594                .unwrap();
9595        }
9596        assert_eq!(
9597            interrupted_wait_errno(
9598                inotify_read.as_ref(),
9599                read(inotify).signal_interrupt_errno()
9600            ),
9601            Errno::EAGAIN
9602        );
9603        assert_eq!(
9604            interrupted_wait_errno(
9605                inotify_read.as_ref(),
9606                syscalls::Readv::new()
9607                    .with_fd(inotify)
9608                    .signal_interrupt_errno()
9609            ),
9610            Errno::EAGAIN
9611        );
9612        assert_eq!(
9613            interrupted_wait_errno(pipe_read.as_ref(), read(pipe).signal_interrupt_errno()),
9614            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
9615        );
9616        // A sibling's dup2 points the pipe read's number at the nonblocking
9617        // inotify instance: the read began on the pipe, whose restart errno
9618        // stands.
9619        guest
9620            .thread
9621            .dup_fd(inotify, pipe, nix::fcntl::OFlag::empty())
9622            .unwrap();
9623        assert_eq!(
9624            interrupted_wait_errno(pipe_read.as_ref(), read(pipe).signal_interrupt_errno()),
9625            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
9626        );
9627        assert!(inotify_description_of(&guest, read(pipe)).is_some());
9628    }

9630    /// The signal a part of a call run in parts completes with carries to the
9631    /// parts after it (`carried_signal`): one the turn found that would end a
9632    /// part after progress, a pending copy or a named wake; where the turn does
9633    /// not decide, its signal wake; and none under the in-guest delivery gate
9634    /// or for a turn that found nothing. It ends the first later part that
9635    /// would wait, once (`carried_signal_ends`).
9636    #[test]
9637    fn a_part_carries_the_signal_its_turn_found_to_the_next() {
9638        let pending = TurnSignals {
9639            named: 0,
9640            pending: kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
9641        };
9642        let named = TurnSignals {
9643            named: kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
9644            pending: 0,
9645        };
9646        let wake = ResumeStatus::Signaled(None);
9647        assert!(matches!(
9648            carried_signal(Some(pending), &ResumeStatus::Normal, false),
9649            Some(CarriedSignal::Decided)
9650        ));
9651        assert!(matches!(
9652            carried_signal(Some(named), &wake, false),
9653            Some(CarriedSignal::Decided)
9654        ));
9655        assert!(carried_signal(Some(TurnSignals::default()), &wake, false).is_none());
9656        assert!(matches!(
9657            carried_signal(None, &wake, false),
9658            Some(CarriedSignal::Wake(ResumeStatus::Signaled(None)))
9659        ));
9660        assert!(carried_signal(None, &wake, true).is_none());
9661        assert!(carried_signal(None, &ResumeStatus::Normal, false).is_none());
9662
9663        let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
9664        let ends = |guest: &mut WaitGuest, carried, decides_itself, gated| {
9665            guest.thread.call_parts = Some(CallParts {
9666                progress: true,
9667                carried,
9668            });
9669            let ends =
9670                futures::executor::block_on(carried_signal_ends(guest, decides_itself, gated))
9671                    .unwrap();
9672            let left = guest.thread.call_parts.as_ref().unwrap().carried.is_some();
9673            (ends, left)
9674        };
9675        assert_eq!(
9676            ends(&mut guest, Some(CarriedSignal::Decided), false, false),
9677            (true, false)
9678        );
9679        assert_eq!(
9680            ends(
9681                &mut guest,
9682                Some(CarriedSignal::Wake(wake.clone())),
9683                false,
9684                false
9685            ),
9686            (true, false)
9687        );
9688        assert_eq!(
9689            ends(&mut guest, Some(CarriedSignal::Wake(wake)), false, true),
9690            (false, false)
9691        );
9692        assert_eq!(ends(&mut guest, None, false, false), (false, false));
9693    }

9695    /// The error-queue branch of `ioaction_based_on_fd_status`. A receive
9696    /// with `MSG_ERRQUEUE` on a socket whose protocol reads that queue
9697    /// without waiting (`crate::fd::error_queue_read_never_waits`, a UDP or
9698    /// TCP socket) runs once (`PassThru`) on a socket the guest left
9699    /// blocking, which Detcore keeps physically nonblocking, where the same
9700    /// receive on a socket whose protocol ignores the flag (AF_UNIX) and a
9701    /// call without it are retried (`NonblockizeRetry`). On a socket Detcore
9702    /// leaves physically blocking the receive keeps the blocking path, and on
9703    /// one the guest made `O_NONBLOCK` it runs once anyway.
9704    /// `ioaction_based_on_fd`, the descriptor-only answer for a call that has
9705    /// no per-call flags, ignores all of this and follows the descriptor.
9706    #[test]
9707    fn an_error_queue_read_runs_once_only_where_its_protocol_never_waits() {
9708        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
9709
9710        use reverie::syscalls::Recvfrom;
9711        use reverie::syscalls::Recvmmsg;
9712        use reverie::syscalls::Recvmsg;
9713        use reverie::syscalls::Sendto;
9714
9715        let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
9716        let (socket, _peer) = std::os::unix::net::UnixDatagram::pair().unwrap();
9717        let fd = socket.as_raw_fd();
9718        guest
9719            .thread
9720            .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDWR, FdType::Socket, None)
9721            .unwrap();
9722        let errqueue = libc::MSG_ERRQUEUE;
9723        // Each error-queue receive, and calls on the same socket that do not
9724        // read the queue: a plain receive, and a send whose flags carry the
9725        // bit (a send never reads the queue).
9726        let decisions = |guest: &mut WaitGuest| {
9727            [
9728                (
9729                    "recvfrom MSG_ERRQUEUE",
9730                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9731                        guest,
9732                        Recvfrom::new().with_fd(fd).with_flags(errqueue),
9733                    ),
9734                ),
9735                (
9736                    "recvmsg MSG_ERRQUEUE",
9737                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9738                        guest,
9739                        Recvmsg::new().with_sockfd(fd).with_flags(errqueue),
9740                    ),
9741                ),
9742                (
9743                    "recvmmsg MSG_ERRQUEUE",
9744                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9745                        guest,
9746                        Recvmmsg::new().with_fd(fd).with_flags(errqueue as u32),
9747                    ),
9748                ),
9749            ]
9750        };
9751        let others = |guest: &mut WaitGuest| {
9752            [
9753                (
9754                    "recvfrom",
9755                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, Recvfrom::new().with_fd(fd)),
9756                ),
9757                (
9758                    "sendto MSG_ERRQUEUE",
9759                    ioaction_based_on_fd_status(
9760                        guest,
9761                        Sendto::new().with_fd(fd).with_flags(errqueue as u32),
9762                    ),
9763                ),
9764            ]
9765        };
9766        let set_never_waits = |guest: &mut WaitGuest, never_waits: bool| {
9767            guest
9768                .thread
9769                .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.set_error_queue_never_waits(never_waits))
9770                .unwrap();
9771        };
9772        let by_fd = |guest: &mut WaitGuest| ioaction_based_on_fd(guest, fd);
9773        let blocking = Ok(IOAction::Blocking);
9774        let once = Ok(IOAction::PassThru);
9775        let retry = Ok(IOAction::NonblockizeRetry);
9776
9777        // Physically blocking (an external socket under record and replay):
9778        // the blocking path, whatever the protocol.
9779        set_never_waits(&mut guest, true);
9780        for (name, action) in decisions(&mut guest) {
9781            assert_eq!(action, blocking, "{name}, physically blocking");
9782        }
9783        assert_eq!(by_fd(&mut guest), blocking, "by fd, physically blocking");
9784
9785        // Left blocking by the guest, physically nonblocking.
9786        guest
9787            .thread
9788            .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.set_physically_nonblocking())
9789            .unwrap();
9790        // A protocol that ignores the flag (AF_UNIX): retried.
9791        set_never_waits(&mut guest, false);
9792        for (name, action) in decisions(&mut guest) {
9793            assert_eq!(action, retry, "{name}, protocol waits");
9794        }
9795        // A protocol that reads the queue without waiting: runs once, and
9796        // only the error-queue receives do.
9797        set_never_waits(&mut guest, true);
9798        for (name, action) in decisions(&mut guest) {
9799            assert_eq!(action, once, "{name}, protocol never waits");
9800        }
9801        for (name, action) in others(&mut guest) {
9802            assert_eq!(action, retry, "{name}, protocol never waits");
9803        }
9804        assert_eq!(by_fd(&mut guest), retry, "by fd, left blocking");
9805
9806        // Made O_NONBLOCK by the guest: every call runs once.
9807        guest
9808            .thread
9809            .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.set_nonblocking(true))
9810            .unwrap();
9811        for (name, action) in decisions(&mut guest).into_iter().chain(others(&mut guest)) {
9812            assert_eq!(action, once, "{name}, O_NONBLOCK");
9813        }
9814        assert_eq!(by_fd(&mut guest), once, "by fd, O_NONBLOCK");
9815    }

9817    #[test]
9818    fn inherited_input_exempts_only_authenticated_reads_from_the_internal_guard() {
9819        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
9820        let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
9821        let slot = tempfile::tempfile().unwrap();
9822        let fd = slot.as_raw_fd();
9823        let input = reverie::InheritedInput::pipe(fd).unwrap();
9824        let identity = input.identity().clone();
9825        let (reader, _writer) = input.into_reader_and_writer();
9826        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::dup2(reader.as_raw_fd(), fd) }, fd);
9827        guest
9828            .thread
9829            .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY, FdType::Pipe, None)
9830            .unwrap();
9831        let calls = [
9832            Syscall::from(syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd)),
9833            Syscall::from(syscalls::Readv::new().with_fd(fd)),
9834            Syscall::from(syscalls::Write::new().with_fd(fd)),
9835            Syscall::from(syscalls::Writev::new().with_fd(fd)),
9836        ];
9837        for call in calls {
9838            assert!(syscall_targets_internal_fd(&mut guest, call));
9839        }
9840        guest
9841            .thread
9842            .file_metadata
9843            .lock()
9844            .unwrap()
9845            .apply_exec_fd_state(
9846                guest.thread.dettid,
9847                crate::tool_local::ExecFdState {
9848                    initial_input: Some(identity),
9849                    ..Default::default()
9850                },
9851                true,
9852            )
9853            .unwrap();
9854        for (index, call) in calls.into_iter().enumerate() {
9855            assert_eq!(syscall_targets_internal_fd(&mut guest, call), index >= 2);
9856        }
9857        assert!(
9858            !guest
9859                .thread
9860                .with_detfd(fd, |d| d.physically_nonblocking())
9861                .unwrap()
9862        );
9863        assert_eq!(
9864            unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_GETFL) } & libc::O_NONBLOCK,
9865            0
9866        );
9867        let (internal, _writer) = nix::unistd::pipe().unwrap();
9868        guest
9869            .thread
9870            .add_fd(
9871                internal.as_raw_fd(),
9872                nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY,
9873                FdType::Pipe,
9874                None,
9875            )
9876            .unwrap();
9877        assert!(syscall_targets_internal_fd(
9878            &mut guest,
9879            syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(internal.as_raw_fd()).into()
9880        ));
9881        // Socketpair ownership remains internal as well.
9882        let (socket, _peer) = std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
9883        guest
9884            .thread
9885            .add_fd(
9886                socket.as_raw_fd(),
9887                nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDWR,
9888                FdType::Socket,
9889                None,
9890            )
9891            .unwrap();
9892        guest
9893            .thread
9894            .with_detfd(socket.as_raw_fd(), |d| d.set_socketpair_endpoint())
9895            .unwrap();
9896        assert!(syscall_targets_internal_fd(
9897            &mut guest,
9898            syscalls::Readv::new().with_fd(socket.as_raw_fd()).into()
9899        ));
9900    }

9902    #[test]
9903    fn a_socketpair_poll_uses_revocable_provenance_without_changing_internal_routing() {
9904        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
9905
9906        use nix::sys::socket::AddressFamily;
9907        use nix::sys::socket::SockFlag;
9908        use nix::sys::socket::SockType;
9909        use nix::sys::socket::socketpair;
9910
9911        let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
9912        let pairs = [SockType::Datagram, SockType::Stream, SockType::SeqPacket].map(|kind| {
9913            let (socket, peer) =
9914                socketpair(AddressFamily::Unix, kind, None, SockFlag::empty()).unwrap();
9915            (kind, socket, peer)
9916        });
9917        for (kind, socket, _peer) in &pairs {
9918            let fd = socket.as_raw_fd();
9919            guest
9920                .thread
9921                .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDWR, FdType::Socket, None)
9922                .unwrap();
9923            let alias = guest
9924                .thread
9925                .with_detfd(fd, |d| {
9926                    d.set_socketpair_endpoint();
9927                    d.clone()
9928                })
9929                .unwrap();
9930            // Datagram pairs are deliberately not guest-held at creation:
9931            // binding and AF_UNSPEC disconnect can admit outside senders.
9932            // Connected stream/seqpacket pairs have the stronger mark.
9933            let connection = *kind != SockType::Datagram;
9934            if connection {
9935                alias.set_guest_held();
9936            }
9937            let calls = [
9938                syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd).into(),
9939                syscalls::Readv::new().with_fd(fd).into(),
9940                syscalls::Recvfrom::new().with_fd(fd).into(),
9941                syscalls::Recvmsg::new().with_sockfd(fd).into(),
9942            ];
9943            for call in calls {
9944                let internal = syscall_targets_internal_fd(&mut guest, call);
9945                assert!(internal, "{kind:?}: live record/replay routing is retained");
9946                let readiness = single_fd_poll_readiness(&mut guest, call, internal);
9947                assert_eq!(
9948                    readiness,
9949                    (connection, connection),
9950                    "{kind:?}: readiness needs revocable provenance"
9951                );
9952                let mut request = Resources::new(DetTid::from_raw(5));
9953                request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
9954                request.poll_attempt = 1;
9955                (
9956                    request.polls_guest_state_only,
9957                    request.relies_on_guest_held_marks,
9958                ) = readiness;
9959                crate::scheduler::assert_poll_export_revocation_for_test(request, connection);
9960            }
9961            // Cached record/replay peer credentials are another routing fact,
9962            // and must not override a socketpair's readiness provenance either.
9963            alias.set_guest_peer();
9964            for call in calls {
9965                let internal = syscall_targets_internal_fd(&mut guest, call);
9966                assert_eq!(
9967                    single_fd_poll_readiness(&mut guest, call, internal),
9968                    (connection, connection),
9969                    "cached guest-peer routing is not socketpair readiness proof"
9970                );
9971            }
9972            alias.clear_guest_held();
9973            for call in calls {
9974                let internal = syscall_targets_internal_fd(&mut guest, call);
9975                assert!(internal, "revocation must not change live routing");
9976                assert_eq!(
9977                    single_fd_poll_readiness(&mut guest, call, internal),
9978                    (false, false),
9979                    "withdrawing a mark through an alias withdraws readiness"
9980                );
9981            }
9982        }
9983
9984        // The socketpair repair does not reclassify other internal descriptors.
9985        let (pipe, _writer) = nix::unistd::pipe().unwrap();
9986        guest
9987            .thread
9988            .add_fd(
9989                pipe.as_raw_fd(),
9990                nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY,
9991                FdType::Pipe,
9992                None,
9993            )
9994            .unwrap();
9995        let (socket, _peer) = std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
9996        guest
9997            .thread
9998            .add_fd(
9999                socket.as_raw_fd(),
10000                nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDWR,
10001                FdType::Socket,
10002                None,
10003            )
10004            .unwrap();
10005        guest
10006            .thread
10007            .with_detfd(socket.as_raw_fd(), |d| d.set_guest_peer())
10008            .unwrap();
10009        for fd in [pipe.as_raw_fd(), socket.as_raw_fd()] {
10010            let call = syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd).into();
10011            let internal = syscall_targets_internal_fd(&mut guest, call);
10012            assert!(internal);
10013            assert_eq!(
10014                single_fd_poll_readiness(&mut guest, call, internal),
10015                (true, false)
10016            );
10017        }
10018    }

10020    /// Answer this thread's `/proc` reads from `kernel` until the result drops.
10021    fn scripted_proc(kernel: &Kernel) -> signal_state_read_seam::Installed {
10022        let kernel = kernel.clone();
10023        signal_state_read_seam::install(move |_, _| {
10024            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
10025            let read = match kernel
10026                .gone
10027                .then_some(Errno::ESRCH)
10028                .or_else(|| kernel.read_failures.pop_front())
10029            {
10030                Some(errno) => Err(errno),
10031                None => Ok(KernelSignalState {
10032                    pending: kernel.pending,
10033                    thread_pending: kernel.pending & !kernel.shared,
10034                    shared_pending: kernel.pending & kernel.shared,
10035                    blocked: kernel.blocked,
10036                    caught: kernel.caught,
10037                    ignored: kernel.ignored,
10038                }),
10039            };
10040            kernel.pending |= std::mem::take(&mut kernel.pending_repost);
10041            Some(read)
10042        })
10043    }

10045    #[reverie::tool]
10046    impl GlobalRPC<GlobalState> for WaitGuest {
10047        async fn send_rpc(
10048            &self,
10049            message: <GlobalState as GlobalTool>::Request,
10050        ) -> <GlobalState as GlobalTool>::Response {
10051            if let Some(script) = &self.proof_script {
10052                use crate::tool_global::GlobalRequest;
10053                use crate::tool_global::GlobalResponse;
10054                match &message.2 {
10055                    GlobalRequest::RequestResources(resources, _) => {
10056                        let (action, signal) = {
10057                            let mut script = script.lock().unwrap();
10058                            assert!(script.requests.len() < 4, "unbounded retry fixture");
10059                            script.requests.push(resources.clone());
10060                            let mut signal = None;
10061                            if script.observe_retry_masks {
10062                                let mut kernel = self.kernel.lock().unwrap();
10063                                let published = script.published_mask;
10064                                script.retry_boundaries.push((
10065                                    "request",
10066                                    kernel.blocked,
10067                                    published,
10068                                ));
10069                                // Model the ptrace target selector: a caught
10070                                // child notification is sent only to a task
10071                                // whose physical mask admits it at this yield.
10072                                if script.route_child_on_retry
10073                                    && script.requests.len() == 2
10074                                    && kernel.blocked & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) == 0
10075                                {
10076                                    kernel.pending |= kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
10077                                    signal = Some(crate::types::SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
10078                                }
10079                            }
10080                            (
10081                                script.actions.pop_front().unwrap_or(ProofAction::None),
10082                                signal,
10083                            )
10084                        };
10085                        self.proof_action(action).await;
10086                        return (
10087                            None,
10088                            GlobalResponse::RequestResources(
10089                                signal.map_or(ResumeStatus::Normal, |signal| {
10090                                    ResumeStatus::Signaled(Some(vec![signal]))
10091                                }),
10092                            ),
10093                        );
10094                    }
10095                    GlobalRequest::ReleasePort(_) => {
10096                        return (None, GlobalResponse::ReleasePort(None));
10097                    }
10098                    GlobalRequest::HostTimedAndPrivateSigchld(_) => {
10099                        return (None, GlobalResponse::HostTimedAndPrivateSigchld(0, 0));
10100                    }
10101                    GlobalRequest::SetSavedGuestSigmask(mask) => {
10102                        let mut script = script.lock().unwrap();
10103                        script.published_mask = *mask;
10104                        script.publications.push(*mask);
10105                        return (None, GlobalResponse::SetSavedGuestSigmask(()));
10106                    }
10107                    GlobalRequest::BeginWaitMask(mask) => {
10108                        let mut script = script.lock().unwrap();
10109                        script.published_mask = *mask;
10110                        script.publications.push(*mask);
10111                        return (None, GlobalResponse::BeginWaitMask(()));
10112                    }
10113                    GlobalRequest::WithdrawWaitMask => {
10114                        let mut script = script.lock().unwrap();
10115                        script.published_mask = None;
10116                        script.publications.push(None);
10117                        return (None, GlobalResponse::WithdrawWaitMask(()));
10118                    }
10119                    GlobalRequest::EndWaitMask => {
10120                        return (None, GlobalResponse::EndWaitMask(()));
10121                    }
10122                    GlobalRequest::PopDeliveryMask => {
10123                        return (None, GlobalResponse::PopDeliveryMask(()));
10124                    }
10125                    GlobalRequest::TraceSchedEvent(..) => {
10126                        let mut script = script.lock().unwrap();
10127                        assert!(script.observe_retry_masks);
10128                        let blocked = self.kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked;
10129                        let published = script.published_mask;
10130                        script.retry_boundaries.push(("trace", blocked, published));
10131                        return (
10132                            None,
10133                            GlobalResponse::TraceSchedEvent(
10134                                serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({
10135                                    "print_stack_strace": null,
10136                                    "timeslice": null,
10137                                    "schedule_released": false,
10138                                    "schedule_over": false,
10139                                }))
10140                                .unwrap(),
10141                            ),
10142                        );
10143                    }
10144                    GlobalRequest::DiscardedSignal(_) => {
10145                        return (
10146                            None,
10147                            GlobalResponse::DiscardedSignal(
10148                                crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalAnswer::Bits {
10149                                    thread: 0,
10150                                    process: 0,
10151                                },
10152                            ),
10153                        );
10154                    }
10155                    GlobalRequest::PendingRealTimeExpirations(_) => {
10156                        return (None, GlobalResponse::PendingRealTimeExpirations(0));
10157                    }
10158                    _ => panic!("unexpected proof fixture RPC: {:?}", message.2),
10159                }
10160            }
10161            match (&message.2, self.kernel.lock().unwrap().private_record) {
10162                (
10163                    crate::tool_global::GlobalRequest::HostTimedAndPrivateSigchld(_),
10164                    Some((host_timed, private)),
10165                ) => (
10166                    None,
10167                    crate::tool_global::GlobalResponse::HostTimedAndPrivateSigchld(
10168                        host_timed, private,
10169                    ),
10170                ),
10171                _ => panic!("these waits must not send an RPC: {:?}", message.2),
10172            }
10173        }
10174        fn config(&self) -> &Config {
10175            &self.config
10176        }
10177    }

10180    impl Guest<Detcore> for WaitGuest {
10181        type Memory = LocalMemory;
10182        type Stack = WaitStack;
10183
10184        fn tid(&self) -> Pid {
10185            self.tid
10186        }
10187        fn pid(&self) -> Pid {
10188            self.pid
10189        }
10190        fn ppid(&self) -> Option<Pid> {
10191            None
10192        }

10194            LocalMemory::new()
