10196        /// The test's own `sets` where it installed any; otherwise the fake
10197        /// kernel's sets, as a backend that delivers signals itself reports them
10198        /// (`provides_process_signal_control`, KVM here); every other backend
10199        /// reports nothing, as the trait's default.
10200        fn signal_sets(&self, tid: Pid) -> Result<reverie::SignalSets, reverie::FactError> {
10201            if let Some(sets) = self.sets {
10202                return Ok(sets);
10203            }
10204            if !self.config.backend.provides_process_signal_control {
10205                return Err(reverie::FactError::NotProvided);
10206            }
10207            let mut kernel = self.kernel.lock().unwrap();
10208            if tid != self.tid || kernel.gone {
10209                return Err(reverie::FactError::Errno(Errno::ESRCH));
10210            }
10211            if let Some(errno) = kernel.read_failures.pop_front() {
10212                return Err(reverie::FactError::Errno(errno));
10213            }
10214            Ok(reverie::SignalSets::new(
10215                kernel.pending & !kernel.shared,
10216                kernel.pending & kernel.shared,
10217                kernel.blocked,
10218                kernel.ignored,
10219                kernel.caught,
10220            ))
10221        }
10222        fn thread_state_mut(&mut self) -> &mut ThreadState<()> {
10223            &mut self.thread
10224        }
10225        fn thread_state(&self) -> &ThreadState<()> {
10226            &self.thread
10227        }
10228        async fn regs(&mut self) -> libc::user_regs_struct {
10229            if self
10230                .proof_script
10231                .as_ref()
10232                .is_some_and(|script| script.lock().unwrap().observe_retry_masks)
10233            {
10234                let mut regs: libc::user_regs_struct = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
10235                #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
10236                {
10237                    regs.rip = self.arena.as_ptr() as u64;
10238                }
10239                #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
10240                {
10241                    regs.pc = self.arena.as_ptr() as u64;
10242                }
10243                return regs;
10244            }
10245            panic!("a blocked wait must not read registers")
10246        }
10247        async fn stack(&mut self) -> Self::Stack {
10248            WaitStack {
10249                commit_fails: self.commit_fails,
10250                arena: self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
10251            }
10252        }
10253        async fn daemonize(&mut self) {
10254            panic!("a blocked wait must not daemonize")
10255        }
10256        async fn inject<S: SyscallInfo>(&mut self, syscall: S) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
10257            let (number, args) = syscall.into_parts();
10258            if let Some(script) = &self.proof_script {
10259                match Syscall::from_raw(number, args) {
10260                    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
10261                    Syscall::Dup2(call) => {
10262                        // These descriptors are owned by this test. The real
10263                        // handler performs the corresponding model update.
10264                        let result = unsafe { libc::dup2(call.oldfd(), call.newfd()) };
10265                        assert!(result >= 0, "owned fixture descriptor duplication failed");
10266                        return Ok(i64::from(result));
10267                    }
10268                    #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
10269                    Syscall::Dup3(call) => {
10270                        let result =
10271                            unsafe { libc::dup3(call.oldfd(), call.newfd(), call.flags().bits()) };
10272                        assert!(result >= 0, "owned fixture descriptor duplication failed");
10273                        return Ok(i64::from(result));
10274                    }
10275                    // x86_64 only: aarch64 has ppoll alone (next arm).
10276                    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
10277                    Syscall::Poll(_) => {
10278                        let mut script = script.lock().unwrap();
10279                        script.probes += 1;
10280                        return if script.probes == 4 { Ok(1) } else { Ok(0) };
10281                    }
10282                    Syscall::Readv(_) | Syscall::Ppoll(_) => {
10283                        let mut script = script.lock().unwrap();
10284                        script.probes += 1;
10285                        return if script.probes == 4 {
10286                            Ok(1)
10287                        } else if matches!(Syscall::from_raw(number, args), Syscall::Readv(_)) {
10288                            Err(Errno::EAGAIN)
10289                        } else {
10290                            Ok(0)
10291                        };
10292                    }
10293                    _ => {}
10294                }
10295            }
10296            if matches!(Syscall::from_raw(number, args), Syscall::Read(_)) {
10297                let mut kernel = self.kernel.lock().unwrap();
10298                assert!(kernel.empty_read_probes.is_some(), "unexpected read probe");
10299                let deliverable = kernel.pending & !kernel.blocked;
10300                if kernel.stops_for_pending && deliverable != 0 {
10301                    let signal = deliverable.trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1;
10302                    kernel.pending &= !kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
10303                    kernel.taken.push(signal);
10304                    kernel.hold(signal);
10305                    return Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
10306                }
10307                *kernel.empty_read_probes.as_mut().unwrap() += 1;
10308                let blocked = kernel.blocked;
10309                kernel.read_probe_masks.push(blocked);
10310                if kernel
10311                    .read_ready_after
10312                    .is_some_and(|ready| kernel.empty_read_probes.unwrap() >= ready)
10313                {
10314                    return Ok(1);
10315                }
10316                return Err(Errno::EAGAIN);
10317            }
10318            if matches!(Syscall::from_raw(number, args), Syscall::Write(_)) {
10319                let mut kernel = self.kernel.lock().unwrap();
10320                let blocked = kernel.blocked;
10321                let probes = kernel
10322                    .write_probe_masks
10323                    .as_mut()
10324                    .expect("unexpected write probe");
10325                probes.push(blocked);
10326                let attempt = probes.len();
10327                assert!(attempt <= 3, "unbounded scalar-write fixture");
10328                if attempt == 1 {
10329                    let pending = std::mem::take(&mut kernel.pending_after_first_write);
10330                    kernel.pending |= pending;
10331                }
10332                return if attempt == 3 {
10333                    Ok(1)
10334                } else {
10335                    Err(Errno::EAGAIN)
10336                };
10337            }
10338            let Syscall::RtSigprocmask(call) = Syscall::from_raw(number, args) else {
10339                panic!("a blocked wait injected {number}, not rt_sigprocmask")
10340            };
10341            assert_eq!(call.how(), libc::SIG_SETMASK);
10342            assert!(call.oldset().is_none());
10343            let set = call.set().expect("rt_sigprocmask without a mask");
10344            let mask: KernelSigset = LocalMemory::new().read_value(set.cast::<KernelSigset>())?;
10345            let mut kernel = self.kernel.lock().unwrap();
10346            kernel.requested.push(mask);
10347            let deliverable = kernel.pending & !kernel.blocked;
10348            if kernel.stops_for_pending && deliverable != 0 {
10349                let signal = deliverable.trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1;
10350                kernel.pending &= !kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
10351                kernel.taken.push(signal);
10352                kernel.hold(signal);
10353                if kernel.repost_after_take > 0 {
10354                    kernel.repost_after_take -= 1;
10355                    kernel.pending_repost |= kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
10356                }
10357                return Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
10358            }
10359            match kernel.outcomes.pop_front().unwrap_or(MaskOutcome::Apply) {
10360                MaskOutcome::Apply => {
10361                    kernel.blocked = mask;
10362                    Ok(0)
10363                }
10364                MaskOutcome::StoppedBefore => Err(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR),
10365                MaskOutcome::StoppedBy(signal) => {
10366                    kernel.hold(signal);
10367                    Err(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR)
10368                }
10369                MaskOutcome::Fail(errno) => Err(errno),
10370            }
10371        }
10372        async fn set_blocked_signals(&mut self, mask: u64) -> Result<u64, MaskChangeRefused> {
10373            let mut kernel = self.kernel.lock().unwrap();
10374            kernel.set_calls.push(mask);
10375            match kernel.setter.pop_front() {
10376                Some(None) => Ok(std::mem::replace(&mut kernel.blocked, mask)),
10377                Some(Some(refused)) => {
10378                    if matches!(refused, MaskChangeRefused::Gone) {
10379                        kernel.gone = true;
10380                    }
10381                    Err(refused)
10382                }
10383                None => Err(MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported),
10384            }
10385        }
10386
10387        async fn tail_inject<S: SyscallInfo>(&mut self, _: S) -> reverie::Never {
10388            panic!("a blocked wait must not retire the guest")
10389        }
10390        fn set_timer(&mut self, _: reverie::TimerSchedule) -> Result<(), Error> {
10391            panic!("a blocked wait must not set a timer")
10392        }
10393        fn set_timer_precise(&mut self, _: reverie::TimerSchedule) -> Result<(), Error> {
10394            panic!("a blocked wait must not set a timer")
10395        }
10396        fn read_clock(&mut self) -> Result<u64, Error> {
10397            panic!("a blocked wait must not read a clock")
10398        }
10399    }

10401    /// Exercise the actual retry/publication path. The host owns the second
10402    /// pipe's writer; replacing the slot or poll operand can therefore make
10403    /// the next physical probe depend on input from outside the guest.
10404    async fn proof_requests(case: &str, kernel_wait: bool, masked_ppoll: bool) -> Vec<Resources> {
10405        proof_requests_from(case, kernel_wait, masked_ppoll, false).await
10406    }
10407
10408    async fn proof_requests_from(
10409        case: &str,
10410        kernel_wait: bool,
10411        masked_ppoll: bool,
10412        generic_fd_entry: bool,
10413    ) -> Vec<Resources> {
10414        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
10415
10416        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(3), 0);
10417        guest.config.sequentialize_threads = true;
10418        guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_targets_are_predictable = false;
10419        guest.thread.dettid = DetTid::from_raw(3);
10420        guest.thread.detpid = Some(DetPid::from_raw(3));
10421        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
10422        let (internal, _internal_writer) =
10423            nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_NONBLOCK).unwrap();
10424        let (external, _external_writer) =
10425            nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_NONBLOCK).unwrap();
10426        let saved = nix::unistd::dup(&internal).unwrap();
10427        let fd = internal.as_raw_fd();
10428        let external_fd = external.as_raw_fd();
10429        for raw in [fd, external_fd] {
10430            guest
10431                .thread
10432                .add_fd(raw, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY, FdType::Pipe, None)
10433                .unwrap();
10434            guest
10435                .thread
10436                .with_detfd(raw, |entry| entry.set_physically_nonblocking())
10437                .unwrap();
10438        }
10439        let initially_held = !matches!(case, "unclaimed-dup" | "late-mark");
10440        if initially_held {
10441            guest
10442                .thread
10443                .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.set_guest_held())
10444                .unwrap();
10445        }
10446        if matches!(case, "dup-guest" | "unclaimed-dup") {
10447            guest
10448                .thread
10449                .with_detfd(external_fd, |entry| entry.set_guest_held())
10450                .unwrap();
10451        }
10452        guest
10453            .thread
10454            .dup_fd(fd, saved.as_raw_fd(), nix::fcntl::OFlag::empty())
10455            .unwrap();
10456        let original = guest
10457            .thread
10458            .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.open_file_id())
10459            .unwrap();
10460        let mut operands = [libc::pollfd {
10461            fd,
10462            events: libc::POLLIN,
10463            revents: 0,
10464        }];
10465        let address = operands.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
10466        let (change, restore) = match case {
10467            "same" => (ProofAction::None, ProofAction::None),
10468            "noop-dup" => (ProofAction::Dup { from: fd, to: fd }, ProofAction::None),
10469            "dup" | "dup-guest" | "unclaimed-dup" => (
10470                ProofAction::Dup {
10471                    from: external_fd,
10472                    to: fd,
10473                },
10474                ProofAction::Dup {
10475                    from: saved.as_raw_fd(),
10476                    to: fd,
10477                },
10478            ),
10479            "operand" => (
10480                ProofAction::Operand {
10481                    address,
10482                    fd: external_fd,
10483                },
10484                ProofAction::Operand { address, fd },
10485            ),
10486            "mark" => (
10487                ProofAction::Mark { fd, held: false },
10488                ProofAction::Mark { fd, held: true },
10489            ),
10490            "late-mark" => (ProofAction::Mark { fd, held: true }, ProofAction::None),
10491            "unknown" => {
10492                guest.thread.remove_fd(fd);
10493                (ProofAction::None, ProofAction::None)
10494            }
10495            _ => panic!("unknown proof case {case}"),
10496        };
10497        let script = Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProofScript {
10498            actions: [ProofAction::None, change, restore, ProofAction::None].into(),
10499            ..Default::default()
10500        }));
10501        guest.proof_script = Some(script.clone());
10502        let mut resources = Resources::new(guest.thread.dettid);
10503        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
10504        if !generic_fd_entry {
10505            resources.polls_guest_state_only = true;
10506            resources.relies_on_guest_held_marks = true;
10507        }
10508        // Match the real unmasked poll/ppoll producers. Readv's generic
10509        // retry helper itself supplies its restart errno and task identity.
10510        if kernel_wait || matches!(case, "operand" | "unknown") {
10511            resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::EINTR);
10512            resources.signal_state_task = guest_signal_state_task(&guest);
10513        }
10514        let mask = 0_u64;
10515        let zero_timeout = reverie::syscalls::Timespec {
10516            tv_sec: 0,
10517            tv_nsec: 0,
10518        };
10519        let mut byte = 0_u8;
10520        let iov = libc::iovec {
10521            iov_base: (&mut byte as *mut u8).cast(),
10522            iov_len: 1,
10523        };
10524        // The retry probe is poll on x86_64, ppoll on aarch64.
10525        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
10526        let poll_probe = syscalls::Poll::new()
10527            .with_fds(AddrMut::from_raw(address))
10528            .with_nfds(1)
10529            .with_timeout(-1);
10530        #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
10531        let poll_probe = syscalls::Ppoll::new()
10532            .with_fds(AddrMut::from_raw(address))
10533            .with_nfds(1)
10534            // NULL timeout: ppoll's equivalent of poll(-1), an infinite wait.
10535            .with_timeout(None);
10536        let result = if generic_fd_entry {
10537            let tool = Detcore {
10538                detpid: guest.thread.detpid.unwrap(),
10539                cfg: guest.config.clone(),
10540                record_or_replay: crate::record_or_replay::NoopTool,
10541            };
10542            // The ordinary logically blocking pipe must enter through the
10543            // production classifier, without a pre-armed resource request.
10544            tool.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(
10545                &mut guest,
10546                syscalls::Readv::new()
10547                    .with_fd(fd)
10548                    .with_iov(Addr::from_raw(&iov as *const _ as usize))
10549                    .with_len(1),
10550            )
10551            .await
10552        } else if masked_ppoll {
10553            let tool = Detcore {
10554                detpid: guest.thread.detpid.unwrap(),
10555                cfg: guest.config.clone(),
10556                record_or_replay: crate::record_or_replay::NoopTool,
10557            };
10558            tool.masked_ppoll_probe_for_test(
10559                &mut guest,
10560                syscalls::Ppoll::new()
10561                    .with_fds(AddrMut::from_raw(address))
10562                    .with_nfds(1)
10563                    .with_timeout(AddrMut::from_raw(&zero_timeout as *const _ as usize))
10564                    .with_sigmask(Addr::from_raw(&mask as *const _ as usize))
10565                    .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE),
10566                &mask as *const _ as usize,
10567            )
10568            .await
10569        } else if kernel_wait {
10570            retry_blocking_wait_under_mask(&mut guest, poll_probe, resources, None, None)
10571                .await
10572                .0
10573        } else if matches!(case, "operand" | "unknown") {
10574            retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(
10575                &mut guest, poll_probe, resources, None, None, None, false,
10576            )
10577            .await
10578        } else {
10579            retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(
10580                &mut guest,
10581                syscalls::Readv::new().with_fd(fd),
10582                resources,
10583                None,
10584                None,
10585                None,
10586                false,
10587            )
10588            .await
10589        };
10590        assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), 1, "retry syscall result is unchanged");
10591        let script = script.lock().unwrap();
10592        assert_eq!(script.probes, 4);
10593        assert_eq!(
10594            script
10595                .requests
10596                .iter()
10597                .map(|r| r.poll_attempt)
10598                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
10599            [0, 1, 2, 3]
10600        );
10601        if case != "unknown" {
10602            assert_eq!(
10603                guest
10604                    .thread
10605                    .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.open_file_id())
10606                    .unwrap(),
10607                original
10608            );
10609            if case == "unclaimed-dup" {
10610                assert!(
10611                    !guest
10612                        .thread
10613                        .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.is_guest_held())
10614                        .unwrap()
10615                );
10616            } else {
10617                assert!(
10618                    guest
10619                        .thread
10620                        .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.is_guest_held())
10621                        .unwrap()
10622                );
10623            }
10624            assert_eq!(
10625                operands[0].fd, fd,
10626                "restored operands cannot restore a lost proof"
10627            );
10628        }
10629        script.requests.clone()
10630    }

10754    /// Protect the generic loop's first-turn call site, independently of
10755    /// turn_signals_with_block's internal mask-install condition. A signal
10756    /// arrives after its first empty snapshot and before the private read.
10757    #[tokio::test]
10758    async fn a_generic_reads_first_probe_keeps_a_late_signal_visible() {
10759        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
10760
10761        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
10762        for (sent, blocked) in [(true, false), (false, false), (true, true)] {
10763            let own_mask = guest_mask() | if blocked { usr1 } else { 0 };
10764            let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(3), own_mask);
10765            guest.config.sequentialize_threads = true;
10766            guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_targets_are_predictable = true;
10767            guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_state_is_guests = true;
10768            guest.thread.dettid = DetTid::from_raw(3);
10769            guest.thread.detpid = Some(DetPid::from_raw(3));
10770            let (reader, _writer) = nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_NONBLOCK).unwrap();
10771            let fd = reader.as_raw_fd();
10772            guest
10773                .thread
10774                .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY, FdType::Pipe, None)
10775                .unwrap();
10776            guest
10777                .thread
10778                .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.set_physically_nonblocking())
10779                .unwrap();
10780            let script = Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProofScript::default()));
10781            guest.proof_script = Some(script.clone());
10782            {
10783                let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
10784                kernel.caught = usr1;
10785                kernel.pending_repost = if sent { usr1 } else { 0 };
10786                kernel.stops_for_pending = true;
10787                kernel.empty_read_probes = Some(0);
10788                kernel.read_ready_after = Some(4);
10789                // A successful in-place setter remains available on every
10790                // probe and restoration, not just the first and final ones.
10791                kernel.setter.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(None, 8));
10792            }
10793            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
10794            let mut resources = Resources::new(guest.thread.dettid);
10795            resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
10796            let result = retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(
10797                &mut guest,
10798                syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd).with_len(1),
10799                resources,
10800                None,
10801                None,
10802                None,
10803                false,
10804            )
10805            .await
10806            .map_err(|error| error.into_errno().expect("guest errno"));
10807            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
10808            assert_eq!(
10809                kernel.blocked, own_mask,
10810                "the original guest mask is restored"
10811            );
10812            assert_eq!(
10813                result,
10814                if sent && !blocked {
10815                    Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)
10816                } else {
10817                    Ok(1)
10818                },
10819                "sent={sent}, blocked={blocked}, pending={:#x}, held={:?}, taken={:?}",
10820                kernel.pending,
10821                kernel.held_slot,
10822                kernel.taken
10823            );
10824            assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, None);
10825            assert_eq!(kernel.pending, if sent { usr1 } else { 0 });
10826            assert_eq!(
10827                kernel.empty_read_probes,
10828                Some(if sent && !blocked { 2 } else { 4 })
10829            );
10830            assert_eq!(
10831                script.lock().unwrap().requests.len(),
10832                if sent && !blocked { 2 } else { 4 }
10833            );
10834        }
10835    }

10837    /// An already-expired socket timeout returns its expiry result after
10838    /// the first would-block attempt without taking a deliverable pending
10839    /// signal first: Linux with a zero timeo fails at once without looking
10840    /// at signals (`sock_alloc_send_pskb`'s `if (!timeo) goto failure`
10841    /// before its signal check, net/core/sock.c:2951-2956 at v6.17). The
10842    /// same scripted late signal that ends the untimed read above with
10843    /// ERESTARTSYS here stays pending, and exactly one probe runs. On the
10844    /// code before the immediate-expiry break this returned the interrupt
10845    /// errno instead, so this test discriminates where a guest with the
10846    /// signal blocked cannot.
10847    #[tokio::test]
10848    async fn an_immediate_expiry_precedes_a_deliverable_signal() {
10849        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
10850
10851        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
10852        let own_mask = guest_mask();
10853        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(3), own_mask);
10854        guest.config.sequentialize_threads = true;
10855        guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_targets_are_predictable = true;
10856        guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_state_is_guests = true;
10857        guest.thread.dettid = DetTid::from_raw(3);
10858        guest.thread.detpid = Some(DetPid::from_raw(3));
10859        let (reader, _writer) = nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_NONBLOCK).unwrap();
10860        let fd = reader.as_raw_fd();
10861        guest
10862            .thread
10863            .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY, FdType::Pipe, None)
10864            .unwrap();
10865        guest
10866            .thread
10867            .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.set_physically_nonblocking())
10868            .unwrap();
10869        let script = Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProofScript::default()));
10870        guest.proof_script = Some(script.clone());
10871        {
10872            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
10873            kernel.caught = usr1;
10874            // Pending and deliverable when the call begins, so its first
10875            // turn is a Signaled one: only the immediate-expiry break,
10876            // ahead of the signal checks, keeps the expiry result.
10877            kernel.pending = usr1;
10878            kernel.stops_for_pending = true;
10879            kernel.empty_read_probes = Some(0);
10880            kernel.read_ready_after = Some(4);
10881            kernel.setter.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(None, 8));
10882        }
10883        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
10884        let mut resources = Resources::new(guest.thread.dettid);
10885        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
10886        let result = retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(
10887            &mut guest,
10888            syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd).with_len(1),
10889            resources,
10890            Some((LogicalTime::from_nanos(0), Err(Errno::EAGAIN))),
10891            None,
10892            Some(Errno::EINTR),
10893            true,
10894        )
10895        .await
10896        .map_err(|error| error.into_errno().expect("guest errno"));
10897        assert_eq!(result, Err(Errno::EAGAIN));
10898        let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
10899        assert_eq!(kernel.pending, usr1, "the signal stays pending");
10900        assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, None);
10901        assert_eq!(kernel.empty_read_probes, Some(1), "exactly one probe ran");
10902        assert_eq!(script.lock().unwrap().requests.len(), 1);
10903    }

10905    /// Run the real generic read loop, including its retry TraceSchedEvent.
10906    /// A fourth ready probe bounds a broken implementation without a timeout.
10907    async fn read_observing_retry_masks(
10908        route_child: bool,
10909        late_signal: bool,
10910        setter: Vec<Option<MaskChangeRefused>>,
10911        outcomes: Vec<MaskOutcome>,
10912    ) -> (Result<i64, Error>, Kernel, Arc<Mutex<ProofScript>>) {
10913        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
10914
10915        let own_mask = guest_mask();
10916        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(3), own_mask);
10917        guest.config.sequentialize_threads = true;
10918        guest.config.record_preemptions = true;
10919        guest.config.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = false;
10920        guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_targets_are_predictable = true;
10921        guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_state_is_guests = true;
10922        guest.thread.dettid = DetTid::from_raw(3);
10923        guest.thread.detpid = Some(DetPid::from_raw(3));
10924        let (reader, _writer) = nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_NONBLOCK).unwrap();
10925        let fd = reader.as_raw_fd();
10926        guest
10927            .thread
10928            .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_RDONLY, FdType::Pipe, None)
10929            .unwrap();
10930        guest
10931            .thread
10932            .with_detfd(fd, |entry| entry.set_physically_nonblocking())
10933            .unwrap();
10934        let script = Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProofScript {
10935            observe_retry_masks: true,
10936            route_child_on_retry: route_child,
10937            ..ProofScript::default()
10938        }));
10939        guest.proof_script = Some(script.clone());
10940        {
10941            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
10942            kernel.caught = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
10943            kernel.pending_repost = if late_signal {
10944                kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1)
10945            } else {
10946                0
10947            };
10948            kernel.stops_for_pending = true;
10949            kernel.empty_read_probes = Some(0);
10950            kernel.read_ready_after = Some(4);
10951            kernel.setter.extend(setter);
10952            kernel.outcomes.extend(outcomes);
10953        }
10954        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
10955        let mut resources = Resources::new(guest.thread.dettid);
10956        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
10957        let result = retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(
10958            &mut guest,
10959            syscalls::Read::new().with_fd(fd).with_len(1),
10960            resources,
10961            None,
10962            None,
10963            None,
10964            false,
10965        )
10966        .await;
10967        (result, kernel, script)
10968    }

10970    /// Mutation M23 of the coord7 review of
10971    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/5221 (finding 4): a woken
10972    /// `poll` with an end time keeps it in the thread's restart record, as a
10973    /// rerun record (`RestartCall::PollRerun`), on a backend that restarts a
10974    /// woken call only through `ERESTARTSYS` (KVM today), so the rerun ends when
10975    /// the first call would have (`do_restart_poll`, fs/select.c:1076-1090 at
10976    /// v6.17). A backend that hands the delivery a restart errno (ptrace, or
10977    /// KVM once N8a declares `supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`)
10978    /// keeps none: the kernel's restart block holds the end time there.
10979    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
10980    #[tokio::test]
10981    async fn a_woken_poll_keeps_its_end_time_for_its_rerun() {
10982        let deadline = Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(7_000_000));
10983        for (label, signal_control, restart_codes, kept) in [
10984            ("KVM", true, false, true),
10985            ("ptrace", false, true, false),
10986            ("KVM after N8a", true, true, false),
10987        ] {
10988            let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(0);
10989            guest.config.backend.provides_process_signal_control = signal_control;
10990            guest
10991                .config
10992                .backend
10993                .supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption = restart_codes;
10994            guest.proof_script = Some(Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProofScript {
10995                observe_retry_masks: true,
10996                ..ProofScript::default()
10997            })));
10998            guest.thread.woken_wait = WokenWait::Poll;
10999            let call = syscalls::Poll::new().with_nfds(0).with_timeout(7);
11000            <crate::Detcore>::keep_deadline_for_rerun(&mut guest, &Ok(0), call, deadline).await;
11001            match guest.thread.restart_block {
11002                Some(RestartBlock {
11003                    deadline: kept_deadline,
11004                    call: RestartCall::PollRerun(rerun),
11005                    ..
11006                }) if kept => {
11007                    assert_eq!(kept_deadline, deadline, "{label}");
11008                    assert_eq!(rerun, call, "{label}");
11009                }
11010                None if !kept => {}
11011                other => panic!("{label}: {other:?}"),
11012            }
11013        }
11014    }

11016    #[tokio::test]
11017    async fn a_generic_read_restores_its_mask_before_retry_yields() {
11018        for (route_child, late_signal) in [(true, false), (false, true), (false, false)] {
11019            let (result, kernel, script) =
11020                read_observing_retry_masks(route_child, late_signal, vec![None; 8], vec![]).await;
11021            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11022            let script = script.lock().unwrap();
11023            assert_eq!(
11024                result.map_err(|error| error.into_errno().expect("guest errno")),
11025                if route_child || late_signal {
11026                    Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)
11027                } else {
11028                    Ok(1)
11029                },
11030                "route_child={route_child}, late_signal={late_signal}",
11031            );
11032            let attempts = if route_child || late_signal { 2 } else { 4 };
11033            assert_eq!(script.requests.len(), attempts);
11034            assert_eq!(kernel.empty_read_probes, Some(attempts));
11035            assert_eq!(
11036                kernel.read_probe_masks,
11037                vec![blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask(); attempts]
11038            );
11039            assert_eq!(script.retry_boundaries.len(), attempts * 2 - 1);
11040            for (boundary, blocked, published) in &script.retry_boundaries {
11041                assert_eq!(
11042                    *blocked,
11043                    guest_mask(),
11044                    "{boundary} must see the guest's mask"
11045                );
11046                assert_eq!(
11047                    *published, None,
11048                    "{boundary} must not keep a private-mask publication"
11049                );
11050            }
11051            assert_eq!(
11052                script.publications,
11053                [Some(guest_mask()), None].repeat(attempts)
11054            );
11055            assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, guest_mask());
11056            assert_eq!(
11057                kernel.pending,
11058                if route_child {
11059                    kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD)
11060                } else if late_signal {
11061                    kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1)
11062                } else {
11063                    0
11064                }
11065            );
11066            assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, None);
11067            assert!(kernel.taken.is_empty());
11068            assert!(kernel.lost.is_empty());
11069        }
11070    }

11072    #[tokio::test]
11073    async fn a_generic_read_does_not_retry_after_an_in_place_release_refusal() {
11074        for refused in [
11075            MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported,
11076            MaskChangeRefused::RestorePending {

11078                effective: blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask(),

11087                    .await;

11099            );

11101                kernel.blocked,
11102                guest_mask(),
11103                "final cleanup still restores the mask"
11104            );

11106            assert!(
11107                kernel.requested.is_empty(),
11108                "no injected restoration was needed"
11109            );

11136        ));

11138        let script = script.lock().unwrap();
11139        assert_eq!(kernel.empty_read_probes, Some(1));
11140        assert_eq!(script.requests.len(), 1);
11141        assert_eq!(
11142            script.retry_boundaries,
11143            vec![("request", guest_mask(), None)]
11144        );
11145        assert_eq!(
11146            kernel.set_calls.len(),
11147            2,
11148            "an unknown mask is not probed or restored speculatively"
11149        );
11150        assert!(kernel.requested.is_empty());
11151    }

11153    #[tokio::test]
11154    async fn a_generic_read_keeps_a_release_failure_fatal_after_loss_during_cleanup() {
11155        let (result, kernel, script) = read_observing_retry_masks(
11156            false,
11157            false,
11158            vec![
11159                None,
11160                Some(MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported),
11161                Some(MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported),
11162            ],
11163            vec![
11164                MaskOutcome::StoppedBy(libc::SIGUSR1),
11165                MaskOutcome::StoppedBy(libc::SIGUSR2),
11166                MaskOutcome::Apply,
11167            ],
11168        )
11169        .await;
11170        // allow-unsupported must not turn this failed atomic release into the
11171        // HeldSignalRefusal policy's transparent ERESTARTNOINTR retry.
11172        assert!(matches!(
11173            diagnostic(result),
11174            BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored { attempts: 1, .. }
11175        ));
11176        let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11177        let script = script.lock().unwrap();
11178        assert_eq!(kernel.empty_read_probes, Some(1));
11179        assert_eq!(script.requests.len(), 1);
11180        assert_eq!(
11181            script.retry_boundaries,
11182            vec![("request", guest_mask(), None)]
11183        );
11184        assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, guest_mask());
11185        assert_eq!(kernel.requested, vec![guest_mask(); 3]);
11186        assert_eq!(kernel.lost, vec![libc::SIGUSR1]);
11187        assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, Some(libc::SIGUSR2));
11188    }

11190    #[tokio::test]
11191    async fn a_scalar_write_keeps_its_pending_only_probe_mask_policy() {
11192        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
11193
11194        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
11195        for (sent, blocked) in [(false, false), (true, false), (true, true)] {
11196            let own_mask = guest_mask() | if blocked { usr1 } else { 0 };
11197            let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(3), own_mask);
11198            guest.config.sequentialize_threads = true;
11199            guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_targets_are_predictable = true;
11200            guest.config.backend.kernel_signal_state_is_guests = true;
11201            guest.thread.dettid = DetTid::from_raw(3);
11202            guest.thread.detpid = Some(DetPid::from_raw(3));
11203            let (_reader, writer) = nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_NONBLOCK).unwrap();
11204            let fd = writer.as_raw_fd();
11205            guest
11206                .thread
11207                .add_fd(fd, nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_WRONLY, FdType::Pipe, None)
11208                .unwrap();
11209            let open_file = guest
11210                .thread
11211                .with_detfd(fd, |entry| {
11212                    entry.set_physically_nonblocking();
11213                    entry.open_file_id()
11214                })
11215                .unwrap();
11216            let script = Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProofScript::default()));
11217            guest.proof_script = Some(script.clone());
11218            {
11219                let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11220                kernel.caught = usr1;
11221                kernel.write_probe_masks = Some(vec![]);
11222                kernel.pending_after_first_write = if sent { usr1 } else { 0 };
11223                kernel.setter.extend([None, None]);
11224            }
11225            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11226            let tool = Detcore {
11227                detpid: guest.thread.detpid.unwrap(),
11228                cfg: guest.config.clone(),
11229                record_or_replay: crate::record_or_replay::NoopTool,
11230            };
11231            let byte = 0u8;
11232            let result = tool
11233                .execute_blocking_pipe_write(
11234                    &mut guest,
11235                    syscalls::Write::new()
11236                        .with_fd(fd)
11237                        .with_buf(Addr::from_ptr(&byte))
11238                        .with_len(1),
11239                    open_file,
11240                )
11241                .await
11242                .map_err(|error| error.into_errno().expect("guest errno"));
11243            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11244            let script = script.lock().unwrap();
11245            if sent && !blocked {
11246                assert_eq!(result, Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS));
11247                assert_eq!(
11248                    kernel.write_probe_masks.as_deref(),
11249                    Some([own_mask, blocked_signal_mask() | own_mask].as_slice())
11250                );
11251                assert_eq!(
11252                    kernel.set_calls,
11253                    vec![blocked_signal_mask() | own_mask, own_mask]
11254                );
11255                assert_eq!(script.publications, vec![Some(own_mask), None]);
11256                assert_eq!(script.requests.len(), 1);
11257            } else {
11258                assert_eq!(result, Ok(1));
11259                assert_eq!(
11260                    kernel.write_probe_masks.as_deref(),
11261                    Some([own_mask; 3].as_slice()),
11262                    "sent={sent}, blocked={blocked}"
11263                );
11264                assert!(
11265                    kernel.set_calls.is_empty(),
11266                    "an empty or guest-blocked snapshot must not change the scalar writer's mask"
11267                );
11268                assert!(script.publications.is_empty());
11269                assert_eq!(script.requests.len(), 2);
11270            }
11271            assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, own_mask);
11272            assert_eq!(kernel.pending, if sent { usr1 } else { 0 });
11273            assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, None);
11274            assert!(kernel.lost.is_empty());
11275        }
11276    }

11306    /// The guest's own mask in these tests.
11307    fn guest_mask() -> KernelSigset {
11308        kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR2)
11309    }
11310
11311    /// The diagnostic a result ends the run with.
11312    fn diagnostic<V: std::fmt::Debug>(result: Result<V, Error>) -> BlockedWaitSignalError {
11313        match result {
11314            Err(Error::Tool(error)) => *error
11315                .downcast_ref::<BlockedWaitSignalError>()
11316                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("not a blocked-wait diagnostic: {error:#}")),
11317            other => panic!("expected the run to end with a diagnostic, got {other:?}"),
11318        }
11319    }
11320
11321    /// The held-signal refusal a result ends the wait with.
11322    fn refusal<V: std::fmt::Debug>(result: Result<V, Error>) -> HeldSignalRefusal {
11323        match result {
11324            Err(Error::Tool(error)) => *error
11325                .downcast_ref::<HeldSignalRefusal>()
11326                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("not a held-signal refusal: {error:#}")),
11327            other => panic!("expected the wait to end with a held-signal refusal, got {other:?}"),
11328        }
11329    }
11330
11331    /// A wait whose guest mask `block` replaced with the all-blocked mask.
11332    async fn blocked_wait(guest: &mut WaitGuest, kernel: &Kernel) -> KernelSignalWait {
11333        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11334        wait.block(guest, None).await.unwrap();
11335        assert!(!wait.needs_block());
11336        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked, blocked_signal_mask());
11337        wait
11338    }
11339
11340    /// Each stopped attempt is a stop by a signal that `/proc` cannot identify,
11341    /// which the backend holds in place of the one before. `restore` used to
11342    /// return success here; the second stop drops the first unidentified one,
11343    /// which may matter, so the mask is still put back and the wait now ends
11344    /// with a `HeldSignalRefusal`, as a wait loop that meets two such stops
11345    /// does (round-11 High F1 on
11346    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
11347    #[tokio::test]
11348    async fn restore_repeats_the_mask_change_until_the_kernel_reports_it() {
11349        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
11350        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11351        let mut wait = blocked_wait(&mut guest, &kernel).await;
11352        kernel
11353            .lock()
11354            .unwrap()
11355            .outcomes
11356            .extend([MaskOutcome::StoppedBefore; 5]);
11357
11358        let result = wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await;
11359
11360        assert_eq!(
11361            refusal(result),
11362            HeldSignalRefusal {
11363                wait: None,
11364                held: None,
11365                replacing: None,
11366                loss: HeldSignalLoss::Restoration,
11367            }
11368        );
11369        let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11370        assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, guest_mask());
11371        assert_eq!(
11372            kernel.requested.len(),
11373            1 + 6,
11374            "block, then five stopped attempts and one that ran"
11375        );
11376        assert!(
11377            kernel.requested[1..]
11378                .iter()
11379                .all(|&mask| mask == guest_mask())
11380        );
11381    }

11440    /// `block_in_place` blocks through `Guest::set_blocked_signals`, with no
11441    /// injection, and `restore` puts the guest's mask back the same way: no
11442    /// scratch memory is touched, so a stack with no room below it (a failing
11443    /// commit) changes nothing (Claude review of the R2b-2 design, M1).
11444    #[tokio::test]
11445    async fn an_in_place_block_and_its_restore_make_no_injection() {
11446        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
11447        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11448        guest.commit_fails = true;
11449        kernel.lock().unwrap().setter.extend([None, None]);
11450        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11451        assert!(wait.block_in_place(&mut guest, 0).await.unwrap());
11452        assert_eq!(wait.effective_mask(), Some(guest_mask()));
11453        assert_eq!(
11454            kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked,
11455            blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask()
11456        );
11457        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
11458        let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11459        assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, guest_mask());
11460        assert_eq!(
11461            kernel.set_calls,
11462            vec![blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask(), guest_mask()]
11463        );
11464        assert!(
11465            kernel.requested.is_empty(),
11466            "no rt_sigprocmask was injected"
11467        );
11468        assert_eq!(wait.effective_mask(), None);
11469    }

11471    /// The in-place block holds the turn's host-timed signals until the call
11472    /// returns (`hold_until_return`), as `install_turn_mask` does for
11473    /// `writev`, so a fallback injected restoration that one of them stops
11474    /// holds it rather than counting it lost (Claude re-check of R2b-2 stage
11475    /// 2, F2).
11476    #[tokio::test]
11477    async fn an_in_place_block_holds_the_host_timed_signals() {
11478        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
11479        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11480        kernel.lock().unwrap().setter.push_back(None);
11481        let host_timed = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGIO) | kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGHUP);
11482        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11483        assert!(wait.block_in_place(&mut guest, host_timed).await.unwrap());
11484        assert_eq!(wait.held_until_return & host_timed, host_timed);
11485        assert_eq!(wait.host_timed & host_timed, host_timed);
11486    }

11488    /// A refused in-place block changes nothing: the wait goes on under the
11489    /// guest's own mask, does not try again (`needs_block`), and has nothing
11490    /// to restore.
11491    #[tokio::test]
11492    async fn a_refused_in_place_block_leaves_the_guest_mask() {

11495        kernel
11496            .lock()
11497            .unwrap()
11498            .setter
11499            .push_back(Some(MaskChangeRefused::RestorePending {
11500                saved: guest_mask(),
11501                effective: 0,
11502            }));
11503        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11504        assert!(!wait.block_in_place(&mut guest, 0).await.unwrap());
11505        assert!(!wait.needs_block());

11507        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();

11509        assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, guest_mask());
11510        assert_eq!(kernel.set_calls.len(), 1);

11600    #[tokio::test]
11601    async fn an_unreadable_signal_state_of_a_live_thread_ends_the_run() {
11602        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
11603        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11604        let (pid, tid) = (guest.pid, guest.tid);
11605        let expected = |errno| BlockedWaitSignalError::StateUnreadable { pid, tid, errno };
11606
11607        // The turn's check, before the mask is set.
11608        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11609        kernel.lock().unwrap().read_failures.push_back(Errno::EIO);
11610        assert_eq!(diagnostic(wait.interrupted()), expected(Errno::EIO));
11611
11612        // `block`'s read of the guest's mask.
11613        kernel.lock().unwrap().read_failures.push_back(Errno::ESRCH);
11614        assert_eq!(
11615            diagnostic(wait.block(&mut guest, None).await),
11616            expected(Errno::ESRCH)
11617        );
11618        assert!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.is_empty());
11619
11620        // `restore`'s read, with every signal blocked.
11621        wait.block(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
11622        kernel.lock().unwrap().read_failures.push_back(Errno::ESRCH);
11623        assert_eq!(
11624            diagnostic(wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await),
11625            expected(Errno::ESRCH)
11626        );
11627        let error = expected(Errno::EIO).to_string();
11628        assert!(
11629            error.starts_with("cannot read the signal state of guest thread"),
11630            "{error}"
11631        );
11632    }

11634    #[tokio::test]
11635    async fn a_thread_that_no_longer_exists_ends_its_wait_with_erestartnointr() {
11636        // SAFETY: gettid has no preconditions.
11637        let exited = std::thread::spawn(|| unsafe { libc::gettid() })
11638            .join()
11639            .unwrap();
11640        // `join` returns when the kernel clears the thread's TID word, early in
11641        // its exit; the thread stays in `/proc` and answers `tgkill` until the
11642        // kernel releases it a moment later. Measured on the development host,
11643        // 62 of 20000 joined threads were still listed right after `join`, and
11644        // a GitHub-hosted run read such a thread's status here
11645        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/actions/runs/37683205050). So wait
11646        // for the release. The path is in this process's own task directory, so
11647        // no other process's thread can appear under it, and Linux hands out
11648        // TIDs cyclically, so this one is not reissued here before the counter
11649        // wraps.
11650        let task = format!("/proc/self/task/{exited}");
11651        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
11652        while std::path::Path::new(&task).exists() {
11653            assert!(
11654                std::time::Instant::now() < deadline,
11655                "thread {exited} is still in /proc 10 s after it was joined"
11656            );
11657            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(1));
11658        }
11659        let (guest, _kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(exited), guest_mask());
11660        // No script: the read goes to the real `/proc`, where the thread is gone.
11661
11662        let wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11663        assert!(matches!(
11664            wait.interrupted(),
11665            Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR))
11666        ));
11667        assert!(matches!(
11668            read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid, guest.tid),
11669            Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR))
11670        ));
11671    }
11672
11673    /// SIGSHARE S3a: on a backend whose guest threads are not host tasks
11674    /// (KVM), a blocked wait reads its thread's state from the backend
11675    /// (`Guest::signal_sets`) at every read, and never host `/proc`, which
11676    /// would describe an unrelated host task. Host reads are refused here
11677    /// (the latch) and the `/proc` seam panics, so a wait that kept its
11678    /// `/proc` read fails. A thread the backend no longer knows ends the call
11679    /// with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, and any other failure ends the run, as for the
11680    /// `/proc` read.
11681    #[tokio::test]
11682    async fn a_kvm_wait_reads_its_backend_and_never_host_proc() {
11683        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
11684        guest.config = Config {
11685            sequentialize_threads: true,
11686            ..Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
11687                *backend = reverie::BackendCapabilities::KVM;
11688            })
11689        };
11690        crate::syscalls::refuse_host_signal_state_reads(&reverie::BackendCapabilities::KVM);
11691        let _proc = signal_state_read_seam::install(|pid, tid| {
11692            panic!("a KVM wait read host /proc of {pid}/{tid}")
11693        });
11694        let wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11695        {
11696            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11697            kernel.caught = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
11698            kernel.pending = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
11699        }
11700        let (interrupted, state) = wait.interrupted_with_state(&guest).unwrap();
11701        assert!(!interrupted, "SIGUSR2 is blocked");
11702        assert_eq!(state.blocked, guest_mask());
11703        // The signals that could end the wait: the caught SIGUSR1, never the
11704        // blocked SIGUSR2.
11705        let observable = wait.observable_now(&guest).unwrap();
11706        assert_ne!(observable & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1), 0);
11707        assert_eq!(observable & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR2), 0);
11708        kernel.lock().unwrap().pending = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
11709        assert!(
11710            wait.interrupted_with_state(&guest).unwrap().0,
11711            "SIGUSR1 is not blocked"
11712        );
11713        assert_eq!(
11714            crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(&guest)
11715                .unwrap()
11716                .pending,
11717            kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1)
11718        );
11719
11720        kernel.lock().unwrap().read_failures.push_back(Errno::EIO);
11721        assert_eq!(
11722            diagnostic(crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(&guest)),
11723            BlockedWaitSignalError::StateUnreadable {
11724                pid: guest.pid,
11725                tid: guest.tid,
11726                errno: Errno::EIO,
11727            }
11728        );
11729        kernel.lock().unwrap().gone = true;
11730        assert!(matches!(
11731            crate::syscalls::read_guest_group_wait_signal_state(&guest),
11732            Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR))
11733        ));
11734        assert!(matches!(
11735            wait.interrupted_with_state(&guest),
11736            Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR))
11737        ));
11738        assert_eq!(
11739            crate::syscalls::read_guest_task_signal_state(&guest, guest.pid, guest.tid),
11740            Err(Errno::ESRCH)
11741        );
11742    }
11743
11744    #[tokio::test]
11745    async fn a_stack_with_no_scratch_room_leaves_the_wait_under_the_guest_mask() {
11746        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
11747        guest.commit_fails = true;
11748        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11749        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11750
11751        wait.block(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
11752
11753        assert!(!wait.needs_block(), "block must not be tried again");
11754        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked, guest_mask());
11755        assert!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.is_empty());
11756
11757        // Later turns classify against the guest's own mask, read each turn.
11758        {
11759            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11760            kernel.caught = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
11761            kernel.pending = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
11762        }
11763        assert!(!wait.interrupted().unwrap(), "SIGUSR2 is blocked");
11764        kernel.lock().unwrap().pending = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
11765        assert!(wait.interrupted().unwrap(), "SIGUSR1 is not blocked");
11766
11767        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
11768        assert!(
11769            kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.is_empty(),
11770            "nothing to put back"
11771        );
11772        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked, guest_mask());
11773    }

11775    /// A guest whose injections a pending signal outside the mask stops, as on
11776    /// ptrace, with `pending` queued and `ignored` set to `SIG_IGN`.
11777    fn stopping_guest(pending: KernelSigset, ignored: KernelSigset) -> (WaitGuest, Kernel) {
11778        let (guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
11779        {
11780            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11781            kernel.stops_for_pending = true;
11782            kernel.pending = pending;
11783            kernel.ignored = ignored;
11784        }
11785        (guest, kernel)
11786    }
11787
11788    /// Inject a mask change to `mask` through `wait.inject_absorbing`.
11789    async fn inject_mask_absorbing(
11790        wait: &mut KernelSignalWait,
11791        guest: &mut WaitGuest,
11792        mask: KernelSigset,
11793    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error> {
11794        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
11795        let cell = stack.push(mask);
11796        let _guard = stack.commit().unwrap();
11797        wait.inject_absorbing(guest, set_signal_mask_call(cell))
11798            .await
11799    }
11800
11801    /// An ignored signal that was already pending stops the mask change of
11802    /// `block`, which used to end the wait with a restart (review finding F2 on
11803    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). Linux would not end the
11804    /// wait for it, so the stop is absorbed: the backend holds the signal, the
11805    /// change runs again, and the held signal does not interrupt the wait.
11806    #[tokio::test]
11807    async fn an_ignored_signal_that_stops_the_mask_change_does_not_end_the_wait() {
11808        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
11809        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(usr1, usr1);
11810        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11811        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11812
11813        wait.block(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
11814
11815        assert!(!wait.needs_block());
11816        let all_blocked = blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask();
11817        {
11818            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11819            assert_eq!(kernel.taken, vec![libc::SIGUSR1]);
11820            assert_eq!(kernel.requested, vec![all_blocked, all_blocked]);
11821            assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, all_blocked);
11822        }
11823        assert_eq!(
11824            wait.held,
11825            Some(HeldSignal {
11826                signal: libc::SIGUSR1,
11827                queue: SignalQueue::Thread,
11828                kind: HeldKind::Harmless,
11829            })
11830        );
11831        assert!(
11832            !wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
11833            "an ignored signal does not end the wait"
11834        );
11835        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
11836        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked, guest_mask());
11837    }
11838
11839    /// A default-ignored signal that stops an injection is held the same way,
11840    /// and the injection then returns its own result (review finding F2 on
11841    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
11842    #[tokio::test]
11843    async fn a_default_ignored_signal_that_stops_an_injection_is_held() {
11844        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGWINCH), 0);
11845        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11846        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11847
11848        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
11849
11850        assert!(matches!(result, Ok(Ok(0))), "{result:?}");
11851        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().taken, vec![libc::SIGWINCH]);
11852        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.len(), 2);
11853        assert_eq!(wait.held.map(|held| held.kind), Some(HeldKind::Harmless));
11854        assert!(!wait.interrupted().unwrap());
11855    }

11857    /// A pending signal that would end the wait natively ends it before any
11858    /// injection, with the restart errno, and stays queued for the guest.
11859    #[tokio::test]
11860    async fn a_pending_caught_signal_ends_the_wait_before_the_injection() {
11861        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
11862        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(usr1, 0);
11863        kernel.lock().unwrap().caught = usr1;
11864        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11865        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11866
11867        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
11868
11869        assert!(
11870            matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS))),
11871            "{result:?}"
11872        );
11873        let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11874        assert!(kernel.requested.is_empty(), "nothing is injected");
11875        assert_eq!(kernel.pending, usr1);
11876        assert_eq!(wait.held, None);
11877    }
11878
11879    /// The backend holds one signal. Once it holds one whose loss would matter,
11880    /// a `SIGCHLD` here, an injection that a different pending signal would stop
11881    /// is not made. The wait used to end with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, a transparent
11882    /// restart; it now ends with a `HeldSignalRefusal`, which its caller turns
11883    /// into the unsupported-operation refusal (round-10 High 1 on
11884    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
11885    #[tokio::test]
11886    async fn a_held_sigchld_is_never_replaced_by_another_stop() {
11887        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(
11888            kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGWINCH),
11889            0,
11890        );
11891        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11892        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11893
11894        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
11895
11896        assert_eq!(
11897            refusal(result),
11898            HeldSignalRefusal {
11899                wait: None,
11900                held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
11901                replacing: Some(libc::SIGWINCH),
11902                loss: HeldSignalLoss::Replaced,
11903            }
11904        );
11905        let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11906        assert_eq!(kernel.taken, vec![libc::SIGCHLD]);
11907        assert_eq!(
11908            kernel.requested.len(),
11909            1,
11910            "the second injection is not made"
11911        );
11912        assert_eq!(kernel.pending, kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGWINCH));
11913        assert_eq!(wait.held.map(|held| held.kind), Some(HeldKind::Precious));
11914    }
11915
11916    /// A wait whose `block` was stopped by a default `SIGCHLD`, which the
11917    /// backend holds as a signal whose loss matters (`HeldKind::Precious`).
11918    async fn wait_holding_sigchld(guest: &mut WaitGuest, kernel: &Kernel) -> KernelSignalWait {
11919        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&*guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11920        wait.block(guest, None).await.unwrap();
11921        assert_eq!(
11922            wait.held.map(|held| (held.signal, held.kind)),
11923            Some((libc::SIGCHLD, HeldKind::Precious))
11924        );
11925        let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11926        assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask());
11927        assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, Some(libc::SIGCHLD));
11928        wait
11929    }
