11931    /// A signal that `/proc` never showed, a `SIGSTOP` sent from outside here,
11932    /// stops the injection that puts the guest's mask back before it runs, and
11933    /// the next attempt runs. The backend holds one signal, so the `SIGSTOP`
11934    /// replaced the held `SIGCHLD`, and `restore` used to return success, so
11935    /// the guest resumed without its `SIGCHLD` (round-11 High F1 on
11936    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). The mask is still put
11937    /// back, and the wait now ends with a `HeldSignalRefusal`.
11938    #[tokio::test]
11939    async fn a_stop_of_the_mask_restoration_that_replaces_a_held_sigchld_is_refused() {
11940        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD), 0);
11941        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11942        let mut wait = wait_holding_sigchld(&mut guest, &kernel).await;
11943        kernel
11944            .lock()
11945            .unwrap()
11946            .outcomes
11947            .push_back(MaskOutcome::StoppedBy(libc::SIGSTOP));
11948
11949        let result = wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await;
11950
11951        {
11952            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11953            assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, guest_mask(), "the guest's mask is back");
11954            assert_eq!(
11955                kernel.requested[2..],
11956                [guest_mask(), guest_mask()],
11957                "one stopped restoration attempt and one that ran"
11958            );
11959            assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, Some(libc::SIGSTOP));
11960            assert_eq!(kernel.lost, vec![libc::SIGCHLD]);
11961        }
11962        assert_eq!(
11963            refusal(result),
11964            HeldSignalRefusal {
11965                wait: None,
11966                held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
11967                replacing: None,
11968                loss: HeldSignalLoss::Restoration,
11969            }
11970        );
11971    }
11972
11973    /// The same with a signal that `/proc` shows before the restoration and
11974    /// that the all-blocked mask leaves unblocked: signal 32, which the C
11975    /// library reserves and leaves out of the blockable set. The refusal names
11976    /// it.
11977    #[tokio::test]
11978    async fn an_identified_stop_of_the_mask_restoration_that_replaces_a_held_sigchld_is_refused() {
11979        const RESERVED: i32 = 32;
11980        assert_eq!(blocked_signal_mask() & kernel_sigset_bit(RESERVED), 0);
11981        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD), 0);
11982        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
11983        let mut wait = wait_holding_sigchld(&mut guest, &kernel).await;
11984        kernel.lock().unwrap().pending = kernel_sigset_bit(RESERVED);
11985
11986        let result = wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await;
11987
11988        {
11989            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
11990            assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, guest_mask(), "the guest's mask is back");
11991            assert_eq!(kernel.taken, vec![libc::SIGCHLD, RESERVED]);
11992            assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, Some(RESERVED));
11993            assert_eq!(kernel.lost, vec![libc::SIGCHLD]);
11994        }
11995        let refused = refusal(result);
11996        assert_eq!(
11997            refused,
11998            HeldSignalRefusal {
11999                wait: None,
12000                held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
12001                replacing: Some(RESERVED),
12002                loss: HeldSignalLoss::Restoration,
12003            }
12004        );
12005        let message = refused.to_string();
12006        assert!(
12007            message.starts_with(
12008                "unsupported: the a blocking wait cannot keep the held signal SIGCHLD: signal 32 \
12009                 stopped the injection that puts the guest's signal mask back and replaced it"
12010            ),
12011            "{message}"
12012        );
12013    }
12014
12015    /// A refusal from the mask restoration replaces the wait's result, whether
12016    /// that is a value or an errno, unless the wait already ended with a refusal
12017    /// of its own, which came first. A mask that could not be put back still
12018    /// ends the run.
12019    #[test]
12020    fn a_restoration_refusal_replaces_the_result_unless_the_wait_refused_first() {
12021        let tool = |refusal: HeldSignalRefusal| Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(refusal));
12022        let restoration = HeldSignalRefusal {
12023            wait: None,
12024            held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
12025            replacing: None,
12026            loss: HeldSignalLoss::Restoration,
12027        };
12028        let replaced = HeldSignalRefusal {
12029            wait: None,
12030            held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
12031            replacing: Some(libc::SIGUSR1),
12032            loss: HeldSignalLoss::Replaced,
12033        };
12034        let not_restored = BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored {
12035            pid: Pid::from_raw(1),
12036            tid: Pid::from_raw(1),
12037            attempts: 16,
12038            last_error: Some(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR),
12039        };
12040
12041        assert_eq!(result_after_restore(Ok(()), Ok(3)).unwrap().unwrap(), 3);
12042        assert_eq!(
12043            refusal(result_after_restore(Err(tool(restoration)), Ok(3)).unwrap()),
12044            restoration
12045        );
12046        assert_eq!(
12047            refusal(
12048                result_after_restore(Err(tool(restoration)), Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into()))
12049                    .unwrap()
12050            ),
12051            restoration
12052        );
12053        assert_eq!(
12054            refusal(result_after_restore(Err(tool(restoration)), Err(tool(replaced))).unwrap()),
12055            replaced
12056        );
12057        assert_eq!(
12058            diagnostic(result_after_restore(
12059                Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(not_restored))),
12060                Ok(3)
12061            )),
12062            not_restored
12063        );
12064    }
12065
12066    /// A guest whose next `stops` injections are stopped by a signal that
12067    /// `/proc` never shows, as one that arrives after the read before an
12068    /// injection and that the backend then holds: nothing leaves a queue, so the
12069    /// stop cannot be identified.
12070    fn unidentified_stops_guest(stops: usize) -> (WaitGuest, Kernel) {
12071        let (guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
12072        kernel.lock().unwrap().outcomes =
12073            std::iter::repeat_n(MaskOutcome::StoppedBefore, stops).collect();
12074        (guest, kernel)
12075    }
12076
12077    /// A stop that cannot be identified, such as a default-ignored `SIGCHLD`
12078    /// that arrives after the read, used to end the wait with `ERESTARTNOHAND`
12079    /// for a call whose restart code is not a kernel restart code. With no
12080    /// handler to run, the call then restarted, and a relative `poll` timeout
12081    /// or a timed polling `FUTEX_WAIT` started again with a fresh deadline
12082    /// (round-8 High 1 on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). The
12083    /// stop is now held and the injection runs again, so the wait goes on with
12084    /// its absolute deadline, as the blind retry before this machinery did.
12085    #[tokio::test]
12086    async fn a_stop_that_cannot_be_identified_keeps_a_timed_wait_and_its_deadline() {
12087        for deadline in [true, false] {
12088            let (mut guest, kernel) = unidentified_stops_guest(1);
12089            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12090            let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, true, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
12091                .with_deadline(deadline);
12092
12093            let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
12094
12095            assert!(
12096                matches!(result, Ok(Ok(0))),
12097                "deadline={deadline}: {result:?}"
12098            );
12099            assert_eq!(
12100                kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.len(),
12101                2,
12102                "deadline={deadline}"
12103            );
12104            assert_eq!(wait.held, None, "deadline={deadline}");
12105        }
12106    }
12107
12108    /// A wait with a deadline absorbs stops without the bound that ends any
12109    /// other wait after `MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS`, because a restart would start its
12110    /// timeout again (round-8 High 1 on
12111    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). A wait without one still
12112    /// ends at the bound, and, while the backend holds only a signal whose loss
12113    /// does not matter (an ignored `SIGUSR1` sent again and again here), with
12114    /// `ERESTARTNOINTR`: it is not refused.
12115    #[tokio::test]
12116    async fn only_a_wait_without_a_deadline_ends_after_the_absorbed_stop_bound() {
12117        let stops = 100;
12118        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
12119        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(usr1, usr1);
12120        kernel.lock().unwrap().repost_after_take = stops - 1;
12121        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12122        let mut wait =
12123            KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, true, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND).with_deadline(true);
12124        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
12125        assert!(matches!(result, Ok(Ok(0))), "{result:?}");
12126        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.len(), stops + 1);
12127        assert_eq!(wait.held.map(|held| held.kind), Some(HeldKind::Harmless));
12128
12129        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(usr1, usr1);
12130        kernel.lock().unwrap().repost_after_take = stops - 1;
12131        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12132        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, true, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12133        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
12134        assert!(
12135            matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR))),
12136            "{result:?}"
12137        );
12138        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.len(), 65);
12139    }
12140
12141    /// At the same bound, a wait without a deadline whose backend holds a
12142    /// signal whose loss matters (a default `SIGCHLD`, sent again and again)
12143    /// used to end with `ERESTARTNOINTR` too. It now ends with a
12144    /// `HeldSignalRefusal` (round-10 High 1 on
12145    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
12146    #[tokio::test]
12147    async fn a_wait_that_reaches_the_stop_bound_holding_a_sigchld_is_refused() {
12148        let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD), 0);
12149        kernel.lock().unwrap().repost_after_take = 100;
12150        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12151        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
12152
12153        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
12154
12155        assert_eq!(
12156            refusal(result),
12157            HeldSignalRefusal {
12158                wait: None,
12159                held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
12160                replacing: None,
12161                loss: HeldSignalLoss::StopBound,
12162            }
12163        );
12164        assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.len(), 65);
12165    }
12166
12167    /// At the same bound, a stop that cannot be identified, after stops by a
12168    /// signal whose loss does not matter (an ignored `SIGUSR1` sent again and
12169    /// again), used to end a wait without a deadline with `ERESTARTNOINTR`,
12170    /// which let the backend deliver the unidentified signal, possibly a
12171    /// `SIGCHLD`, at a moment host timing could set. It now ends with a
12172    /// `HeldSignalRefusal`; a wait with a deadline, which has no bound, goes on
12173    /// (round-10 High 1 on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
12174    #[tokio::test]
12175    async fn an_unidentified_stop_at_the_stop_bound_is_refused() {
12176        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
12177        for deadline in [false, true] {
12178            let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(usr1, usr1);
12179            {
12180                let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
12181                // 64 identified stops, the bound, then one that `/proc` never
12182                // shows.
12183                kernel.repost_after_take = 63;
12184                kernel.outcomes = VecDeque::from([MaskOutcome::StoppedBefore]);
12185            }
12186            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12187            let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, true, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
12188                .with_deadline(deadline);
12189
12190            let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
12191
12192            if deadline {
12193                assert!(matches!(result, Ok(Ok(0))), "{result:?}");
12194                assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.len(), 66);
12195                assert!(wait.held_unidentified);
12196            } else {
12197                assert_eq!(
12198                    refusal(result),
12199                    HeldSignalRefusal {
12200                        wait: None,
12201                        held: None,
12202                        replacing: None,
12203                        loss: HeldSignalLoss::StopBound,
12204                    }
12205                );
12206                assert_eq!(kernel.lock().unwrap().requested.len(), 65);
12207            }
12208            assert_eq!(
12209                kernel.lock().unwrap().taken.len(),
12210                64,
12211                "deadline={deadline}"
12212            );
12213        }
12214    }

12279    /// A `SIGCHLD` that arrives after the read before an injection stops it in a
12280    /// way that cannot be identified, and a second one, pending at the next
12281    /// read, would stop the injection made again and replace the first in the
12282    /// backend's one slot. The first may have been a signal whose loss matters,
12283    /// so the wait is refused before that injection, with or without a
12284    /// deadline (round-10 High 1 on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361),
12285    /// and the backend still holds the first signal. This is the refusal a
12286    /// flood of external `SIGCHLD` racing a timed futex wait's first injections
12287    /// met on hermit main ccbe5ae8 (`external_signal_interrupt`'s test of the
12288    /// flood, now
12289    /// `ptrace_timed_futex_wait_and_poll_keep_their_deadline_after_a_sigchld_flood`,
12290    /// which sends its flood before the wait starts).
12291    #[tokio::test]
12292    async fn a_sigchld_after_an_unidentified_stop_is_refused_before_it_replaces_it() {
12293        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12294        for deadline in [true, false] {
12295            let (mut guest, kernel) = stopping_guest(0, 0);
12296            {
12297                let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
12298                // Pending only after the first read: the injection's stop is not
12299                // identified. Sent once more, so it is pending again at the read
12300                // before the injection made again.
12301                kernel.pending_repost = chld;
12302                kernel.repost_after_take = 1;
12303            }
12304            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12305            let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, true, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
12306                .with_deadline(deadline);
12307
12308            let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut wait, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
12309
12310            let refused = refusal(result);
12311            assert_eq!(
12312                refused,
12313                HeldSignalRefusal {
12314                    wait: None,
12315                    held: None,
12316                    replacing: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
12317                    loss: HeldSignalLoss::Replaced,
12318                },
12319                "deadline={deadline}"
12320            );
12321            let message = HeldSignalRefusal {
12322                wait: Some(Sysno::futex),
12323                ..refused
12324            }
12325            .to_string();
12326            assert!(
12327                message.starts_with(
12328                    "unsupported: the futex wait cannot keep a held signal that could not be \
12329                     identified: the pending SIGCHLD would stop the next injection and replace it"
12330                ),
12331                "deadline={deadline}: {message}"
12332            );
12333            assert!(wait.held_unidentified, "deadline={deadline}");
12334            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
12335            assert_eq!(
12336                kernel.requested.len(),
12337                1,
12338                "deadline={deadline}: the second injection is not made"
12339            );
12340            assert_eq!(kernel.taken, vec![libc::SIGCHLD], "deadline={deadline}");
12341            assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, Some(libc::SIGCHLD), "deadline={deadline}");
12342            assert!(kernel.lost.is_empty(), "deadline={deadline}");
12343            assert_eq!(kernel.pending, chld, "deadline={deadline}");
12344        }
12345    }

12367            refusal(result),

12369                wait: None,

12385    /// In a wait with a deadline, a held signal that would end the wait natively

12502    /// A wait that ends with a `HeldSignalRefusal` is refused through the
12503    /// unsupported-operation policy that `refuse_unserviceable_operation`
12504    /// applies: a run that is not fail-closed gets the `ERESTARTNOINTR` restart
12505    /// it got before, and a fail-closed one with `exit_on_unsupported_syscall`
12506    /// ends with the typed `UnsupportedSyscallError` for the wait's call. Every
12507    /// other result passes through, and the message names the wait, the
12508    /// signals and the pull request.
12509    #[tokio::test]
12510    async fn a_held_signal_refusal_follows_the_unsupported_operation_policy() {
12511        // Any wait will do; aarch64 has ppoll, not poll.
12512        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
12513        const WAIT: Sysno = Sysno::poll;
12514        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
12515        const WAIT: Sysno = Sysno::ppoll;
12516        let refused = || {
12517            Err::<i64, Error>(Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(HeldSignalRefusal {
12518                wait: None,
12519                held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
12520                replacing: Some(libc::SIGWINCH),
12521                loss: HeldSignalLoss::Replaced,
12522            })))
12523        };
12524        let (mut guest, _kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
12525        guest.config.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = false;
12526        let result = refuse_held_signal_loss(&mut guest, WAIT, refused()).await;
12527        assert!(
12528            matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR))),
12529            "{result:?}"
12530        );
12531        let result = refuse_held_signal_loss(&mut guest, WAIT, Ok(3)).await;
12532        assert!(matches!(result, Ok(3)), "{result:?}");
12533        let result =
12534            refuse_held_signal_loss(&mut guest, WAIT, Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into())).await;
12535        assert!(
12536            matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS))),
12537            "{result:?}"
12538        );
12539
12540        guest.config.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = true;
12541        guest.config.exit_on_unsupported_syscall = true;
12542        guest.config.shutdown_on_unsupported_syscall = false;
12543        let result = refuse_held_signal_loss(&mut guest, WAIT, refused()).await;
12544        match result {
12545            Err(Error::Tool(error)) => assert!(
12546                matches!(
12547                    error.downcast_ref::<crate::UnsupportedSyscallError>(),
12548                    Some(crate::UnsupportedSyscallError(WAIT))
12549                ),
12550                "{error:#}"
12551            ),
12552            other => panic!("expected the typed refusal, got {other:?}"),
12553        }
12554
12555        let message = HeldSignalRefusal {
12556            wait: Some(WAIT),
12557            held: Some(libc::SIGCHLD),
12558            replacing: Some(libc::SIGWINCH),
12559            loss: HeldSignalLoss::Replaced,
12560        }
12561        .to_string();
12562        for part in [
12563            "poll",
12564            "SIGCHLD",
12565            "SIGWINCH",
12566            "https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361",
12567        ] {
12568            assert!(message.contains(part), "{part} missing from: {message}");
12569        }
12570    }
12571
12572    /// A guest with a caught `SIGCHLD` pending, outside its mask. With
12573    /// `gated_backend`, its configuration is the one under which the scheduler
12574    /// models signal targets: serialized threads and a backend that reports the
12575    /// kernel's signal state.
12576    fn caught_sigchld_guest(gated_backend: bool) -> (WaitGuest, Kernel) {
12577        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
12578        guest.config.sequentialize_threads = gated_backend;
12579        detcore_model::config::set_kernel_signal_facts(&mut guest.config.backend, gated_backend);
12580        {
12581            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
12582            kernel.pending = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12583            kernel.caught = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12584        }
12585        (guest, kernel)
12586    }
12587
12588    /// A caught `SIGCHLD` pending outside the guest's mask, which the scheduler
12589    /// did not commit in this turn (`admit`), never ends a gated
12590    /// wait, on any backend and whoever sent it: `/proc` cannot tell a
12591    /// `SIGCHLD` a guest or the scheduler sent at a deterministic point from the
12592    /// one the kernel posts for a child event at a moment set by host timing
12593    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). The signal stays queued
12594    /// and is delivered when the call returns. The waits of `select` and
12595    /// `pselect6` hold nothing and end for it, as Linux ends them for any caught
12596    /// signal (`core_sys_select`).
12597    #[tokio::test]
12598    async fn a_pending_caught_sigchld_ends_a_select_wait_but_no_gated_wait() {
12599        for gated_backend in [false, true] {
12600            let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(gated_backend);
12601            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12602
12603            let gated = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12604            assert!(
12605                !gated.interrupted().unwrap(),
12606                "a pending caught SIGCHLD does not end a gated wait \
12607                 (gated_backend={gated_backend})"
12608            );
12609
12610            let select = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest);
12611            assert!(
12612                select.interrupted().unwrap(),
12613                "the pending caught SIGCHLD ends a select wait (gated_backend={gated_backend})"
12614            );
12615            assert_eq!(
12616                kernel.lock().unwrap().pending,
12617                kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
12618                "the signal stays queued for the guest's handler"
12619            );
12620        }
12621    }
12622
12623    /// A caught `SIGCHLD` the scheduler committed to the thread ends a gated
12624    /// wait, but only in the turn whose resume names it
12625    /// (`KernelSignalWait::admit`), and never when a host-timed
12626    /// source a guest armed can post `SIGCHLD` too: that copy could arrive at a
12627    /// moment host timing sets (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
12628    #[tokio::test]
12629    async fn a_committed_sigchld_ends_a_gated_wait_unless_a_host_timed_source_can_post_it() {
12630        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12631        let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12632        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12633
12634        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12635        assert!(
12636            !wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
12637            "an uncommitted SIGCHLD is held"
12638        );
12639        wait.admit(chld, 0);
12640        assert!(
12641            wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
12642            "a committed SIGCHLD ends the wait"
12643        );
12644        wait.admit(0, 0);
12645        assert!(
12646            !wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
12647            "the next turn's resume names nothing, so the SIGCHLD is held again"
12648        );
12649
12650        let mut host_timed = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12651        host_timed.hold_until_return(chld);
12652        host_timed.admit(chld, 0);
12653        assert!(
12654            !host_timed.interrupted().unwrap(),
12655            "a SIGCHLD a host-timed source can post stays held although committed"
12656        );
12657    }
12658
12659    /// A `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, which the schedule recorded in its
12660    /// private queue and the turn admits (`KernelSignalWait::admit`), ends a
12661    /// gated wait from the thread's own queue only: one pending only on the
12662    /// shared queue, which a host-timed child event can fill, decides nothing.
12663    /// It is admitted for the turn alone, and never when a host-timed source
12664    /// can post `SIGCHLD` (R2b-2 stage 3,
12665    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
12666    #[tokio::test]
12667    async fn an_admitted_private_sigchld_ends_a_gated_wait_from_the_threads_own_queue_only() {
12668        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12669        let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12670        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12671
12672        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12673        wait.admit(0, chld);
12674        assert!(
12675            wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
12676            "the thread's own copy ends the wait"
12677        );
12678        assert!(
12679            wait.interrupts_only_by_committed(
12680                &read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid()).unwrap()
12681            ),
12682            "only the admitted copy ends it, so the turn's probe runs first"
12683        );
12684        kernel.lock().unwrap().shared = chld;
12685        assert!(
12686            !wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
12687            "a SIGCHLD pending only on the shared queue is held"
12688        );
12689        kernel.lock().unwrap().shared = 0;
12690        wait.admit(0, 0);
12691        assert!(!wait.interrupted().unwrap(), "the next turn holds it again");
12692
12693        let mut host_timed = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12694        host_timed.hold_until_return(chld);
12695        host_timed.admit(0, chld);
12696        assert!(
12697            !host_timed.interrupted().unwrap(),
12698            "a SIGCHLD a host-timed source can post stays held"
12699        );
12700    }
12701
12702    /// An admitted private `SIGCHLD` that only the wait mask lets in is
12703    /// delivered under that mask (`interrupts_only_under_wait_mask`), as a
12704    /// committed one is: an `epoll_pwait` whose temporary mask unblocks a
12705    /// `SIGCHLD` the thread's own mask blocks (R2b-2 stage 3).
12706    #[tokio::test]
12707    async fn an_admitted_private_sigchld_that_only_the_wait_mask_lets_in_is_delivered_under_it() {
12708        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12709        let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12710        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12711        kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked |= chld;
12712        let mut wait =
12713            KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::EINTR).with_wait_mask(Some(0));
12714        let state = read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid()).unwrap();
12715        assert!(
12716            !wait.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state),
12717            "held while not admitted"
12718        );
12719        wait.admit(0, chld);
12720        assert!(wait.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state));
12721    }

12723    /// `admit_under_block` keeps a recorded private `SIGCHLD` only once every
12724    /// blockable signal is blocked in place, and only if the thread's own
12725    /// queue holds `SIGCHLD`, read after the block. A turn that admits nothing
12726    /// makes no request; a refused setter keeps the wait's fallback, the
12727    /// injected `block` after the first probe; a wait whose earlier injected
12728    /// `block` failed (`unblockable`, no `saved_mask`) keeps nothing (R2b-2
12729    /// stage 3, M3c of the rev5 review).
12730    #[tokio::test]
12731    async fn a_recorded_private_sigchld_is_kept_only_under_a_block_in_place() {
12732        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12733        // The block publishes the guest's own mask, already published here,
12734        // so no request leaves the test (`publish_wait_mask`).
12735        let mut published = PublishedWaitMask(Some(guest_mask()));
12736
12737        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12738        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12739        kernel.lock().unwrap().setter.push_back(None);
12740        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12741        assert_eq!(
12742            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
12743                .await
12744                .unwrap(),
12745            chld,
12746            "blocked in place, and the thread's own queue holds it"
12747        );
12748        assert!(wait.blocked_in_place);
12749        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
12750        drop(_proc);
12751
12752        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12753        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12754        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12755        assert_eq!(
12756            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, 0, 0, &mut published)
12757                .await
12758                .unwrap(),
12759            0
12760        );
12761        assert!(
12762            kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty(),
12763            "nothing admitted, no request"
12764        );
12765        assert_eq!(
12766            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, chld, &mut published)
12767                .await
12768                .unwrap(),
12769            0,
12770            "a SIGCHLD a host-timed source can post is not admitted"
12771        );
12772        assert!(kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty());
12773        drop(_proc);
12774
12775        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12776        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12777        kernel.lock().unwrap().shared = chld;
12778        kernel.lock().unwrap().setter.push_back(None);
12779        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12780        assert_eq!(
12781            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
12782                .await
12783                .unwrap(),
12784            0,
12785            "only on the shared queue: not the recorded copy"
12786        );
12787        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
12788        drop(_proc);
12789
12790        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12791        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12792        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12793        assert_eq!(
12794            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
12795                .await
12796                .unwrap(),
12797            0,
12798            "the setter refuses (no answer queued)"
12799        );
12800        assert!(
12801            wait.needs_block(),
12802            "the injected block after the first probe stays"
12803        );
12804        drop(_proc);
12805
12806        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12807        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12808        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
12809        wait.unblockable = true;
12810        assert_eq!(
12811            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
12812                .await
12813                .unwrap(),
12814            0,
12815            "an earlier injected block failed: no block, no private copy"
12816        );
12817        assert!(kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty());
12818    }

12820    /// A host signal can arrive after a pipe turn read an empty pending set.
12821    /// The private probe must not take it into the backend's held slot and
12822    /// retry to EAGAIN: later /proc reads cannot see that slot, and the guest
12823    /// cannot run its handler until the polling call returns. This uses the
12824    /// real Guest::inject_with_retry, with the ptrace outcome modeled by
12825    /// WaitGuest: the first stopped attempt holds the signal and returns
12826    /// ERESTARTSYS; a retried empty probe returns EAGAIN.
12827    #[tokio::test]
12828    async fn a_signal_after_an_empty_pipe_turn_snapshot_still_interrupts() {
12829        let usr1 = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
12830        for (sent, blocked) in [(true, false), (false, false), (true, true)] {
12831            let own_mask = guest_mask() | if blocked { usr1 } else { 0 };
12832            let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(1), own_mask);
12833            {
12834                let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
12835                kernel.caught = usr1;
12836                kernel.pending_repost = if sent { usr1 } else { 0 };
12837                kernel.stops_for_pending = true;
12838                kernel.empty_read_probes = Some(0);
12839                kernel.private_record = Some((0, 0));
12840                kernel.setter.extend([None, None]);
12841            }
12842            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12843            let mut wait = Some(KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS));
12844            let mut published = PublishedWaitMask(Some(own_mask));
12845            let read = syscalls::Read::new()
12846                .with_fd(3)
12847                .with_buf(AddrMut::from_raw(guest.arena.as_mut_ptr() as usize))
12848                .with_len(1);
12849            let first = turn_signals_with_block(
12850                &mut guest,
12851                &mut wait,
12852                ProbeMaskPolicy::PrivateProbe,
12853                0,
12854                false,
12855                &mut published,
12856            )
12857            .await
12858            .unwrap();
12859            assert!(!first.ends(false), "the snapshot preceded the signal");
12860            assert_eq!(
12861                guest.inject_with_retry(read).await,
12862                Err(Errno::EAGAIN),
12863                "an empty nonblocking read transfers no bytes"
12864            );
12865            let next = turn_signals_with_block(
12866                &mut guest,
12867                &mut wait,
12868                ProbeMaskPolicy::PrivateProbe,
12869                0,
12870                false,
12871                &mut published,
12872            )
12873            .await
12874            .unwrap();
12875            wait.as_mut()
12876                .unwrap()
12877                .restore(&mut guest, None)
12878                .await
12879                .unwrap();
12880            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
12881            assert_eq!(kernel.blocked, own_mask, "the guest's mask is restored");
12882            assert_eq!(kernel.empty_read_probes, Some(1));
12883            assert_eq!(
12884                next.ends(false),
12885                sent && !blocked,
12886                "sent={sent}, blocked={blocked}, pending={:#x}, held={:?}, taken={:?}",
12887                kernel.pending,
12888                kernel.held_slot,
12889                kernel.taken
12890            );
12891            assert_eq!(kernel.pending, if sent { usr1 } else { 0 });
12892            assert_eq!(kernel.held_slot, None, "the signal stays kernel-pending");
12893        }
12894    }

12896    /// A pipe turn (`turn_signals_with_block`) counts the recorded private
12897    /// `SIGCHLD` only where the gate holds, a block is in force and the
12898    /// thread's own queue holds it. Not on the scalar writer's first attempt,
12899    /// the guest's own write, which blocks nothing (`ProbeMaskPolicy::Guest`): an
12900    /// injection of that turn could take the copy into the backend's single
12901    /// held slot. Not without the gate, as on a socket. Not from the shared
12902    /// queue alone (R2b-2 stage 3).
12903    #[tokio::test]
12904    async fn a_pipe_turn_counts_a_recorded_private_sigchld_only_under_a_block_in_place() {
12905        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12906        let turn = |may_block: bool, gate: bool, shared: bool| async move {
12907            // Thread 1, the thread state's own number, so a request may leave.
12908            let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(1), guest_mask());
12909            {
12910                let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
12911                kernel.pending = chld;
12912                kernel.caught = chld;
12913                kernel.shared = if shared { chld } else { 0 };
12914                kernel.setter.push_back(None);
12915                kernel.private_record = Some((0, chld));
12916            }
12917            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12918            let mut wait = Some(KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS));
12919            let mut published = PublishedWaitMask(Some(guest_mask()));
12920            let pending = turn_signals_with_block(
12921                &mut guest,
12922                &mut wait,
12923                if may_block {
12924                    ProbeMaskPolicy::PendingSignals
12925                } else {
12926                    ProbeMaskPolicy::Guest
12927                },
12928                0,
12929                gate,
12930                &mut published,
12931            )
12932            .await
12933            .unwrap()
12934            .pending;
12935            if let Some(wait) = wait.as_mut() {
12936                wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
12937            }
12938            let blocked_in_place = !kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty();
12939            (pending & chld, blocked_in_place)
12940        };
12941        assert_eq!(
12942            turn(true, true, false).await,
12943            (chld, true),
12944            "blocked in place: admitted"
12945        );
12946        assert_eq!(
12947            turn(false, true, false).await,
12948            (0, false),
12949            "the writer's first attempt blocks nothing: held"
12950        );
12951        assert_eq!(turn(true, false, false).await, (0, true), "no gate: held");
12952        assert_eq!(
12953            turn(true, true, true).await,
12954            (0, true),
12955            "the shared queue alone: held"
12956        );
12957    }

12959    /// The pipe path's hold leaves out an admitted private `SIGCHLD`
12960    /// (`turn_signals_before_discard`'s `private`): it counts in the turn's
12961    /// `pending`, where without it the hold keeps it out (R2b-2 stage 3).
12962    #[test]
12963    fn a_pipe_turn_counts_an_admitted_private_sigchld() {
12964        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
12965        let state = KernelSignalState {
12966            pending: chld,
12967            thread_pending: chld,
12968            caught: chld,
12969            ..KernelSignalState::default()
12970        };
12971        assert_eq!(
12972            turn_signals_before_discard(&state, 0, 0, 0, NamedRealTime::Woken, 0).pending,
12973            0,
12974            "held"
12975        );

12977            turn_signals_before_discard(&state, 0, 0, 0, NamedRealTime::Woken, chld).pending,
12978            chld,
12979            "admitted"
12980        );

12983    /// The same `SIGCHLD` ends a select wait before an injection that is not a
12984    /// probe (`inject_absorbing`: the change of mask that blocks signals for the
12985    /// wait), with `ERESTARTNOHAND`, which the handler's run turns into `EINTR`.
12986    /// The waits of `select` and `pselect6` make every probe with
12987    /// `inject_first_probe`. A gated wait makes the injection, and the `SIGCHLD`
12988    /// that stops it is held until the call returns.
12989    #[tokio::test]
12990    async fn a_pending_caught_sigchld_ends_a_select_wait_before_the_injection() {
12991        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
12992        kernel.lock().unwrap().stops_for_pending = true;
12993        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
12994
12995        let mut select = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest);
12996        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut select, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
12997        assert!(
12998            matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND))),
12999            "{result:?}"
13000        );
13001        {
13002            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
13003            assert!(kernel.requested.is_empty(), "nothing is injected");
13004            assert_eq!(kernel.pending, kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD));
13005        }
13006        assert_eq!(select.held, None);
13007
13008        let mut gated = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
13009        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut gated, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
13010        assert!(matches!(result, Ok(Ok(0))), "{result:?}");
13011        {
13012            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
13013            assert_eq!(kernel.taken, vec![libc::SIGCHLD]);
13014            assert_eq!(kernel.requested.len(), 2, "stopped once, then ran");
13015        }
13016        assert_eq!(gated.held.map(|held| held.kind), Some(HeldKind::Precious));
13017    }

13019    /// The kernel's next dequeue: the private queue before the shared one, a
13020    /// synchronous signal first, then the lowest number, outside the mask.
13021    #[test]
13022    fn next_dequeued_follows_the_kernel_order() {
13023        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit;
13024        let state = KernelSignalState {
13025            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGUSR2) | bit(libc::SIGSEGV),
13026            shared_pending: bit(libc::SIGHUP),
13027            ..KernelSignalState::default()
13028        };
13029        assert_eq!(
13030            state.next_dequeued(0),
13031            Some((libc::SIGSEGV, SignalQueue::Thread))
13032        );
13033        assert_eq!(
13034            state.next_dequeued(bit(libc::SIGSEGV)),
13035            Some((libc::SIGUSR2, SignalQueue::Thread))
13036        );
13037        assert_eq!(
13038            state.next_dequeued(bit(libc::SIGSEGV) | bit(libc::SIGUSR2)),
13039            Some((libc::SIGHUP, SignalQueue::Shared))
13040        );
13041        assert_eq!(state.next_dequeued(!0), None);
13042    }

13044    /// A stop is identified only when exactly the predicted signal left its
13045    /// queue and the mask and dispositions are unchanged; arrivals do not matter.
13046    #[test]
13047    fn a_stop_is_identified_only_by_exactly_its_signal() {
13048        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit;
13049        let before = KernelSignalState {
13050            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | bit(libc::SIGWINCH),
13051            shared_pending: bit(libc::SIGHUP),
13052            ..KernelSignalState::default()
13053        };
13054        let took = |after: KernelSignalState, signal, queue| {
13055            stop_took_only(&before, &after, signal, queue)
13056        };
13057        let after = KernelSignalState {
13058            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGWINCH) | bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
13059            ..before
13060        };
13061        assert!(took(after, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
13062        assert!(
13063            !took(after, libc::SIGWINCH, SignalQueue::Thread),
13064            "SIGWINCH is still queued"
13065        );
13066        let two_left = KernelSignalState {
13067            thread_pending: 0,
13068            ..before
13069        };
13070        assert!(!took(two_left, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
13071        let shared_left = KernelSignalState {
13072            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGWINCH),
13073            shared_pending: 0,
13074            ..before
13075        };
13076        assert!(!took(shared_left, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
13077        let mask_changed = KernelSignalState {
13078            blocked: bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
13079            ..after
13080        };
13081        assert!(!took(mask_changed, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
13082        let disposition_changed = KernelSignalState {
13083            ignored: bit(libc::SIGWINCH),
13084            ..after
13085        };
13086        assert!(!took(
13087            disposition_changed,
13088            libc::SIGUSR1,
13089            SignalQueue::Thread
13090        ));
13091    }

13093    /// A select wait with a pselect6 temporary mask (`with_wait_mask`) holds a
13094    /// caught signal that the temporary mask blocks, and the guest's own mask
13095    /// does not, when it stops an injection before `block` takes effect, as
13096    /// Linux keeps it pending for the whole call; without the temporary mask
13097    /// the same stop ends the wait, and a signal only the temporary mask
13098    /// unblocks ends it too (review of
13099    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4051).
13100    #[test]
13101    fn a_signal_the_temporary_mask_blocks_is_held_not_ended() {
13102        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit;
13103        let (guest, _kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
13104        let before = KernelSignalState {
13105            pending: bit(libc::SIGALRM),
13106            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGALRM),
13107            blocked: guest_mask(),
13108            caught: bit(libc::SIGALRM) | bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
13109            ..KernelSignalState::default()
13110        };
13111        let plain = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest);
13112        assert_eq!(
13113            plain.stop_verdict(&before, libc::SIGALRM),
13114            StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
13115        );
13116        let masked = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest).with_wait_mask(Some(bit(libc::SIGALRM)));
13117        assert_eq!(
13118            masked.stop_verdict(&before, libc::SIGALRM),
13119            StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
13120        );
13121        let unblocking = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest).with_wait_mask(Some(0));
13122        assert_eq!(
13123            unblocking.stop_verdict(&before, libc::SIGUSR2),
13124            StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
13125        );
13126    }

13128    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929> (the Codex review of
13129    /// slice 2, round 4, finding A): the errno a woken `poll` answered where
13130    /// its wait ended is settled again at the handler's last step, from the
13131    /// signal sets as they stand there, and that answer is what the call
13132    /// returns. Between the two, other threads may have run and taken the
13133    /// caught copy (EINTR becomes ERESTARTSYS, and the deadline kept for the
13134    /// rerun stays), or sent one (ERESTARTSYS becomes EINTR, the kept deadline
13135    /// is dropped, and the delivery's record of the result follows). A call
13136    /// that did not end that way, a result that is not one of the two, or
13137    /// sets the backend does not report, leave the result as it is.
13138    // x86_64 only: the restart block is poll's; ppoll has none.
13139    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
13140    #[test]
13141    fn a_woken_wait_is_settled_again_at_its_return() {
13142        let bit = |signal: i32| 1u64 << (signal - 1);
13143        let alrm = bit(libc::SIGALRM);
13144        let caught_copy = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, alrm, 0, 0, alrm);
13145        let taken = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, 0, 0, 0, alrm);
13146        let kept = || RestartBlock {
13147            rip: 0x1234,
13148            deadline: Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(4567)),
13149            call: RestartCall::PollRerun(reverie::syscalls::Poll::new().with_timeout(100)),
13150        };
13151        let erestartsys = || Err::<i64, Error>(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into());
13152        let eintr = || Err::<i64, Error>(Errno::EINTR.into());
13153        let errno_of = |res: &Result<i64, Error>| match res {
13154            Err(Error::Errno(errno)) => Some(*errno),
13155            _ => None,
13156        };
13157        for (label, flagged, sets, res, settled, keeps_restart) in [
13158            (
13159                "sent",
13160                true,
13161                Some(caught_copy),
13162                erestartsys(),
13163                Some(Errno::EINTR),
13164                false,
13165            ),
13166            (
13167                "taken",
13168                true,
13169                Some(taken),
13170                eintr(),
13171                Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS),
13172                true,
13173            ),
13174            (
13175                "unchanged",
13176                true,
13177                Some(caught_copy),
13178                eintr(),
13179                Some(Errno::EINTR),
13180                false,
13181            ),
13182            (
13183                "not flagged",
13184                false,
13185                Some(caught_copy),
13186                erestartsys(),
13187                Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS),
13188                true,
13189            ),
13190            (
13191                "no sets",
13192                true,
13193                None,
13194                erestartsys(),
13195                Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS),
13196                true,
13197            ),
13198            ("a result", true, Some(caught_copy), Ok(1), None, true),
13199        ] {
13200            let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
13201            guest.sets = sets;
13202            guest.thread.woken_wait = if flagged {
13203                WokenWait::Poll
13204            } else {
13205                WokenWait::None
13206            };
13207            guest.thread.restart_block = Some(kept());
13208            guest.thread.delivery_interruption = Some(reverie::Interruption::Return {
13209                syscall: Sysno::poll as i64,
13210                result: errno_of(&res).map_or(1, |errno| -i64::from(errno.into_raw())),
13211            });
13212            let Settlement::Return(res) = settle_woken_wait_at_return(&mut guest, Sysno::poll, res)
13213            else {
13214                panic!("{label}: a poll's settlement refused");
13215            };
13216            assert_eq!(errno_of(&res), settled, "{label}");
13217            // Kept for the return's deliveries only where it was settled.
13218            assert_eq!(
13219                matches!(guest.thread.woken_wait, WokenWait::Settled(_)),
13220                flagged && sets.is_some() && settled.is_some(),
13221                "{label}"
13222            );
13223            assert_eq!(
13224                guest.thread.restart_block.is_some(),
13225                keeps_restart,
13226                "{label}"
13227            );
13228            if let Some(settled) = settled {
13229                assert_eq!(
13230                    guest.thread.delivery_interruption,
13231                    Some(reverie::Interruption::Return {
13232                        syscall: Sysno::poll as i64,
13233                        result: -i64::from(settled.into_raw()),
13234                    }),
13235                    "{label}"
13236                );
13237            }
13238        }
13239    }
13240
13241    /// A recorded send's ERESTARTSYS is admitted again at its return: a
13242    /// signal with an effect there refuses the run, and only ignored copies
13243    /// keep the restart, settled for the return's deliveries.
13244    #[test]
13245    fn a_recorded_sends_restart_is_admitted_again_at_its_return() {
13246        let alrm = 1u64 << (libc::SIGALRM - 1);
13247        for (label, sets, refused) in [
13248            (
13249                "ignored",
13250                reverie::SignalSets::new(0, alrm, 0, alrm, 0),
13251                false,
13252            ),
13253            (
13254                "caught",
13255                reverie::SignalSets::new(0, alrm, 0, 0, alrm),
13256                true,
13257            ),
13258            ("default", reverie::SignalSets::new(0, alrm, 0, 0, 0), true),
13259        ] {
13260            let (mut guest, _) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
13261            guest.sets = Some(sets);
13262            guest.thread.woken_wait = WokenWait::Send;
13263            let settlement = settle_woken_wait_at_return(
13264                &mut guest,
13265                Sysno::sendto,
13266                Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into()),
13267            );
13268            assert_eq!(
13269                matches!(settlement, Settlement::Refuse(_)),
13270                refused,
13271                "{label}"
13272            );
13273            assert_eq!(
13274                matches!(guest.thread.woken_wait, WokenWait::Settled(_)),
13275                !refused,
13276                "{label}"
13277            );
13278        }
13279    }
13280}

13286    fn bit(signal: i32) -> u64 {

13290    fn settled(send: bool, errno: Errno, pending: u64) -> SettledWait {
13291        SettledWait {
13292            send,
13293            sysno: if send {
13294                Sysno::sendto
13295            } else {
13296                #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
13297                {
13298                    Sysno::poll
13299                }
13300                #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]

13310
13311    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929> (the Codex review of
13312    /// slice 2, round 5, findings 1 and 2, Claude's round-5 finding 1, and
13313    /// both round-6 reviews): each delivery at the return of a woken wait is
13314    /// checked against its settlement, and refused where the backend would
13315    /// settle the call as Linux never does. A poll settled EINTR is refused at
13316    /// the delivery that ends its return with no handler run: one that runs no
13317    /// handler (a sibling ignored the signal during the delivery's turn) and
13318    /// after which nothing the mask leaves unblocked is pending, not while
13319    /// another signal is left for the return to deliver next, and not when the
13320    /// default action ends the process. A poll settled ERESTARTSYS whose
13321    /// handler has SA_RESTART is refused while a signal that was pending at
13322    /// the settlement, behind the one with no handler, with a handler, is that
13323    /// signal or still pending; without SA_RESTART the backend's protocol fails
13324    /// the call with EINTR, which drops the record kept for its rerun, and for
13325    /// a signal that came later, with no such signal left, it restarts the
13326    /// call. A recorded send settled ERESTARTSYS is refused for a handler
13327    /// without SA_RESTART, which would fail it with EINTR. An unread flag
13328    /// refuses, and is taken as no SA_RESTART for the record.
13329    #[test]
13330    fn each_delivery_at_a_woken_return_is_checked_against_its_settlement() {
13331        let alrm = bit(libc::SIGALRM);
13332        let usr1 = bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
13333        let term = bit(libc::SIGTERM);
13334        // SignalSets::new(pending, shared_pending, blocked, ignored, caught).
13335        let caught = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, 0, 0, usr1, alrm);
13336        let ignored_now = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, 0, 0, usr1 | alrm, 0);
13337        let handler_left = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, term, 0, usr1 | alrm, term);
13338        let fatal_left = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, term, 0, usr1 | alrm, 0);
13339        let ignored_left = reverie::SignalSets::new(usr1, 0, 0, usr1 | alrm, 0);
13340        let blocked_left = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, term, term, usr1 | alrm, term);
13341        let default_now = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, 0, 0, usr1, 0);
13342        let pending_handler_left = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, term, 0, usr1, alrm | term);
13343        let pending_handler_taken = reverie::SignalSets::new(0, 0, 0, usr1, alrm | term);
13344        use WokenRefusal::*;
13345        for (label, settled, delivered, sets, sa_restart, refusal, eintr) in [
13346            // A poll settled EINTR.
13347            (
13348                "eintr, handler",
13349                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13350                true,
13351                caught,
13352                None,
13353                None,
13354                false,
13355            ),
13356            (
13357                "eintr, ignored meanwhile, nothing left",
13358                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13359                true,
13360                ignored_now,
13361                None,
13362                Some(EintrWithoutHandler),
13363                false,
13364            ),
13365            (
13366                "eintr, ignored meanwhile, a handler left",
13367                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13368                true,
13369                handler_left,
13370                None,
13371                None,
13372                false,
13373            ),
13374            (
13375                "eintr, ignored meanwhile, a fatal default left",
13376                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13377                true,
13378                fatal_left,
13379                None,
13380                None,
13381                false,
13382            ),
13383            (
13384                "eintr, ignored meanwhile, an ignored copy left",
13385                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13386                true,
13387                ignored_left,
13388                None,
13389                None,
13390                false,
13391            ),
13392            (
13393                "eintr, ignored meanwhile, only a blocked handler left",
13394                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13395                true,
13396                blocked_left,
13397                None,
13398                Some(EintrWithoutHandler),
13399                false,
13400            ),
13401            (
13402                "eintr, dropped",
13403                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13404                false,
13405                caught,
13406                None,
13407                Some(EintrWithoutHandler),
13408                false,
13409            ),
13410            (
13411                "eintr, the default ends the process",
13412                settled(false, Errno::EINTR, alrm),
13413                true,
13414                default_now,
13415                None,
13416                None,
13417                false,
13418            ),
13419            // A poll settled ERESTARTSYS.
13420            (
13421                "erestartsys, SA_RESTART, pending",
13422                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1 | alrm),
13423                true,
13424                caught,
13425                Some(true),
13426                Some(RestartAfterHandler),
13427                false,
13428            ),
13429            (
13430                "erestartsys, no SA_RESTART, pending",
13431                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1 | alrm),
13432                true,
13433                caught,
13434                Some(false),
13435                None,
13436                true,
13437            ),
13438            (
13439                "erestartsys, SA_RESTART, came later",
13440                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1),
13441                true,
13442                caught,
13443                Some(true),
13444                None,
13445                false,
13446            ),
13447            (
13448                "erestartsys, SA_RESTART, came later, a pending handler left",
13449                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1 | term),
13450                true,
13451                pending_handler_left,
13452                Some(true),
13453                Some(RestartAfterHandler),
13454                false,
13455            ),
13456            (
13457                "erestartsys, SA_RESTART, came later, the pending handler taken",
13458                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1 | term),
13459                true,
13460                pending_handler_taken,
13461                Some(true),
13462                None,
13463                false,
13464            ),
13465            (
13466                "erestartsys, no SA_RESTART, came later",
13467                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1),
13468                true,
13469                caught,
13470                Some(false),
13471                None,
13472                true,
13473            ),
13474            (
13475                "erestartsys, flag unread",
13476                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1 | alrm),
13477                true,
13478                caught,
13479                None,
13480                Some(RestartAfterHandler),
13481                true,
13482            ),
13483            (
13484                "erestartsys, ignored",
13485                settled(false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1 | alrm),
13486                true,
13487                ignored_now,
13488                None,
13489                None,
13490                false,
13491            ),
13492            // A recorded send.
13493            (
13494                "send, no SA_RESTART",
13495                settled(true, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1),
13496                true,
13497                caught,
13498                Some(false),
13499                Some(SendEintr),
13500                false,
13501            ),
13502            (
13503                "send, SA_RESTART",
13504                settled(true, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1),
13505                true,
13506                caught,
13507                Some(true),
13508                None,
13509                false,
13510            ),
13511            (
13512                "send, ignored",
13513                settled(true, Errno::ERESTARTSYS, usr1),
13514                true,
13515                ignored_now,
13516                None,
13517                None,
13518                false,
13519            ),
13520        ] {
13521            let delivery = WokenDelivery::new(libc::SIGALRM, delivered, Some(sets));
13522            assert_eq!(delivery.refusal(&settled, sa_restart), refusal, "{label}");
13523            assert_eq!(

13532#[cfg(test)]
13533mod turn_signal_tests {
13534    use super::*;
13535
13536    fn bit(signal: libc::c_int) -> KernelSigset {
13537        kernel_sigset_bit(signal)
13538    }
13539
13540    fn state(
13541        pending: KernelSigset,
13542        caught: KernelSigset,
13543        blocked: KernelSigset,
13544    ) -> KernelSignalState {
13545        KernelSignalState {
13546            pending,
13547            thread_pending: pending,
13548            caught,
13549            blocked,
13550            ..Default::default()
13551        }
13552    }
13553
13554    /// Rule 3 of R2b-1 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273): with
13555    /// no progress only a pending copy ends the call; after progress a named
13556    /// wake does too.
13557    #[test]
13558    fn a_named_wake_ends_a_call_only_after_progress() {
13559        let named = TurnSignals {
13560            named: bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
13561            pending: 0,
13562        };
13563        assert!(!named.ends(false));
13564        assert!(named.ends(true));
13565        let pending = TurnSignals {
13566            named: 0,
13567            pending: bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
13568        };
13569        assert!(pending.ends(false));
13570        assert!(pending.ends(true));
13571        assert!(!TurnSignals::default().ends(true));
13572    }
13573
13574    /// A caught SIGCHLD pending at a poll's turn is held unless the scheduler
13575    /// committed it, and a host-timed signal is held even then (arm A8).
13576    #[test]
13577    fn the_hold_leaves_out_an_uncommitted_sigchld_and_every_host_timed_signal() {
13578        let chld = bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
13579        let hup = bit(libc::SIGHUP);
13580        let s = state(chld | hup, chld | hup, 0);
13581        assert_eq!(
13582            turn_signals_before_discard(&s, 0, hup, 0, NamedRealTime::Woken, 0).pending,
13583            0
13584        );
13585        assert_eq!(
13586            turn_signals_before_discard(&s, 0, hup, chld, NamedRealTime::Woken, 0).pending,
13587            chld
13588        );
13589        assert_eq!(
13590            turn_signals_before_discard(&s, 0, hup, chld | hup, NamedRealTime::Woken, 0).pending,
13591            chld
13592        );
13593    }
13594
13595    /// A named signal counts only if the call's mask leaves it unblocked
13596    /// (rule 2). A real-time one counts only if its disposition delivers it
13597    /// for `writev`, which the drain never filters (rule 2), and as woken for
13598    /// the generic poll and the scalar writer, whose drain already tested it
13599    /// (rule 1), so a flush after the wake does not undo it (the Claude
13600    /// implementation review of R2b-1, F1).
13601    #[test]
13602    fn a_named_signal_counts_only_unblocked_and_a_real_time_one_by_its_call() {
13603        use NamedRealTime::ByDisposition;
13604        use NamedRealTime::Woken;
13605        let usr1 = bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
13606        let rt = bit(libc::SIGRTMIN());
13607        let s = state(0, usr1, usr1);
13608        for real_time in [Woken, ByDisposition] {
13609            assert_eq!(
13610                turn_signals_before_discard(&s, usr1, 0, usr1, real_time, 0).named,
13611                0
13612            );
13613            assert_eq!(
13614                turn_signals_before_discard(&s, 0, 0, usr1, real_time, 0).named,
13615                usr1
13616            );
13617        }
13618        let ignored_rt = KernelSignalState {
13619            ignored: rt,
13620            ..state(0, 0, 0)
13621        };
13622        assert_eq!(
13623            turn_signals_before_discard(&ignored_rt, 0, 0, rt, ByDisposition, 0).named,
13624            0
13625        );
13626        assert_eq!(
13627            turn_signals_before_discard(&ignored_rt, 0, 0, rt, Woken, 0).named,
13628            rt
13629        );
13630        assert_eq!(
13631            turn_signals_before_discard(&ignored_rt, rt, 0, rt, Woken, 0).named,
13632            0
13633        );
13634        let caught_rt = state(0, rt, 0);
13635        assert_eq!(
13636            turn_signals_before_discard(&caught_rt, 0, 0, rt, ByDisposition, 0).named,
13637            rt
13638        );
13639    }
13640}

13642/// The mask a thread is stopped under where its blocking call returned, until
13643/// its continuation turn (`continuation_mask`).
13644#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
13645pub(crate) enum ContinuationMask {
13646    /// The call's temporary mask: the call ran and a signal ended it.
13647    Temporary,
13648    /// Not known to the scheduler, in record and replay alike.
13649    Unknown,
13650    /// The thread's own mask, which the kernel restored before the call
13651    /// returned and holds in record and replay alike (with the signals it
13652    /// ignores blocked over it until after the continuation, when the call
13653    /// raised an `IgnoredSignalShield`).
13654    Restored,
13655}
13656
13657/// The mask `call`, having returned `result`, leaves its thread stopped under,
13658/// decided from what the kernel did, which the raw result tells and replay
13659/// serves as recorded:
13660/// - pselect6 and ppoll that a signal ended return `-ERESTARTNOHAND`, or the
13661///   `-EINTR` that `poll_select_finish` can still turn it into after keeping
13662///   the mask (a timeout write-back that faults, or the STICKY_TIMEOUTS
13663///   personality); epoll_pwait and epoll_pwait2 return `-EINTR`. Linux then
13664///   delivers the signal under the temporary mask and `rt_sigreturn` restores
13665///   the saved one (`restore_saved_sigmask_unless`, fs/select.c, fs/eventpoll.c
13666///   and kernel/signal.c at v6.9): `Temporary`.
13667/// - Their normal return: Linux restored the saved mask before returning. Their
13668///   `-ERESTARTSYS`, which the host reports when the signal reached the thread
13669///   before the call ran: the kernel never installed the mask, and the
13670///   recording holds that result. Either way `Restored`.
13671/// - rt_sigsuspend: `Unknown`, whatever its result. Whether it ran is not
13672///   recorded: record injects it live, where a signal arriving first yields a
13673///   host-timed `-ERESTARTSYS` (the kernel never installed the mask), and
13674///   replay re-injects it with retry, which never shows that. A rule on its
13675///   result would differ between the two (the Claude review of d1b9404c), and
13676///   a known temporary mask would claim one the kernel may not have installed
13677///   (the Codex review of da662bb2). The scheduler treats an unknown mask
13678///   alike in both: no `SIGCHLD` taker or signal target, no discard.
13679/// - Any other call: `Restored`; it installed no temporary mask.
13680pub(crate) fn continuation_mask(call: Syscall, result: &Result<i64, Error>) -> ContinuationMask {
13681    let ended_by = |errno: Errno| matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(error)) if *error == errno);
13682    let kept = match call {
13683        Syscall::RtSigsuspend(_) => return ContinuationMask::Unknown,
13684        Syscall::Pselect6(_) | Syscall::Ppoll(_) => {
13685            ended_by(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND) || ended_by(Errno::EINTR)
13686        }
13687        Syscall::EpollPwait(_) | Syscall::Other(Sysno::epoll_pwait2, _) => ended_by(Errno::EINTR),
13688        _ => false,
13689    };
13690    if kept {
13691        ContinuationMask::Temporary
13692    } else {
13693        ContinuationMask::Restored
13694    }
13695}
13696
13697#[cfg(test)]
13698mod temporary_mask_tests {
13699    use super::*;
13700
13701    /// The continuation mask follows what the kernel did: the temporary mask
13702    /// for an interrupted pselect6 or ppoll (`-ERESTARTNOHAND`, or the `-EINTR`
13703    /// it can become after the kernel kept the mask) and an interrupted
13704    /// epoll_pwait or epoll_pwait2 (`-EINTR`); the restored own mask for their
13705    /// normal return, a call the signal reached before it ran (`-ERESTARTSYS`)
13706    /// or another errno; unknown for every rt_sigsuspend, whose `-ERESTARTSYS`
13707    /// is host-timed in record and absent in replay; restored for a call
13708    /// without a temporary mask.
13709    #[test]
13710    fn the_continuation_mask_follows_what_the_kernel_did() {
13711        let restart = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND));
13712        let eintr = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EINTR));
13713        let pselect = Syscall::Pselect6(syscalls::Pselect6::new());
13714        let ppoll = Syscall::Ppoll(syscalls::Ppoll::new());
13715        let epoll = Syscall::EpollPwait(syscalls::EpollPwait::new());
13716        let epoll2 = Syscall::Other(
13717            Sysno::epoll_pwait2,
13718            reverie::syscalls::SyscallArgs::new(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
13719        );
13720        let before_entry = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS));
13721        let sigsuspend = Syscall::RtSigsuspend(syscalls::RtSigsuspend::new());
13722        let read = Syscall::Read(syscalls::Read::new());
13723        let ebadf = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EBADF));
13724        use ContinuationMask::*;
13725        for call in [pselect, ppoll] {
13726            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &restart), Temporary, "{call:?}");
13727            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &eintr), Temporary, "{call:?}");
13728            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &before_entry), Restored, "{call:?}");
13729            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &ebadf), Restored, "{call:?}");
13730            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &Ok(1)), Restored, "{call:?}");
13731        }
13732        for result in [&restart, &eintr, &before_entry, &Ok(0)] {
13733            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(sigsuspend, result), Unknown, "{result:?}");
13734        }
13735        for call in [epoll, epoll2] {
13736            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &eintr), Temporary, "{call:?}");
13737            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &restart), Restored, "{call:?}");
13738            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &before_entry), Restored, "{call:?}");
13739            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &Ok(0)), Restored, "{call:?}");
13740        }
13741        assert_eq!(continuation_mask(read, &restart), Restored);
13742    }
13743}

13745#[cfg(test)]
13746mod tool_decided_injection_tests {
13747    use super::*;
13748
13749    fn refusal(operation: reverie::UnsupportedOperation) -> Option<reverie::UnsupportedRefusal> {
13750        Some(reverie::UnsupportedRefusal::new(
13751            operation,
13752            Errno::ENOSYS,
13753            "KVM leaves this call to the Tool",
13754        ))
13755    }

13757    /// Only a `ToolDecided` refusal of an injected call is a Detcore defect;
13758    /// no refusal, or a refusal another call site owns (flock, process
13759    /// groups, a signal), is not judged here.
13760    #[test]
13761    fn only_a_tool_decided_refusal_is_an_internal_failure() {
13762        // Any injected call will do; aarch64 has getpgid, not getpgrp.
13763        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
13764        let (sysno, name) = (Sysno::getpgrp, "getpgrp");
13765        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
13766        let (sysno, name) = (Sysno::getpgid, "getpgid");
13767        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(7);
13768        let failure = tool_decided_injection_failure(
13769            refusal(reverie::UnsupportedOperation::ToolDecided),
13770            dettid,
13771            sysno,
13772        )
13773        .expect("a ToolDecided refusal is an internal failure");
13774        assert!(
13775            failure.starts_with(&format!(
13776                "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=tool-decided-injection dtid=7 syscall={name}"
13777            )),
13778            "{failure}"
13779        );
13780        assert!(
13781            failure.contains("KVM leaves this call to the Tool"),
13782            "{failure}"
13783        );
13784        assert_eq!(tool_decided_injection_failure(None, dettid, sysno), None);
13785        for operation in [
13786            reverie::UnsupportedOperation::Flock,
13787            reverie::UnsupportedOperation::ProcessGroups,
13788            reverie::UnsupportedOperation::Signal,
13789            reverie::UnsupportedOperation::NonLeaderExec,
13790        ] {
13791            assert_eq!(
13792                tool_decided_injection_failure(refusal(operation), dettid, sysno),
13793                None,
13794                "{operation:?}"
13795            );
13796        }
13797    }
